### Drip Edge Flashing Benefits & Costs

If you’re in the market for a new shingle roof, there is a lot more to consider than just what color you want. Drip edge flashing is one of the unsung heroes of shingle roofing systems, and in Florida, storm chaser roofers can use that to their advantage.

As your local roofing partner, PITCH Roofing is here to look out for you and your interests. That’s why we’re going to tell you everything you need to know about your drip edge, from what it does to your options during a roof replacement. Keep reading to be ready for your new shingle roof!
What Is Drip Edge Flashing?


In roofing, flashing refers to any thin sheet of metal that helps direct water away from vulnerable points on your roof. Drip edge flashing is the flashing that runs along the exterior of your roof and extends slightly past your shingles. When properly installed, your drip edge should have a flange that curves away from your fascia.

Like all pieces of flashing, your drip edge serves to direct water off your roof. Drip edge serves a more specific function, though. The edge of your roof is a potential spot for water to enter. By covering this edge, this essential piece of flashing greatly extends the length of your roof’s lifespan.

Drip edge flashing also helps protect your soffits and fascia. While soffits and fascia exist to prevent water from being driven by rain into the underside of your roof, drip edge exists to protect the soffits and fascia. By moving water away from these parts of your roof, a well-installed drip edge will keep your roof dry and protected.

So drip edge flashing serves to prevent water damage and keep your roof working longer. What else is it good for?
Benefits of Drip Edge Flashing
Keeping water out of your roof and protecting your fascia is already a tall order. But drip edge flashing can do even more. Let’s talk about the other benefits of installing an effective drip edge!
Keeps Out Pests
In Florida, we’ve got more than our fair share of natural pests. And in our experience, those pests are always looking for a way into local homes. Without a properly installed drip edge, there will be a small gap between your roof decking and fascia. This presents the perfect opportunity for pests to move in and start eating away at your roofing system from the inside out.

With drip edge flashing, however, this isn’t a problem. The flashing covers any potential gaps, preventing insects and birds from making homes in your roof. With how expensive extermination services can be, this is a huge advantage of drip edge flashing!
Increased Wind Resistance
If you have an asphalt shingle roof, then you’ll want all the help you can get keeping your shingles attached during hurricane season. While architectural shingles can resist winds better than old-school 3-tab shingles, even they will struggle to withstand a major hurricane near your home.

Drip edge flashing helps bolster their wind resistance, though. By anchoring your shingles, drip edge will help them withstand hurricane-force winds. Shingle roofs with drip edge flashing aren’t immune to high winds, but when a hurricane is in the neighborhood, every little bit of protection helps!
Enhances Gutter Efficacy
On a shingle roof, gutters do essential work moving water off your roof without wearing down your home’s foundation. And drip edge flashing makes them work even better. By guiding water directly to your gutters, drip edge will minimize the chance of water being stuck on your roof.

Without a drip edge, there’s a chance that water could fall straight down one of the gaps between your roof and gutters. This would both eat away at your foundation and increase the chance that water remains trapped on your roof. Trapped water is a recipe for rot and mold, so having effective gutters and drip edge is a must!
Cost of Drip Edge Flashing


Thus far, we’ve established that drip edge flashing offers a lot of advantages to Florida homeowners. With a roof replacement, though, we know that cost is always a concern. That’s why we’re going to review the average costs to install drip edge in Florida!

With the cost of drip edge flashing, it all comes back to the material. When choosing your drip edge, you’ll be able to pick from a variety of durable metals. In Florida, here’s how much you can expect each one to cost, including the labor for installation:

 	Aluminum: $3 per square foot
 	Steel: $5 per square foot
 	Copper: $10 per square foot

Why Don’t All Roofers Install Drip Edge Flashing?
If drip edge flashing makes your roof last longer, prevents leaks, and is generally affordable, why isn’t it on every roof? Technically, it should be. Florida building codes require drip edges to be installed on all shingle roofs. However, not all roofers follow local regulations and ordinances.

We’re talking about storm chasers, specifically. These roofers will come to town after a major storm and do their best to sell you a dirt-cheap roofing system. In the face of a natural disaster, they use people’s fear and financial concerns to convince them to sign a contract for an extremely cheap shingle roof.

What they don’t tell you is that you are not getting a complete roofing system. If anyone shows up to replace your roof at all, which is not guaranteed, they will only tear off and replace your shingles without taking the time to replace damaged decking, install a new underlayment, or apply drip edge flashing. The result is an incomplete shingle roof made of cheap materials that can’t protect your property.

This is why it’s so important to stick with local roofers and ensure that you’re getting a detailed, itemized roofing quote. Don’t settle for just a flat price. The only way to be sure that you’re getting a complete roofing system, including drip edge, is to receive an itemized estimate that factors in the costs of all parts of your new roof, not just the shingles.

### 3 Causes of Asphalt Shingle Roof Leaks & How We Repair Them

No homeowner wants to deal with a roof leak. But if you’ve got an asphalt shingle roof, leak repair services are something that you will likely need at some point in your roof’s lifetime. With so many potential causes and solutions to roof leaks, though, it can be hard to know where to start.

PITCH Roofing is a full-service roofing company made up of veteran local roofers. Today, we want to talk about why your asphalt shingle roof could be leaking and how we’ll fix these issues to get your roof back to 100%. Keep reading to see what our local roofing pros can do to fix your roof!
Damaged Asphalt Shingles


The most common way for a shingle roof to start leaking is through damage to the shingles. This can come from a lot of different factors, such as:

 	Winds from a tropical storm or hurricane removing or tearing your shingles
 	UV rays causing your shingles to crack and curl
 	Trapped moisture on your roof leading to rot and mold growth, which weakens your shingles
 	Improper installation resulting in poorly-installed shingles that don’t keep out the elements

Whatever the cause, damaged asphalt shingles cannot keep your roof safe. While your roofing system has a water-resistant underlayment beneath the shingles, this protective layer cannot keep out everything. Over time, water will eat away at your underlayment until it completely penetrates into your roof and causes a leak.
Asphalt Shingle Roof Leak Repair for Damaged Shingles
The good news is that replacing a handful of shingles is a quick and easy repair. All your contractors will need to do is tear off the damaged shingles and install new ones. During this process, they will take special care to ensure that your new shingles are the same type and color as your old ones and that your new shingles are properly installed and line up with the rest of your roof.

While this is a simple roof repair, we do not recommend trying to DIY this. For one thing, there is a risk of you accidentally damaging your roof while trying to install new shingles. But even if you do the job right, it’s possible that you could void your roof warranties by working on your roof instead of hiring a contractor. Check the details of your warranty policy before doing any work on your roof!
Damage to Pipe Boot Flashing
Almost every shingle roof has a pipe boot. This is flashing surrounding a pipe vent, a tube sticking out of your roof, usually over your kitchen or bathroom. This vent helps balance your home’s plumbing and prevent leaks. Surrounding the vent is a section of flashing designed to prevent water from entering your home through the vent.

Over time, the sun’s UV rays and thermal contractions can weaken the flashing around your vent. This creates the opportunity for water to slide through these new cracks and gaps and enter your roofing system. Flashing around your vents will not last as long as your shingles, so asphalt shingle roof leak repair services will be necessary for most homeowners.
Fixing Flashing Around Your Vents
Generally, this issue is easy to identify because water will come in directly below wherever your pipe is. And fixing it is also fairly straightforward. To prevent water from getting past your flashing, our roofers will install a rubber collar around the boot to cover any damaged sections.

This collar should be strong enough to last for the remaining lifespan of your roof. Alternatively, you could have your contractors replace the vent entirely. This is not the usual course of action, though, because replacing the pipe is a much more expensive and involved roof repair.
Problems with Roof Flashing


Flashing isn’t just installed around your vents. Metal flashing is common at various points on a shingle roof, including valleys and around skylights and chimneys. These thin strips of metal help direct water off your roof and safeguard the integrity of your shingles. But over time, they can lose their efficacy.

There are many ways for roof flashing to become damaged or stop working properly. Some of the most common ways for flashing to be damaged include:

 	Improper installation
 	Hail or storm debris hitting the flashing at high speeds
 	High winds tearing off or weakening flashing
 	Warping from temperature fluctuations over the years

Regardless of how the damage happens, you can expect damaged flashing to let a lot of water into your home. For this reason, you should seek out asphalt shingle roof leak repair services as soon as you know that you have an issue with your flashing.
Repairing Damaged Flashing
Exactly how a contractor fixes your flashing will depend on the type of flashing you have and how it was damaged. Across the board, however, you can expect this to be a major repair. Replacing flashing is complicated and time-intensive, which increases leak repair costs.

The job can be especially expensive if there is severe water damage to your roof. If this is the case, then the parts of your roof surrounding the damaged flashing may need to be completely replaced. This means removing shingles, your underlayment, and even your roof decking, to replace them all with new materials.

### Causes & Repairs for Metal Roof Leaks

Having a leaking roof is never fun, but it can be especially frustrating if you have a metal roof. You paid a lot for enhanced protection, and it can feel like a let-down when your roof runs into problems anyway. While leaks are a possibility for any roofing system, our metal roof leak repair services will resolve your issue and restore your roof to 100 percent functionality.

We’re PITCH Roofing, and as your local roofing partner, we’re the metal roofing experts you can trust. With decades of experience installing and repairing metal roofs in Florida, we know the common pitfalls that these roofs run into. Before we get into how we can help, let’s review some of the most common reasons that metal roofs start leaking.
Common Causes of Metal Roof Leaks in Florida


Metal roofs can withstand hurricane-force winds, extreme UV rays, and heavy rain. That’s why it’s one of the best roofing systems in Florida! Despite all these protections, though, there are some areas where we tend to see water penetrating into metal roofing systems. To identify how we can help, let’s talk about the areas where your metal roof is vulnerable.
Metal Roofing Fasteners
If you recently got a new metal roof and it’s already leaking, it’s probably because your roof was not fastened correctly. This is most commonly an issue for exposed fastener metal roofing systems, which require screws to be drilled down through your metal roofing sheets to adhere them to your roof.

Normally, installers drill these screws straight down to ensure that your metal panels aren’t going anywhere. If they drill at an angle, however, then they could leave space for water to enter your roofing system. Screwing too tight (or not tight enough) can cause the same problem. If anything goes wrong with your fasteners, then you’re probably going to need metal roof leak repair services.

Additionally, your fasteners can naturally loosen over time. This is especially common in older exposed fastening roofing systems, which tend to suffer some wear and tear. To stay ahead of this issue, it’s always a good idea to get regular roof inspections!
Metal Roof Flashing
Flashing seals penetrations in your roof and helps direct water away from it. When flashing becomes damaged, roof leaks are a common consequence. You’ll usually find flashing around your vents, valleys, and any roofing features like skylights.

Unfortunately, flashing rarely lasts as long as your metal roofing system. Most often, your flashing will be damaged by your roof’s expansion and contraction with the sun’s heat. While metal roofs are made to withstand this subtle movement, flashing just can’t keep up over the years. As a result, you’ll need metal roof leak repair services as your flashing starts to age.
Metal Roof Seams
Metal roof seams are the place where your roofing panels overlap. With proper roof installation, these areas should be tightly sealed to prevent water intrusions. With time or improper installation, however, they can slacken and allow water into your roof.

When your roof is first installed, it will have seals around the seams to keep water out. Over time, these seals start to slacken and can allow small amounts of water into your roof. As the water continues to flow, you can expect the damage to grow and more water to enter your roofing system. Over time, you’ll start to notice the damage to your roof and will require metal roof leak repair services.
How Metal Roof Leak Repair Services Work


When you choose PITCH to handle your metal roof leak repair job, we’ll start by inspecting your roof to identify the cause of your leak. From there, we’ll formulate a plan to address your problem at the source, providing long-term relief.

While every roof repair is tailored to the unique roof we’re working on, there are some tried and true solutions for metal roof leaks. Let’s take a look at some of the ways our experienced metal roofing contractors can fix your leak!
Replacing Fasteners
If your metal roof needs leak repair services because of issues with your fasteners, the simplest solution is usually to reinstall or replace them. This can be more complicated than it sounds, though.

While replacing fasteners does not require much in the way of materials, this is a very labor-intensive repair. This can raise your total metal roof leak repair costs, although you should have a good idea of how much you’ll pay after receiving your initial metal roof repair cost estimate.
Flashing Replacement
If your flashing has weakened over time, there’s no better solution than replacing it. When installing your new flashing, your roofers will make sure that the flashing is sealed to your roof, preventing water from getting in. In terms of cost, this is considered a fairly affordable metal roof leak repair job.
Sealant Application
Sometimes, all a metal roof needs to fix a leak is some strategically applied sealant. With a high-quality, water-resistant roof sealant, our roofers will be able to fix leaks caused by gaps in your seams.

In some cases, sealant by itself may not be enough. If the gap has grown especially wide, your roofers may have to install a protective fabric with the sealant to fill in the gap. This should not affect the overall aesthetic of your metal roof, and the result is still a dry, durable roofing system for your property!

### Can You Paint Roof Tiles in Florida?

If you want to breathe some new life into your roof, painting roof tiles could be exactly what you need. However, there are plenty of cases where painting your roof tiles will do more harm than good. So, how do you know which situation applies to you?

We’re here to help. As a local roofing company, PITCH Roofing has replaced, repaired, and helped maintain countless tile roofs across Florida. That’s how we know when to paint roof tiles, how to do it safely, and when it’s best to look into alternative ways to refresh your roof. Keep reading as we go over everything you need to know about painting your tile roof!
Should You Paint Your Roof Tiles?


When it comes to whether or not you should paint your roof tiles, the answer is a resounding maybe. Like with so many other things in roofing, it depends on the specifics of your roof. More accurately, it depends on the type of tile roof you have on your home.
Painting Clay Tile Roofs
Clay tile roofs are a classic option in Florida. Colored by natural tile pigments, these roofs are famous for their vibrancy and distinctive look. Part of their bold color comes from things naturally in tiles, while another part comes from the glaze that these tiles receive when going through the kiln.

The glaze is why painting clay roof tiles can pose a problem. On the one hand, the glaze improves your tiles’ water resistance and deepens their color. However, the same protective features that help clay tiles resist water also make them resistant to an even coating of paint. With the natural glaze in place, your clay tiles won’t take paint well.

The good news is that clay roof tiles don’t usually find themselves in a position where they need painting. While you may want to change up the color of your tiles, they should retain most or all of their pigmentation across their lifespan. If you decide that you’d like roof tiles in a new color, your best bet is to tear off your current tiles and have them replaced with new tiles in your preferred shade.
Painting Concrete Tile Roofs
If you’re looking into painting roof tiles because your roof has lost some of its pigmentation, you probably have a concrete tile roof. Concrete tiles are great because they’re a cost-effective way to get a high-quality tile roofing system. However, they don’t age quite as well as clay roofing tiles.

That’s largely because of the Florida sun. With our extreme UV, especially in the summer, concrete roof tiles often undergo some sun bleaching as they age. The upside, however, is that painting concrete roof tiles is an effective way to restore their color.

Unlike clay tiles, concrete tiles have no protective glaze. This means that you will have a much easier time getting your paint to stay on and apply evenly. However, since concrete tiles have a textured, porous surface, it can still be difficult to get an even coat of paint on them, especially if you’re not an experienced painter.
How to Prepare for Having Your Tile Roof Painted


Generally, we don’t recommend painting your own roof tiles. While it can be a good idea in some circumstances, painting is already difficult before you add in the extra challenges of safely accessing and working on your roof. Tiles are easy to shatter if you’re not sure how to navigate a tile roof, so it’s often best to leave this work to the pros!

That said, you will want to take some precautionary steps before having someone paint your roof tiles. These simple measures help ensure that the paint on your tiles lasts for as long as possible. Keep reading for our recommendations on prepping for a new coat of paint on your tiles!
Repair Any Damaged Tiles
Florida is tough on roofs. While tile roofs are hardy and durable, they’re not immune to all the wear and tear that Florida throws at them. Whether it’s cracked tiles, tiles that have slid out of place, or any other issue with your roof, it’s important to fix these issues before having someone paint your roof.

Think of it this way. If you paint over a broken or chipped roof tile, you’re paying someone to paint a tile that you’ll probably need to have replaced anyway. This can create a problem when it’s time to install a new tile in that spot, since new tiles may not perfectly match your painted ones. For this reason, it’s best to have your tile roof in top shape before getting it painted!
Clean Your Gutters
When debris gets caught in your gutters, it stops water from moving freely off your roof. This leads to a buildup in moisture, which is the exact opposite of what you want when having your roof tiles painted. By cleaning your gutters before the painters come out, you’re ensuring that your roof will be dry enough to let the paint completely settle and attach to your tiles.
Wash Your Tiles
Check with your painters to see if they’ll clean your roof before painting your roof tiles. While most will, some may not or may charge an extra fee for this service. No matter what, though, you have to make sure that your roof tiles are clean before painting them. Otherwise, the paint won’t adhere to the tiles properly.

That said, be careful when cleaning roof tiles. Not only could you hurt yourself, but you could damage your tile roof. A pressure washer is one of the best ways to efficiently clean a roof, but you need to use a specific PSI to avoid cracking your tiles. Usually, this is lower than 1,200 PSI, but consult with your manufacturer’s information to ensure that you’re using a safe pressure.

### Are You Ready for Hurricane Season 2025?

Hurricane season 2025 is officially underway, but it’s not too late to get ahead of the storms. Last year’s hurricane season was a beast for Floridians, and this year promises another active season. Whether you’re a new Florida resident or an old-school Floridian, PITCH Roofing is here to help you get ready to protect your property this summer!

As longtime Floridians ourselves, we understand the impulse to think that hurricane season won’t be that bad. But as we saw last year, the right storm (or storms) can do serious damage to both critical infrastructure and private property. Keep reading for a guide from real local roofers on how to get your home or commercial property ready for the next big storm!
Lessons from Hurricane Season 2024


If nothing else, last year’s hurricane season was very instructive. And if we look closely at what happened, we can get a lot of helpful information to prepare for hurricane season 2025. Let’s talk about the biggest lessons to be learned from last year’s storms!
Forecasts Are Accurate
It’s pretty common to hear long-term Florida residents express some skepticism about how accurate forecast models are, especially at the start of the season. While forecasters don’t always get it right and hurricanes are complicated, we saw last year that predictive models are largely accurate when they say to expect a more active hurricane season.

Let’s review some of the predictions from last year’s hurricane season and whether or not they came true:

 	Forecast: The NOAA predicted that there would be 17 to 25 named storms in the 2024 hurricane season.
 	Reality: There were 18 named tropical storms and hurricanes in the 2024 season.
 	Forecast: General wisdom was that there would be 8 to 13 total hurricanes in 2024.
 	Reality: There were 11 hurricanes in the Atlantic, much higher than the average number of 7.
 	Forecast: The NOAA warned that the Atlantic would see 4 to 7 major hurricanes in 2024.
 	Reality: There were 5 major hurricanes in and around Florida in 2024.

Forecasters aren't always right — hurricanes are too unpredictable for 100% accuracy. However, the leading forecasting agencies have a proven track record of overall accuracy and reliability. So, when you hear that hurricane season 2025 is going to be especially active, it would be wise to listen to that advice.
Quality Over Quantity
With hurricanes, you don’t need many different storms to do a lot of damage. It just takes the right storm at the right place to devastate both lives and property. We saw this last year with one of the deadliest and most destructive hurricanes in years — Hurricane Helene.

According to the NOAA, Helene made records as one of the most expensive storms in US history. With a total of $78.7 billion in damages, it’s hard to overstate just how devastating Hurricane Helene was to Florida communities. And that’s before considering the lives lost to Helene, which was the deadliest hurricane since Katrina in 2005. Even now, there are still many properties and families across the state that haven’t fully recovered.

When it comes to hurricanes, you don’t need an especially active hurricane season to see mass devastation. All it takes is one bad storm. That’s why it’s essential to be prepared for hurricane season 2025. With life and property on the line, there is no reason to let Florida’s hurricane season catch you unprepared.
Hurricanes Can Form at Any Time During the Season
It’s fairly common for people to think that hurricane season is really only a concern in the heart of the season, during August and September. The truth, though, is that hurricanes are a clear and present danger at any point in the season.

We saw this last year with Hurricane Beryl, which became the earliest Category 5 hurricane on record when it appeared on July 1st. In fact, this was only the second Category 5 storm recorded during the month of July in the Atlantic Ocean. That storm ended up causing $7.2 billion dollars in damage — more than enough to be worth taking seriously!

It’s important to remember that hurricane season goes from June 1st to November 30th. At any time within that range, hurricanes are a real possibility. So if you have preparations to do, don’t assume that you’ll have time to prepare and put off necessary preparations. Severe hurricanes are possible at any point during hurricane season 2025, so it’s important to get ready with that fact in mind.
Preparing for Hurricane Season 2025


There were a lot of lessons in hurricane season 2024. As Floridians, it’s up to us to take those lessons and get ready for the next series of storms. Let’s talk about the best things you can do to get ready for hurricane season 2025!
Plan Your Evacuation
When we had two back-to-back major storms last year, many people were caught off guard. While this was in many ways a worst-case scenario, it’s entirely possible that something similar (or worse) could happen in 2025. And when highways start filling up is not a good time to be figuring out your evacuation plan.

Nobody wants to leave their home behind when a hurricane blows in, but sometimes that’s the best way to keep yourself and your family safe. At the start of hurricane season 2025, it still isn’t too late to plan where you’re going to evacuate to, how you’ll get that, and what supplies you’ll need for the journey. Evacuation is a worst-case scenario, but it’s best to be prepared for the worst!
Stock Up on Provisions
Last year, Helene and Milton left some homes with no power or water for weeks. Hopefully, we won’t see conditions like this again this year. But in the interest of being prepared, you should assume you’ll see similar conditions this year and start getting ready now.

To get ready for hurricane season 2025, you should make sure your home has:

 	At least three days' worth of non-perishable food
 	One gallon of water per day per person in your home, with enough to last at least three days
 	Pet food and sanitary pads in case you can’t let your pets outside
 	Backup phone batteries and cell phone chargers
 	Chlorine bleach and a medicine dropper to clean non-potable water
 	Books, games, and other activities to keep you and your family entertained
 	Battery-operated fans to deal with the Florida summer heat
 	A first aid kit
 	A flashlight

These are just the bare essentials, and without them, you could be looking at an especially difficult hurricane season. By taking precautions now, you can make things much easier on yourself when the next big storm hits.
Get Your Roof Ready Now
In 2024, a lot of the damage went to roofs that were already old or needed work. The best way to deal with these problems is to take care of your roof before the storm comes in, not after. The adage “an ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure” is especially true when it comes to roofing!

If you notice missing shingles or even a minor roof leak, it’s important to get ahead of these issues now. Similarly, if you’ve been putting off a roof replacement, now is the time to get a new one so you can be ready for a major hurricane.

While some homeowners think that waiting for a storm to damage their roof is the way to go, this is a very risky gamble. Not only do you risk the destruction of your home as a whole without a strong roof, but you may only get a pro-rated payout for your old roof. In other words, you’d still be on the hook for most of your roof replacement costs!

If you’re not sure where to start, it’s always a good idea to get a roof inspection ahead of hurricane season. When our expert roofers come to inspect your roof, they’ll carefully look at every part of your roofing system to make sure your property is ready for the worst that hurricane season 2025 has to offer!

### Is Rain Louder on a Metal Roof?

Metal roofs are some of the most popular in Florida. As reliable, durable roofing systems, they're exactly what Floridians need to protect against hurricanes and tropical storms. There are trade-offs with any roofing system, though. One of the most common questions we get about metal roofs is whether rain on a metal roof is louder than rain on a shingle roof.

This is a great question — you don't want to invest in a new roof just to find out that it’s unbearably loud when it rains. PITCH Roofing has been installing metal roofs for years, and we know how these roofs perform in Florida. Stick with us as we answer all of your questions about rain on a metal roof!
Is Rain Louder on a Metal Roof?


The rumors are true: rain on a metal roof is especially loud. However, it may not be as loud as you think. The classic idea of a loud metal roof is based in old tin roofs used on barns — not exactly the kind of thing you’d see on a home or commercial structure in Florida in 2025. So, how loud is rain on a metal roof?

Generally, moderate rain on a metal roof is described as sounding like beads bouncing off your roof. Light rain sounds like a soft tapping sound, whereas some homeowners report that heavy rain sounds like a drum roll throughout their home. No matter how you look at it, rain on a metal roof will certainly be louder than rain on a shingle roof.

The good news is that you have some level of control over how much noise your roof makes. On multiple-story homes, you can expect the noise to be quieter on the ground floor. Additionally, you can cover up some of the sound with a healthy amount of insulation in your attic. This has the added bonus of helping regulate your home’s temperature!

At the end of the day, rain is going to make some extra noise on your metal roof. Before committing to a metal roof, it’s important to make sure you’re comfortable living this way. The good news, though, is that you can retain some control over how much noise your metal roof makes.
How to Dampen the Sound of Rain on a Metal Roof
Just because rain on a metal roof will always make noise doesn’t mean you can’t do anything about it. Here are some steps we recommend Florida homeowners take to reduce the sound of rain on their metal roofs!
Choose Your Type of Metal Roof Carefully
Different types of metal roofs will make more or less noise in the rain. A lot of this has to do with the makeup of the metal. For example, steel is a dense, thick metal roofing material, which helps muffle sound.

Aluminum, on the other hand, is much lighter and less dense. This allows sound to travel more easily through it, making it louder when it rains. Copper metal roofs are even denser than either of these options, although they’re also prohibitively expensive.

In addition to the type of metal, you should also consider what gauge of metal roofing panel you want. Rain on a metal roof with thick panels will be quieter than rain on thinner panels. There are trade-offs with having heavier roofing panels though, so be sure to discuss your options with your roofers!
Add Soundproofing Over Your Decking
If you’re concerned about how loud a metal roof will be in the rain, you can always soundproof your roof. Typically, your roof decking and water-resistant underlayment will add some insulation to muffle the sound. If that isn’t enough for you, though, you can always have your roofers install soundproofing on top of your decking.

By installing wood-fiber insulation boards over your decking, you can dampen a lot of the sound that comes from rain on a metal roof. While this will not completely block out the sound of rain, it’s your best bet if you want to see a significant reduction in noise levels. Since these boards also serve as insulation, you’ll also be helping to lower your monthly energy bills!
Choose Stone-Coated Steel


Traditional metal roofs are always going to be at least a bit loud during the rain. That’s part of the appeal of stone-coated steel roofing. As the name implies, this type of roofing uses metal panels that have been coated in protective stone granules. Usually, the appeal of this is a more welcoming and conventional appearance for residential roofs, but it’s also a great way to quiet rain on a metal roof!

That’s because the layers of stone granules help block raindrops from striking your metal panels directly. This does a lot to muffle sound waves and keep your roof quiet even during a storm. Since the surface texture is not as regular as that of a metal panel, the sound has a lot more difficulty traveling throughout your roofing system.

There are plenty of other benefits to stone-coated metal roofing as well. From improved UV resistance to reduced risk of denting, stone granules really do a lot to make metal roofing that extra little bit stronger. If you’re interested in stone-coated steel for your new metal roof, ask about this option when getting your free roofing estimate!

With many options to mitigate the sound of rain on a metal roof, you don’t have to choose between protection and comfort in your home!

### Effects of Hail Damage on Metal Roofs in Florida

When you think of storms in Florida, you probably think of hurricanes. While these are a serious threat to your roof, so are our occasional hailstorms. Hail can do a real number on your roof, even a metal one. That’s why we’re here to explain everything you need to know about your metal roof and hail damage!

Whether you have a metal roof with hail damage or you’re weighing your options ahead of a roof replacement, PITCH Roofing has your back. With great workmanship and unbeatable customer service, we’re the local roofers you want working on your property. Stick with us as we use our expertise to break down everything you need to know about metal roofs and hail damage in Florida!
Is Hail Damage a Threat to Metal Roofs in Florida?


Hail can do damage to just about any roofing system. And when you think of large balls of ice falling on metal, the risk for damage seems especially high. But are hailstorms really a threat to local metal roofs?

While hailstorms can certainly leave their mark on your metal roof, we wouldn’t say they’re dangerous in most cases. In order for hail to damage your metal roof, it would have to puncture your metal roofing sheets. While we get decent-sized hail in Florida, it’s rare that we see hail large enough to put your roof in danger.

More often, you might notice denting on your metal roof after a storm. This isn’t something that people are happy to see, but it’s also not a threat to the safety or function of your roof. Hail dents on a metal roof are a cosmetic issue. You could have the damage repaired, but even if you don’t, there is no reason to suspect that dents from hail will in any way shorten the life of your metal roofing system.
What Makes Hail Damage More Likely on a Metal Roof?
While hail is rarely dangerous for your metal roof, there are odd cases where hail can puncture sheets of metal. And, of course, homeowners want to minimize their roof’s risk of denting. That’s why we’re going to review some of the biggest factors that will determine if hail damages your metal roof and how severe that damage is!
Size of the Hail
Hail size is a big reason why metal roof hail damage is not a major problem in Florida. For hail to do serious damage, it should be about four and inches around or bigger. In Florida, however, hail is usually somewhere between the size of a pea and a quarter.

There are exceptions, though. The largest hail recorded in Florida was four and a half inches, so it’s certainly possible for hail to damage metal roofs in the Sunshine State. But in most cases, you’re looking at cosmetic damage at the very worst.
Gauge of Your Metal
The thicker your metal roof is, the more force it will take for hail to dent or puncture it. If you’re concerned about hail damage, then choosing a thicker metal may be best for you. With metal, thickness is measured by gauges. The higher the gauge, the thinner the metal.

In this way, a 28-gauge metal roof is thinner than a 22-gauge metal roof, and thus more likely to experience denting in a hailstorm. At the same time, thicker metal roofs are heavier and may not be suitable for all homes. As a homeowner, you’ll have to carefully weigh the pros and cons when selecting the right thickness for your metal roof.
Your Roof’s Paint
Surprisingly, the finish you choose for your metal roof can have a big impact on the appearance of hail damage. To be clear, no roof paint can protect your metal roof from hail damage. However, whether your metal roof has a matte or glossy finish will determine how easy it is to see hail damage on your roof.

Matte paint finishes make it harder to see any indentations in your metal roof. On the other hand, glossy finishes catch and reflect light, which can draw attention to minor roofing damage. If you’re concerned about hail damage marring the appearance of your metal roof, choosing a matte paint can reduce the risk of unsightly dents.
Will Insurance Cover Metal Roof Hail Damage?


If you’ve spotted hail damage on your metal roof, you’re probably wondering if insurance will take on some of the bill to repair it. Like with anything, whether or not you qualify for coverage will come down to the specifics of your damage and your policy. In our time as Florida roofers, though, here’s what we’ve noticed.

Most metal roofs have a cosmetic damage exclusion somewhere in the insurance policy. Specifically, these exclusions usually state that your insurer is not liable for any cosmetic damage that your metal roof receives during a storm. This includes hail as well as storm debris or fallen branches. So if the only hail damage to your metal roof is some denting, you likely won’t be covered for repairs.

On the other hand, if you have roof penetrations from hail damage, then your insurance will likely cover any necessary repairs or replacements. Bear in mind that this may not be for the full cost of the roofing services, however. Many homeowners insurance policies are prorated, meaning you’ll receive less money the older your roof is. Additionally, you will likely need to pay a certain deductible before you qualify for any insurance coverage.

### What Is a Shingle and Metal Roof?

Getting a new roof is not one-size-fits-all. From your materials to your vents to your drip edge, you’ll be making a lot of choices about the specific features of your roof. Lately, more and more Floridians are taking things a step further. By combining shingle and metal roofs, you can get customized protection that suits your needs and tastes.

How Does Combining Shingle and Metal Roofs Work?


If you’re new to the concept, having both shingles and metal on your roof can sound a little confusing. While everyone has heard of shingle roof replacements and metal roof replacements, combining the two isn’t exactly common. While it might be rare, however, combination shingle and metal roofs are a great way to protect your property.

Usually, homeowners approach this by replacing most of their roof with shingles. However, certain areas will have metal installed instead. These are typically porches, bay windows, dormer windows, and other sections of your roof that don’t take up much space. You can choose to install a larger section of metal roof if you like, but this will increase your roof replacement costs.

In Florida, strategically installing metal on your roof can be a great way to improve your hurricane resistance. While shingles are vulnerable to high winds, metal roofs do a much better job of withstanding hurricane-force winds. By combining shingle and metal roofs, you can get some of that top-notch protection without the daunting price tag of a full metal roof replacement.

This is a complicated process, and not just any roofers can do it. As veteran Florida contractors, we want to make sure you’re completely informed before making any big decisions. Keep reading for the things you need to know before committing to a roof replacement!
What to Know Before Getting a Combination Metal and Shingle Roof
Shingle and metal roofs can be perfect for the Florida weather, but they aren’t right for every home. And with something as important as a roof replacement, you need to be sure in your decision. That’s why we’re covering the important things you should know before scheduling your roof replacement!
Shingle and Metal Roofs Have Different Life Expectancies
Normally when replacing a roof, your entire roof will be torn off and reinstalled all at once. If you have a combination shingle and metal roof, however, this schedule gets disrupted. That’s because architectural shingles only last for 20 to 25 years in Florida. A standing seam metal roof, on the other hand, can last for 50 to 70 years.

This means that your shingles will probably need replacing before the metal section(s) of your roof. This isn’t a problem, so long as you choose roofers familiar with metal and shingle roofing. While they won’t need to replace your metal roof while taking off your shingles, it’s best to choose roofers who can safely navigate both materials.
The More Metal Your Roof Has, the More You’ll Pay
Most homeowners know that there is a difference in how much shingle and metal roofs cost. However, many people aren’t aware of just how big the difference is. If you choose to get a larger section of your roof replaced with metal, then those extra roof replacement costs can quickly add up.

For reference, architectural asphalt shingles cost around $7 per square foot, on average. This is a far cry from standing seam metal roofs, which cost closer to $20 per square foot. While metal roofs last much longer, this is a significant investment for most homeowners.

For this reason, many homeowners choose to limit the amount of their roofs that they replace with metal. Still, strategically installing metal roofing can strengthen your roof without drastically inflating the cost of your roof replacement! Alternatively, you could look into roof financing options if you’d like a roof with a larger section of metal.
Your Roofs Will Have Different Warranties


When you have one section with shingles and another with metal roofing, you have one set of warranties for each section of roofing. Navigating roofing warranties can already be tricky, and this only further complicates things. However, with a bit of know-how, you can effectively use your roofing warranties for each roofing system.

When you’re collecting roofing estimates, be sure to ask about your warranty options. Compare both your shingle and metal roofing warranties to make sure that you understand your different workmanship and material warranties, as well as any prorating terms. With two types of roofs on your home, you’ll have to do double the work to get the most out of your warranties!

Average Flat Roof Repair Costs

Low-Cost Flat Roof Repairs (>$600):

 	Patching and sealing small leaks
 	Repairing small sections of cracked or blistering roof materials
 	Fixing small sections of puncture damage or tears
 	Clearing away mold or dirt buildup

Medium-Cost Flat Roof Repairs ($600 - $1,500)

 	Fixing moderately sized leaks that have not reached your roof decking
 	Re-sealing seams that have loosened due to thermal expansion
 	Repairing water ponding and restoring proper drainage

High-Cost Flat Roof Repairs ($1,500 - $4,000+)

 	Widespread water damage that has reached your roof decking
 	Partial flat roof replacements

### Your Guide to Single-Ply Roof Membranes

Whether it’s a commercial or residential structure, all flat roofs in Florida need to be virtually waterproof. If you’re due for a flat roof replacement, you’re probably exploring your material options. As experienced Florida roofers, we can tell you that single-ply roof membranes are worth seriously considering.

We’re PITCH Roofing, and we’re here to tell you everything you need to know about single-ply roofing systems. If you’re planning your new flat roof, keep reading for everything you need to know about these durable, Florida-ready roofs!
What Is a Single-Ply Roof Membrane?
As the name implies, a single-ply roof membrane is a rubberized membrane that installers roll out across your roof in a single layer. Since the 1960s, this approach has provided a flat roofing option that is durable, reliable, and easy to install.

On the surface, a single-ply roof membrane sounds like a flimsy roofing system. After all, couldn’t a single ply easily be punctured? But thanks to advances in roofing technology, even a single-ply roof is strong and resilient enough to withstand the Florida elements.

One of the most popular single-ply roof membranes is thermoplastic polyolefin (TPO). Made of different types of resilient synthetic polymers, these rubber roofs can withstand the worst that Florida can throw at them. The protective polymers stand up to puncture damage as well as water intrusions. These sheets of rubber roofing are heat-welded to the roof, so you can be completely certain that there is a water-tight barrier.

This about covers the basics of single-ply flat roofing. Now, let’s talk about the biggest perks of choosing a single-ply roof membrane for your new flat roof.
Pros of Getting a Single-Ply Roof Membrane


When it comes to single-ply roofs, there is a lot to love. Flat roofs have unique roofing concerns compared to sloped roofs, and a single-ply roofing system is perfectly tailored to the needs of low-slope roofs. Let’s talk about some of the biggest advantages you can expect from your new TPO flat roof!
Easy, Affordable Installation
In roofing, the more complex something is, the more it costs to install. That’s because complicated roofs require both more time and more experience. But with a single-ply roof membrane, you’re looking at an easy, cost-effective roof replacement.

Many other flat roofing systems build up multiple layers on your roof. This requires extra time and labor. But with a TPO flat roof, it’s all rolled out in a single layer. This faster installation can save you a good deal of money during your roof replacement!
Energy-Efficient
In Florida, we’re all looking to lower our energy bills, especially during the summer. And a TPO single-ply roof membrane can help you do exactly that. TPO usually comes in white, which helps it reflect UV rays and heat away from your structure.

It isn’t just the color that helps with energy efficiency, either. The polymers that make up a TPO membrane are inherently UV-reflective. While you can get TPO in darker colors, this reduces its ability to help cool your structure.
Durability
In a lot of ways, a single-ply roof membrane is perfectly suited to Florida’s climate. TPO is able to naturally expand and contract with the sun’s heat. While this may not sound like a huge advantage, it allows your roof to endure heat and solar rays in a way that would destroy other roofing systems.

Thanks to the heat-welded seams, a TPO roof is extremely durable and well-adhered to your roof. Even in the event that water gets trapped on your roof, it’s unlikely that your roof will start to leak. This is also a long-lasting roof installation method — that’s why TPO roofs last for 30 years on average!
Downsides of a Single-Ply Roof Membrane


No roofing system is perfect, and single-ply roof membranes are no exception. To help you make an informed decision, lt’s talk about the downsides of this roofing option!
Untested Roofing Material
In the past decade, TPO roofs have seen a lot of changes in their chemical makeup. These improvements should help your single-ply roof membrane last longer and require less maintenance over time. However, the technology simply hasn’t existed long enough for us to be sure.

Experts firmly believe that a TPO roof should last for 30 years. But unlike with other flat roofing materials, this option hasn’t been on the market long enough for us to be 100% sure how it will age. In this way, there is some level of risk in choosing a single-ply roofing system.
Degrading Seams
Heat-welded seams are one of the most secure ways to secure a flat roof. However, they may not stay strong throughout the life of your roof. That’s because Florida’s extreme heat can weaken the seams over the years, causing them to loosen and potentially allow water inside your roofing system.

For this reason, it’s important to keep up with regular roof inspections if you choose a single-ply roof membrane. While this is certainly a con, it’s hardly unique to TPO flat roofing systems. Florida’s extreme UV rays can damage any roofing system, so this is just a fact of life with roofing in the Sunshine State.

### Deciding Between Roof Restoration & Roof Replacement

Wear and tear is an inevitable fact of life for roofs in Florida. And when you add in seasonal hurricanes, there are a lot of situations that could necessitate a roof replacement. You have alternatives, though. In many situations, roof restoration is a great way to safeguard your roof without replacing it entirely.

We’re PITCH Roofing, your local roofing partner. As veteran Florida roofers, we know when a roof needs restoration services and when you’re better off replacing it. To help you decide which option is best for your home, we’re going to walk you through everything you need to know about roof restoration in Florida!
What Is Roof Restoration?


Roof restoration is the tried and true process of repairing your roof and strengthening it to withstand the elements. Roof restoration services include inspecting the roof for existing damage, repairing that damage, and then applying weather-resistant coatings and sealants to protect your roof in the future.

Through this process, roof restoration strengthens and beautifies your roof to, in some ways, turn back the clock. Your roof will look better, be stronger, and last longer than it would with simple roof repairs. In this way, restoration can be a viable alternative to roof replacement. This process is suited for shingle, flat, metal, and tile roofs.

This is one approach to roof restoration. Another, also known as reroofing, works a bit differently. Instead of repairing existing damage, reroofing installs new shingles or metal over your old roof. This way, you save money because your roofers don’t need to tear off and dispose of your old roofing system.

No matter which type of restoration you get, you can expect it to go a long way in extending the life and durability of your roof. In hurricane-prone Florida, that’s nothing to sneeze at. Now, let’s talk about when roof restoration is appropriate.
When Is Roof Restoration a Good Idea?
There are a lot of situations where roof restoration is the right call. However, there are others where roof repairs or replacements could be more appropriate. Let’s look at how you can know that your roof is a good candidate for roof restoration services!
Your Decking & Insulation Are Dry
Roof restoration can go a long way in undoing many different types of roofing damage. However, restoration can’t address problems with your decking or insulation. Because these parts of your roofing system sit below the roof itself, there is no way to repair damage there without tearing off your old roof.

Usually, decking and insulation are damaged by water intrusions. This means that if your roof has a history of leaking, especially major leaks or many throughout your roof, then restoration may not be the best option. By adding weight to your roof, restoration could actually make your roof less secure if your decking is not dry and strong enough to support it.
Your Roof Is 10 Years Old or Older
With roof restoration, it’s best to act earlier rather than later. While you can get restoration services at any point, provided that your roof can support the weight, it’s best to get these services fairly early. If you can act before your roof sustains major damage, you’ll see better results with your roof’s longevity and durability after restoration.

At the same time, a new roof will not need restoration services. While being proactive is great, there's no need to restore a roof that's new and in great shape. That’s why we recommend roof restoration for roofs that are around 10 years old. This is a good way into your roof’s lifespan, but not so late that your roof is weak or nearing the end of its life.
You Want to Avoid a Roof Replacement


Even the most affordable roof replacement is anything but cheap. While roof financing can go a long way in making high-quality roofing services more accessible, there is still a high price point for replacing your roof. Restoration offers a chance to protect your roof for a fraction of the cost.

In Florida, average roof replacement costs are around $12,000 for shingles. Your numbers for roof restoration will vary. However, you can expect to pay roughly 50% less than what a roof replacement would cost, thanks to lower labor and material costs. If you’re looking to avoid replacing a roof while still protecting your home, there is no better option!
Is Roof Restoration Better Than a Roof Replacement?
This is a question that we get all the time. While it can be tempting to think of one service as better than another, the truth is that both services are great and appropriate for different situations. There are situations where roof restoration can better meet your needs than roof replacement, and vice versa.

To decide which is right for you, use the above tools and information. If you’re still on the fence, the next step is setting up a consultation with professional roofers. With PITCH, we recommend starting with a free, no-obligation roofing estimate.

### Identifying Wind Damage to Roof Shingles in Florida

Hurricane season 2025 is almost here. During the next few months, it’s likely that many Florida homeowners are going to be dealing with wind damage to roof shingles. Whether you’re getting prepared or looking for help after the storm has passed, PITCH Roofing is here to help you take care of your roof and protect your property!

The first step in helping you deal with the aftermath of a storm is sharing the most common signs of wind damage to your roof. We’ll then talk about when your insurance will cover wind damage and when you’ll be better off paying out of pocket. But first, let’s talk about the conditions that can cause wind damage to your asphalt shingles!
What Winds Can Damage Roof Shingles?


Tropical storms and hurricanes are just a fact of life in Florida. But many homeowners are surprised to learn how little wind it actually takes to damage a roof. So, at what wind speeds does shingle damage become a possibility?

 	45-60 mph Winds: If you have an old roof or a roof that already has some damage, this is all it takes to cause minor shingle damage. Thankfully, however, stronger roofing systems should be unaffected by winds at this speed.
 	61-74 mph Winds: At these speeds, 3-tab shingles in good condition will start to be damaged by high winds. Architectural shingles should still be unaffected, however, especially if your roof is under 15 years old.
 	75+ mph Winds: Any speed above 75 mph means that winds could damage your shingles. While 80 mph winds are not likely to tear off your entire roofing system, they can damage individual shingles.

As you can see, winds don’t have to be especially high to damage your roof. With this in mind, let’s talk about the biggest warning signs that your roof shingles have sustained wind damage!
Signs of Wind Damage to Roof Shingles in Florida
If your area has seen high winds recently, wind damage to roof shingles is a serious possibility. Asphalt shingles are made to withstand high winds, but a hurricane or tropical storm can still do serious damage. While there are obvious signs like missing shingles, we want to focus on the subtler signs of roof wind damage. Keep reading for the warning signs of wind damage that you need to know!
Lifted/Curled Shingles
Just because a shingle remains on your roof after a storm doesn’t necessarily mean it has avoided damage. Often, shingles are lifted, curled, or otherwise skewed by high winds without being completely torn off. While the shingle can still offer some protection like this, it’s also an entry point for water.

You’ll know that you have lifted shingles when your formerly straight rows of shingles suddenly show twisted or overlapping shingles. If your shingles look out of place, it’s probably because they’ve been partially moved by high winds.
Flipped Shingles
Sometimes, high winds can remove the nails holding your shingles in place. When one nail is removed but others remain, you’re looking at flipped shingles. This sign of wind damage to roof shingles is easy to spot because you’ll notice your shingles literally flapping in the wind!

In especially severe cases, you could see entire rows of shingles damaged this way. The larger the section of damaged shingles, the higher your risk of developing a roof leak. Water damage is one of the worst things that can happen to your roof, so it’s important to act quickly if you notice this issue!
Leaks in Your Home
In some cases, you may not be able to see any wind damage to your roof shingles from the ground. However, if you notice a leak, especially one that starts shortly after a storm, then you’re probably looking at damage to your roof shingles.

If you feel comfortable, you can get on your roof to take a closer look at your shingles. While shingles may look to be in place from the ground, up close, you’ll likely notice signs of wind damage. These include bending or curling patterns on your shingles. And if you find any shingles that you can easily lift up manually, then you’ve got a shingle roof in need of repairs!
When Does Insurance Cover Wind Damage to Roof Shingles?


Upon learning that their roofs have wind damage, one of the first questions we hear from homeowners is, “Will my insurance handle the costs?” The good news is that, yes, most homeowners insurance policies specifically cover wind damage caused by severe weather events. If you can prove that your roof was damaged in a recent storm, then you should qualify for coverage through your homeowners insurance.

However, using your insurance benefits is not always the best idea. If you only need a few shingles replaced, it may not be worth making a claim with your insurer. While you may be approved for your repairs, this can lead to higher premiums in the future. Additionally, your insurer may get suspicious if you file “too many” claims. You don’t want to get your repairs covered if it means paying out of pocket for a roof replacement!

If, on the other hand, you need a roof replacement due to wind damage to roof shingles, you should absolutely use your homeowners insurance. While they may not cover the full cost of your roof replacement, you pay your premiums so that you can enjoy this coverage, so you should try to get the most out of it that you can. Check out our full guide to filing a homeowners insurance claim here!

You could be looking at a quick repair that takes less than an hour, or you could be faced with the reality of needing a new roof. ### Does TPO Roofing Work Well for Mobile Homes in Florida?

If your home has a flat roof, then TPO could be the perfect material for your structure. Also called thermoplastic polyolefin, TPO roofing for mobile homes is a perfect fit. This single-ply roofing membrane is highly water-resistant, preventing even slow-draining water from penetrating into your roofing system.

Getting a new roof is as much about choosing the right roofers as it is about picking the right material. We’re PITCH Roofing, and as your local flat roofing partner, we’re here to tell you all about TPO roofing and what our crew can do for your roof replacement. Keep reading to see how we can help you protect
Advantages of TPO Roofing for Mobile Homes


As we mentioned, TPO is a single-ply roofing membrane. In other words, it’s a rubberized material made to resist water and other roofing hazards. During installation, contractors will roll out these roofing sheets across the roof of your mobile home, then heat-weld the TPO into place.

There are a lot of advantages to this tried-and-true installation method. When talking about TPO roofing for mobile homes, you can expect benefits like:

 	Durability: TPO is built to withstand heavy rainfall, high winds, and even hail!
 	Lower Energy Bills: Because TPO is so UV-reflective, it can actually cool your home and save you money!
 	Minimal Maintenance: Unlike shingles, TPO rarely needs repairs. If you want a roof you can rely on without frequent repairs, TPO is an excellent choice.
 	Affordable: TPO roofing comes at an affordable price point, making it appealing for a wide variety of homeowners.

Clearly, there are a lot of advantages to TPO roofing. But when you’re paying for a new roof, you want assurances that you’ll see a good return on your investment. So, how long will your TPO roof last on your mobile home in Florida?
How Long Does TPO Roofing Last on Mobile Homes?
A traditional shingle roof will last about 20 years in the Sunshine State. But with TPO roofing, your roof could have a significantly longer lifespan. On average, TPO roofs last for about 20 to 30 years. There are ways that you can increase your odds of having your roof last closer to 30 years, though.

In roofing, how well you take care of your roof is everything. While TPO roofs rarely need repairs, good roof maintenance is important for any roofing system. To get the longest possible lifespan out of your roof, you should:

 	Schedule regular roof inspections. One inspection per year is good when your roof is new, but you should increase it to twice a year if your TPO roof is more than 10 years old.
 	Keep your roof clean. Dirt and debris can slowly degrade your roof over time. To get a long life out of your roof, cleaning it as needed is the best course of action.
 	Repair issues quickly. While TPO roofs don’t need frequent repairs, they can occasionally have issues, like any roof. By acting quickly to get roofing problems resolved, you can save a lot of money on smaller repairs!

TPO roofing is a long-lasting material for mobile homes. But you can help it reach its maximum lifespan with a bit of care and consideration. Of course, we know there is one key area that we haven’t addressed yet: the price.
Cost of TPO Roofing for Mobile Homes

That’s because roofing costs depend on roof accessibility, size, and unique roofing quirks. For these reasons, the best way to find out how much your roof will cost is with a free roofing estimate.

On the other hand, however, we can still give you general pricing information. In Florida, TPO can cost anywhere from $4 to $10 per square foot to install. In practice, this usually looks like $5,000 to $12,000 for a new TPO roof on a mobile home.

### How to Get an Energy-Efficient Roof in Florida

In the thick of Florida summer, you can bet that your AC is working overtime. If you’re due for a new roof and looking for a way to lower your monthly energy bills, an energy-efficient roof is a great way to save some money. If you choose wisely, you could end up saving yourself hundreds of dollars per year on reduced energy costs.

We’re PITCH Roofing, and as your local roofing partner, we’re here to help you get an energy-efficient roof. With more than 60 years of combined experience with Florida roofing, we know how severe the local heat can be. Stick with us as we explain how an energy-efficient roof can help keep your home cool, even during the summer!
What Is an Energy-Efficient Roof?


An energy-efficient roof should, at its core, be a roof that helps your home stay cool even in the sweltering heat. There are three main ways that a roof can accomplish this. Roofs keep your home cool through a combination of the following:

 	UV reflectivity
 	Ventilation
 	Insulation

Each of these factors plays an essential role in cooling your roof. And that’s important in Florida, where the temperature of your roof can easily reach 100 degrees warmer than the ambient air. If you don’t have an energy-efficient roof, that’s heat that is leaking directly into your home and making your air conditioning work much harder than it needs to.

To help you plan your new roof, let’s look at each of the above factors individually. This way, you’ll be able to ensure you’re picking the right roofing system and contractors for your needs!
UV Reflectivity
The sun is always a major cause of heat absorption through your roof. That’s true anywhere, but it’s especially so in the Sunshine State, where we get more sun and more extreme UV rays than most of the nation. So, how are you supposed to deal with all this heat?

If you want a roof that will reflect UV rays away from your home, nothing beats metal roofing. Metal is naturally much more reflective of UV rays than shingles or tiles. And with the right protective coatings, your metal roof will have an extremely high sun reflection index (SRI). This means a cooler roof, which means a cooler attic, which means less heat entering your home and lower energy bills.

Of course, you don’t have to choose metal to get an energy-efficient roof. If you want to stick with classic asphalt shingles, opt for a lighter color that will absorb less light than darker shingles. For tiles, stick with light-colored clay roofing tiles. Clay naturally has a high thermal mass, which allows it to absorb heat during the day and then release it once the sun has gone down.
Ventilation


Keeping your attic cool is the cornerstone of any energy-efficient roof. And that requires air flowing freely through your attic to disperse all the heat that gets built up during the day. Otherwise, heat will build up in your attic and slowly seep into your home.

Let’s talk about some of the most common types of roof vents that we install at PITCH:

 	Turbine Roof Vents: Also called whirly birds, these vents use wind to draw air out of your attic and release it. These vents require wind to work at full capacity, but they do release some hot air even on calm days.
 	Solar Roof Vents: By installing a small solar panel on your roof, you can have the sun energize your vents to help cool your attic. However, these vents do have to pause to charge, which can allow heat to build up.
 	Ridge Vents: The most popular option, ridge vents are cut into the peak of your roof and run across the length of your roof to give hot air plenty of chances to escape. As a bonus, these vents can’t usually be seen from the ground.

When getting a quote for a roof replacement, don’t settle for just a flat price. Instead, insist on an itemized quote that includes every part of your roofing system. This way you’ll be able to ensure that you’re getting a functional roof ventilation system to help cool your roof. In Florida, storm chaser roofers often cut corners to offer cheaper quotes, so it’s important to make sure you’re paying for a high-quality, energy-efficient roof!
Insulation
Having a lot of insulation can help reduce the amount of heat that makes its way into your attic. In conjunction with good ventilation and UV reflection, you can expect insulation to keep your home noticeably cooler. And during a roof replacement is an excellent time to add some insulation to your attic.

While extra insulation can help, it’s not generally included in a standard roof replacement. When you’re collecting quotes, be sure to tell your roofers that you want extra insulation for your attic. They will factor this into the replacement costs to ensure that you have an accurate estimate.
Get an Energy-Efficient Roof Replacement Quote
As we’ve seen, sometimes getting an energy-efficient roof depends on what materials you choose. But even more often, it comes down to the contractors that you choose to trust. As a reputable local roofing company, we’d be honored if you’d consider PITCH Roofing for your next roof replacement.

### How to DIY Clean a Metal Roof

Metal roofing isn’t cheap, so it makes sense that you’d want to take care of it. However, getting a clean metal roof requires a very different process from cleaning a shingle roof. With the wrong cleaning techniques, you could end up doing more harm to your metal roof than good.

That’s what we’re here for. As your trusted local roofing professionals, PITCH Roofing is here to make sure your roof stays in good shape. That means not only making sure your roof gets cleaned, but ensuring that it’s cleaned correctly. Keep reading for everything you need to know to clean your metal roof!
Metal Roofs Are Easy to Damage When Cleaning


When you think of metal roofing, you probably think of strength and durability. That makes sense — metal roofs are some of the best in Florida for resisting hurricanes. Despite this resistance to water and high winds, though, these roofs can be easily damaged by improper cleaning techniques.

That’s because metal roofs are usually coated in paint and/or protective alloys. In Florida, these are necessary to prevent corrosion in our high-humidity climate. If you use the wrong tools or cleaning products, you could accidentally damage these protective features. This creates an opportunity for rust and corrosion to form on your metal roof.
Tools to Clean a Metal Roof
When cleaning a metal roof, it’s important not to use abrasive tools. Plastic sponges, hard bristle brushes, and other rough cleaners can dig away at the outermost protective layers of your roof. To prevent that, use softer tools like:

 	A microfiber washcloth
 	A cellulose sponge
 	A soft-bristle brush
 	A non-abrasive cleaning pad

Cleaners for a Metal Roof
Just like abrasive surfaces can damage your metal roof, so can harsh cleaners. That’s why you need to carefully select a gentle cleaner that’s right for your needs. Depending on how much cleaning your metal roof needs, you could use:

 	Water: If you just want to clean some dirt and dust off your roof, you don’t need anything more than a hose. Spray down your roof, and you should be looking at a clean metal roof in no time!
 	Detergent: When you really want to get a spotless roof, a simple detergent is all you need. These include gentle laundry detergent, car washing soap, and even dish soap.
 	Solvents: Solvents are ideal when you’ve got a small section of hard-to-remove staining. These include oil stains, paint, and graffiti. Isopropyl alcohol is generally safe for metal roofs, although you should limit yourself to only cleaning affected areas with it. Additionally, check your manufacturer’s cleaning directions before applying any solvent to your metal roof.

Always Rinse Your Metal Roof After Cleaning
As we’ve established, metal roofs can be surprisingly sensitive. While the above cleaners are safe to use on your metal roof, they are not safe to sit on it long-term. For example, if you mixed a detergent with bleach, it could stain your roof and corrode your paint if left on for more than 20 minutes or so.

That’s why you should thoroughly rinse a clean metal roof. This ensures that the only thing left sitting on your roof is water. With this approach, there is no risk of residual cleaners damaging your roof over time!
What to Avoid When You Clean a Metal Roof


So far, we’ve talked a lot about what products and tools you should use to clean a metal roof. Just as important, however, is what you should avoid. Let’s talk about things not to do when cleaning a metal roof in Florida!
Don’t Mix and Match Cleaners
There are a variety of cleaners that you can safely use for metal roofs. However, mixing two safe cleaners can quickly turn them into something dangerous for your roof. Mixing even mild cleaners together can have unforeseen consequences, so it’s best to stick with the instructions above and only use one cleaner at a time.
Don’t Clean a Metal Roof on a Sunny Day
We all know that Florida gets extremely hot. But even during the mild winters, it’s best to reserve cleaning a metal roof for a cloudy, overcast day, preferably in the morning. Not only will this keep you comfortable, but it will keep you safe.

Metal roofs are great at reflecting UV rays. On the one hand, this makes them more durable and helps lower energy bills. On the other hand, it makes cleaning a metal roof in the sunshine hazardous. With UV rays coming from both the sun and your roof, you’ll be at very high risk for burns and even damage to your eyes. Waiting for some cloud coverage is a much safer way to clean your roof.
Don’t Use a New Cleaner Without Testing
You can safely use any of the cleaners listed above on your metal roof. However, if you want to try a new cleaner instead, it could still be safe. To be sure, it’s best to test the cleaner on a small, less visible section of your roof. This way, you’ll notice if your paint is degraded by the cleaner before you apply it to a large, central part of your roof.
Don’t Get on a Roof if You Don’t Feel Confident
Navigating a metal roof can be surprisingly difficult. In addition to using a stable ladder to access your roof, you’ll then have to navigate your roof while you’re cleaning. That will get a lot harder when your roof is wet.

If you’re ever unsure of your ability to safely access your roof, do not risk it. Many roof cleaning companies would be happy to clean your metal roof. While this is more expensive than cleaning your roof yourself, it’s also much cheaper and easier than dealing with medical bills after an accident!

With DIY metal roof cleaning, it’s not uncommon for homeowners to notice new issues on their roofs, such as loose fasteners or problems with gutters. No matter what issue you find with your roof, our team of pros will be ready and willing to help.
