### How to Clean Roof Mold from Your Shingles

With all of the local humidity, Floridians are no strangers to mold and algae growing on their roofs. Mold is usually just unsightly, but in severe cases, it can do serious damage to your roofing system. If you want to take care of your roof as it ages, knowing proper roof mold cleaning techniques is an absolute must!

As your local roofing partner, PITCH Roofing is here to help you ensure that your roof stays strong throughout its lifetime. Whether you’re dealing with dark streaks or roof rot, we’re here to help you restore your roof to its former glory.
Focus on Safety During Roof Mold Cleaning


Any time you get on your roof, there is a chance that things could go poorly. That’s why it’s essential to follow proper safety procedures when accessing your roof! Ensure that any ladder you use is firmly supported, wear non-slip shoes, and never get on a roof that can’t support your weight. If there is any doubt about whether or not you can safely access your roof, don't risk it!

Assuming you can safely work on your roof, you’ll also need to be mindful of your cleaning supplies. When undertaking roof mold cleaning, you’ll be working with some chemicals that can be toxic to the human body. It can be a good idea to cover up with a long-sleeve shirt and gloves to ensure that harmful chemicals don’t come into contact with your skin.

Because you’re outside, there is very little risk of breathing in chemicals in a high enough quantity to be harmful. Still, if you feel lightheaded or dizzy at any point, immediately stop spraying and, when you can safely move, get down from your roof. Some people are more sensitive to chemical cleaners than others, and you don’t want to risk having a bad reaction while up on a roof.

Finally, take some time to protect any plants that sit around the edges of your roof. Chemical cleaners will run off your roof during this process, and you don’t want to ruin your garden while working on the roof! You can tarp any garden features, and you can spray grass with water after you've finished cleaning to dilute the chemicals and minimize any damage.
How to Clean Mold from Your Roof
While there are many over-the-counter mold killers, you probably have everything you need for roof mold cleaning sitting in your kitchen. Bleach is deadly to mold, and it’s safe to use in the right quantities. For your roof mold cleaning needs, make a 1:4 solution of bleach to water.

You’ll also need to get your hose onto your roof. Start by spraying down your roof with water. Once you've gotten your roof wet, you’ll want to spray any areas with visible mold. Then, you'll scrub them with a soft-bristle brush. You can then let the solution sit on your shingles for a bit, about 15 minutes. This gives the bleach time to reach and kill more mold.

Once you’ve finished cleaning your shingles, be sure to completely rinse your roof of any bleach cleaner. While bleach does not harm roofs in small quantities, it can discolor and weaken your shingles if you allow it to sit for too long. Also, you should be especially careful moving on your roof after it’s wet. The risk of slipping and having an accident goes up dramatically with water on your roof.
Preventing Roof Mold Growth and Taking Care of Your Shingles


Knowing how to clean roof mold is a great way to take care of your roof. There are other ways to ensure that your roof stays strong and healthy, however. Be mindful of how often you have to use these roof mold cleaning techniques. Cleaning your roof every six months or so is normal, but if you notice mold growing back more rapidly than that, then you may need help from professional roof cleaners.

To minimize mold growth, clean off any branches or other debris from your roof as soon as you notice it. Florida already has easy conditions for mold to grow in, but creating a shaded area on your roof can make the problem much worse. Additionally, leaves and branches hold moisture, which encourages mold. You can also trim back any overhead trees to slow down mold growth.

After cleaning roof mold, it can be a good idea to make sure your shingles are still firmly in place. In severe cases, roof mold can weaken your shingles and prematurely age your roof. If you find shingles that are rotted through or starting to come off, you’ll likely need some roof repairs. While replacing shingles is easy enough as a DIY roof repair, we recommend leaving these jobs to the professionals. Mold damage can be extensive, and if you’re not an experienced roofer, you may not know how to spot signs of larger damage.

You should also consider the age of your shingles. Modern architectural shingles come with anti-mold zinc deposits that release slowly over time. If you’re seeing substantial mold growth, it could mean that your roof is nearing the end of its lifespan. Nobody wants to get an unnecessary roof replacement, but a roof inspection can give you clarity when you’re unsure whether or not you need a new roof.

While we don’t offer roof cleaning services, we can inspect your roof for damage to give you peace of mind and certainty about the state of your roof.

### How Much Do Architectural Shingles Cost in Florida?

There was a time when 3-tab asphalt shingles were the go-to shingle roofing option. Thanks to advances in modern roofing technology, however, there is a new roofing standard. Architectural asphalt shingles have taken North America by storm, and they offer many improvements over old 3-tab shingles. But how much do architectural shingles cost in Florida?

We’re PITCH Roofing, and we’re here to break down everything you need to know about shingle roof replacement costs. Our team of Florida roofers has been replacing shingle roofs in the Sunshine State for a long time. Follow along as we use that expertise to cover the average cost of an architectural shingle roof replacement!
How Much Do Architectural Shingles Cost on Average?


In roofing, averages can be tricky. They’re a great starting place for getting an idea of how much your roof may cost, but since each roof is unique, they aren’t 100% reliable. For that kind of certainty, you’d need a personalized roofing quote. Still, knowing how much architectural shingles cost on average is better than going in blind.

On average, architectural shingles cost $5 to $9 per square foot. And in Florida, the average size of a roof is around 1,700 square feet. This means that an architectural shingle roof replacement will cost between $8,500 and $15,300 in Florida, assuming that you have an “average” roof.

However, many homeowners have unique roofing systems. Your roof’s pitch, unique features, and hills and valleys can all greatly change how much your new shingle roof will cost. To give you a better idea of how much your shingle roof replacement could cost, let’s talk about these common pricing factors in roof replacement estimates.
The Biggest Architectural Shingles Cost Factors
No two roofs are exactly the same. And for every difference or quirk in your roof, you can expect it to affect the price of your shingle roof replacement. Keep reading for a breakdown of the biggest factors that will affect the price of your architectural shingles!
Unique Roofing Features
Your roof is probably more unique than you realize. It’s not only big, flashy homes that have unique roofing features — most roofs have something that sets them apart. Some common roofing features include:

 	Chimneys
 	Skylights
 	Roof vents
 	Dormer windows
 	Multiple valleys

All of these features can add value and personality to your roof. They will increase how much your architectural shingles cost to install, though. That’s because roofers have to work around these things, which increases installation time and may require extra shingles. So if you have several of these features, it’s safe to say that your shingle roof will likely cost more than average.
Roof Pitch
How steep your roof is will have a large impact on how much your architectural shingles cost to install. There are two reasons for this: First, because a steeper roof means more square footage to your roof. Since a larger roof requires more shingles, you can expect to have fairly high material costs.

The steepness of your roof also impacts labor costs. If your roof pitch is steeper than 4:12, then your contractors will need special safety gear to work on your roof. Not only does this slow down the installation process, but you’ll need more experienced roofers who know how to safely work on a steep roof. In any industry, more expertise means more money.
Roof Decking
When trying to determine how much your architectural shingles will cost, roof decking can make everything a lot more difficult. Your decking is what sits underneath your shingles and roof underlayment. Typically made of wood, this creates the base-level support for the rest of your roofing system.

Since it’s under your shingles, there is no way to inspect your roof decking without tearing off your old roof. This makes the process of getting an estimate more difficult, since no roofer can account for the cost of replacing your decking without knowing how much of your decking needs to be replaced. Thankfully, replacing decking rarely costs more than a few hundred dollars.

Most often, decking needs replacing because it has sustained water damage. So if your roof has a history of leaks, there’s a real chance that parts of your roof decking will be replaced during the roof replacement process.
Quality Roofers


It’s normal and reasonable to be suspicious of a roof estimate that’s far more expensive than the average cost of architectural shingles. At the same time, however, you should be wary of a roof quote that’s well below the market price. Often, unreliable roofers will cut corners on workmanship and materials to create a more enticing offer.

This is especially common in Florida, where storm chasers come into town after major storms in an attempt to make a quick buck promising great roofs for cheap. If a roofing estimate seems too good to be true, that might be because it is. While storm chasers promise a lot, the results are always shoddy and create more problems than they solve.

With roofing, it’s always worth it to pay for experienced professionals. While you should always look for a good, fair price for your architectural shingles, it is possible to go too cheap. And if that happens, you’re likely looking at expensive problems down the line as your roof ages and has to deal with the unpredictable Florida weather.

### When to Do a DIY Roof Repair

In Florida, there is no shortage of things that can damage your roof. Whether it’s normal wear and tear or hurricane damage, homeowners often have one thought after they spot roofing damage: Should I try DIY roof repair? Depending on your experience and the severity of the damage, your mileage will vary.

That’s why PITCH Roofing is here to help you identify DIY roof repairs that you can safely take on, and which ones are best left to experienced contractors. Roof repairs are an additional expense that nobody wants to shell out for, but on the other hand, you need a strong roofing system to protect against the Florida elements. To make sure you’re spending your money wisely and keeping your home safe, let’s talk about when you should and shouldn’t try to DIY roof work!
Are DIY Roof Repairs a Good Idea in General?


It’s not hard to see the upside of DIY roof repairs. There’s no process of collecting estimates, and you don’t have to worry about paying labor costs for a contractor to work on your home. There is some trade off, however, since you’ll have to pay for materials and any tools necessary for the job. If you’re handy, you might already have many of these tools, but this can be a significant investment for others.

You should also factor in time considerations. While it can be a hassle to find the right roofers, it can take several hours to perform even simple roof repairs. If it’s the summer, that can mean hours spent on a hot roof.

Finally, you should consider whether or not you can adequately complete a DIY roof repair. With roofing, a bad repair can be worse than the initial damage. That’s because it gives you a false peace of mind while your roof continues to deteriorate. And if your roof isn’t in good shape during a hurricane, it could lead to a catastrophe.

All of that said, there are certainly situations where DIY roof repairs can make sense if you’re handy. To find out which situations those are, let’s talk about three common roof repairs we see almost every day!
3 Common DIY Roof Repairs


There is a wide range in the types of DIY roof repairs that we’ve seen homeowners try. Sometimes they go well, and sometimes they go very poorly. To find out whether your roofing issue is the type of problem you want to DIY, let’s look at these repairs one by one.
Missing Roof Shingles
Loose and missing shingles are common after a storm, especially if your roof is at least 10 years old. Not only are they unsightly, but relatively minor damage like this can grow over time. For example, over a period of months, missing shingles can create an entry point for water or mold to enter into your roofing system.

The good news is that installing new shingles is a great DIY roof repair. While not everyone can do it, you can expect to be successful if you’re comfortable with a hammer and nails. The hardest part of this process is finding the exact right match for your current shingles. If you can find the right shingles, though, installing them should be fairly simple.

The steps to replace missing or damaged shingles are as follows:

 	Tear off the old shingle if it’s still attached
 	Put the new shingle in the place of the old one
 	Line up a nail in the strike zone and hammer the new shingle into place

In terms of roof repairs, it doesn’t get much simpler than this. Before DIYing a shingle replacement, however, you should carefully review your roof’s warranty. There is a chance that working on your own roof could violate the terms of your warranty, which may end up costing you more in the long run.
Damaged Roof Flashing
Most homeowners don’t realize how important flashing is to a roofing system. This thin strip of metal helps direct water off your roof, which means you can have issues with water retention when it’s not working properly. Unfortunately, flashing is easy to damage since the metal is so thin.

Unless you have experience as a roofing contractor, we do not recommend replacing damaged flashing as a DIY roof repair. To replace flashing, you would need to remove (and then later reinstall) several rows of shingles. You’d also need to safely remove the old mortar that runs along the sides of your flashing, then reapply it after installing the new flashing. In short, it just isn’t the kind of job that you want to take on as a DIY roof repair.
Leaking Roof
Leaking roofs are one of the most common problems that Floridians have with their roofs. However, they’re deceptively complicated given that there are so many different causes of roof leaks. For example, a leak in your roof could be caused by damaged shingles, a problem with your underlayment, damage to your fascia, or a dozen other reasons. If you’re looking to do a DIY roof repair, this makes the job much more complicated.

The other issue is that you may not know how much water is already in your roofing system. This means that if you stop more water from entering your roof, you’ll still run the risk of dealing with mold and wood rot due to the trapped water.

Ultimately, it’s your decision whether or not this is a DIY roof repair you feel comfortable taking on. If the cause is damaged shingles and you catch the issue quickly, before water is leaking through your ceiling, you may be able to tear off your old shingles and replace them. If there’s any doubt about what caused the leak or how much damage has already been done, however, it’s best to leave the job in the hands of trustworthy roofing professionals.
Reach Out to Florida’s Top Roof Repair Pros
There are plenty of circumstances where a DIY roof repair makes sense. However, if you’re anything less than 100% confident in your ability to safely fix your roof on your own, it’s best to choose local roofing professionals you can trust. ### What Are the Warning Signs You Need a New Roof?

If you don’t have much roofing experience, it can be hard to know when you need a roof replacement. At the same time, having a strong, functional roofing system is crucial to protecting your property, especially during hurricane season. For this reason, it’s essential that you know the warning signs you need a new roof and have reliable contractors you can turn to.

We’re here to solve both those issues! PITCH Roofing is a Florida roofing company made up of real, long-time roofing professionals. With more than 60 years combined experience, we know all the red flags that a roof shows when it’s nearing the end of its life. Stick with us to find out if it’s time to replace your roof!
5 Warning Signs You Need a New Roof in Florida


Florida is tough on roofs from all angles. On the one hand, you have high winds and storm debris during tropical storms and hurricanes. On the other, extreme UV exposure and high humidity can do a lot to gradually weaken your roofing system. As a result, there are many different warning signs you need a new roof. Let’s talk about the most common ones to watch out for as a homeowner!
1. Balding Shingles
During the manufacturing process, your shingles receive a layer of stone granules on top of the asphalt. These increase their resistance to impact damage and UV rays. As your shingles reach the end of their lifespan, however, these granules gradually start to come off.

Finding stone granules in your gutters or downspouts is one of the biggest warning signs that you need a new roof. While it’s normal to notice some granules coming off immediately after a roof installation, if your roof is more than 10 years old, finding granules means that it’s probably time for a replacement.
2. Shingle Curling
In Florida, UV rays can do a real number on your roof. One of the most common problems it causes is shingle curling. This happens when the sun’s rays gradually dry out your shingles, causing them to wither and curl. This can happen at the edges, which is called cupping, or in the center, which roofers call clawing.

In either case, it’s not a good sign for your roof. If you have a substantial amount of curling shingles (more than 25% of your roof), it’s a warning sign that you need a new roof. However, if you only have one or two curling shingles, this can be resolved with a simple roof repair. You’ll still want to keep an eye on your roof, though, to make sure more shingles don’t start curling in the future.
3. Aging Roof


In roofing, there is just no fighting age. When your shingles reach the end of their lifespan, it’s a surefire sign that you need a new roof. In Florida, shingle roofs can last for 20-25 years. Usually, though, your insurance will want you to replace your roof when it’s 15 to 20 years old.

If you’re not sure how old your shingles are, you have a few options. Here’s what we recommend:

 	Contact the Previous Owner: By reaching out to the seller’s real estate agent, you should be able to get in touch with the previous owner or, even better, receive documentation on the age of your roof. This information should be in the disclosure document.
 	Look at Your Neighbors’ Roofs: The homes in a neighborhood are usually built around the same time. So if you notice that your neighbors are getting new roofs, that’s a warning sign that you need a new roof as well.
 	Inspect the Roof: Since Florida is so hard on roofs, you can usually tell when a roof has been around for a while. Look for dark streaks, loose or missing shingles, and mold or algae growth.

4. Sudden Energy Spikes
One of the most often overlooked warning signs you need a new roof is a sudden spike in your monthly energy bill. Part of your roof’s job is insulating your home and keeping the hot air out. If your energy bill suddenly increases, this could mean that your roof is no longer able to insulate your home.

Usually, this happens as the result of damaged shingles, which create a path for hot air to enter your home. If you notice an increased energy bill, it could be worth taking a look at your roof. If you find signs of extensive shingle damage, then it’s probably time for a roof replacement.
5. Mold and Mildew in Your Home
Many homeowners are surprised to learn that a roof leak can present in a variety of ways, not just water coming from the ceiling. Often, a leak starts small and may only create issues in your attic. Over time, though, the damage spreads, and you may notice mold and mildew growing in your home. Because the issue isn’t obviously related to your roof, this is an often-overlooked warning sign you need a new roof.

Mold will usually grow in your ceiling and along outer walls. If you suspect that you have a roof leak, it’s a good idea to check out your attic. Signs of moisture or mustiness is a surefire sign that water is leaking into your home. You’ll want to schedule a roof inspection with a professional to determine whether or not you need a roof replacement or repair.
Get a Free Estimate for Your New Roof
Clearly, there are many different warning signs you need a new roof. Some are obvious, while others are easy to overlook. If you have any of these warning signs, it’s a good idea to contact a roofing professional just in case. With roofing, it’s always better to err on the side of caution!

### How to Use Your Roof Coverage in Florida

Having trouble with your roof is a hassle. Whether you need a leak fixed or it’s time to replace your roof entirely, it can take time to get roofing services. Even worse, paying for sudden roofing issues is an expense that many homeowners would rather avoid. But by knowing the ins and outs of your roof coverage, you may be able to avoid a surprise roofing bill.

We’re PITCH Roofing, your local roofing partner. With our crew of long-time Florida roofers, we’re more than familiar with Florida homeowners insurance and roofing warranties. The weather in Florida can be unpredictable, so keep reading to see what you can do if and when your roof has been damaged!
Does Insurance Cover Roof Damage in Florida?


Many homeowners are surprised to learn that insurance roof coverage only applies in certain situations. Florida has many harsh weather factors, from the extreme UV rays to the humidity. However, insurance usually only covers roof damage from severe weather events like tropical storms and hurricanes.

This means that your roof coverage will generally apply to:

 	Missing shingles that have been removed by high winds
 	Dents in your roof from hail or storm debris
 	Damage to your roof caused by falling tree limbs
 	Gutters that have been torn out of position by high winds

Notice that all of these examples are instances of severe weather damage. Normal wear and tear, like cracked or curled shingles, will most likely not fall under your insurance’s roof coverage. With roof damage caused by a storm, however, you should be good to have insurance cover your roof. However, that doesn’t always mean that they’ll pay for everything.
How Insurance Pays for Roof Damage
In Florida, there are two primary ways that insurance pays out a policy: an actual cash value policy and a replacement cost value policy. Which plan your insurer offers will greatly affect how much roof coverage you receive. Let’s take a look at each of these options!
Actual Cash Value Policy
Most homeowners insurance policies in Florida have an Actual Cash Value (ACV) policy. This type of roof coverage will not pay for the full cost to replace a roof. Rather, you get paid out the depreciated value of your roof. In other words, you’re given an amount relative to how old and in what condition your roof was when it was damaged.

If you’re talking to storm chaser roofers, they might offer to lower their price to that of your ACV policy. This is almost always a scam. While nobody wants to pay out of pocket for roofing work, it’s better than getting a “free” roof that’s made with low-quality materials and cheap labor. In our experience, those are the roofs that end up costing the most!
Replacement Cost Value Policy
A replacement cost value (RCV) policy is supposed to pay out the value to replace your roof with a new version of itself. This means that if you have an architectural shingle roof, your roof coverage should pay for the cost to install a new roof using the same materials.

Once your insurer approves your claim, you should receive a check in the mail for the actual cost value of your depreciated roof. Then, after replacing your roof and sending the right documentation to your insurer, they should send you a second check with your recoverable depreciation amount. All told, this should roughly cover the cost of replacing your roof. You may have to come out of pocket to some extent, but the vast majority of your costs should be covered.
Can You Use Warranties in Place of Insurance Roof Coverage?


If your homeowners insurance won’t pay for your roof, you may be able to use your roofing warranties as alternative roof coverage. Warranties only apply in specific situations, however. Let’s look at the different types of roof warranties and see if they apply to your situation!
Manufacturers’ Warranties
A manufacturers’ warranty covers roof damage related to a flaw in your roofing materials. For example, say you had shingles blown off your roof during a storm with 70 mph wind gusts. If your shingles were rated for winds up to 120 mph and were installed correctly, then you may qualify for roof coverage under this warranty.

It’s important to note that most manufacturers’ warranties only cover the cost of materials. They will not generally pay for the labor required to install new replacement shingles. Additionally, your coverage may be prorated. So if your shingles are more than 10 years old, you will probably get credit for less than the value of new shingles. Still, this roof coverage is much better than none at all!
Workmanship Warranties
Remember how homeowners insurance only pays for roof damage caused by severe weather? Workmanship warranties are the opposite. These warranties only pay for issues caused by your roof not being installed correctly. So if your home was damaged in a storm that your roof could not reasonably be expected to survive unscathed, you likely won’t qualify for this type of roof coverage.

Even so, workmanship warranties can do a lot of good. This coverage will usually include both material and labor costs to repair or replace damaged sections of your roof. It will likely even cover any damage inside your home caused by the roof failure. Because these policies require roofers to stand behind the quality of their work, only reputable, experienced contractors like PITCH tend to offer them.
Get a Free Roofing Estimate
There are plenty of ways for you to get roof coverage and avoid paying the whole cost of roof repairs or replacements yourself. Whether you use homeowners insurance, roofing warranties, or pay out of pocket, PITCH Roofing will be there to help. At every step of the way, we work hard to keep the roofing process simple and easy for our customers.

That starts with your free, no-obligation roofing estimate. To get started, call us at (727) 677-4824 or schedule your estimate online. ### When to Get a Mobile Home Roof Replacement

Hurricanes are hard on every Florida property, but they’re especially tough on mobile homes. That’s why it’s crucial that you have a strong, durable roofing system in place. If your roof is nearing the end of its lifespan, then it’s essential that you get a mobile home roof replacement from qualified roofing professionals.

We should know: PITCH Roofing has over 60 years of experience replacing roofs across the Greater Tampa Bay area. We’ve worked on plenty of mobile homes in that time, and we know how to install a roof that’s built to last. If you think that it could be time to replace the roof of your mobile home, keep reading for a guide with everything you need to know about tearing off and replacing a mobile home’s roof!
Signs It’s Time to Replace Your Mobile Home’s Roof


In mobile home roofing, contractors typically install one of three options: shingles, flat roofing, or metal. While all three roofs can be great, the material on your home will determine when you need a mobile home roof replacement. To start off, let’s look at signs it’s time to replace your shingles:

 	Shingles are more than 20 years old
 	Your shingles are cracked or curling
 	Stone granules are coming off your shingles
 	Moss or algae are growing across your roof

Mobile home flat roofs are usually made from TPO or modified bitumen, both of which have very different signs of aging from shingles. Signs it’s time to replace a mobile home's flat roof include:

 	Your flat roof is more than 20 years old
 	Roof leaks, especially large or multiple leaks
 	Increased monthly energy bills
 	Visible blistering or cracking on your roof

Finally, metal roofs are the gold standard when it comes to mobile home roofing. These roofs are hardy and tough, but even they need replacing sooner or later. Here’s how to know when to replace a metal roof on a mobile home:

 	Your metal roof is over 30 years old
 	Rust or fading paint across your roof
 	Your fasteners are starting to lift from your metal panels
 	Heavy damage to your metal panels during a severe storm

As you can see, there are a lot of ways to tell that it’s time to replace your roof. If you see your roof reflected in these signs that it’s time for a replacement, then it’s best to act fast before the next storm blows into town. But how much is a mobile home roof replacement going to cost you?

### How 30-Year Shingles Work in Florida

When you’re getting a new shingle roof, you expect your roof to last for a long time. If you’ve heard contractors talking about 30-year shingles, this may seem like a perfect way to get a long-lasting roof. However, there are a lot of misconceptions about 30-year shingles and what you can expect from them.

We’re PITCH Roofing, your local roofing partner. In our decades as Florida roofers, we’ve installed plenty of new shingle roofs using a variety of shingle products. That’s how we know everything that 30-year shingles can, and cannot, offer. Stick with us as we debunk the most common myths about 30-year shingles!
Do 30-Year Shingles Last for 30 Years?


The hands-down most common misconception we see about 30-year shingles is that you can count on them to last for three decades. Unfortunately, 30-year shingles do not last for 30 years. This is true for 50-year shingles as well — when someone describes shingles this way, they aren’t telling you how long the asphalt shingles will last.

So, what do the years describe? These numbers actually reflect how long your manufacturer’s warranty will last. So for 30-year shingles, your manufacturer will cover your shingles for three decades after installation. Realistically, though, your asphalt shingles are not going to last that long.

In Florida, architectural asphalt shingles last for 20-25 years on average, although you may need to replace your roof sooner if you’re hit by a major hurricane. No matter how long a shingle’s warranty is, it’s unlikely that your homeowners insurance will let you go much longer than 20 years without replacing your roof.

Usually, distinctions like “30-year shingles” are there for marketing purposes. Some manufacturers may intentionally mislead you in order to more easily sell you their shingles. If you want to see what your warranty really covers, it’s best to take a look at what your manufacturer and installer are offering.
Alternatives to 30-Year Shingles
These days, many manufacturers have stopped producing 30-year shingles. This is true for Owens Corning, which offers lifetime warranties instead. In this context, “lifetime” means for as long as you own your home. To get the most coverage, though, you’ll need to pick the right roofers.

 	Coverage for labor during repairs or replacements for the first 50 years
 	Blow off coverage for the first 15 years
 	Algae resistance coverage for the first 25 years
 	A 10-year workmanship warranty covering any mistakes made during your roof installation

To be clear, not even an Owens Corning shingle roof is likely to last for much longer than 25 years. But with comprehensive coverage like this, you will be covered for nearly any eventuality during your roof’s lifespan. ### Is a White Shingle Roof a Good Idea in Florida? Pros and Cons

Every day, PITCH Roofing tears off old shingle roofs and installs new, resilient shingle roofing systems. Everyone wants a roof that can withstand the next big storm, but we’ve noticed a lot of homeowners expressing interest in getting a white shingle roof, specifically. But is this a good idea for Florida homeowners?

As your local roofing partner, PITCH Roofing is here to help you plan your shingle roof replacement. Today, we’re talking about the good and the bad of getting a white shingle roof. When it comes to picking out your new roof, the color of your shingles impacts much more than the aesthetics of your home!
Pros of a White Shingle Roof in Florida


White roofing shingles are in high demand in Florida, and for good reason. Painted white and topped with white reflective stone granules, these shingles have a lot to offer any Florida homeowner. Let’s talk about the biggest reasons that you might choose a white shingle roof.
Energy Efficiency
If you’re considering getting a white shingle roof, it’s probably because you’ve heard that light-colored roofs do a better job of reflecting heat away from your home. The Florida summer heat is no joke, and most homeowners would love to see lower energy bills. The good news is that what you’ve heard is true, and white shingles are better at reflecting UV rays than dark-colored shingles.

It’s important to keep in mind that these are still asphalt shingles, so they won’t reflect 100% of UV rays away from your home. But on a hot summer day, you’ll be glad you have a white shingle roof that can help keep your home cool and your energy bills low.
Appearance of a Larger Roof
Getting a white shingle roof is an excellent option if you’d like to make your home look larger. Lighter and brighter colors tend to make things appear larger, and this extends to your roof as well. With white shingles, you’ll create the optical illusion of a larger roof.

This pairs well with dimensional shingles, which create visual texture on your roof through their unique patterning. By investing in white dimensional shingles, you’ll be able to greatly improve the look of your roof while simultaneously getting your home hurricane-ready.
Modern Aesthetic
Shingle roofs have been the most popular roofing material for nearly a century. Over that time, we’ve grown used to the sight of cozy, earth-toned shingles. But with a white shingle roof, you have the opportunity to update your home’s aesthetic and generate curb appeal.

White shingles have a sleek, modern aesthetic that other shingle colors may not offer. If you want an updated, modern look for your home but want to stick with classic asphalt shingles, getting a white shingle roof is a great option!
Cons of a White Shingle Roof in Florida


Many local factors make white shingle roofs appealing to Floridians. But there are other local considerations to make that can greatly reduce the benefits of a white shingle roof. Let’s talk about all the downsides of going with white asphalt shingles!
Dirt and Debris
It can be tough to keep a roof clean in Florida. In addition to storm debris being deposited on your roof, our humidity makes algae and mold growth a real concern. With a white shingle roof, any dirt or algae is going to be very apparent on your roof, and many homeowners would prefer not to have a roof that shows dirt so easily.

This isn’t just an aesthetic issue, either. As your white shingle roof gets dirtied, it loses its ability to reflect UV rays. In other words, if you can’t keep up with a regular roof cleaning schedule, you may not get the full benefits of having white roofing shingles.
High Demand
When you start your roof replacement, you’ll have the option to pick the color of your shingles. Many people have heard that white shingles are better at cooling your roof, however, which means that there is a high demand for these shingles. As a result, you may have to wait longer for your roof replacement if you choose white shingles.

If you still want a light-colored roof but don’t want to wait, you may be able to opt for a light grey shingle instead. This will have similar benefits when compared to a white shingle roof, although it may also have the downside of showing dirt quickly.
Issues with Selling
White shingles can be a surprisingly divisive issue. While some homeowners love them, others would never want a white shingle roof. Because they’re so polarizing, having a white shingle roof could make it harder to sell your home if local buyers don’t want to commit to that kind of roof cleaning schedule.

If you plan on reselling your home, it could be a better idea to choose a neutral-toned shingle. While this is less of a modern look, it could have a broader appeal that makes it easier to sell. Ultimately, of course, your mileage will depend on your home and the neighborhood in which you’re looking to sell.

As a homeowner, you have to look at your situation and decide what color shingles are right for you. ### What Is the Best Roof for Hurricanes?

As a Florida homeowner, you know how severe tropical storms can be. And you know that you need to protect your property against our unpredictable weather patterns. But how can you do that? A good place to start is finding out what the best roof for hurricanes is and planning your new roof.

We’re PITCH Roofing, a locally based roofing company. We’re a crew of veteran Florida roofers, and we’ve had plenty of time to see how different roofing systems withstand the local climate. Today, we’re talking about what your roof has to stand up against and which roofing materials are best able to withstand hurricanes and other tropical storms!
What Hurricanes Do to Your Roof


A hurricane is a lot more than just high winds. When it comes to protecting your home, your roof needs to be able to withstand a lot of punishment. To help identify the best roof for hurricane readiness, let’s first discuss what your is up against!
Hurricane-force Winds
During hurricane season, you’ll hear a lot of chatter about hurricane-force winds. But how fast are those winds, exactly? Well, a category one hurricane will have winds of at least 74 mph. On the other end of the spectrum, a category five hurricane has winds at 157 mph or higher. This is quite a large range, and your roof needs to be ready for all of it!

Some homeowners believe that only shingle roofs are vulnerable to wind damage, but this isn’t true. Any roofing system can experience uplift due to hurricane-force winds. When considering the best roof for hurricanes, it’s essential to pick a material that is ready to deal with extreme wind speeds like these!
Wind-driven Rain
When installed correctly, any roofing system can handle rain with no issue. Wind-driven rain is a different beast, however. Propelled by extreme winds, rainwater can work its way under and into your roofing system, leading to leaks and even internal floods in extreme circumstances.

The best roof for hurricanes will be able to protect your home against wind-driven rain. To do that, however, your roof is going to need regular maintenance. Even the best roofs need occasional repairs, and falling behind on this upkeep could drastically increase your risk of your roof receiving storm damage!
Storm Debris
Many homeowners overlook storm debris, but it’s a serious threat both during and after a hurricane. Storm debris is whatever gets picked up and thrown around by high winds — branches and leaves are common, but anything left outside can become a projectile. When these items hit your roof at high speeds, they pose a serious risk of damaging it.

That isn’t the only threat of storm debris, though. After a storm, it can become trapped on your roof. It then becomes a place for algae and pests to move in, which endangers your entire roofing system. Even with the best roof for hurricanes, you’ll want to clean off your roof after a hurricane to keep it secure!
What Is the Best Roof for Hurricanes?


As you can see, hurricanes pose plenty of danger to your roof. Thankfully, roofs in Florida are built with these risk factors in mind. Even shingle roofs can withstand some hurricane conditions. But when we’re talking about the very best roof for hurricanes, then there are only two real contenders.
Metal Roofing
Every year, more and more homeowners turn to metal roofing to secure their homes. These roofs are durable, long-lasting, and uniquely resilient against hurricane conditions. For example, a properly installed metal roof can withstand winds up to 180 mph. That’s equivalent to a category 5 hurricane!

During installation, contractors will firmly adhere your metal roof to your home, ensuring that it’s not going anywhere and that it’s watertight. While storm debris can still cause minor denting, these are usual aesthetic issues and not a threat to the security of your roof. Another great feature of metal roofs is that they rarely need repairs.

To top it all off, metal roofs are built to last. That’s why they have some of the longest lifespans of any roof in Florida. Let’s look at standing seam metal roofs, for instance. These roofs can last anywhere from 40 to 70 years with the proper maintenance. If you’re looking for the best roof for hurricane readiness, metal will protect your home for many years to come!
Clay Tile Roofing
Where metal roofing is a new approach to roofing, clay tiles are timeless. These roofing materials have been used in Florida for centuries, and they’re still going strong as one of the best roofs for hurricanes. Clay tile roofs have been approved for winds up to 150 mph, making them capable of withstanding direct hits from even major hurricanes.

Manufacturers design clay tiles to help water flow easily and freely off your roof, making them highly water resistant. However, wind-driven rain can force itself under your tiles. Thankfully, this water is then kept out by a water-resistant underlayment, so you don’t have to worry about leaks. You should be wary of storm debris, though, since it can crack your tiles! While this is a small repair, it’s also a crucial one.

In terms of longevity, clay tiles are tough to beat. These roofs can last anywhere from 50 to 100 years, making them the longest-lasting roofs on the market. As a bonus, they have an elegant and classic look that many homeowners prefer over metal roofing. That’s what makes these roofs a strong contender for the best way to hurricane-prep your home!

While many different types of roofs can protect your home, metal and clay tile roofing are the best roofs for hurricanes. If you want to upgrade to this top-tier protection, all you have to do is reach out to the trusted professionals at PITCH.

### The Good and Bad of Installing a Composition Roof in Florida

In Florida, all homeowners have one thing in common: they want to protect their property from the next big storm. For many local Floridians, that means choosing a composition roof when it’s time to get a roof replacement. In other situations, though, this might not be the right roofing material. So, which camp do you fall into?

That’s what we’re here to help you figure out. We’re PITCH Roofing, your local roofing partner. And today, we’re looking at the good and the bad of composition roofing in Florida. Before we delve too deep into how these roofs perform in the Sunshine State, however, we first need to establish a baseline for what a composition roof is.
What Is a Composition Roof?


No matter what neighborhood you live in, it’s a safe bet that some or even most of your neighbors will have a composition roof. In fact, composition roofing is the most popular option across North America. But what is it made of, exactly?

Composition roofing is the same thing as asphalt shingle roofing. This means that a composition roof is made using individual roofing shingles that start with a layer of fiberglass baseboard that is then dipped in a thick asphalt coating. From there, manufacturers coat the shingle in protective stone granules.

You should note that composition roofing is different from composite roofing, which uses synthetic shingles to replicate the look of slate or cedar tiles. Asphalt shingle roofs, on the other hand, are famous for their cozy, familiar aesthetic and reliable durability.

But is that durability enough to withstand Florida’s unpredictable hurricane seasons? Let’s take a closer look at how a composition roof performs in your community.
Pros and Cons of a Composition Roof in Florida


No matter where you go in the United States, you’ll find plenty of shingle roofs. But are these the right roofs for Floridians? To answer that question, we have to consider the good and the bad of a composition roof’s performance!
Pro: Durable and Strong
There was a time when a composition roof wouldn’t be able to withstand severe weather conditions. When these roofs used 3-tab shingles, their wind resistance was 70 mph at best. Nowadays, however, architectural asphalt shingles have changed the game. That’s why modern composition roofs can withstand winds up to 120 mph!

Shingles also do a great job of resisting water intrusion thanks to that thick layer of asphalt. And their stone-coated granules help resist UV rays and deflect them away from your home. While they are not the best option for UV resistance on the market, they do have some defenses in place, which helps them last in sunny Florida.
Con: Relatively Short Lifespans
When you get a new roof, you expect it to last. A composition roof is not the longest-lasting option on the market, not even close, but it can last for quite a long time. Thanks to improvements in shingle technology over the years, a composition roof lasts for about 20 years on average.

On the other hand, tile roofs can last for 50 to 100 years or more. And metal roofs average around 40-70 years of life. Of course, all of these options are much more expensive than composition roofing. For its price point, we’d still say that shingle roofs last for a good long while!
Pro: Affordable, Reliable Roofing
A big reason for shingles’ popularity is that they’re relatively cheap to manufacture and easy to install. This is a big contributor to their overall popularity. Roofing prices are always changing and your exact costs will depend on your circumstances. That said, a square foot of composition roofing costs $5 to $9. This is an accessible price point that suits a variety of budgets!

Another factor in the popularity of composition roofing is that it’s a known quantity. These roofs have been used across the country for over a century. While modern architectural shingles offer improved performance thanks to advancements in roofing technology, roofers and homeowners know how these shingles are going to perform, which gives peace of mind. This contrasts with newer roofing materials like TPO, which are still somewhat experimental.
Con: Regular Maintenance
When you get a new roof, you don’t want to deal with a lot of upkeep. Unfortunately, with a composition roof, you can expect occasional maintenance. While these roofs are strong and hardy, hurricane-force winds can tear off a small number of shingles, which could leave your roof vulnerable if not addressed quickly.

You’ll also need to clear debris off your roof, especially after major storms. Over time, it can create a home for pests and moss on your roof, which can weaken your roofing system. Sun damage is also a big risk for shingles, so you’ll want to watch out for cracked or curled shingles, which you’ll need to replace.
Pro: Great Warranties
In roofing, warranties determine how much protection you’ll have as your roof ages. If there is an issue with your shingles or how they were installed, it can take a long time for issues to start showing up. That’s why it pays to have long-lasting, strong warranties.

At PITCH, we can offer the best composition roof warranties thanks to our status as Owens Corning Preferred Contractors. With us, both your manufacturer warranty and your workmanship warranty will be backed by Owens Corning, a giant of the roofing industry. This means that if there is ever a problem with your roof due to poor materials or workmanship errors, you’ll be covered and won’t have to pay out of pocket for repairs!

If you’re in the market for a new roof, asphalt shingles are certainly worth considering. When you need experienced contractors to install your new roof, all you have to do is reach out to PITCH.

### Is Rolled Asphalt Roofing Right for You?

In Florida, flat roofs are common on both residential and commercial roofs. While there are many flat roofing options, rolled asphalt roofing is a popular choice across the Sunshine State. But is it the right fit for your structure?

That’s what we’re here to help you figure out. As a local roofing company, PITCH Roofing contractors have been installing rolled flat roofs in Florida for a long time. We’re putting that expertise to work by explaining everything you need to know about rolled roofing before you commit to a roof replacement. Keep reading for our complete guide!
What Is Rolled Asphalt Roofing?


In terms of materials, rolled asphalt roofing is very similar to shingle roofing. Both options start with a fiberglass baseboard that is then coated in a thick layer of asphalt. To top it off, the asphalt then receives a coating of protective stone granules.

This is basic rolled asphalt roofing. But at PITCH, we don’t want to give you a low-quality roofing system. That’s why we provide modified bitumen flat roof replacements. With this approach, your rolled roof has rubberized polymers that greatly increase its water resistance. This means that even if water takes some time to drain from your low-slope roof, you’ll still have protection from leaks.

There are many advantages to rolled flat roofs. Like shingles, rolled roofing is very affordable. On average, modified bitumen costs $4 to $8 per square foot, making it about as affordable as asphalt architectural shingles. You can also expect to enjoy low installation costs, since rolled roofing is quick and easy to install. Less labor means a cheaper roof replacement!

Conventional rolled roofing is not the most durable of materials. But modified bitumen is much hardier and better suited for the Florida elements. These roofs tend to last about 20 years and can even withstand severe storms. This is a great lifespan for a flat roof, especially one at such a low price point!
Is Rolled Asphalt Roofing Right for Your Structure?
Rolled roofing can be a good fit for any flat roofing system. But is it right for yours? We’re going to look at some of the most common types of jobs where we install these roofs to help you decide if rolled asphalt roofing is the right material for you:

 	Shed or Garage Roofing: If there’s a flat roof over your shed or garage, rolled asphalt roofing could be the perfect fit. It’s durable, affordable, and long-lasting enough to provide long-term protection.
 	Residential Roofing: For homeowners on a budget, there is no better option than a rolled modified bitumen flat roof. It’s especially common to get this material over a carport or porch.
 	Commercial Roofing: Since it’s usually dark, rolled asphalt roofing helps cover signs of dirt, which is a great advantage for hospitals and other structures where you can see the roof from inside the building. It’s also good for roofs that see a lot of foot traffic.
 	Budget Roofing: If you’re on a tight budget but still need a reliable roof, there is no better option than rolled modified bitumen. It’s as cheap as quality roofing gets, and it’s durable enough to keep your property protected against tropical storms and hurricanes.
 	Fast Roofing: Rolled roofing is perfect for when you need a roof installed ASAP. With a quick and simple installation process, most roofs can be successfully replaced in one day. Roof replacements don’t get faster than this!

As you can see, there are a wide variety of situations where rolled asphalt roofing could be the right choice for you. This affordable, versatile roofing material has a lot to offer. Sometimes, however, there may be a better material for your structure. That’s why it’s important to be aware of other flat roofing materials available to you.
Alternatives to Rolled Roofing


Rolled modified bitumen roofing is great in a lot of situations. Sometimes, however, you need something a little more durable and waterproof. For Floridians in this position, we recommend thermoplastic polyolefin (TPO) flat roofing.

TPO is a rubberized roofing membrane. This means that, similar to rolled asphalt roofing, it is rolled out across your roof. Unlike rolled roofing, however, TPO is a rubber roofing system. This means that it is much more resistant to water intrusions. It’s also better at withstanding Florida’s harsh UV rays, which helps it last longer.

As you might expect, the enhanced performance of TPO comes at a cost. Thankfully, though, TPO is only slightly more expensive than modified bitumen rolled roofing. On average, TPO roofing costs $4 to $10 per square foot. And since it’s white, it helps reflect UV rays away from your structure, which can help with cooling it and lowering monthly energy bills.

In Florida, a TPO roof can last anywhere from 20-30 years. These are durable, long-lasting roofing systems. While rolled asphalt roofing is great, if you want an upgraded option, TPO roofing is certainly worth considering.

And with world-class customer service, we know how to keep our customers happy throughout the roofing process. We even make it easy to get started!

### Can Insurance Make You Replace a Roof? Know Your Rights & Responsibilities

The situation with homeowners insurance in Florida has been difficult for a long time. And part of the issue is that homeowners aren’t totally clear on what their rights and protections are. For example, many Floridians are asking, can insurance make you replace a roof?

The answer is more complicated than a yes or no, which is why PITCH Roofing is here to fully explain your rights and responsibilities when getting a roof insured. As long-time Florida roofers, we know the local homeowners insurance landscape. Stick with us as we explain everything you need to know about replacing a roof and homeowners insurance!
Can Insurance Make You Replace a Roof in Florida?


Technically speaking, no, your homeowners insurance company can’t force you to get a new roof. As the homeowner, you have the final say on any work done on your property. Realistically speaking, though, your insurance provider can require you to replace your roof or risk losing coverage on your roof.

In some cases, an insurer may be completely unwilling to insure your property at all without a roof replacement. That’s because your roof protects the entirety of your structure, and without a sound, stable roofing system, everything else is also at risk.

It’s worth noting, however, that your insurer is limited in when they can make getting a new roof a requirement for insuring your property. Let’s take a look at the specific rules and requirements!
When Can Insurance Make You Replace a Roof?
Once upon a time, insurance companies would make you replace a roof that was getting older. Since shingle roofs average around 20 years of life in Florida, this meant that insurers required all roofs more than 15 years old to be replaced before they would issue a policy. Thankfully, this is no longer the case.

Nowadays, your insurer can’t require you to replace a roof simply because it’s 15 years old or older. That’s thanks to a new law that went into effect in 2022. However, there are still circumstances where your insurer can require you to replace your roof to get or maintain a policy.

If your roof is 15 years old or older, your insurer will likely require a roof inspection. If the inspection comes back without issues, they’ll issue a policy. However, if they find signs of damage, then you will still have to replace your roof to get coverage. This is how insurance companies get around the new Florida law.

Additionally, insurance companies can require you to replace a roof if your roof is made with poor materials. For homeowners with 3-tab shingle roofs, it’s common for an insurer to require you to upgrade to architectural shingles before they’ll insure your property.

They can also require you to replace your roof if you haven’t been taking care of it. If your roof has had missing shingles for a long time, this creates a weak point in your roofing system. As the damage spreads, your roof becomes less secure and riskier to insure.

These are all the situations where an insurer can, and can’t, require you to replace a roof. Now, let’s talk about what you can do to make sure this doesn’t happen to you.
How to Avoid Insurance Making You Replace Your Roof


When insurance makes you replace a roof, it’s because they don’t want to risk protecting a weak roofing system. So the best way to avoid this situation is to have a strong, robust roof. Let’s talk about some ways you can make that happen.
Stay Up-to-Date on Maintenance
Taking care of your roof is the best way to avoid having your insurance company make you replace it. If you’re unsure where to start, it’s a good idea to get a roof inspection every year or two. If your roof is 15 years old or older, you can increase that to yearly and after major storms.

You’ll get a report on your roof after an inspection, and it’s important to take any damage or wear and tear seriously. Minor problems today become major issues over the course of months. Whether it’s missing shingles, a leak, or anything else, timely roof repairs are the best way to avoid needing a replacement!
Choose High-Quality Roofing Materials
When you do need a new roof, it’s best to invest in high-quality products. That doesn’t mean breaking the bank with a standing seam metal roof, either. You can get a quality roof by choosing architectural asphalt shingles, the most popular roofing material in Florida.

These shingles are much better able to protect your home than 3-tab shingles. This is exactly the kind of assurance and quality that insurers are looking for when issuing policies!
Only File Claims When You Need To
If you have an old or low-quality roofing system, you should only file a claim when you’re prepared to replace your roof. When you file a claim for an old roof, the company will likely send someone out to assess the state of your roof. While they might not have been aware of any problems before, they will get a complete picture of the state of your roof during that inspection.

For an old roof that has minor damage, it’s often best just to handle the repairs on your own dime. Of course, if you’re prepared to replace your roof, then there’s no harm in reaching out to your insurer. Just know that they may not cover the full value of your roof if it is especially old or in poor shape.
Get a Free Roof Replacement or Repair Estimate
There are some circumstances where insurance can make you replace a roof or revoke your policy. Whether you’ve found yourself in this position or are looking to avoid it, PITCH Roofing has your back. As a full-service roofing company, we can handle roof repairs to keep you ahead of the game or replace your roof to satisfy any insurance company requirements.

### Picking a New Metal Roof: Galvalume vs. Aluminum vs. Steel

Upgrading to a metal roof is a great way to get your property ready for the next major storm. But which type of metal roof is right for you? When looking at Galvalume vs. aluminum vs. steel, there are major differences and considerations to make to ensure that you’re getting the best roof for your property.

PITCH Roofing comes with a combined 60+ years of experience installing metal roofs in Florida. That makes us the perfect local roofing experts to help you decide on the right type of metal roof for your home or commercial property. Let’s talk about the good, the bad, and the costs of different metal roofing materials available in Florida!
Steel Roofing
For Florida metal roofing, steel is often the “default” option. And there are good reasons for that — steel roofs are strong, durable, and reliable. If you’re looking for a roof that can stand up to the next major storm, steel roofing is certainly worth considering. In Florida, most steel roofs use galvanized steel for its rust protection and resistance.
Upsides of Steel Roofs in Florida
There are a lot of great reasons to get a steel roof replacement in Florida. If you’re stuck deciding between Galvalume vs. aluminum vs. steel, consider these upsides to steel roofing:

 	Long-Lasting: When installed properly, a steel roof can last for 50 years or more, even in hurricane-prone Florida.
 	Affordable: Metal roofing is never cheap, but steel is one of the most affordable metal roofing materials!
 	Durable: Steel roofing is great at resisting UV rays and hail. It can even withstand hurricane-force winds with no issues!
 	Minimal Maintenance: Because steel is so hardy and resilient, it doesn’t require much upkeep.
 	Color Variety: Steel roofs often come painted to provide an extra layer of protection. Since steel comes in a wide range of colors, it’s easy to find a steel roof that suits your taste and aesthetic.

Cons of Steel Roofs in Florida
Steel roofs have a lot to offer, but they’re not perfect. And there are some circumstances where steel might not be right for your Florida property. Some of the biggest cons of steel roofing are:

 	Vulnerable to Rust: Galvanized steel has a rust-resistant coating, but that doesn’t make it immune to rust. If you’re in a coastal part of Florida, steel roofing may not be rust-resistant enough to protect your property.
 	Weak to Scratches: During a hurricane, storm debris can scratch your steel roof. If this happens, you’ll need to reapply any paints or anti-corrosive coatings to prevent rust from spreading through your roof.

Steel Roof Costs
Calculating metal roofing costs by material can be tricky for Galvalume, steel, and aluminum. That’s because your total roofing costs will depend on who installs your roof, what type of fasteners you choose, and the thickness of your metal. That said, steel roofing costs $5 to $12 per square foot on average.
Galvalume Roofing


Galvalume is very similar to galvanized steel. Both roofs use steel sheets of metal that are protected by an anti-corrosion alloy. Galvalume has zinc, however, where galvanized steel does not. Thanks to the presence of zinc, Galvalume can “self-heal” by shedding rusted or damaged pieces. This makes it even more durable than conventional steel roofing!
Pros of Galvalume Roofs in Florida
Galvalume steel is a very in-demand material in Florida. That’s because it has a lot to offer both residential and commercial property owners! Here are some of the features that Floridians love about Galvalume:

 	Rust Resistant: Even more so than galvanized steel, Galvalume is heavily resistant to rust. This makes it great for Florida, where humidity can make rust a serious concern!
 	Longevity: Galvalume roofs can last for 60 years or more, making them perfect for long-term protection!
 	Steel Strong: Like galvanized steel roofing, Galvalume roofs can withstand high winds, hail, and UV rays. That’s why they’re a great choice for Florida roofing!
 	Affordable: Galvalume steel roofing is less expensive than other types of metal roofing like aluminum or copper.

Downsides of Galvalume Roofs in Florida
Galvalume roofs are great, but they’re not perfect. Here are the cons of Galvalume roofing that you should know before committing to a roof replacement:

 	Minimal Versatility: Galvalume steel only comes in one color, so you’ll have to have a grey roof. This isn’t a negative for everyone, but it’s important to be aware of!
 	Not Right for the Coasts: Coastal Florida has a lot of saltwater in the air. While Galvalume is resistant, it can’t take that much corrosion, so it’s not great for structures within a mile of the coastline.
 	Vulnerable to Scratches: Like galvanized steel, Galvalume gets its rust protection from its coatings. If your Galvalume roof gets scratched up, that creates an opportunity for rust to form.

Galvalume Roof Costs
Galvalume roofing offers enhanced protection compared to galvanized steel. This improved protection comes at a cost, however. On average, Galvalume steel costs $8 to $14 per square foot. While this is more expensive, many homeowners consider these roofs to be well worth the initial investment!
Aluminum Roofing


Two factors set aluminum apart from other metal roofing materials. First, it is extremely lightweight without sacrificing strength or durability. Additionally, it’s the most rust-resistant metal on the market. These two features make it extremely popular for metal roof replacements in Florida!
Pros of Aluminum Roofs in Florida
Aluminum roofs have more than a few upsides, even when compared to Galvalume and galvanized steel. Some of the biggest reasons that Floridians get aluminum roof replacements include:

 	Energy Efficient: Even more than steel, aluminum reflects UV rays away from your home. This means your AC doesn’t have to work as hard, which saves you money on energy bills!
 	Color Options: Aluminum comes in a wide range of colors, so you should have no trouble finding a roof to match your property.
 	Perfect for Coasts: Aluminum is all but immune to rust, even in areas with saltwater. This makes it the ideal roofing material for coastal Floridians!
 	Low Maintenance: Aluminum roofs need very little maintenance over the course of their lives.
 	Long-Lasting: On average, aluminum roofs last 50 years or more.
 	Hardy: Despite being extremely lightweight, aluminum can resist hurricane-force winds just as well as steel!

Negatives of Aluminum Roofs in Florida
Aluminum is a highly desirable roofing material. Like all roofs, though, it has its drawbacks. Here’s what you should know about aluminum before choosing it as your new roofing material:

 	Costly: Aluminum is an expensive roofing material. While it’s not as pricey as copper, it costs more than Galvalume or galvanized steel roofs.
 	Susceptible to Dents: While aluminum is durable, it is a softer metal. This means it can dent during hailstorms. This damage is usually just aesthetic and does not impact the performance of your roof, however.

Aluminum Roof Costs
Aluminum roofs are not the most expensive roofs on the market, but they’re also a far cry from the cheapest. Prices vary, but aluminum can cost anywhere from $9 to $18 per square foot. If you’re in coastal Florida and want robust protection, you won’t find a better option at this price point.

But no matter what type of metal roof you need, you can count on PITCH Roofing to install it perfectly.

### Are Roof Prices Going Down Soon in Florida?

Roof prices are almost always in flux. With a variety of material and logistic cost factors, it can be hard to keep track of where roof prices are falling these days. And things only get more complicated when roofers use dishonest communication practices to hide the realities of roof prices. That’s why we’re here to give you a complete, clear update on if roof prices are going down or not.

We’re PITCH Roofing, and we pride ourselves on roofing done right. For us, that means transparent pricing information when you need it most. So, are roof prices going to go down in Florida this year? The answer is a little complicated, so let’s talk about the state of roof replacement costs in 2025!
Are Roof Prices Going Down in Florida This Year?


Economic inflation is a hot topic right now. Since the pandemic, the price of many essentials, from groceries to utilities, has gradually increased. At its peak, supply chain issues raised inflation as high as 8% in 2022. With the price of everything going up, it was unsurprising when roofing prices skyrocketed to match.

Now, though, the situation has changed. Inflation has been decreasing since the summer of 2022, and as of early 2025, we’re seeing inflation rates around 3%. While this is still high, it’s much closer to the Fed’s goal of 2% year-over-year inflation. So since inflation has gone down, are roof prices going down alongside it?

Well, not exactly. While inflation has slowed, that doesn’t undo the years of price increases, it just means that future increases should be slower. For this reason, a slowing in inflation doesn’t mean that prices are going to drop. The other side of this issue is that, while inflation has generally slowed down, the roofing industry continues to see significant price increases in 2025.
The State of Roofing Costs in 2025
As contractors, our material manufacturers send us updates once a quarter about how much they will be raising their prices. Since inflation was at its peak, those numbers have tended to be between 7 and 12 percent price increases per quarter. And while inflation has slowed in many areas, these roofing material costs continue to surge in price every quarter.

As of February 2025, the average cost of a roof in Florida is somewhere around $13,000. The specifics of your roof replacement costs will depend on the size of the project, your material, and your roofers, to name a few of the biggest cost factors. Given that the roofing industry continued to see quarterly prices increases, there is every reason to believe that this number will only increase in 2025.

Among homeowners, everyone seems to agree that the best time to get a new roof was before the pandemic. Now that we’re here, though, many homeowners are wondering when prices will lower again. Essentially, the question becomes: When are roof prices going down?
When Are Roof Prices Going Down in Florida?


While inflation became especially severe in 2022, it has always been a fact of life. Similarly, although roofing cost increases now can be especially staggering, the price of roofing has always gone up. Across our decades as local Florida roofers, we have never seen the average price of a new roof decrease.

In other words, there is no reason to expect roof prices to go down in Florida. Although the roofing industry’s high inflation rates may one day slow down, roofs will continue to be more expensive year over year. The only difference will be in how great that difference is, but you can bank on it continuing to trend upward.

In the roofing industry, we have a saying. “The best time to get a roof was 10 years ago. The second best time to get a roof is today.” Roofing prices are always going to go up, and there’s nothing you can do to get around inflation that has already happened. What you can do, however, is act before the next price increase.

We have established that while roofing prices may slow the rate at which they increase, they are very unlikely to decrease. This means that the best time to get a roof replacement is right now, before we see another quarterly cost increase. ### What to Do After Homeowners Insurance Denies Your Roof Damage Claim

Having your roof damaged in a hurricane shouldn’t be a big headache. Unfortunately, sometimes getting insurance to cover the damage is not as easy as you’d like. There is good news, though. If homeowners insurance denies your roof damage claim, you still have recourse to get your roof replacement covered.

We’re PITCH Roofing, and as your local roofing partner, we’re here to help you get your new roof covered by insurance. On the one hand, it’s true that roofers can’t (and shouldn’t) get between you and your insurer. At the same time, we’ve been in this industry long enough to know the common pitfalls that homeowners run into when trying to file a roof damage claim. That’s why we’re telling you everything you need +to know about getting your roof damage claim approved!
Should Homeowners Insurance Cover My Roof Damage Claim?


Before we talk about how to get your claim covered, we first need to establish if your situation qualifies. Hurricane damage is usually a valid reason for homeowners insurance to accept your claim. These are called “acts of God,” and since there’s no way to account for them as a homeowner, your insurer should be able to cover the costs of fixing any roof damage.

But what if homeowners insurance denies your roof damage claim anyway? It happens, and there can be a lot of reasons why. Identifying why your claim was denied is the first step in getting an approval. In our experience, these are some of the biggest reasons that roof damage claims get denied after a storm:

 	Your insurance company claims that there was no damage to your roof or that the damage was minimal
 	You filed your roof damage claim too late. Most insurers allow you to file a claim within one year of your roof being damaged
 	Your insurer claims that your roof was not eligible to be covered by your policy. This usually happens if your roof was 20+ years old or already had extensive damage
 	Your roof was made with defective materials. Insurers won’t cover roofs that aren’t installed properly and made with high-quality materials. If you’re still under your manufacturer's warranty, you can use that to get your roof covered

There are plenty of reasons why roof damage claims get denied. Similarly, there are different paths you can take when trying to get your claim approved.
What to Do After Homeowners Insurance Denies Your Roof Damage Claim


Try not to get discouraged if your insurer denies your claim. Receiving an initial rejection does not necessarily mean you will be on the hook for a new roof. Submit a request for them to identify the reason that your claim was denied. Depending on the answer, you may have a way to get your roof covered.

Unfortunately, there is not much you can do if your claim was denied due to submitting it too late, poor materials, or if your roof was too old or damaged to qualify for the policy. However, if your homeowners insurance denies your roof damage claim because they claim that your roof wasn’t severely damaged, you still have options.
Get a Second Opinion
To determine the extent of the damage, your insurer will have already sent an adjuster to your home. If that adjuster determined that your roof was not damaged, then you can request that they send out a second adjuster to conduct a second appraisal. Adjusters make mistakes, and sometimes getting a fresh set of eyes can yield a very different result.

Ideally, the second adjuster will find that there’s enough damage to approve your claim. Sometimes, though, the adjuster will come back and agree with the findings of the first. As a homeowner, this can leave you in an uncomfortable position after your homeowners insurance denies your roof damage claim twice. From here, you have the option of pursuing other ways to pay for a new roof (like roof financing) or continuing to try to get your claim approved.
Hire a Structural Engineer
If you’re certain that your roof was severely damaged and you want to prove it, your final option is to reach out to a structural engineer and ask them to take a look. With any luck, they will find that your roof was damaged in a recent storm. After that, they’ll write a report that you can send to your insurance company to supplement your claim.

This is an uncommon step, but it’s one you can take if the first two adjusters did not find damage. It’s important to note, however, that your insurer is not obligated to accept the structural engineer’s findings. Suppose the structural engineer doesn’t find damage, or your insurer doesn’t accept their report. In that case, you can either accept the denial or get in touch with the Florida Office of Insurance Regulation to explore further options.
Get a Free Roofing Estimate from Veteran Local Roofers
At PITCH, we hate to see homeowners having trouble with their insurance companies. Needing a new roof is stressful enough without the added hassle. If homeowners insurance denies your roof damage claim, use this guide to explore your options and get your claim approved. And when it’s time to get a new roof put on, make sure to choose local professionals who know how to help.

As a full-service roofing company, PITCH Roofing knows local roofing systems inside and out. No matter what storm damage your roof has suffered, we’ll know how to resolve the issue and ensure that you have a robust, durable roofing system to protect your property against the next major storm. And with friendly, knowledgeable customer service staff, you can count on us to make the roofing process easier at every step of the way.
