### Should You Replace Your Roof Before Selling Your Home

As the Florida housing market starts to slow down, many homeowners are looking for a way to make their property more appealing. But should you replace your roof before selling your home? Rather than a simple yes or no, the answer often depends on your home and your situation.

We’re PITCH Roofing, your local roofing partner. As veteran contractors, we’ve seen situations where replacing a roof before selling a home was essential, and others where it wasn’t necessary at all. Keep reading to see whether or not you should replace your roof before selling your Florida home!
Should You Replace Your Roof Before Selling Your Home?
There are a few scenarios where it makes sense to replace your roof before selling your home. Specifically, it could be worth replacing your roof if it is old or has extensive damage. We don’t mean things like a couple missing shingles, either — while that should be repaired before selling your home, you only need to replace a roof when there is no way to salvage your roofing system.

Signs that you should replace your roof before selling your home include:

 	Major roof leaks
 	Bald shingles and finding stone granules in your downspouts
 	Roof sagging
 	Cracked or curled shingles
 	Many missing roof shingles

Additionally, you may want to replace your roof before selling if it is especially old. Shingle roofs last for about 20 years on average, so if your roof is nearing 20 years of age, then you may need to replace it before selling. Even if your roof is 15 years old, you may find it hard to find buyers who want to sign up to buy a new roof so soon after purchasing the home.

If your roof needs replacing when you sell, the buyers will likely ask for a lower price or a credit. For this reason, it’s best to get ahead of things by replacing your roof before listing your home. On the other hand, if your roof is in good shape and still has plenty of life left, then there is no reason to replace it.
How Much Does It Cost to Replace a Roof in Florida?


If you think that you should replace your roof before selling your home, your next question is likely how much that will cost. With roofing, exact numbers always depend on the specifics of your home and your chosen roofing materials. For our purposes, we’re going to focus on roofs with architectural asphalt shingles, the most popular roofing material in Florida.

There are factors that could increase this price, though. Roofs with water damage often cost more to replace because your roofers need to replace the decking. Unfortunately, since the decking sits under your shingles, there is no way to assess this damage before tearing off your old roofing system.

Some other factors that can increase your roof replacement costs are:

 	Skylights, chimneys, hills and valleys, dormer windows, and other unique roofing features
 	The presence of solar panels
 	Having a roof that is difficult to access
 	A steep pitch, which may require contractors to use safety gear to access your roof
 	Choosing national roofing companies, which have larger overhead costs than local roofers

FAQs About Replacing Your Roof Before Selling Your Home
1. Q: Will replacing my roof help my home sell faster?

A: Yes, replacing your roof can make your home much more appealing to potential buyers. Not only does a new roof add curb appeal, but it also gives buyers peace of mind that their investment is going to be safe and protected. While there is no guarantee that replacing your roof will make your home sell faster, it certainly increases your chances of selling quickly.

2. Q: Will replacing my roof before selling my home pay for itself?

A: It’s true that getting a new roof will drastically increase the value of your home. However, it’s hard to say whether or not you’ll completely recoup the cost of a roof replacement in resale value. More often, we expect homeowners to see around a 60% recoup on their initial investment.

3. Q: Can’t I just lower the cost of my home instead of replacing the roof?

A: In some cases, yes, you can simply accept a lower resale value rather than replacing your roof. However, this is not always an option. For example, insurance companies may not want to insure a roof that’s old or worn down. If your buyers aren’t confident that they will be able to get home insurance, then they are much less likely to complete the purchase.

4. Q: Should I replace my roof before selling, even if it’s not old or damaged?

A: If your roof has a lot of life left in it and isn’t severely damaged, then you do not need to replace it before selling. While you should make sure your roof is in good shape before selling, repairs and maintenance should be your primary focus if you have a young, healthy roof.

5. Q: Can I get more money for my house if I upgrade my roof?

A: When replacing a roof before selling, the most common choice is to install architectural asphalt shingles. But by upgrading to metal or tile, you can drastically increase the value of your home. While these roofs are more expensive to install, that may be worth the added value and interest in your home.

### Pros and Cons of Painting Roof Shingles

Asphalt shingles are an extremely popular residential roofing material. Homeowners love their low cost, durability, and easy maintenance. Over time, though, you can get tired of seeing the same old shingles and want a change. For many homeowners, the first thing they consider is painting roof shingles.

But is it a good idea to paint asphalt roof shingles in Florida? We’re PITCH Roofing, and as your dedicated Florida roofers, we’re here to talk about the best way to care for your roof. If you’re considering painting your shingle roof, check out our advice before picking up the paintbrush!
Pros of Painting Roof Shingles


When people consider painting roof shingles, it’s usually for one of three reasons. They either want to improve their home’s energy efficiency, change their aesthetic, or cover up surface damage to shingles. Let’s take an in-depth look at each of these motivations and how painting your roof shingles can accomplish them!
Cooling Your Home
While shingles come in a variety of colors, they’re often a somewhat dark shade or even completely black. Up north, these colors attract heat and help warm your home in the winter. But in Florida, that’s a recipe for drawing heat to your home during our brutal summers.

By painting your roof shingles, you can give your roof a lighter color that doesn’t attract UV rays. As a result, your roof won’t have to work so hard in the summer. This means lower energy bills, even during the hot summer months!
Changing Styles
There are a lot of reasons that you might want to change the color of your roof. If you’ve recently repainted your home or added a new addition, then you may want to update your roof to make sure everything matches. Alternatively, if you recently had some shingles replaced, you may want to paint the new shingles to match the exact color of the old ones.

For any of these cases, painting roof shingles is one way to get a cohesive roof that suits your style. This can also help with curb appeal, which is a huge factor if you’re reselling your home.
Putting Off a Roof Replacement
One of the most common reasons we see people painting roof shingles is to avoid a roof replacement. This happens when people have roof shingles with unsightly surface damage that doesn’t affect the structural integrity of the shingles. In terms of aesthetics, painting a roof is a much cheaper and easier way to get it looking new than tearing off and replacing your roof.

When homeowners use proper painting materials designed for asphalt shingles, the paint can also serve as an additional layer of protection. With paints made from acrylic latex, you can expect your paint to help your shingles resist Florida’s harmful UV rays.
Cons of Painting Roof Shingles


There are a lot of tempting reasons to paint your shingle roof. But the truth is that painting roof shingles is rarely a good idea. While there are some advantages, the cons outweigh the pros in the majority of cases. Let’s take a closer look at the downsides of painting your roof shingles!
High Risk of Damaging Your Shingles
If you’re not a licensed roofing professional, then working on your roof puts your shingles in danger. For one thing, you need to ensure that you’re using the correct type of paint. If you use the wrong painting materials, then you could end up weakening your shingles instead of strengthening them.

You also have to make sure conditions are just right to paint your roof. If there is any moisture at all on your roof, you could trap it inside with your shingles, leading to rot and deterioration. Even applying uneven coatings can cause long-term problems with your shingles! For all of these reasons, painting roof shingles is often too great a risk for the reward.
Increases Roof Maintenance
One of the great things about shingles is that they require minimal, simple maintenance. But once you’ve painted your roof, that’s going to change. That’s because your shingles are covered in stone granules. Over time, these granules will naturally fall off your shingles. If you’ve painted your shingles, they’re going to take paint with them, which will leave your roof looking spotty.

Paint also tends to bubble and chip over time, especially in our hot climate. For all these reasons, you’ll likely need to repaint your roof every five years or so. This adds a lot of expensive maintenance to your roof, costing you a good deal in the long run!
Does Not Repair Damage
As we mentioned, homeowners sometimes paint roof shingles to put off a roof replacement. However, if your roof is damaged, painting your shingles isn’t going to fix it. In fact, you only put your roof in more danger by putting off necessary repairs or replacements.

Let’s say, for example, that your roof is leaking. Painting shingles might seem like a way to cover up any weaknesses in your roof with a thick coating of paint. The issue, however, is that water is already in your roofing system. Over time, that damage will spread and lead to higher overall roofing costs. For this reason, we strongly discourage homeowners from painting over damaged shingles.
Get a Free Roof Replacement or Repair Quote
Painting roof shingles can be a good idea if you know what you’re doing and want to update the color of your roof. But it is never a solution for damaged roof shingles. If your roof is having troubles, the best thing you can do is reach out to licensed roofers who know how to help.

That’s us. At PITCH, we deliver quality workmanship and customer service. We even offer roof replacement financing for homeowners who don’t have the funds for a new roof right away. This way, you can get the help you need without waiting for the problem to get worse.

### Are Stone-Coated Metal Roofing Tiles Better Than Other Tiles?

Tile roofs have been a popular roofing material in Florida for more than 200 years. Clay and concrete are two of the traditional types of tiles that Floridians use to keep their homes hurricane-ready. With new stone-coated metal roofing tiles on the market, though, many homeowners are interested in combining the strength of metal roofing with the classic charm of Florida roof tiles.

We’re PITCH Roofing, and as your local roofing partner, we’re here to help you decide on the right material for your new roof. Today, that means telling you everything you need to know about stone-coated steel roofing. To get started, let’s talk about what these metal roof tiles are and how they work!
What Are Stone-Coated Metal Roofing Tiles?


When most people think of metal and tiles, they’re thinking of two distinct types of roofing. However, with stone-coated metal roofing tiles, you can get the best of both worlds. To demonstrate that, let’s talk a little more about how manufacturers make these tiles.

As the name implies, these tiles start as sheets of metal. They’re then shaped into tiles using the same molds that shape clay and concrete into roofing tiles. Because of this, they come in a variety of styles, just like other roofing tiles. From there, they receive a thick coating of stone granules. These granules serve a few different purposes, including the following:

 	Making the metal tiles look more natural
 	Improving UV resistance to help protect your metal roof from the sun
 	Enhancing impact resistance so your metal roof won’t be dented by hail or storm debris

But the biggest advantage to these stone granules is that they make your metal roof all but identical to a conventional tile roof. This means that instead of the industrial look, you’ll have a metal roof that supports your home’s welcoming aesthetic.

At the same time, you’ll get to enjoy the strengths of a metal roofing system. Stone-coated metal tiles are usually installed by drilling them down into your roof. This is an exposed fastener roofing system, and you can count on your metal tiles staying in place even during a major storm.

We’re here to see how metal tiles compare to traditional roofing tiles, though. To do that, let’s look at these roofing materials side by side.
Stone-Coated Metal Roofing Tiles vs. Traditional Tile Materials


When you’re getting a new roof, it needs to have three essential traits. It needs to fit within your budget, it needs to last for a long time, and it needs to keep your home safe. To see how stone-coated metal roofing tiles compare to clay and concrete, let’s examine each of these areas a bit more closely!
Cost
When people think of metal roofing systems, their first thought is often that they must be expensive. While metal roofs aren’t cheap, they also aren’t the mosts expensive material. And in most cases, stone-coated metal roofing tiles cost less than clay or concrete.

On average, metal roofing tiles cost $7 to $15 per square foot. That’s not cheap, but it’s certainly more affordable than clay tile roofing costs, which fall between $12 and $21 per square foot. They’re even more affordable than concrete roof tiles, which cost $9 to $19 per square foot. This makes metal one of the most affordable roofing materials for tile roofing!
Lifespan
Nobody wants to pay for a new roof that isn’t built to last. But how long your new roof lasts will depend a lot on which material you choose. And with tile roofing, there is a wide range in how many years of protection your roof will provide, depending on which material your tiles are made from!

Let’s look at how long each type of tile roofing material will last in Florida, on average:

 	Stone-Coated Steel: 40 to 70 years
 	Clay: 50 to 100 years or more
 	Concrete: 50 years

As you can see, stone-coated steel is highly competitive when it comes to lifespan. While it’s hard to compete with long-lasting clay, metal roof tiles still last much longer than asphalt shingles, which only provide 20 years of protection on average!
Durability
Stone-coated metal roofing tiles enjoy hardy and comprehensive protection. In Florida, that’s exactly what you need — between hurricane-force winds, sun exposure, and year-round humidity, your roof has a lot of factors working against it. Thankfully, metal tile roofs are ready for all of this and more.

 	Stone-coated steel roofing tiles offer all of the following protective features:
 	The ability to resist winds up to 170 mph
 	Surfaces that discourage mold and algae growth since they’re inorganic
 	Almost total immunity to pest infestations
 	Rust resistance via specialized roof coatings
 	Class A fire rating

When you invest in a high-quality metal tile roofing system, you can count on it to hold up. Clay and concrete roofing tiles are similarly durable, but they do face a higher risk of damage during a storm because they’re vulnerable to cracks and winds removing one or two tiles. These aren’t issues for metal tiles, though, thanks to the way they’re drilled down in rows and their great, impact-resistant stone coatings!

### What to Do if Your Roof Was Damaged in a Hurricane

After a storm, most homeowners know to take a look around their property to see if there’s any damage. If you’ve gotten unlucky with a recent storm and found damage on your roof, it’s easy to feel overwhelmed or disheartened. The situation isn’t as dire as it seems, though. PITCH Roofing is here to handle all of your storm damage roofing needs after a hurricane!

PITCH contractors have been helping homeowners restore their properties for decades. As local roofers, we know how nasty seasonal hurricanes can be. That’s why we’ve put together this guide on what to do after a hurricane passes if your roof has storm damage. Keep reading for our step-by-step instructions on how to protect your home and your finances!
1. Confirm Your Policy and Document Damage


Most homeowners insurance policies cover damage caused by extreme weather events like hurricanes. And if there’s a hurricane in your area, your insurer likely expects some of their customers to report damages. So once you’ve confirmed that your policy covers hurricane damage to your home, it’s time to document the damage.

This means taking photos of any and all damage. If you’re missing shingles, take photos of both where the shingles are missing and any shingles scattered through your yard. Also be sure to take note of any cracked or lifted materials on your roof. Please note that you should only get on your roof to take photos after the storm has passed and conditions have calmed down — and even then, only if you can safely access your roof.

If you have any doubt about your ability to safely get on your roof, do not risk it. When you call in storm damage roofing professionals for help, they’ll be more than capable of taking photos for you to submit with your insurance claim.
2. Check the Details of Your Policy’s Payout
With Florida homeowners insurance, there are two main types of policies: ACV and RCV. Both of these options will cover some amount of storm roof damage. However, how much you receive will depend greatly on what type of payout your policy stipulates.

With an ACV (actual cash value) policy, your insurer will cover the value of your roof at the time it was damaged. This means that if your roof was 20 years old and damaged by a hurricane, you’ll get much less money than if your roof was 5 years old and received storm damage. In Florida, this is the coverage that most homeowners have.

An RCV (replacement cash value) policy means that your insurer will send you a check with enough money to cover the installation of a new roofing system. RCV policies are uncommon and more expensive, but if your roof has been damaged in a hurricane, they’re great to have.

It’s important to note, however, that RCV policies usually don’t cover important roofing costs like overhead. Roofers can’t accept jobs where they don’t make money, so most homeowners will either have to talk with their insurers or contribute to some part of the storm damage roofing costs. It’s worth noting that this is still generally a better deal than an ACV policy.
3. Account for Your Deductible
Most homeowners insurance policies will require you to put a certain amount of money toward any storm damage roofing costs before they’ll pay out your policy. This is your deductible, and it’s best to know how much you’ll be expected to pay going in.

Deductibles can vary wildly — on one policy it might be $1,000, and for another it could be $5,000 or more. Whatever that number is, you’ll have to contribute that much to your storm damage roofing costs in order to receive your payout.

An important note: Scam roofers might offer to pay your deductible. This is a major red flag and a sign that you cannot trust these people with your roof. No matter what any roofer tells you, nobody else can pay your deductible for you. This is a common tactic of storm chasers who take advantage of hurricane damage to line their pockets while scamming you and your insurer.
4. Start the Process of Submitting Your Claim


The best way to find out how to submit your claim is to give your insurer a call. They’ll collect your information and probably want you to submit photos of the damage. From there, they should direct you on the next steps in completing your claim.

In most cases, they will either tell you to start acquiring roofing quotes, or they’ll send out an adjuster to personally inspect your roof and determine how much it should cost to replace or repair. While many adjusters are professionals doing honest work, we have heard horror stories of adjusters favoring the insurer and lowballing estimates. If you’re concerned about this, it can help to have a storm damage roofing professional on hand when the adjuster is there to take a second look at everything.
5. Start Collecting Storm Damage Roofing Quotes
After your home has been damaged in a hurricane, getting roofing quotes is essential. These accomplish two important tasks. First, it gets storm damage roofing contractors on your roof and assessing the full scope of the damage. They’ll then let you know how bad the damage is and what your options are for addressing it.

It also lets you know how much restoring your roof after a hurricane will cost. Your insurer will want to verify any quotes that you receive, which is why it’s essential that you receive itemized estimates. These are what we provide to our customers — detailed, line-by-line roofing estimates that cover every part of the job. This ensures that at the end of the day, you’ll have a complete roofing system that’s ready to stand up to the next big storm!
Get a Free Quote from Florida’s Top Storm Damage Roofing Professionals
Finding out you have storm damage after a hurricane can be devastating. But no matter how bad the damage is, help is out there. When you’ve checked your policy and are ready to collect quotes, PITCH Roofing will be there to provide a free, no-obligation roofing estimate.

For your free quote, call us at (727) 677-4824 or schedule your estimate online. We’ll come inspect the extent of your roof storm damage and prepare a plan to get your roof hurricane-ready again. If you’re not sure what to do after a hurricane, follow these instructions to get help. And if you need reliable, local roofing professionals, PITCH has your back. As long-time Florida roofers, we know local best practices and ordinances, so we’ll keep your roof strong and ready for the worst that hurricane season can dish out!

Treasure Island Roof Replacement Costs by Material

With that said, let’s examine how much the most popular roofing materials in Treasure Island cost!
Shingle Roof Replacement Cost
Shingles are the most popular roofing material in Florida by far. Not only are they reliable, but architectural asphalt shingles are one of the most affordable options on the market. There are other options that are also worth considering, though.

On average, here is how much Treasure Island shingle roof replacements cost:

 	Architectural Shingles: With distinctive dimensional patterning and a wide range of colors, these roofs suit nearly any home. These shingles last for about 20 years and cost $5 to $9 per square foot.
 	Luxury Shingles: An upgraded asphalt shingle option, these shingles closely resemble slate roofing tiles. While they’re not cheap, they’re much more affordable than real slate at $8 to $17 per square foot.
 	Synthetic Shingles: These are not asphalt shingles, but instead are made of recycled plastics and other weather-resistant polymers. Made to look like wood or slate tiles, these hardy shingles cost $7 to $14 per square foot.

Tile Roof Replacement Cost
Tile roofs have deep roots in Florida, just like PITCH Roofing. First seen when Florida was a Spanish colony, tile roofs have certainly stood the test of time. There are more options than many people realize, though, with Treasure Island tile roof replacement costs being the following:

 	Clay Tiles: The classic option, these tiles are gorgeous, elegant, and long-lasting. All of that comes with a price, though. On average, clay roofing tiles cost between $12 and $21 per square foot.
 	Concrete Tiles: More affordable, concrete tiles are still hardy and resilient even if they don’t last as long as clay. With a wider range of color options, these shingles come in at $9 to $19 per square foot.

Metal Roof Replacement Cost
Metal roofing has become the gold standard for people who want to get their property hurricane-ready. And while there are certainly more expensive options, metal roof replacements are more affordable than many people realize. Let us show you by sharing how much Treasure Island metal roof replacements cost:

 	Exposed Fastener Metal Roofs: Roofs with exposed fasteners, or 5V metal roofs, are the most affordable by far at $7 to $12 per square foot. While the fasteners can have some trouble as they age, these roofs are still extremely resistant to hurricane-force winds.
 	Hidden Fastener Metal Roof: Also called standing seam, hidden fastener metal roofs are some of the highest-quality roofing systems on the market. These roofs are extremely durable and long-lasting, although that comes at a premium with replacement costs ranging from $10 to $35 per square foot.
 	Stone-Coated Steel: Stone-coated steel roofing is made to create metal shingles and tiles. With the strength of metal and the cozy aesthetic of more familiar roofing materials, these roofs cost $7 to $15 per square foot.

Flat Roof Replacement Cost
In Pinellas County, flat roofs are common on both homes and commercial properties. And since they’re for low-slope roofs, they come with their own roofing concerns. That’s why flat roofs require specialized, water-resistant roofing materials. Let’s see how much the average flat roof replacement costs in Treasure Island:

 	TPO: Thermoplastic polyolefin is a single-ply roofing membrane that’s nearly 100% waterproof. Hardy and durable, this flat rubber roofing system costs $4 to $10 per square foot.
 	Modified Bitumen: Made of rubberized asphalt, mod bit can handle both impact damage and slow-draining water. It’s also the most affordable flat roofing material at $4 to $8 per square foot.

### Got Roof Mold? Here Are the Next Steps to Take

Living in Florida, you already know that your roof has to deal with a lot of challenges. But while hurricanes and sun exposure can do a number on your home, roof mold is also a serious concern. If you've noticed signs of mold or algae growing on your roof, it's important to act quickly to protect your home.

But what are you supposed to do about roof mold? And why is it such a big deal, anyway? We're PITCH Roofing, and as your local roofing partner, we're here to help you take care of your roof and protect it against local threats like mold and algae. We're going to start by talking about how mold forms on your roof and why it's worth doing something about.
Why Is Roof Mold Such a Big Deal in Florida?


When you're dealing with roof mold, it can feel like you're the only one with this problem. But the truth is that mold and algae have an easy time growing in Florida. With our hot, humid summers, your roof can easily develop unsightly growths. While most homeowners first notice signs of staining as the main issue, the danger is much more than skin deep.

Roof mold may not be a fast-acting concern, but it is a serious one. Over time, mold or algae will slowly eat away at your roofing materials. Some of the first signs of serious damage that homeowners notice are cracked shingles and roof leaks. If action isn't taken at this stage, the mold or algae could spread and eventually cause a complete roof failure.

Mold isn't just dangerous to your property, either. Breathing in mold can be dangerous depending on the strain, but it's certainly never good for you. As mold spreads through your roofing system, it could make its way into your attic and, through there, the rest of your home. Mold spores can worsen allergies and asthma, as well as cause new breathing problems. For these reasons, it's essential to act quickly when you see mold growing.

What are you supposed to do about roof mold, though? You have several options depending on your budget and your ability!
How to Get Rid of Mold on Your Roof
When it comes to fighting roof mold, there are plenty of cleaners and products to help you get the job done. While only professionals can access the highest-grade roof cleaners necessary for getting rid of mold and algae, you already have access to one of the best tools on the market: bleach.

Bleach is one of the best, easiest ways to kill mold growing on your roof. If you want to try DIY roof mold removal, all you need to do is make a solution that’s ten parts water to one part bleach. Spray it generously over your roof, especially on parts where you can already see mold growing, and it should fix your issue!

It’s important to keep an eye on your roof after cleaning it, though. If you missed a spot, the mold can grow back surprisingly quickly. Noticing mold regrowth means you can either try to spray it with a bleach solution again or you can get a professional cleaning.

Professional roof cleanings are great if you can’t access your roof or DIY roof mold removal hasn’t worked. And in some cases, professional roof cleaning should be your first solution. For example, if your shingles are cracked from mold damage, then it’s time to call in the professionals to make sure the damage doesn’t spread. Additionally, if the mold growth is widespread over your roofing system, then it's best to let experienced professionals clean it up.

Whatever you do, never use a pressure washer to remove roof mold. For one thing, pressurized water will likely leave patches of mold intact. But just as importantly, you could severely damage your roof by using a pressure washer on it. Missing shingles and cracked tiles are two common side effects of people trying to pressure wash their roofs!
What to Do After Your Roof Is Mold-Free


When you've got your roof mold taken care of, it can be tempting to think that there's nothing left to do. But with roofing, it's better to be safe than sorry. That's why we strongly recommend getting a roof inspection after removing your roof mold. Once the mold staining has been cleared, you could still have damaged or weakened shingles. While some signs of this can be obvious, others are harder to spot, especially if you're not a roofing professional.

To make sure your roof is in good shape after clearing off the mold, reach out to PITCH Roofing for a roof inspection. We'll personally inspect your roof and take a close, thorough look to make sure every part of your roofing system is working as intended. If you've fallen behind on your annual roof inspections, then right after clearing off mold is actually a great time to get caught up!

If we find any issues with your roof, one of our veteran Florida contractors will explain exactly what's wrong and what we can do about it. And when you get roof repairs with PITCH, you can count on long-term solutions. Unlike other roofers, we don't do patch jobs. Instead, we address the root of the problem. ### Choosing the Best Roof Shingles in Florida

Nobody wants the second-best roofers working on their home or commercial property. Just like you need the best roofers, you also need the best roof shingles to get the best results. But with so many options on the market, it can be hard to tell which shingle products are worth the investment.

This way, we’ll help you plan a roof replacement that can protect your home for decades without costing an arm and a leg. To get started, let’s discuss the best type of asphalt shingle for your Florida home.
What Is the Best Type of Roof Shingles for Florida?


Before looking at brands, it’s important to understand what type of shingle you’re paying for. Asphalt shingles are the most popular roofing material on the continent, but these shingles vary a lot depending on what type is being used. Generally speaking, there are three main types of asphalt shingles: 3-tab, architectural, and luxury.
3-Tab Asphalt Shingles
If you want the best roof shingles, then 3-tab shingles are not the option for you. The main selling point of these shingles is that they’re cheap — about $2 to $4 per square foot. The trade-off, however, is that these roofs rarely last longer than 15 years at most. And with wind resistance no higher than 70 mph, there are much better options on the market.
Architectural Shingles
Architectural shingles are a good example of a better type of asphalt shingle. They’re made of the same material as three-tab shingles, but they’re thicker and double-layered, which adds to their heft and durability. These are also called dimensional shingles because of their unique patterning, which adds visual depth and dimension to your roof.

Aesthetics aren’t the only way that these shingles add value to your home. They’re also sturdy and capable of withstanding Florida’s unpredictable weather patterns. In fact, top-rated architectural shingles are known to resist winds up to 130 mph. Add in water resistance and strength against UV rays thanks to their stone granules, and these shingles are built to last in Florida. With an average lifespan of 20-25 years, these shingles offer long-term protection.

These would already be some of the best roof shingles on the market even without a great, affordable price point. But it doesn’t hurt that these shingles are also budget-friendly. Architectural shingles cost $5 to $9 per square foot, making them some of the most affordable roofing materials around. Altogether, there’s no doubt that these are some of the best shingles for Florida homeowners!
Luxury Shingles
When talking about the best roof shingles in Florida, it’s hard to beat luxury shingles. For one thing, these shingles don’t even look like shingles. Rather, they recreate the aesthetic of slate shingles at a fraction of the cost.

In addition to looking like a luxurious roofing material, these shingles are also remarkably durable. They’re able to withstand high winds, impact damage, and even moss and algae growth. With all of these protective features, it’s no surprise that these roofs last for 40 years!

That kind of protection and high-quality aesthetics is going to cost you, though. Luxury shingles cost $8 to $17 per square foot. While these may not be the most affordable option, if they’re in your budget, then these could be the perfect shingles for your home!
The Best Brand of Roof Shingles


Whether you choose architectural shingles or luxury shingles, picking the right manufacturer makes all the difference. While there are plenty of brands that make great shingles, only one makes the best roof shingles on the market. For our money, that’s Owens Corning.

Originally founded in 1938, Owens Corning has become a titan of the roofing industry. ### 5 Red Flags of Bad Roofing Companies in Florida

As a homeowner, you want the best local contractors working on your property. But bad roofing companies abound in Florida, especially after a hurricane. When you’re trying to put the pieces back together, underhanded businesses can come in and take advantage of your vulnerable position.

We’re PITCH Roofing, and we hate to see our local community members taken in by untrustworthy roofing schemes. That’s why we’re going over the classic signs of an unreliable roofer. Your roof is a major investment in your property, so it’s essential to make sure you’re trusting the right contractors with your business!
1. Bad Roofing Companies Come from Out of State


When you want a quality roofing system, you need experienced local roofers to install it. That’s because roofing is an extremely localized industry. Knowing how to hammer shingles into place may be a universal skill. But knowing local best practices and county regulations only comes with local experience.

For example, let’s say you wanted to get a metal roof. An out-of-state roofer might not know that if you live within a mile of the coast, you’ll need an aluminum roof to prevent rust and corrosion. If they install the roof, you’ll be the one dealing with a headache in a couple of years when your roofing system starts to rust and weaken.

In roofing, we call out-of-state roofers who come into town after a hurricane “storm chasers.” These aren’t just bad roofing companies — they’re scam roofers. These contractors promise a lot, but they use dirt-cheap labor and materials that leave your home unprepared for the next storm. That’s the best-case scenario; in the worst-case scenario, they might just take your money and leave the state without working on your roof at all.

For all of these reasons, it’s best to keep it local. Not only do local roofers know how to Florida-proof your roof, but you can count on us to still be here and be accountable if there’s a problem with your roof!
2. Skipping the Roof Inspection Is a Red Flag
When you’re trying to get a roof replacement or repair, it can be frustrating to hear that you have to wait for a roof inspection. You want a quick and easy solution, especially if you’re dealing with a leaking roof. Unfortunately, bad roofing companies know that you want an easy fix, and they’ll use that to lock you into a deal that benefits them.

As roofers, we need to see your roof before we agree to any kind of job. That’s because your roof is unique, both in its size and features as well as in the wear and tear that’s already done to it. Just like a roof with a chimney and multiple hills and valleys will have unique pricing factors, we need to see the state of your roof to know what kind of work it needs and how much it will cost to complete that job.

Still, you’ll find some roofers out there who offer to skip this inspection and get you under contract right away. While this seems convenient, you should take it as a massive red flag. Good roofing is individualized and tailored to each customer. On the other hand, this kind of one-size-fits-all roofing means your roofers are doing the same thing to every roof. And that’s a recipe for disaster, because different roofs have very different needs.
3. Vague Estimates Are as Bad as No Estimate
As we’ve established, every roofing job should start with an estimate. But not all estimates are created equal. When you get a quote from your roofers, that quote should go line-by-line explaining every part of your roofing job, including the price and where that money is going.

On the other end of the spectrum, bad roofing companies often offer flat-rate estimates. This means that instead of getting an itemized list, all you get is a flat total. While these rates are often extremely competitive, we strongly discourage Floridians from agreeing to anything that isn’t broken down item by item.

That’s because your roofing system is more complex than you might realize. Between vents and underlayments and decking, your roof contains a lot of parts. Without any one of these, your home is at risk of severe danger. Bad roofing contractors don’t care about that, though, which is why they cut corners and hide that fact by providing a vague estimate.

At PITCH, that’s not how we operate. All of our customers receive an itemized quote detailing every part of the roofing job. This gives you peace of mind while also allowing you to make an apples-to-apples comparison between any roofing estimates that you receive!
4. You Can’t Find Local Reviews
No matter how many quotes you collect, you will never find a roofing company that tells you anything other than “We’re the best in the area.” But what are other people saying? Roofers aren’t always honest about the quality of their work, but you can bet that their customers will be.

Don’t just trust reviews on a website, either. Bad roofing companies can hand-pick reviews or even make them up entirely if they’re especially underhanded. It’s best to look on Google or Yelp for reviews, where you can verify that each one is real and was left by a real person living in Florida.

If you can’t find any reviews, it means one of two things. One: Your roofers are misleading you about their work history. Or two: They are a new roofing company that doesn’t have much work history. In either case, it’s best to go with roofers who have proven themselves in your community.
5. Bad Roofing Companies Always Lower the Price


When you need roofing services, it goes without saying that you want to get a good price. But bad roofing companies will use your desire for the best possible price against you.

When you get a quote, it’s not unheard of for roofers to drop the price a little in negotiations. But reliable roofers will never be able to compete with bad roofers when it comes to price. While good roofers will quickly hit a point where they can’t drop the price any lower due to material and labor costs, bad roofers will have no trouble using lower-quality materials to make sure they get your business.

At the end of the day, we understand that price is always going to matter. But if you let it be the only deciding factor, you open yourself up to potential abuse from bad-faith contractors. While you should always advocate for yourself if you feel like you’re getting a bad deal, it’s important to keep in mind that reliable roofers will charge you enough to pay for high-quality materials and labor!

### Is Metal Barrel Tile Roofing Right for You?

Spanish barrel tiles are a Florida classic. Also called mission tiles, these tiles were first popularized in North America by Spanish churches. Now, centuries later, Floridians still love the look of these rounded roofing tiles. But with new metal barrel tile roofing making waves on the market, there is a way to keep the classic aesthetic and combine it with modern roofing technology.

But are metal barrel tiles a good idea for structures in Florida? And what should you know before investing in a metal tile roof? We’re PITCH Roofing, and we’re just the local roofers to answer these questions and any others you could have about metal tile roofing. Keep reading for our full breakdown of barrel tile roofs made from metal!
What Are Metal Barrel Tile Roofs and How Do They Work?


Metal barrel tile roofing shares some similarities to roofing with clay barrel tiles, but there are also crucial differences. In terms of similarities, both options offer a roof that’s made using the classic look of barrel tiles. These tiles got their name from the comparison to a barrel cut in half vertically, since each tile looks like the rounded half of a barrel. Because of their shape and overlapping installation, they help water move easily off your roof.

Where these roofs differ is in installation techniques. A traditional clay tile roof sees each tile installed individually over wooden trusses. Metal barrel tile roofing, on the other hand, is more streamlined. Tiles come in rows of metal roofing sheets, which contractors then drill down into place during installation.

This covers the essential premise behind a metal barrel tile roof. But how do these roofs perform in humid, hurricane-prone Florida? To answer this question, we’re going to look at all of the essential factors that you want to consider before committing to a metal tile roof replacement.
Aesthetics and Style
The look of barrel tiles has been highly sought after in Florida for centuries. So it stands to reason that when investing in metal barrel tile roofing, you want to make sure you’re still getting the timeless style that Floridians know and love. Well, good news: metal barrel tiles look just like clay barrel tiles. In fact, many homeowners struggle to tell the two apart!

Metal barrel tiles also come with some advantages over traditional clay tiles. With clay, you’re limited to the natural colors that clay comes in — reds and earth tones. With metal, however, many more options are available to you. Since metal roofs can be painted, you can get a tile roof in virtually any color you could imagine!
Roof Durability
If you want a roof that’s ready for the worst that Florida’s weather patterns can dish out, then there’s no better option than metal roofing. Metal roofs routinely resist winds up to 160 mph or more. While there is no way to guarantee that your roof will withstand a hurricane, metal roofs certainly give your property the best odds of standing strong.

Rust is a common concern that homeowners have when considering metal barrel tile roofing. Thankfully, however, rust is not a major concern for metal tile roofs. Steel is vulnerable to rust, which is why contractors generally use galvanized steel or Galvalume steel to protect against corrosion. If you really want to ensure 100% rust resistance, though, aluminum barrel tiles are the way to go.

Metal roofs stand up well to other Florida roof killers as well. From UV rays to mold to dents from storm debris, metal tiles are an excellent way to get your roof Florida-ready!
Longevity & Lifespan
Frankly, it’s hard to compete with clay tile roofing when it comes to longevity. Clay roofing tiles last for around 50 years on average. However, in truly exceptional circumstances and with diligent maintenance, they have been known to stay strong for 100 years or more.

While metal barrel tile roofs can’t last for 100 years, they can certainly hold up for a long time. Metal roofs last for 40-70 years on average, and metal tiles are no different. Despite being much more lightweight than clay tiles, you can expect your metal roofing tiles to last for a long time after installation!
Roof Replacement Costs


At PITCH, we understand that price is always an important factor in deciding what kind of new roof is right for your home or commercial property. While we don’t think that price should be the end-all-be-all, it’s reasonable to want to know how much your new roof will cost.

Calculating roof costs can be tricky, though. Let’s take metal barrel tile roofing, for example. How much your roof costs will depend on the brand of tiles you pick, the costs to transport them to your location, and the roofers you pick — and that’s all before considering unique roofing factors like chimneys or skylights. With all of these variables, it’s impossible to say how much a roof will cost without examining your roof ourselves.

We can still give you a price range for metal barrel tile roofing, however. Metal barrel tiles tend to cost between $8 and $20 per square foot. While this is far from a budget roofing system, it’s also well worth the up-front costs. Many homeowners think of metal tile roofs as investments in their properties, especially with the great curb appeal and longevity that metal barrel tiles can offer!

### What Is the Best Type of Flat Roof in Florida?

In many parts of the US, flat roofs are reserved for commercial structures. In Florida, though, flat roofs are common for both homes and commercial properties. These roofs have a lot to offer — they’re much less likely to be damaged by hurricane-force winds, for one thing, and they do a great job resisting water damage. But what flat roof is best for a Florida structure?

We’re PITCH Roofing, and as your local flat roofing experts, we’re here to walk you through the best flat roofing options in Florida. Roofing is a highly localized industry, so getting insights from roofers in your area is crucial. Stick with us as we review your options and help you decide which flat roofing material is right for your property!
What Flat Roof Is Best for a Florida Home or Business?


There are three main roofing materials for flat roofs in Florida: TPO, modified bitumen, and metal. While each of these options has its own strengths and weaknesses, none of them is the “best.” Rather, each option is the best for different situations, structures, and budgets. With that said, let’s take a look at each of your material options so you can decide which flat roof is best for your property!
TPO Flat Roofing
TPO, or thermoplastic polyolefin, is a single-ply roofing membrane. It’s also what many people refer to as a “rubber roof.” Together, this means that durable, water-resistant, rubberized polymers are rolled out across your roof in a single sheet. This creates a waterproof barrier that will keep out any moisture as water drains from your flat roof.

There are many benefits to TPO roofing. It’s white, for one thing, which helps it reflect heat and UV rays away from your home. As a result, you can expect to enjoy lower energy bills with a TPO roof. It’s also hardy and durable, which helps it resist puncture damage. When installed by experienced contractors, TPO roofs should drain easily and with no risk of damage to your home or commercial property. That’s why these roofs last for 20-25 years on average!

When considering what flat roof is best, price is obviously going to be part of the conversation. While TPO flat roofs are not the most affordable choice, they’re also far from the most expensive. On average, expect to spend $4 to $10 per square foot for TPO roofing membranes.

No roofing material is without its flaws, and TPO is no exception. White roofs tend to look dirtier faster, so you may need to clean your roof more often than with another material, especially if parts of your roof are visible from inside. Additionally, the seams of your roof can weaken over time, which means your roof may need more maintenance as it ages.
Modified Bitumen Flat Roofing


Modified bitumen is a great, affordable flat roofing option. Made of rubberized asphalt, these roofs combine the strength and durability of asphalt with the water-resistance and flexibility of rubber. Unlike TPO, modified bitumen is installed with multiple layers, which can provide additional protection and insulation for your roof.

Modified bitumen is popular for commercial structures that see a lot of foot traffic on their roofs. With a durable asphalt base, these roofs take minimal wear and tear from people walking on top of them. While modified bitumen roofs do not have the longest lifespans, they still last for a respectable 15-20 years.

Where mod bit roofs really shine is in their price point. If you want the flat roof with the best price, this is it. Prices always vary depending on the specifics of your structure, but generally, these roofs cost $4 to $8 per square foot. If you need a new flat roof and you’re working with a small budget, this is easily the best option!

In terms of downsides, mod bit has a few worth considering. Since these roofs are black, they attract more heat in the summer, which can increase your energy bills. It’s also less waterproof than a rubber roof like TPO, which means you may experience leaks if your mod bit is damaged in a hurricane or other major storm.
Standing Seam Metal Roofing
Standing seam is a strong contender for the best flat roof available in Florida. These roofs use a hidden fastener system, which means your metal roofing sheets connect and “fasten” underneath the panels. As a result, your fasteners are protected by your roofing system, which makes these roofs extremely durable and resistant to wear and tear.

In terms of appearance, standing seam offers a sleek and modern look. And since your roofing sheets are connected beneath the panels instead of drilled down into your roof, the sheets of metal freely expand and contract with the sun’s heat. This means a longer life for your roof and minimal maintenance as it ages!

If not for its high price point, a metal flat roof would easily be the best” option for most situations. However, metal roofing is not cheap, and standing seam can be particularly expensive. On average, standing seam metal flat roofs cost $10 to $35 per square foot, making it easily the most expensive flat roofing material.

For many Floridians, though, a metal flat roof is worth the cost. These roofs resist wind and rain, making them extremely effective at weathering hurricanes. And with a lifespan of 40-70 years, there is no flat roofing material that can last as long!

### How to Spot Wind Damage to Your Florida Roofing System

Hurricane season is almost upon us. In addition to making sure you’re up to date on any necessary roof repairs and replacements, now is also a great time to familiarize yourself with the signs of storm damage. After a hurricane, the first thing you’ll want to do is take a look at your roof to make sure everything is where it’s supposed to be. And to do that, you’ll need to know how to spot roof wind damage.

We’re here to help with exactly that. As your local roofing partner, PITCH Roofing is going to help make sure you’re hurricane-ready. Once you’ve taken preventative steps to get your roof ready for hurricane season, the only thing left to do is familiarize yourself with the signs of wind damage!
How to Spot Roof Wind Damage in Florida


Wind damage can happen all across the United States, but hurricanes are a different ballgame entirely. And since hurricanes started being reliably tracked and recorded in 1851, Florida has seen the greatest number of these tropical storms by far. With hurricane seasons projected to become more active in the near future, it makes a lot of sense to prepare for some hurricane damage to your home.

Learning how to spot roof wind damage is one of the best things you can do to prep for hurricane season 2025. Let’s talk about some of the easiest ways to identify wind damage to your home or commercial structure!
Missing or Loosened Shingles
This is the most obvious way to spot roof wind damage — after a storm, you’ll want to take a look at your roof and see if you notice any missing shingles. If you can’t see all parts of your roof from your property, you may want to check your yard as well. After a major storm, it’s common to find missing shingles strewn about your property.

Sometimes, though, shingles are knocked loose without being completely removed. Lifted shingles might look slightly out of place or not aligned with other shingles in your roof. While these shingles are still on your roof, you should take this wind damage just as seriously as you would missing shingles!
Dents or Cracks in Your Shingles
When discovering how to spot roof wind damage, this is one of the trickier steps. From the ground, it can be hard to see if your shingles have taken any impact damage from storm debris. But if your shingles are cracked or dented, they won’t be able to protect your structure as effectively.

One option is to get on your roof and look for bald patches or cracks on your shingles. If you can’t or don’t want to get on your roof, another strategy is to inspect your downspouts. You’ll know that your shingles have been damaged if you find stone granules near your downspouts.
Damaged Gutters


A lot of people get wrapped up in their shingles. However, there are other parts of your roofing system to examine when learning how to spot roof wind damage. During a hurricane, high winds can tear your gutters away from your structure. And if you system was old, it could even crack under the pressure.

That’s why you’ll want to take a walk around the perimeter of your structure and make sure your gutters are still in place. Additionally, it doesn’t hurt to make sure water is still being directed to your downspouts. Hurricanes tend to knock leaves and branches off trees, which can lead to them clogging up your gutters!
Water Leaks
Spotting roof wind damage is not always easy. Even if you don’t see signs of storm damage, a leak immediately after a hurricane means that some part of your roof isn’t working properly. The best thing you can do is tarp your roof to prevent more damage from happening. However, we understand that not everyone can or is comfortable getting up on a roof. You can also place a bucket under the leak to catch water until contractors can come take a look if you prefer!
What to Do After You Spot Roof Wind Damage
Once you’ve identified that your roof has been damaged, you’ll want to reach out to a professional team to help. Any of these signs of roof wind damage could do long-term harm to your roof if not addressed. There can be significant wait times after a hurricane, so it’s best to call your trusted roofers ASAP!

After calling in help, there is another important step to take. Most homeowners insurance policies will cover damage caused by hurricanes and other storms with high winds. However, to qualify for coverage, you’ll need to prove that the damage was caused by high winds.

To get started, take photos of any and all damage to your roof. If you find shingles in your yard, take pictures of those as well. When submitting your claim, you’ll want to include the photos as well as a local article about the storm to demonstrate that there really was a severe weather event in your area. For more information on how to submit a claim after a hurricane, check out our guide!

No matter what signs of roof damage you notice, PITCH Roofing will be there to make sure the problem is addressed. As veteran Florida roofers, we don’t believe in patch jobs. Instead, we believe in clear communication, great workmanship, and above all else, roofing done right!

### Pros and Cons of Putting a Metal Roof Over Shingles in Florida

You’ve probably heard of re-roofing — the process of putting a new roof on top of your old one. Traditionally, this has been accomplished by installing shingles over your old shingle roofing system. But what about putting a metal roof over shingles?

While many homeowners aren’t aware of this option, it is a viable strategy for saving money on a new metal roof. It isn’t right for every home or every situation, though. That’s why PITCH Roofing is here to explain the pros and cons of metal reroofing in Florida!
Pros of Putting a Metal Roof Over Shingles in Florida


As experienced roofers, we can confirm that it’s perfectly safe to install a metal roof on top of old shingles. In fact, there are many benefits to putting a metal roof over shingles! Let’s take a closer look and identify the biggest pros to this method of metal roof installation!
The Complete Protection of Metal Roofing
When discussing putting a metal roof over shingles, the first question most homeowners have is about how well their new roofing system will perform. Is a metal roof installed on top of old shingles as structurally sound as a metal roof installed over fresh roof decking? We’ve been installing metal roofs in Florida for a long time, and we can confidently say that yes, metal reroofing provides all the protection and durability that you’d want for a metal roofing system.

This means you can expect the same strong wind resistance and durability that you’d get with any other metal roofing system. While there are cons to metal reroofing (just like there are cons to any type of roofing), you won’t have to worry about your installation method making your metal roof less effective.
Saves Time and Money
In Florida, many homeowners want metal roofs to better protect their homes against hurricanes. However, price can be a big hurdle in getting a metal roofing system. By putting a metal roof over shingles, though, you can save substantial amounts of money on your metal roof installation.

That’s because installing a metal roof over your old shingles removes a time-consuming step: tearing off your old roof. Since your roofers don’t have to remove and dispose of your previous roofing system, you enjoy lower labor costs. Exact numbers vary, but you may save as much as 25% when choosing reroofing over a full metal roof replacement.

As an added bonus, skipping this step also saves time. If you don’t want roofers working on your home for longer than strictly necessary, this is a great way to speed up the roofing process!
Extra Insulation
Florida’s summers are no joke. When it’s sweltering outside, you want your roofing system to keep your cool air in and the hot air out. While every roof is installed with insulation, putting your new metal roof over your old shingles provides an extra layer of insulation. In this way, you can save money on your utility bills by putting a metal roof over shingles!
Cons of Putting a Metal Roof Over Shingles in Florida


Like with any type of roof installation, there are drawbacks to putting a metal roof over shingles. While some of these reasons might mean that metal reroofing isn’t right for you, none of them are so bad that they completely outweigh the many advantages of installing a metal roof on top of old shingles. Let’s help you make an informed decision by looking at the downsides of this roof installation method!
Unseen Damages and Issues
With a traditional roof replacement, your roofers will inspect your roof decking after tearing off your old roof. This gives them the opportunity to spot water damage and other signs of wear and tear on your decking and replace any damaged sections. In this way, your roof gets a new, fresh start with a solid foundation.

But when putting a metal roof over shingles, there’s no opportunity to inspect your decking. So if your decking is weak or damaged, your roofers may not detect the issue. Over time, this could lead to problems for your roof if the decking continues to degrade. In the worst-case scenario, your roof could prematurely fail and need replacing.

While there is no way to guarantee that your roof decking is in good shape without tearing off your old roof, there are signs of damage to avoid. Leaks are a big one — if your roof has or has had a leak, then metal reroofing may not be for you. Additionally, if you notice a musty scent or mold growing in your attic, then your decking may not be strong enough to support a metal roof over shingles.
You Can Only Reroof Once
Reroofing is a great way to save money on a roof installation. However, putting a metal roof over shingles is something you can only do on your roof once. After that, the system becomes too heavy and you risk developing structural problems.

This means that when the time comes to replace your metal roof, your roofers will have to tear off both the metal and the shingles. As a result, you’ll end up losing any time or money saved by reroofing instead of replacing. That said, this isn’t a problem if you don’t plan to own your home when the time comes to install another new roof!
Difficulty Making Repairs
For things like minor scrapes and scratches, maintaining a metal roof over shingles is no more difficult than taking care of any other metal roof. However, some roofing problems do become more complicated to fix when reroofing. Leaks can be especially problematic since the water can get lost between the different layers of your roof, making it hard to tell where the actual point of entry is.

On the other hand, putting a metal roof over shingles provides extra protection. So while fixing problems can be trickier with these roofs, some homeowners focus instead on the additional protection, which makes needing repairs less likely!

### How Water Drains from a Flat Roof

If your home or commercial structure has a flat roof or sections of a flat roof, then you know that these roofs are special. They need specialized materials and they have unique concerns that don’t affect sloped roofing systems. Specifically, draining a flat roof is one of the most essential jobs of your low-slope roofing system.

We’re PITCH Roofing, your local partner in flat roofing. As experienced Florida roofers, we’re extremely familiar with the ins and outs of flat roofing systems. Today we’re putting that expertise to work and explaining the different ways that a flat roof should drain itself and what to do if you see ponding water on your flat roof.
The Different Ways of Draining a Flat Roof


Proper roof installation is essential to making sure that your roofing system doesn’t have any issues. For example, Florida roofing standards require contractors to make sure that your flat roof has a slope of at least a quarter of an inch per foot of your roof. This greatly helps with draining a flat roof since water doesn’t have the opportunity to pool.

However, a low slope isn’t the only way that flat roofs are designed to move water. Your flat roof will also have a drainage system that makes it easy to shed water before it pools and threatens the integrity of your roof. Let’s look at some of the most common ways that flat roofs in Florida accomplish this!
Gutters
Gutters are the most popular method of draining a flat roof. By lining the edge of your roof with gutters, you give water somewhere to go without it falling against your structure’s foundation. It’s worth noting that while gutters are the most affordable option for draining a flat roof, they also require the most maintenance.
Inner Drains
Think of inner drains as a kind of internal guttering system. Contractors install these drains inside of a roof or parapet wall to provide a place for water to go without disrupting the structure’s aesthetic with external gutters. Usually, a water drain is placed in the center of the roof to catch any trapped water and safely remove it.

During a hurricane, inner drains are a much more effective means of draining a flat roof since they’re not at risk of being damaged by high winds. On the other hand, these internal drains are more expensive to install and repair. For this reason, they’re typically only used for larger commercial structures.
Scuppers
Scuppers work similarly to gutters, but they have a very different aesthetic. They’re made via large openings in the side of a flat roof’s outer wall that lead directly into downspouts. Scuppers are easier to maintain than gutters because their wide mouth makes them less prone to blockages.

Clogs can still happen, though, which is why it’s a good idea to check your downspouts regularly to make sure that water is still flowing normally. Like gutters, these roofs can also be damaged by storms. However, this is less likely since they run in a straight line rather than following the perimeter of your roofing systems.
Siphonic Roof Drain
Up to now, all of the ways of draining a flat roof have relied on gravity. With a siphonic roof drain, though, air is kept out of your drains. This creates a lower-pressure environment, which causes water to drain much faster than it would with regular gravity. As a result, siphonic roof drains are ideal for large roofs that need to move a lot of water quickly.

This is another internal draining system, which is one of the best ways of draining a flat roof if you don’t want to risk hurricane damage. It’s also rare for these systems to clog. However, given how small the pipes are, it is always a possibility. That’s why you should get regular roof inspections to ensure that your siphonic roof drain is still working.
What to Do if Your Flat Roof Isn’t Draining


While sloped roofs have to worry about high winds, the biggest issue for a flat roof is ponding water. Flat roofing materials are made to withstand water damage, but no flat roofing material is completely immune to standing water. The longer water sits on your roof, the more likely that it will wear away at your roof and cause a leak.

If you’ve recently noticed issues with your flat roof not draining, it’s important to get help ASAP. While flat roofs do a great job resisting water damage, they can’t hold out forever. And a problem with draining means that there’s either a problem with your drains or a fundamental issue with your flat roof. Either way, the experienced contractors at PTICH Roofing will know how to help.

At PITCH, we’re proud of our rave roofing reviews. And as a full-service roofing company, we know flat roofing systems inside and out. If you see water ponding on your flat roof, the time has come to call in the professionals. And with PITCH, we make it simple and easy to start the roofing process!

### Metal vs Tile Roofing: Planning Your Hurricane-Ready Roof

Across the Sunshine State, homeowners are making the decision to upgrade their roofs. And with strong hurricanes forecasted to become more frequent in the coming years, that’s an excellent choice. But how do you choose between a metal vs. tile roof to protect your home or commercial property?

PITCH Roofing has a combined 60 years of experience installing metal and tile roofs in Florida. That makes us the perfect local experts to help you decide which roof is right for you! Keep reading for our complete guide to picking the best roof for hurricane-proofing your property.
Choosing a Metal vs. Tile Roof in Florida


From the start, we want to be clear that a metal roof is not inherently better than a tile roof, nor is the opposite true. Both metal and tile roofs are great; the trick is that, as the property owner, you have to decide which one is a better fit for your tastes and your structure. So rather than telling you which material is best, we’re going to see how they stack up side by side in a variety of different areas.

With that said, let’s take a look at the essential information you need to know about metal and tile roofing!
Durability
When trying to get ready for hurricane season with a new roof, durability is arguably the biggest factor. So do metal and tile roofs compare when it comes to withstanding the Florida elements?

Both metal and tile roofs do a great job keeping water out of your roofing system. Each of these roofs is carefully designed to move water off your roof. And thanks to their respective water-resistant underlayments, you don’t have to worry about water getting into your roof during a storm.

Wind resistance is equally important, and again, both metal and tile perform well in this area. Metal roofs can resist winds up to 140 mph, while tile roof wind resistances range from 150 to 180 mph depending on whether you use clay or concrete tiles. All of these numbers are great and will be enough to protect your home, but if we’re comparing a metal vs. tile roof, then tile roofs do have slightly better wind resistance.

Finally, humidity is a big factor in how your roof will age in Florida. Tile roofs are a Florida staple, so it’s no surprise that they do a fantastic job of withstanding high humidity year-round. Conversely, many homeowners expect metal roofs to rust easily. But with rust-resistant Galvalume coatings, modern metal roofs are at minimal risk of rust, although they will usually show signs of corrosion as they near the end of their lifespans.
Longevity
When you buy a new roof, you expect it to last. And the good news is whether you get a metal or tile roof, you can expect your roof to last a long time. But we’re looking to compare these two roofing materials, so which one lasts longer?

For both metal and tile roofs, how long your roof lasts will depend on what type of metal or tile you get. Let’s look at how long a metal vs. tile roof lasts in Florida:

 	Exposed fastener metal roofing: 20-30 years
 	Hidden fastener metal roofing: 40-70 years
 	Concrete roofing tiles: 50 years
 	Clay roofing tiles: 50-100+ years

As you can see, there is a lot of variety in terms of how long your new roof could last. And some metal roofs do last longer than tile roofing systems. However, if we look at the numbers as a whole when comparing a metal vs. tile roof in terms of longevity, tile roofs come out on top.
Cost
Price shouldn’t be everything in a roof replacement, but we understand that cost does matter when getting a new roof. Similar to longevity, though, how much a new roof costs will depend on which type of metal or tile roof you’re considering. Let’s look at the specifics to give you an idea of your roof replacement costs with each option:

 	Clay roofing tiles: $12 to $21 per square foot
 	Concrete roofing tiles: $9 to $19 per square foot
 	Exposed fastener metal roofing: $7 to $12 per square foot
 	Hidden fastener metal roofing: $10 to $35 per square foot

It’s hard to say which material “wins” this round. On the one hand, metal roofing has the most affordable option by far. On the other, the most expensive metal roofing option can cost more than clay roofing tiles. If we had to choose a winner for this metal vs. tile roof comparison, we’d say metal roofing wins since it’s got the lowest-cost option.
An Alternative to the Metal vs. Tile Roof Debate


We’ve shown that there is a lot of variety in how metal and tile roofs perform in Florida. While they both do great across the board, there is no one “best” option. This means that you can either choose which option you personally prefer, or you can take a third path that offers the best of both worlds.

Metal roofing tiles are rapidly growing in popularity across Florida. These roofs are made using stone-coated steel, which replicates the look of tiles while retaining the strength and durability of metal roofing. This is an exposed fastener metal roofing option, which comes with all of the good and the bad of these roofing systems.

If you’re partial to the durability and cost of a metal roofing system but love the look of shingle roofs, this could be the perfect compromise. While looking at the issues as a metal vs. tile roof, it’s worth considering this third option that offers the best of both worlds!

### Deciding When to Repair or Replace a Roof

As a homeowner, you’ll probably notice major signs that your roof isn’t doing well. But how do you know when to repair a roof vs. replace it? These different roofing services come with very different price tags, so it’s important to know which one you need!

We’re PITCH Roofing, and we’ve seen more than our fiar share of Florida roof repairs and replacements. Today, we’re using that experience to help you tell when it’s time to repair vs. replace your roof. Local weather conditions can do a real number on your roof both through major storms and normal wear and tear, so we’ll walk you through how you can tell what signs of damage need which specialized roofing service!
When to Repair a Roof


If you spot a problem on your roof, repairs are the best-case scenario. While there is a wide range in how much roof repairs can cost, repairs are uniformly more affordable than roof replacements. They’re also faster to implement, which means less disruption for you and your family. Now, let’s take a look at when to repair a roof instead of replacing it!
Small Section of Missing or Damaged Shingles
Damaged shingles are one of the most common roofing issues that we see. And while widespread shingle damage can be a sign that you need a new roof, small sections of damage are an indicator of when to repair a roof rather than replace it. There are many ways that your shingles could be damaged, including:

 	Shingles missing entirely
 	Cracked or curling shingles
 	Shingles with bald spots of missing granules

If you’re only seeing a handful of missing or damaged shingles, you’re looking at a fairly easy roof repair. While the cost can go up if you’re dealing with a larger area of damage, conventional wisdom is that as long as 75% or more of your shingles are undamaged, you will not need a roof replacement.
Minor Leaks
Leaks are one of the most unpredictable types of roofing damage. It’s tough to know when to repair or replace a roof based on a leak because there’s so much variety in the amount of damage to your roof that a leak implies.

For example, you could just be missing a shingle or two and some water could have intruded into your roofing system. If this happens, you’re looking at a cheap, easy roof repair. On the other hand, water damage can spread throughout your roofing system and weaken your decking, which could require a full or partial roof replacement to address.

Thankfully, there are a few ways to tell if you have a minor leak that only needs repairing. While professional roof inspections are always the gold standard, some signs that you have a minor roof leak are:

 	Uneven textures or coloring on parts of your ceiling
 	Rusted nails in your attic
 	A humid or musty smell in your attic

If your roof is actively leaking water, it’s hard to say if you’ll need a roof repair or replacement. But by calling in roofing professionals ASAP, you’ll minimize your risk of needing a new roof!
High Energy Bills
Your roof does more than just protect your home during a storm. It also acts as insulation to keep your cool air in and the hot air out. If you notice especially high energy bills in the summer, this could be an indicator that something in your roofing system isn’t performing as it should.

There can be a lot of causes for this. Your attic vents could be having problems, there could be gaps or cracks in your decking, or your roof could just need more insulation. The only way to know for sure when to repair or replace your roof is to get an expert to take a look around!
When to Replace a Roof


While there are many signs of when to repair a roof, there are just as many indicators that it’s time to start fresh with a new roofing system. No homeowner wants to hear this news, but when your roof has reached the end of its life, the best thing you can do is tear it off and protect your home with a new roof. Let’s look at some of the easiest ways to tell that your roof is due for a replacement!
Your Roof Has Gotten Old
At the end of the day, there is no cure for a roof's old age. When your roof has reached its maximum lifespan, it’s time for a replacement. Even if your roof is not showing problems yet, the system will be too weak to stand up against a hurricane or other major storms. But how do you know when your roof is at the end of its life?

Figuring out when to replace or repair a roof hinges on knowing your roof’s life expectancy. That depends on your roofing material since they all have different average lifespans:

 	Asphalt shingles: 20 years
 	Synthetic shingles: 40-50 years
 	Exposed fastener metal roofs: 20-30 years
 	Hidden fastener metal roofs: 50-70 years
 	Clay tile roofs: 50+ years
 	Concrete tile roofs: 50 years
 	Flat roofing materials: 10-20 years

Your Neighbors Are Getting New Roofs
Not sure how old your roof is? That’s not a problem for determining whether to repair or replace your roof. A good rule of thumb is that if you notice your neighbors are getting new roofs, it’s probably time to replace yours as well.

While blindly following the pack isn’t always a good idea, there is good reason to take your neighbors’ cue when it comes to replacing your roof. That’s because neighborhoods are usually built at roughly the same time and with similar materials. This means that, even decades later, your neighborhoods’ roofs are all on a similar cycle. If your neighbors’ roofs are due for replacement, then there’s every chance that yours is as well!
Moss or Algae Growth on Your Shingles
Moss and algae are not going to destroy your roof. While they can damage it over time, they’re more a symptom of a roofing system that needs replacing than a cause. That’s because most modern shingles come equipped with technology to prevent the growth of moss and algae. So if you see growth on your roof, it likely means that your shingles are nearing the end of their lifespan.

One of the most common signs of mold on a roof is dark streaks across your shingles. If algae is growing especially well on your roof, you may even see patches of green forming between and around your shingles. While you can clean your roof to get rid of the stains and vegetation, this will not change your roof’s age or delay its need for a replacement. When a roof is done, there is nothing to do but tear it off and install a new one!

While there can be signs to help guide your way, sometimes it really is difficult to tell when to repair a roof or replace it. Whether you know exactly what your roof needs or you’d like some expert insights, PITCH has your back. As a full-service roofing company, there is no roofing issue that we can’t help you with.
