### Shingle Roof Maintenance Tips for Floridians

Did you know that asphalt shingles are the most popular roofing material in Florida? While these roofs are not the best at resisting hurricane-force winds, they still go a long way in keeping your home safe from the Florida elements. But if you want to get the best possible performance out of your roof, proper shingle roof maintenance is essential.

But how are you supposed to take care of a shingle roof in Florida? As your local roofing partner, PITCH Roofing is here to answer this question and more. While it’s never too late to improve your roof, it’s best to get any repairs or maintenance done before hurricane season rolls around. With that in mind, let’s talk about how you can get your shingle roof ready for hurricane season 2025!
The Best Shingle Roof Maintenance Practices for Florida


Roofing is a lot like real estate where location is everything. How you take care of a roof that’s going to see snow is very different from how you look after a roof that will need to withstand a hurricane. That’s why we’re using our local expertise to cover the shingle roof maintenance practices that will get your roof Florida-ready!
Keep an Eye Out for Signs of Shingle Damage
One of the most important parts of shingle roof maintenance is just paying attention to your roof. While you probably know that missing shingles are a problem, there are plenty of other signs that your shingles are having trouble. Some of the signs of damaged shingles include:

 	Cracked or curling shingles
 	Finding shingle granules in your gutters or near your downspouts
 	Mold or algae staining on your roof
 	Dents or smooth patches on your shingles
 	Bubbles or blistering on your shingles

If you notice any of these issues on your roof, it’s important to reach out to experienced contractors ASAP. Some of these issues are quick, cheap roof repairs. Others may require a complete roof replacement. But regardless of which roofing service you need, it’s crucial that you get help before the next hurricane blows into town!
Maintain a Clean Roof and Clean Gutters
Some parts of shingle roof maintenance are simple, and this is one of them. If you want to keep your shingles healthy, it’s important to make sure debris doesn’t pile up on your roof. It can be easy to dismiss debris as just a few branches or leaves, but these become hot spots for pests and opportunities for water to get trapped on your roof. Either of those issues can drastically shorten the lifespan of your shingles.

It isn’t just your roof that you should keep an eye on, either. Keeping your gutters clear is essential to preventing water from getting trapped in them. The more water that gets stuck in your gutters, the more moisture you have accumulating around the edge of your roof. This can cause your shingles to age prematurely and is a common sign of roof leaks! That’s why we strongly recommend cleaning your gutters at least twice a year.
Trim Back Tree Limbs
Generally, architectural asphalt shingles are rated for winds up to 120 mph. However, this number assumes that your shingles are performing in the best possible circumstances. And if you have tree limbs hanging over your roof, then the real wind resistance of your shingles could be much lower.

That’s because, during a storm, low-hanging branches will strike your shingles. This puts your roof at a much higher risk of losing shingles than if you were just dealing with high winds. That’s why we recommend trimming branches over your roof at least once a year, ideally right before the start of hurricane season.
Take a Peak at Your Attic


Looking at your shingles isn’t the only way to tell if your roof is damaged. Another key part of shingle roof maintenance is knowing what’s going on in your attic. Oftentimes, your attic is the first place that you’ll notice signs of roof damage.

There are a few things to look out for when checking your attic for damage. The first thing you should do is take a sniff around. If things smell musty or moldy, that means water is getting into your attic, in which case you’ll want to call in roofers before the leak starts to spread.

Additionally, look for dark, wet stains in your decking and mold development. When you catch a roof leak while it’s only affecting your attic, you’re much more likely to get ahead of major damage than if you wait until water is leaking into your home!
Don’t Fall Behind on Roof Inspections
DIY shingle roof maintenance is great and can go a long way in keeping your roof safe. But at the end of the day, there is no substitute for a professional getting up on your roof and taking a look around. That’s why we strongly encourage homeowners to keep up with annual roof inspections.

There are a lot of benefits to having an experienced contractor take a look at your roof. In addition to them being more likely to find early signs of damage, many roofing warranties require you to keep up with annual inspections. If you fall behind, you could risk losing coverage when you need it most!

### How to Waterproof Your Roof in Florida

Florida’s rainy season is almost here, so there has never been a better time to waterproof your roof. In our hot, humid summers, afternoon showers are an everyday occurrence. And while your roofing materials are already capable of withstanding rain and humidity, there are some steps you can take to minimize your roof’s risk of water damage.

We’re PITCH Roofing, and as your local roofing partner, we’re here to help you protect your home. Today, that means giving you tips to get ready for summer 2025. Let’s discuss the best ways to waterproof your roof in Florida!
The Best Ways to Waterproof Your Roof in Florida


Every climate has different roofing concerns. That’s why you need advice from local experts when you’re looking to protect your roof. PITCH contractors come with years of Florida roofing experience, and these are their recommendations!
Keep Your Roof Clear of Debris
Having debris on your roof is a great way to let water into your roofing system. Branches and leaves become excellent homes for pests and algae, both of which can eat away at your shingles and lead to leaks. That’s why clearing off any tree limbs or other debris from your roof is essential, preferably as soon as you notice they’re there.

This isn’t the only step in keeping your roof clear of debris, though. Even better than cleaning your roof regularly is preventing debris from getting onto your roof. The best way to do this is to regularly trim any overhanging branches. While this won’t guarantee that your roof stays clean, it will go a long way in helping you waterproof your roof!
Upgrade Your Attic’s Insulation
Many homeowners are surprised to learn how important attic insulation is in waterproofing your roof. While insulation may make you think of energy bills, the truth is that it also goes a long way in keeping your roof dry. Over the years, temperature fluctuations in your attic can weaken your decking and even warp your roof.

At first, this may only lead to small leaks and other minor issues. Over time, however, problems with your decking can cause roof sagging and even a total roofing failure in the worst-case scenario.

With robust insulation, though, your attic will stay at a more consistent temperature. As a result, there will be no expanding and contracting process to weaken your roof decking. While your attic likely already has insulation, it could be worth checking with a roofer to see if you could benefit from additional insulation. This is a great roof upgrade to get before the summer both for its protection as well as for the money it will save you in air conditioning costs!
Avoid Roof Sealants


Every summer, we see people pushing roof sealants and other coatings for shingle roofs. While these products promise a lot, in our experience, they don’t deliver on much. While roof sealants can be a good idea for flat roofs, we generally discourage people from applying sealants to their shingle roofs.

Your asphalt roofing shingles are already made to resist water damage. And by trying to waterproof your roof with a sealant, you could actually damage it. That’s because sealants trap heat and moisture in with your shingles, so this can actually bake your shingles. This is doubled because coatings may reduce the efficacy of UV-reflective granules on your shingles, which means your roof will take on more heat.

All in all, it’s best to avoid sealants if you want to waterproof your roof. They sound good on paper, but in reality, they often cause more problems than they prevent!
Get a Roof Inspection
Unless you’re a roofing professional, it can be hard to identify the early signs of roofing problems. While you’re probably capable of identifying missing or even cracked shingles, there are other, subtler signs of wear and tear on your roof that you’ll want to stay ahead of. To keep an eye on these issues, it’s best to get annual roof inspections.

Oftentimes, the issues discovered during a roof inspection are not immediate threats to your roof. Rather, they may be early signs that your roof needs repairs. While you could wait until after the rainy season is over to get these repairs, you run the risk of a tropical storm doing damage to your roof and making a tiny problem into a major concern.

While we understand that homeowners want to keep roofing costs down, there is no better way to waterproof your roof than having a professional take a look. Oftentimes, getting a small repair today means saving yourself a lot in roofing costs down the line!

While not every idea you hear about roof waterproofing will work, there are clear roofing fundamentals you can follow to get the best performance from your roof. And with how unpredictable Florida summers can be, it’s a good idea to get ahead of the game and prepare for the worst.

### A Floridian's Guide to TPO Roofing Installation

Thermoplastic polyolefin, or TPO, is one of the best flat roofing materials in Florida. It’s resistant to water and puncture damage, and as a rubber roofing system, it’s remarkably resilient. While Florida homeowners agree that these roofs are great, some still have questions about the process of TPO roofing installation.

We’re PITCH Roofing, and as experienced Florida roofers, we’ve installed more than a few TPO roofs in our time. We understand the roof installation process inside and out, and we want to walk you through every step. Keep reading to see how we install TPO roofs and make sure your roofing system is built to last!4
TPO Roofing Installation in 7 Steps


Since rubber roofs are single-ply roofing systems, many homeowners think TPO roofing installation can be accomplished in one or two steps. But the truth is that these are complex roofs that require a lot of skill and know-how to make sure every part of the job is handled correctly.

For our purposes, we’re going to assume that there is no old roofing system to remove. With this in mind, let’s take a step-by-step look at TPO roof installation!
1. Clear the Roof Decking
Having a good foundation is everything in roofing. Before we start applying anything else, we’ll make sure your roof is clear of debris like leaves, branches, and dirt. These things can build up quickly on a roof, so we rent dumpsters to ensure that none of the mess ends up in your yard.

We’ll also repair any damage to your roof decking at this stage. Damaged decking won’t be able to support your roof, and leaving it in place will only mean a lot of headaches for you down the line. By being careful when we start the TPO roofing installation process, we make sure that your roof is set up for long-term success!
2. Install the Roof Insulation
Every roof needs good insulation. Not only does it help keep your home cool in the summer, but it also quiets the sound of rain on your roof. When you receive a PITCH Roofing estimate, we’ll go over your options for different insulation materials and help you choose one that is right for your home and your needs.
3. Rolling Out the TPO
With your insulation in place, the next step in your TPO roofing installation is to lay your roofing membrane. This step is essentially what it sounds like — taking your sheets of TPO material and rolling them across your roof. Once they’re out, we like to wait 30 minutes to allow them to flatten and settle.
4. Securing Your TPO Membrane
Once your TPO has settled, we’ll be ready to securely attach it to your roof. In Florida, your roof will have to withstand a lot of punishment. That’s why when PITCH handles your TPO roofing installation, we’ll make sure that your roofing material isn’t going anywhere.

How we attach your roof will depend on the specifics of your structure. We don’t believe in one-size-fits-all roofing, which is why we tailor our installation methods to your roof’s needs. Some of the common ways we adhere TPO roofs are:

 	Mechanical Fastening: With this technique, your TPO sheets are screwed down into your roof to adhere them to your decking. This is the quickest and least expensive option.
 	Full Adhesion: Instead of mechanically adhering your roof, this option uses a specialized adhesive to marry your membrane to your roof.

5. Adhering Your TPO Seams
On a membrane roof, having secure seams is the difference between your home being protected and it being exposed. When handling your TPO roofing installation, we’ll make sure your seams are sealed watertight. Typically we do this by using a hot-air welder to partially melt the seams and allow them to re-solidify so that they protect the most vulnerable part of your roofing system.
6. Installing Flashing
Flashing is a thin strip of metal that helps guide water off your roof and prevent it from getting where you don’t want it. Typically we install flashing around vents, skylights, and any other places we want to keep dry.

The process is more complicated than just installing the flashing, though. First we have to measure the dimensions of the areas that need flashing. We then cut the flashing to make sure it’s the perfect size for your roof. This is just another way that TPO roofing installation needs to be tailored to the specific factors of the roof!
7. Getting a Final Roof Inspection
Once your roof is finished, the final step of any TPO roof installation is to get an inspection. As local roofers, we’ll make sure that your roof has been installed according to local standards and ordinances. After a county inspector has approved your roof, the job will be done and you’ll be free to enjoy your new TPO roofing system!
FAQs About TPO Roofing Installation in Florida


Q: How much does a TPO roof installation cost?

A: Roofing prices always vary and tend to increase over time. Generally, though, TPO roofs cost $4 to $10 per square foot.

Q: Should I DIY installing my TPO roof?

A: Technically, anyone could follow these steps and install a TPO roof. Practically, though, it just isn’t that simple. Making sure your roof is correctly installed takes a professional’s skills. If you want a roof that will pass final inspection, it’s always best to leave the job in the hands of experienced contractors.

Q: Do TPO roofs need a lot of maintenance?

A: After paying for a TPO roofing installation, most Floridians are happy to hear that TPO roofs need minimal maintenance. As long as you keep your roof clean and don’t fall behind on regular roof inspections, you should be able to go a long time without needing to worry about roof repairs!

Q: Can a lot go wrong during a TPO roof installation?

A: Yes, if a roofer is inexperienced, there are many errors they could make while installing your TPO roof. Some of the most common issues we’ve heard about are failure to properly adhere the seams and not installing flashing, both of which can cause serious problems for your roof.

### How to Extend the Life of Your Roof in Florida

Everyone wants their roof to have a long life. Unfortunately, there is a lot of unreliable information out there. When trying to extend the life of your roof, you can run the risk of doing something to damage your roofing system instead of helping it. That’s why it’s essential to have reliable information from roofers near you who know your climate and local best roofing practices!

PITCH Roofing is here to make sure that you get as much life out of your roof as possible. Today, we’re giving you our tips for making your shingle roof last. Keep reading for actionable advice from local roofing experts!
5 Ways to Extend the Life of Your Roof


In general, picking quality roofers and materials is the best way to get a long life out of your roof. But once the roof is installed, there is still a lot you can do to help your roof last longer. Let’s talk about the biggest things you can do to extend the life of your roof in Florida!
Trim Overhanging Trees
Everyone loves the gorgeous plant life in Florida, but having palm fronds over your roof can pose some serious issues. Branches that fall on your roof can quickly become home for pests. And during a hurricane, high winds can whip up palm fronds and smack them against your shingles, which greatly increases the chances of your roof losing shingles during a storm.

To extend the life of your roof and prevent these issues, all you need to do is occasionally trim back any overhanging branches.We recommend that you trim your trees at least once a year, ideally right before the start of hurricane season. Depending on how fast the regrowth is, you may need to plan additional trimmings. A good rule of thumb is that if a branch is long enough that it could possibly touch your roof during a storm, it’s time for a trim!
Keep Your Gutters Clean and Clear
In theory, your gutters exist to help protect your home’s foundation. But without proper gutter maintenance, they could actually end up endangering your roof. That’s because blocked gutters will retain water, which can lead to water pooling on your roof. A good rule of thumb is the more moisture on your roof, the greater the chances that it’s going to develop a problem.

That’s why it’s essential to make sure your gutters are functional if you want to extend the life of your roof. Conventional wisdom is to clean your gutters twice a year. However, you can reduce this down to once a year if you have gutter guards installed.

Additionally, you should make sure that water is coming out of your downspouts. If it isn’t, then there may be a hole in your gutters or another issue that’s preventing them from working properly. If you suspect that there is a problem with your gutters beyond them needing cleaning, reach out to professional roofers who can take a look and get your gutters back in working order again.
Don’t Apply Sealant to Your Shingles
When you ask someone how to extend the life of your roof, they might suggest a roof sealant or coating. While these people usually mean well, this is not great advice. While sealants can do great things for some roofs, they aren’t usually the right call for asphalt shingles.

Your shingles are already designed to deal with high winds, water, and UV rays. But by covering them in sealant, you can accidentally weaken your shingles. For example, some coatings trap heat inside, which can effectively bake your shingles under the hot sun. This actually makes it more likely for your shingles to fail than if you’d never applied anything to them.

That’s why most shingle warranties will be voided by applying sealants or other coatings. While it’s natural to want to extend the life of your roof, messing with your roofing material isn’t usually a good way to go about it. Before applying any kind of sealant, always make sure to consult with a reputable roofer who is familiar with your roof’s warranties!
Keep Your Roof Clean


Oftentimes, the best thing you can do to extend the life of your roof in Florida is just keep it clean. Over time, a lot of things can accumulate on your roof — debris, mold, and algae are just a few. If you notice leaves, branches, or staining on your roof, it’s time to get it cleaned.

Whether you clean your roof yourself or hire someone for the job, it’s important to make sure there’s no buildup or debris left on your roof. Mold and algae spread over time, so a full, deep cleaning is the best way to prevent them from eating away at your shingles!
Don’t Pressure Wash Your Roof
This is another piece of advice that isn’t going to do much to extend the life of your roof. In fact, using a pressure washer on your roof can blow your shingles clean off. Even if your shingles stay in place, they will likely lose granules, which makes them more vulnerable to impact damage and UV rays.

While it’s important to keep your roof clean, a power washer is not the way to do it. If you don’t want to use a professional roof cleaning service, then you’ll need to clean your roof with a gentle brush and a mild cleaner. This isn’t as fast as power washing your roof, but it’s much more likely to make your roof last longer!
Let PITCH Help You Extend the Life of Your Roof
As a homeowner, there is a lot you can do to help your roof last longer. But sooner or later, every roof needs professional help. There is no amount of preparation that can make your roof immune to hurricanes or everyday wear and tear, which is why it’s important to have roofers you can trust in your back pocket.

### Deciding if Galvanized Steel Roofing Is Right for Your Home or Business

With hurricane season just around the corner, lots of Florida homeowners are looking for ways to get their homes hurricane-ready. Naturally, upgrading to metal roofing is one of the most popular ways to prepare Florida homes for storm-force winds. But is galvanized steel roofing the right type of metal roofing for your home?

We’re PITCH Roofing, and as your local metal roofers, we’ve seen firsthand what a great job galvanized steel can do in keeping your home safe and protected. At the same time, we know that no type of metal roofing is right for everyone. So whether you’re looking for the basics or insider industry knowledge, we’re covering everything you need to know about galvanized steel roofing!
What Is Galvanized Steel Roofing?


Before we delve into figuring out the right type of metal roof for your home, we first need to establish what galvanized steel is. As the name implies, this material starts with steel metal roofing sheets. This alone creates a strong, solid base for your roof. But the galvanization process is what makes these roofs viable in Florida.

If you’ve lived through a Florida summer, you know how wet and humid the weather can get. Normally, that humidity would cause steel to start rusting almost immediately. As you might imagine, a rusting roof is a major problem in any situation. This is not an issue for galvanized steel roofing, though, because the roofing panels get a coating of zinc to protect them against the Florida elements.

Zinc is a fascinating metal that’s commonly used to prevent rust on various metals. What sets zinc apart is that it isn’t just rust-resistant. Rather, zinc “self heals” by shedding parts of itself that begin to rust. In this way, it prevents damage from spreading throughout your roofing system!

This covers the fundamentals of what galvanized steel roofing is. But why is it so popular among Florida homeowners?
How Galvanized Steel Roofing Performs in Florida
In Florida, there are a lot of natural weather phenomena that can damage your roof, even if you invest in a metal roofing system. Hurricane-force winds, humidity, and UV rays all pose serious threats to your roof. So how does galvanized steel roofing hold up against these roof killers?

When it comes to wind resistance, how you install your metal roof matters. No matter which style you pick, though, you can count on a galvanized steel roof to stay in place even through major hurricanes. With standing seam metal roofing you can expect wind resistance up to 180 mph, which is all but impossible to beat. While 5V metal roofing has slightly lower numbers, wind resistance up to 150 mph is more than enough to keep your home safe during hurricane season.

As we’ve established, galvanized steel has great rust resistance. However, this doesn’t mean it’s right for all parts of Florida. Coastal Florida, for example, has unique roofing needs due to the saltwater air, which can rust through the protective coating on a galvanized steel roof. For this reason, we tend to recommend aluminum roofing if you live within a mile of the coastline.

Finally, the sun’s UV rays are a serious roofing concern. Thankfully, galvanized steel is capable of reflecting a lot of those UV rays away from your home. This has two crucial benefits. First, your roof experiences less wear and tear, which leads to a longer lifespan. As an added bonus, you can also expect a lower electricity bill since it will be easier for your attic to release hot air, which improves ventilation and means your AC system won’t have to work as hard.
Alternative Metal Roofing Options in Florida


While galvanized steel roofing has a lot to offer, it isn’t right for every situation or homeowner. As we mentioned, we don’t usually recommend galvanized steel if you live near the coasts, as saltwater in the air can cause your roof to corrode. There are other situations where you may want to choose another type of metal as well.

For example, if you want a roof that will last for a long time, galvanized steel may not be the right fit. In Florida, galvanized steel tends to last about 20 years before it begins to rust. Most homeowners looking to invest in a metal roof want better durability, which is why many turn to galvalume steel instead. With a protective coating of aluminum and zinc, galvalume offers better rust resistance than galvanized steel, even though they come at similar price points.

Additionally, galvanized steel does not usually come with a substrate warranty. A substrate warranty is a guarantee that your roofing material will not fail due to rust or corrosion. Other materials, including galvalume, usually carry these warranties for decades, so galvanized steel roofing is not the best option for long-term protection. Nobody can guarantee what will happen in the future, and having strong warranties is a good way to be ready for anything!
Get a Free Metal Roofing Estimate

### Are Plastic Roof Tiles a Good Idea for Florida?

When you first think of plastic roof tiles, the image in your head may be less than flattering. For many people, plastic products are synonymous with cheap, poorly made items that are made to go into a landfill. Naturally, few homeowners want something cheap or poorly made on their roofs. But plastic roof tiles have more to offer than you might expect.

We should know — PITCH Roofing is made up of contractors with decades of local roofing experience. In our time, we’ve installed plenty of plastic shingle roofs and seen them stand up wonderfully against hurricanes and other Florida roof killers. Don’t just take our word for it, though. Let’s talk about everything you need to know about plastic roof tiles before planning your roof replacement!
What Are Plastic Roof Tiles?


While the idea of a plastic roof may not be appealing, the reality has a lot to offer. Also called composite or synthetic shingles, these roofing materials are made via specialized protective polymers and recycled plastics. As a result, your roofing system is both lightweight and durable, which is an excellent combination.

Everyday plastic may be flimsy, but plastic roof tiles are anything but. In fact, these hardy tiles have a Class 4 impact rating. This means that you can count on your synthetic shingles to stay strong in the face of hail and even storm debris! And with wind resistance up to 130 mph, it would take a direct hit from a major hurricane to make these tiles budge.

This covers the basics of how these roofs perform, but what about how they look? Good news — if you want a roof that will generate curb appeal, few options can compete with plastic roof tiles. That’s because composite shingles don’t actually look like traditional asphalt shingles. Instead, they imitate the looks of wood shake or slate tiles. In this way, you can get the aesthetic of a luxury roofing material without paying a luxury price tag!

The best part of synthetic shingles might be their longevity. Old-school asphalt shingles would be lucky to last 20 years in Florida. On the other hand, plastic roof tiles last for 40-50 years on average. This means that you’re getting twice the life of the most common roofing material in Florida! Not bad for plastic, right?
Do Plastic Shingles Perform Well in Florida?
In roofing, location is everything. A roof that can stand up against ice and snow could be completely unprepared for a hurricane, and vice versa. That’s why it’s always best to have local roofers working on your roofing project. With this in mind, how do plastic roof tiles hold up to the infamous Florida elements?

We’re happy to report that, on the whole, plastic shingles do a great job in Florida. Their wind resistance is perfect for protecting your property during hurricane season, for one thing. And because they’re made of inorganic materials, plastic roof tiles are not naturally welcoming to algae or mold. Not only does this mean your roof will stay pristine, but you’ll also enjoy reduced maintenance since mold will not be prone to developing on your roof!

Water resistance is another concern, especially in Florida’s rainy season. But again, composite shingles are more than up to the challenge. Water has no way to easily penetrate their hardened plastic, and when properly installed, these tiles create an excellent water-resistant barrier on top of your home. While roof leaks can happen with any material that is damaged, plastic roof tiles are at no additional risk of developing water damage.

So far we’ve covered a lot of great things about plastic shingles and their performance in Florida. But what’s the downside?
Downsides to Composite Shingles in Florida


No roofing material is perfect, and plastic roof tiles are no exception to this rule. The good news, however, is that the “downsides” to composite shingles are pretty minor. Especially if you’re comparing them to the many strengths of these roofing materials! But what are these negatives, anyway?

Well, one potential con of composite shingles is that they’re pretty new to the roofing scene. Plastic roof tiles first started gaining popularity around the year 2000. This means that, while we’re confident these shingles will last for 30 to 50 years, nobody knows for sure. Additionally, there is a chance that they could develop a serious issue as they age that nobody has experienced yet because their roofs are simply too young.

While this is certainly a risk that you should be aware of before getting your roof replaced, it’s also not likely to present a problem. Manufacturers do a lot of research when making their products, and so far they have no reason to suspect that these tiles won’t age well. Moreover, almost all manufacturers offer limited lifetime warranties on their plastic roof tiles, so if there is an issue due to a failure in your roofing material, you’ll be covered whether the problem arises in 10 years or 40.

Otherwise, it’s hard to see many drawbacks to plastic shingles. While they don’t resell for quite as much as real slate or cedar shake roofs, they also cost substantially less, so that’s hardly a con. If you’re this far in and still interested in plastic roof tiles, the only potential hurdle to choosing them could be the price tag.
How Much Do Plastic Roof Tiles Cost in Florida?
Giving roof pricing guidelines is always tricky. Material costs are always in flux, for one thing, not to mention how heavily your roof’s size and dimensions will influence your total roof replacement costs. Still, we can give you a rough outline for how much plastic roof tiles cost in Florida as of 2025.

In general, synthetic shingles are a middle-of-the-road option in terms of price. They are not the most affordable roofing material, but they’re also a far cry from the most expensive. In 2025, we’re seeing plastic roof tiles cost between $7 and $14 per square foot. If your roof is around the average size of 1,700 square feet, and without accounting for unique roofing factors, you’re looking at roof replacement costs of $11,900 to $23,800.

While plastic roof tiles have many great things to offer, we understand that their price means they simply aren’t an option for everyone. If they’re in your budget, though, then these shingles are seriously worth considering!

### Is Reroofing Over Old Shingles Safe in Florida?

With Florida weather being what it is, it’s never a good idea to leave your roof unprotected. This means that if you start noticing signs of old age on your shingle roof, you’re going to need some new protection. Contrary to popular belief, however, this doesn’t always mean tearing off and replacing your shingles. Sometimes, roofing over old shingles can be the best way to protect your home and save money.

We should know — PITCH Roofing is made up of veteran Florida roofers who come with years of experience protecting local homes and businesses against the worst that our local weather patterns have to offer. Today, we’re sharing everything you need to know about roofing over old shingles and when it may be an option for you!
Is Roofing Over Old Shingles a Good Idea in Florida?


When your roof has reached the end of its lifespan, there will be several signs that show it. These include things like finding granules in your gutters, missing or curling shingles, and dark streaks on your roof. Any combination of these issues means that more likely than not, your current roof cannot protect your home against a severe storm. But is roofing over old shingles really a viable option?

In many cases, yes. This process is called reroofing, and it’s essentially a roof replacement where nobody removes your old roof before installing the new one. This means that contractors will install a new layer of shingles over your old shingles, which is a secure and reliable method of protecting your home against high winds and other roofing hazards.

While roofing over old shingles is perfectly safe, it’s not for every person or every roof. On the other hand, in some respects reroofing has several advantages over a traditional roof replacement. To find out if reroofing is right for your situation, it’s important to look at the pros and cons of this new roof installation technique.
Reroofing Pros and Cons
No matter what type of roof you get or how it’s installed, there will always be pros and cons to your choice. And roofing over old shingles is no different. Let’s discuss the pros and cons so you can make the right plans for your new roof!
Pro: Roofing Over Old Shingles Is Cheaper Than Replacing
If you’re worried about being able to afford a roof replacement, reroofing could be the perfect solution. It’s cheaper than replacing your roof for a number of reasons, including lower labor costs because contractors don’t have to tear off your old roof, which saves time. Additionally, you save money on renting a dumpster since nobody is tearing off your old shingles.

Since roofing over old shingles requires less labor than replacing a roof, you can expect it to cost substantially less. Exact numbers will vary, but you could save as much as 30% on your new roof by installing it over your old one!
Con: Reroofing Doesn’t Last as Long
While roofing over old shingles is cheaper than replacing them, it doesn’t result in a higher-quality roof. In fact, because you don’t have the same solid plywood base that you do with a roof replacement, your new roof will not last as long as you might expect.

That’s because, even under your new layer of shingles, your old shingle roof continues to age. As the shingles continue to break down, your new roof will become destabilized. If you start to notice sections of shingles coming lose, it means your new roof has lasted as long as it can on top of your old one.

With a roof replacement, newly installed architectural shingles can last for 20-25 years. When you choose reroofing, though, you’re looking at a life expectancy of around 15 years or so. This isn’t always a dealbreaker, but it’s very important you know how much life you’ll get out of your new roof before signing any contracts!
Pro: Reroofing Is Faster and More Convenient
Since roofing over old shingles skips the tear-off step of a roof replacement, it’s appreciably faster than replacing your roof. With a roof replacement, contractors will tear off your old shingles and then inspect your roof decking to see if they need to replace sections of that as well. Because reroofing skips all of this work, it’s much faster than installing a new roof from scratch.

As an added bonus, reroofing creates less of a mess than replacing your roof. After a roof replacement, it’s common to find nails and even shingles in your yard if your roofers haven’t cleaned up well. But since no shingles have to be torn from your roof, there is minimal risk of debris being left on your property after the job is finished.
Con: Roofing Over Old Shingles Is Not Always an Option


While roofing over old shingles is faster and more convenient than replacing a roof, it isn’t always an option. That’s because with reroofing, nobody can access your roof decking. So if there is a problem with your decking, which forms the foundation of your roof, then your contractors won’t be able to address it. And putting another layer of roofing over damaged decking could jeopardize the structural safety of your home.

That’s why experienced contractors will carefully inspect your roof before agreeing to reroof it. Signs of damaged roof decking include leaks, ceiling stains, and moisture building up in your attic. If there is any doubt as to the stability of your decking, it’s a good idea to get a roof replacement instead. The last thing you want is to pay for a new roof that is in danger of collapsing in a few years!
Get a Free Roof Replacement or Reroofing Estimate
Roofing over old shingles comes with noteworthy pros, but the drawbacks are just as considerable. In many cases, homeowners lose interest in reroofing once they know the downsides. But whether you want to install a new roof over your old shingles or start from scratch, PITCH Roofing is here to make sure you get top-quality roofing services from local professionals.

For a free, no-obligation roofing estimate, call us at (727) 677-4824 or schedule your estimate online. We’ll be happy to provide a thorough estimate that we tailor to your roof and your needs. Whether you’re roofing over old shingles or replacing an entire roof, getting a new roof is a big decision. No matter what method you prefer, the crew at PITCH is ready to help. Reach out to us today, and we’ll earn your business through our friendly, clear approach to customer service and our commitment to roofing done right!

### Pros and Cons of Black Shingle Roofs in Florida

For many years, browns were the go-to shingle color because people wanted their asphalt shingles to look like wooden shingles. Nowadays, though, there are virtually unlimited color options. In recent years, we’ve noticed a sizable uptick in interest in black shingles across Florida.

But are these a good fit for the Florida environment? We’re PITCH Roofing, and we’re here to look at the good and the bad of black roofing shingles to help you plan your next roof replacement. Let’s talk about the must-know information that will make sure you get the right roof for your Florida home!
Pros of Black Shingles for Florida Homes


While black shingles are perhaps not the most traditional choice, there’s no denying that they offer unique benefits to Florida homeowners. To see if these are the right fit for your home, let’s talk about some of the advantages of choosing black roofing shingles.
A Modern Look
Asphalt shingles are the most popular roof in North America. This means that your neighbors will likely have shingle roofs, although most likely in neutral tones of brown or grey. As a result, getting a black shingle roof is a way to stand out and differentiate your home without paying top dollar for metal or tile roof replacements.

A black roof offers a very modern aesthetic that is starkly different from the cozy, homey colors that shingles usually come in. This is a great way to boost curb appeal without paying extra for your new roof. When you invest in black architectural asphalt shingles, you can count on getting a roof that will generate plenty of visual interest!
Aesthetic Flexibility
As a homeowner, it can be challenging to identify the right color for your roof. This can be especially troubling with shingle roofs, which come in a nearly unlimited variety of colors. But with black shingles, you can take the guesswork out of your roof replacement and feel confident that your new roof will suit the overall look of your home.

The adage that black goes with everything definitely holds true in roofing. On some homes, a black roof is dramatic, while it can look completely natural on others. But no matter what color your home is, there’s a very high chance that a black roof will complement the aesthetic and contribute to increased curb appeal.
Cons of Black Shingles for Florida Homes


While there are great things about black shingles, they are far from a perfect roofing material, especially in Florida. And when picking something as important as your new roof’s color, it’s important to be aware of the bad as well as the good. Let’s talk about the biggest downsides to getting a black shingle roof replacement in Florida!
Higher Energy Bills
If you’ve heard that black materials attract more heat, you probably won’t be surprised that the same rule applies with roof shingles. Since black absorbs more light than other colors, it also takes on more heat. This means that your home may have a harder time releasing hot air through your attic, which in turn means your AC system has to work harder.

While it's true that black shingles come with higher energy bills, the difference is not night and day. Your energy bill will not suddenly double if you get back roofing shingles. However, you can expect to have higher energy bills over the course of your roof’s life, especially during the summer months.
Premature Aging
When people think of Florida roof killers, hurricanes are usually the first thing that comes to mind. And while tropical storms pose a real danger to every roof in Florida, they’re not the only threat to your roof. In Florida, extreme exposure to UV rays does as much to damage roofs as any tropical storm.

Since black shingles absorb more light, they also attract more UV rays. This can lead to your shingles drying out and cracking early. Generally, you’ll know your shingles are nearing the end of their lifespan when you start finding stone granules in your gutters. And while asphalt shingles last for 20-25 years in Florida, black shingles have lifespans closer to 15-20 years due to their increased risk of UV damage.
Higher Risk of Mold Development
Mold is another serious risk for roofs in Florida. Mold and algae can grow on roofs with damaged shingles, especially in the rainy season when things are warm and wet. Over time, that mold eats away at your shingles and can lead to widespread roofing issues including missing sections of shingles and roof leaks.

Because black shingles attract more heat than other colors, they’re an even more appealing home for mold and algae. The good news is that some shingles come with anti-mold protection, like slow-release zinc deposits that kill anything growing on your shingle. That’s why you’ll want to discuss this with your roofing contractor before they order your shingles!

### The Good and Bad of Black Metal Roofs in Florida

Metal roofing is experiencing a renaissance in Florida. As homeowners gear up for more active hurricane seasons, they’re choosing to upgrade their homes’ protections via metal roof replacements. While many homeowners love the protection of metal roofing, though, not everyone loves the look. This is where interest in getting a black metal roof usually stems from.

We’re PITCH Roofing, and our roofing contractors have been installing metal roofs across Florida for years. We’ve noticed an uptick in interest in black metal roofs, so we want to give you the good and the bad so that there are no nasty surprises after your roof replacement. Keep reading for our complete guide to getting a black metal roof in Florida!
Pros of Getting a Black Metal Roof in Florida


The Florida elements are harsh on any roof, even metal ones. Thankfully, metal roofs are generally able to withstand the worst that the Sunshine State has to offer. In most cases, this even includes black metal roofs. To show you what we mean, let’s talk about all the advantages that come with having a darker metal roof!
A Modern, Homey Aesthetic
One of the biggest hurdles preventing homeowners from getting a metal roof is the “industrial” look. But with a black metal roof, you don’t have to worry about this. Whether you decide to get a painted standing seam roof or a black stone-coated steel roof, the end result is a roofing system that suits your home and neighborhood.

Black famously goes with everything, and this is also true in roofing. In this way, a black metal roof is one of the most aesthetically versatile roofs you can get. When you combine the traditional protection of metal roofing with a modern aesthetic that generates curb appeal, it’s hard to say no to this innovative style of roofing!
Hides Oil Canning
Standing seam metal roofs have a lot to love. One downside of this type of metal roof, however, is that it can develop oil canning. Over time, your roof can develop a kind of waviness that distorts the sleek, smooth finish that homeowners have come to expect from a standing seam metal roofing system.

While oil canning is not a structural concern, it can be unsightly. Thankfully, it isn’t a problem when you choose a black metal roof. The black paint covers the worst effects of oil canning, making it much harder to see. This is especially effective if you choose a matte or low-gloss roof color since the reduced light reflection helps hide any perceived waviness.
Covers Imperfections
It’s no secret that metal roofs are durable. However, they’re not completely invulnerable. Over time, it’s not uncommon for a metal roof to take on dents and scrapes. While these rarely pose any real danger to your roof, they can disrupt the sleek, smooth look of metal roofing.

With a black metal roof, many of these imperfections can be hidden under paint. While you still need to keep up with proper metal roof maintenance and regular cleanings, minor imperfections should be less visible than on a silver metal roof. This can go a long way in helping your roof retain its curb appeal as it ages!
Cons of Getting a Black Metal Roof in Florida


While there are a lot of advantages to getting a black metal roof, there are downsides as well. When planning something as important as a roof replacement, it’s important to ensure you’re aware of both the advantages and disadvantages of your choice. With that in mind, let’s look at the downsides of a black metal roof that may give you pause!
Reduced Solar Reflection
Generally speaking, metal roofs are pretty good at deflecting UV rays away from your home. However, this strength is reduced with a black metal roof. Because black absorbs more light and heat than other colors, your roof will be more prone to attracting UV rays than reflecting them like other metal roofs.

As a result, your home may experience difficulties dispersing this extra heat. Often, this means a higher energy bill as your AC system works harder to compensate for the additional heat. While this likely won’t double your energy bill or anything that drastic, you can expect your energy bill to be higher if you have a black metal roof when compared to a silver-colored one.
Trouble Color Matching
While black goes with nearly any color, it can be hard to match a black metal roof with other shades of black. For example, many homeowners choose to get a black roof trim. With a black metal roof, there is a chance that these will be slightly different shades of black, which can be a problem if you want a cohesive, homogenous look.

In the vast majority of cases, the difference in coloring will be negligible. However, this is the kind of thing that homeowners should be aware of before having roofers order materials for their new roofing system. Talk to your roofers about any shade-matching concerns to ensure they work with you to find black materials that work well together!

If you need a roof replacement but don't have the funds readily available, you're not alone. What Is Roof Financing?


Technically, roof financing is whatever way you pay for a new roof. But in the context of financing vs. home equity loans, “roof financing” refers specifically to getting a pre-approved loan through your roofing company of choice.

In terms of convenience, it’s hard to beat roof financing. Usually, this option is first discussed during the process of paying your roof estimate. When a PITCH roofing professional comes to your home, they’ll mention that we offer financing to our costumes and ask if you’re interested in exploring your options.

From there, the process is easy. Our roof financing has minimal credit requirements, so most homeowners can expect approval for this loan. As a bonus, PITCH Roofing financing has many great features, including:

 	No interest and no mandatory payments for the first year
 	Low-interest roof financing after the first year
 	No upfront payment required for most plans
 	Quick processing so your roof replacement isn’t delayed

Clearly, there is a lot of good that comes with roof financing through PITCH Roofing. But what about home equity loans? This is a very different roof financing option that comes with its own advantages and challenges!
What Is a Home Equity Loan?
Financing through a roofing company is a fantastic option, but choosing financing vs. home equity loans is still a tough decision because these loans have their own pros. For one thing, a home equity loan has some of the lowest interest rates on the market. So if you’re someone who is committed to getting the best rate, this could be the perfect loan for you!

But why do home equity loans come with such good rates? That’s because, unlike other loans, home equity loans are taken out by using equity in your home as collateral. This gives the lender assurance that their money is safe, so they’re more willing to offer better rates.

There are some caveats to this, though. To get the best rates, you’ll need a credit score of at least 660, although 750 or higher is preferable. You also may not qualify for a home equity loan depending on your income, income history, and debt-to-income ratio. For homeowners who qualify, though, a home equity loan can be a great way to pay for a new roof.
Deciding Between Roof Financing vs. a Home Equity Loan


Choosing between financing vs. a home equity loan is a very personal choice. Neither of these options is better than the other; instead, each choice comes with its own pros and cons. So how do you know which method of paying for a new roof is right for you?

If you have less-than-perfect credit, financing through your roofing company is often the way to go. When you choose PITCH, you can still get low-interest roof financing, even if the rates are not as low as those of a home equity loan. Additionally, it’s much faster and easier to get approved for these loans, so they’re ideal for anyone on a time crunch or who otherwise wouldn’t qualify for a home equity loan.

Alternatively, a home equity loan is ideal for Florida homeowners with good credit and a fair amount of equity in their homes already. Provided you meet all the high requirements for these loans, there is no better way to get rates these low. While most home equity loans don’t offer 0% roof financing for the first year like PITCH does, these loans do offer lower interest rates when compared to PITCH loans after the first year.

All in all, there are good reasons to choose both of these roof financing options. When deciding between traditional roof financing vs. home equity loans, it’s important to look at your own situation and see which is best for you. And if you’re still unsure, the pro roofers at PITCH will be happy to help you weigh your options!

### New Roof Financing Options Near You

In our experience, roofing problems rarely come at a convenient time. More often, they pop up unexpectedly, and it’s up to the homeowners to find a solution. That solution needs to be timely, too, given the risks of having a damaged or old roof during hurricane season. This is why more and more Floridians are looking into their new roof financing options.

Should You Get New Roof Financing?


Financing a new roof can be a tricky subject. On the one hand, it is usually cheaper to pay out of pocket. That’s because roof financing often comes with fees and varying interest rates that will increase the overall cost of your roof replacement. So if you want the cheapest possible roof replacement, roof financing might not be for you.

Of course, the problem with that is that not everyone has the money to cover a new roof. That’s not surprising, given that the average cost of a roof replacement in Florida is around $13,000. And while it can be tempting to wait and save up money for a new roof, that isn’t usually a good idea. When you need a new roof, it’s important to act quickly before any weakness in your roof leads to long-term structural damage.

This is why new roof financing is so often necessary. While it’s cheaper to pay for a roof out of pocket, that simply isn’t an option for many homeowners. That said, you can still save yourself money with new roof financing. The important thing is to find the right financing program for your situation.

To help you find the best new roof financing program for your roof replacement, let’s discuss your options!
New Roof Financing Options in Florida
The good news is that no matter what your financial situation, there are many options available to pay for your new roof. And which one is best for you will depend on a variety of factors. Let’s look at each option to determine which new roof financing plan is right for you!
Financing Through Your Roofing Company
Oftentimes, the easiest thing for a homeowner to do is finance their new roof via their chosen roofing company. And if you pick the right roofers, this could easily be your best option.  	0% interest for the first 12 months of your loan
 	Low interest rates after the initial 0% interest period
 	Flexible repayment schedules

HELOC Roof Financing


A home equity line of credit (HELOC) is another great way to pay for a new roof. These loans work by borrowing against the equity you have in your home. For this reason, they offer extremely low rates that can be a great option for many homeowners.

They aren’t for every homeowner, though. For one thing, you need to have enough equity in your home to cover your roof replacement. And compared to other new roof financing options, HELOCs have much higher credit requirements. To get the best rates, you’ll need to have a credit score of at least 680, although borrowers with credit scores of 780 or higher have the best chances of being approved for a low-interest loan.
Personal Loans
If all else fails, one new roof financing option is to take out a personal loan from your bank. This can be an option for homeowners who don’t qualify for a HELOC and have chosen a roofing company that doesn’t offer financing. While this type of loan is easier to access, though, we don’t generally recommend it for financing a roof replacement.

That’s because personal loans tend to have higher interest rates. This is especially true if your credit is anything less than stellar. While financing through your roofers often has better terms than a personal loan, this can still be a viable option in select circumstances.
Credit Card Roof Financing
In some ways, a credit card is the most convenient way to pay for a new roof. If you already have a credit card, then there’s no application process, which means no application fees and no risk of being denied. And there is nothing stopping you from paying for your roof replacement via your credit card.

We don’t generally recommend credit cards for new roof financing, though. That’s because credit cards tend to have the highest APRs of all your financing options. While they’re convenient to use, you’ll end up paying more in the long run. This is doubly true because most roofers charge an extra fee to pay via credit card to cover the costs of accepting the card. 3% may not sound like much, but when talking about a $13,000 roof, that’s hundreds of dollars in extra fees before you’ve even started paying off the roof!

### What Is the Best Roofing Material for Floridians?

If you’re looking to replace your roof in 2025, then you’ve come to the right place. As dedicated local roofers, PITCH Roofing has the skilled crew and the know-how to get you the perfect roof for your home or commercial structure. And all of that starts with identifying the best roofing material for your property.

Whether you’re concerned about durability, longevity, aesthetics, or cost, we’re here to help you find the best roofing material for your Florida property. Let’s take a look at the different options on the market to help you plan your next roof replacement!
The Best Roofing Materials for Florida


In Florida, there are more than a few roofing options available to you. No matter what your budget is, you’ll find that you have several options to choose from. And with something as important as your roof, it’s important that you choose the right material!

As Floridians, we need our roofs to stand up to humidity, UV rays, and even hurricanes. That’s a lot to ask from a roof! In our experience as veteran Florida roofing contractors, we’ve found that there are three primary categories of roofing materials that homeowners can rely on:

 	Shingle roofing
 	Tile roofing
 	Metal roofing

Contrary to popular belief, there is no objective “best” roofing material for Florida homes and commercial properties. Instead, each roof has its own pros and cons for you to weigh. To make sure you’re getting the full picture, we’re going to look at the good and the bad of each of these roofing materials, as well as your options within each category!
Shingle Roofs in Florida
In Florida, there are two main types of roofing shingles: asphalt and synthetic. While these are both shingle roofs, they offer widely different benefits and have starkly contrasting cons. Let’s take a look at them individually to get a better idea of what sets these shingles apart!
Asphalt Roofing Shingles
Asphalt shingles are the most common roofing material in North America, and the one you’re probably most familiar with. Made by coating a fiberglass baseboard in hot asphalt and topping it with stone granules, these shingles have been a staple roofing material for over a century.

In Florida, architectural shingles are one of the best roofing materials on the market. These shingles are thick and resilient, which makes them a great choice for withstanding Florida’s destructive weather patterns. Now it’s time to take a look at the good and bad of architectural asphalt shingles!

Pros:

 	Low Cost: Architectural shingles are popular in part because of their low roofing costs. Cheap to manufacture and quick to install, asphalt shingles are the go-to option for an affordable roof replacement that doesn’t sacrifice quality.
 	Color Options: Asphalt shingles come in nearly any color you can imagine, so there will always be an option to suit your style and tastes.
 	Visual Interest: Architectural shingles have a unique multi-dimensional pattern that creates visual interest on your roof and increases curb appeal.
 	Durability: Architectural shingles can withstand heavy rains and extreme UV exposure without issue.

Cons:

 	Vulnerable to High Winds: Architectural shingles are rated for winds up to 120 mph, which isn’t bad, but Floridians do see winds higher than this during hurricanes. After a major storm, it’s not uncommon to see shingles in your yard, especially as your roof gets older.
 	Maintenance: Asphalt shingle roofs require regular maintenance to stay ahead of roofing problems and keep your structure protected.
 	Lifespan: Architectural shingles last 20-25 years in Florida, which isn’t a short amount of time but is noticeably shorter than some other roofing materials.

Cost:

Architectural shingles cost between $5 and $9 per square foot on average.
Synthetic Roofing Shingles
Synthetic (or composite) shingles are made from specialized polymers and recycled materials. A newcomer on the scene, these first hit the market around the year 2000. And ever since, they’ve been growing in popularity across North America and in Florida especially.

What makes synthetic shingles stand out is their looks. These shingles are specially crafted to replicate the look of cedar shake or slate tiles. At a fraction of the cost, these are one of the best roofing materials for homeowners who want a luxury roof without the luxury price tag. Let’s take a look at the good and the bad to see if these are the right fit for you!

Pros:

 	Resilience: Synthetic shingles have great resistance to water, wind, and UV rays, which makes them an excellent choice for getting your property hurricane-ready.
 	Longevity: Composite shingles are projected to last for around 50 years in Florida.
 	Great Aesthetics: With the look of slate or cedar shake, synthetic shingles emulate the looks of luxury roofing materials at a fraction of the cost.
 	Eco-Friendly: Since they’re made from recycled materials, synthetic shingles are a great way to re-use old plastics for a great cause.

Cons:

 	Pricey: While synthetic shingles are much cheaper than cedar shake or slate, they are not a cheap roofing material and cost much more than more budget-friendly options like asphalt shingles.
 	New: Since synthetic shingles have only been widely used since the year 2000, nobody is completely sure of how they will age. Experts have no reason to suspect that there will be a problem as these roofs get older, but there is some level of risk that an unpleasant defect will be found in these shingles.

Cost:

Synthetic shingles cost $7 to $12 per square foot.
Tile Roofs in Florida


Florida is well-known for its love of tile roofing. In fact, Florida was one of the first places in North America to have tile roofs imported from Spain. While tiles are certainly a popular option, whether they’re the best roofing material for Florida depends on who you ask. Let’s look at the two most popular tile roofing materials to help you decide if a tile roof is a good fit!
Clay Roofing Tiles
Clay tiles are a classic roofing material made from natural, heat-treated clay. But are they the best roofing material for Florida? Well, they’re certainly among the most durable. And with gorgeous, timeless aesthetics, these tiles can go a long way in adding value to your home.

Now, it’s time to look at the good and the bad of clay tile roofing in Florida!

Pros:

 	Long Lifespans: Clay tiles can last for anywhere from 50 to 100+ years in Florida, making them one of the longest-lasting materials on the market.
 	Variety of Styles: Clay tiles come in a wide range of colors and styles, which allows you to customize your roof.
 	Florida Ready: With high wind resistance, it’s very unlikely that storm-force winds will be able to move your clay roofing tiles.

Cons:

 	High Cost: Clay tiles are a luxury roofing material. This means they’re quite expensive. However, many homeowners feel that they’re worth the initial up-front investment.
 	Underlayment Life Expectancy: A clay tile roof can last for a century or more, but your underlayment is still only going to last for 20 years or so. This means that after 20 years, your roof will need to be removed and re-installed so that roofers can replace your underlayment.

Cost:

Clay roofing tiles cost between $12 and $21 per square foot.
Concrete Roofing Tiles
While clay tiles are the classic option, concrete tiles are a modern, more affordable alternative. Whereas clay tiles get their color from the clay they’re made of, concrete tiles are painted before being installed. This allows you to enjoy the same look as clay roofing tiles without the same intimidating price tag.

To see if these are the best roofing material for your home, let’s discuss the pros and cons of concrete tiles.

Pros:

 	Low Price: Concrete roofing tiles are not cheap. But compared to clay roofing tiles, they are much more affordable and accessible!
 	Versatile: Like clay tiles, concrete roofing tiles come in a wide array of colors and styles. In fact, they come with even more color options since they’re painted instead of relying on natural coloring.
 	Durable: Concrete tiles are every bit as durable as clay tiles. In fact, they’re even heavier, which means it would take a major hurricane to move your tiles after they’ve been installed.
 	Long-Lasting: Concrete tile roofs last for about 50 years in Florida. This is less than clay tile roofs, but still a good, long lifespan for a roof!

Cons:

Bleaching: Over time (usually decades), UV rays can break down the pigment in your tiles’ paint. This can lead to bleaching, which will require re-painting to restore your tiles to their original color.
Heavy: Concrete tiles are exceptionally heavy. In some cases, your roof may not be capable of holding all this weight. If your home can’t support the weight, you will need to have additional supports installed prior to your roof replacement.

Cost:

Concrete roofing tiles cost anywhere from $9 to $19 per square foot.
Metal Roofs in Florida
As major hurricanes become more common, more and more Floridians are choosing metal roofs to protect their homes. But are metal roofs the best roofing material on the market today? They’re certainly a competitive option, but like all roofing materials, they have their own drawbacks.

The two styles of metal roofing are hidden and exposed fastener metal roofs. Each option comes with its own advantages and disadvantages, so let’s take a closer look to see if a metal roof replacement is right for you!
Exposed Fastener Metal Roof
Exposed fastener metal roofing is also known as 5V or corrugated metal roofing. Its primary name comes from the way that this type of metal roof is installed; by drilling corrugated metal roofing sheets straight down into your roof. This leaves the fasteners “exposed” on the top of your metal roofing panels.

There’s a lot to love about these roofs, as well as some red flags to be aware of. Check out the good and the bad to make an informed decision about your new roof!

Pros:

 	Affordable: 5V metal roofing is easily the most affordable metal roofing option. Because the sheets are easy to manufacture and quick to install, this is the best roofing material for a low-cost metal roof replacement.
 	Secure: Drilled down into your roof, you can rest assured that your metal roofing panels aren’t going anywhere.

Cons:

 	Fastener Maintenance: Because your fasteners sit on top of your roof, they’re exposed to the elements. This means they need regular maintenance to make sure they don’t develop rust, leaks, and other problems that weaken your roofing system.
 	Short Lifespan: Drill down metal roofs last for 20-30 years on average. This is largely because the metal panels can’t expand and contract with the sun’s heat due to being drilled into place, which causes premature aging.

Cost:

Exposed fastener metal roofing costs between $7 and $12 per square foot.
Hidden Fastener Metal Roof
A hidden fastener metal roof, or standing seam, is the gold standard for metal roofing in Florida. Made with sleek, smooth roofing panels that connect via an overlapping lock mechanism, this type of metal roof keeps your fasteners safely “hidden” beneath your roofing panels.

Does the placement of your fasteners make a big difference? Let’s look at the good and the bad of standing seam metal roofing to see!

Pros:

 	Longevity: Standing seam metal roofs can last for up to 70 years with proper maintenance.
 	Low Maintenance: Every roof needs occasional maintenance, but standing seam metal roofs have very low maintenance needs compared to other materials.
 	Not Industrial: Some people don’t like the industrial look of metal roofing. Standing seam, however, is sleek and modern without losing that warm, homey feeling.
 	Home Value: Standing seam roofs are very desirable in Florida. With a sleek exterior and great protection, you can count on seeing a big return on your initial investment if you decide to sell your home!

Cons:

 	Expensive: Standing seam metal roofing is a high-cost roofing material. This is due to their more complicated manufacturing process as well as the more difficult roof installation, both of which can significantly raise roofing costs.

Cost:

Standing seam metal roofing costs between $10 and $35 per square foot.

At the end of the day, you’re the only one who can weigh the pros and the cons of each material and decide what’s best for you. ### Roof Shingle Types: A Comprehensive Guide for Florida Homeowners

When you think of shingle roofing, asphalt shingles are probably the first thing that comes to mind. While asphalt shingles are excellent, timeless roofing materials, they are far from the only type of roof shingle available in Florida. When planning a roof replacement, it’s important to consider all of the roof shingle types available to you!

That’s what we’re here for. We’re PITCH Roofing, your local shingle roofing partner. To help you plan your next roof replacement, we’re covering everything you need to know about your shingle roofing options. Keep reading for our complete guide to asphalt, synthetic, and metal shingles!
Asphalt Roof Shingles


Asphalt shingles are the most well-known of all the roof shingle types. Made from a baseboard of felt or fiberglass, these shingles are coated in thick layers of asphalt that make them water-resistant and durable. And with a variety of color options available, there’s an asphalt shingle option that will appeal to nearly any homeowner.

Many homeowners don’t realize, however, that there is more than one type of asphalt shingle. In fact, three distinct types of asphalt roofing shingles have made their mark on the roofing industry. Let’s talk about these different roofing options and what they can offer your home!
3-Tab Asphalt Shingles
This is an old-school roofing material that has largely been phased out in modern roofing. While some contractors still install 3-tab shingles, most Florida roofers recommend against it. That’s because 3-tab shingles are made using a single layer of asphalt. As a result, they simply aren’t ready for Florida’s severe weather patterns.

Let’s take wind resistance for example. 3-tab asphalt shingles can only withstand winds up to 70 mph — the lowest of all the roof shingle types. This isn’t secure enough to withstand a tropical storm, let alone a major hurricane. For this reason, a 3-tab shingle roof is lucky to last more than 10-15 years in the Sunshine State.

So why do some people still choose this type of roofing shingle? Well, they’re cheap. Extremely cheap, in fact, with 3-tab shingle prices ranging from $1.50 to $3 per square foot. While this is easily the cheapest roofing material on the market, it’s almost always a better idea to invest in a high-quality shingle roof for your home’s long-term protection.
Architectural Asphalt Shingles
Also known as dimensional shingles, architectural asphalt shingles have several key upgrades over 3-tab shingles. For one thing, they’re made of a double layer of asphalt. This may not sound like a huge difference, but it gives these shingles the weight and heft to be much more secure on your roof. For comparison, architectural shingles are rated for winds up to 120 mph — almost double that of 3-tab shingles!

That improved performance is why dimensional shingle roofs last 20-25 years in Florida, on average. But improved performance isn’t even the limit of the upgrades that come with dimensional shingles. These shingles get their name for a unique trait that they hold among all of the roof shingle types. Namely, they create a textured, layered look on your roof thanks to their unique patterning. This creates visual dimension on your roof, which can greatly increase curb appeal!

While architectural shingles are more expensive than 3-tab, they’re still very competitively priced. With architectural shingle prices between $5 and $9 per square foot, you can still get a very affordable roof replacement by choosing these asphalt shingles!
Premium Asphalt Shingles
These shingles have many names, including luxury or presidential shingles. Whatever you call them, they’re the best that asphalt shingle roofing has to offer. These laminated shingles are thick and durable, designed to replicate both the look and the protection of slate roofing tiles. With wind resistance up to 130 mph, these roofing shingles are as hurricane-ready as asphalt shingles can be.

Of all the asphalt roof shingle types, premium asphalt shingles are unique in that they are the only luxury roofing material. Part of this means getting a luxury roofing experience, including a lifespan of 30 to 50 years with proper shingle roof maintenance. The other part of the luxury roofing experience, though, is the cost.

Luxury asphalt shingles are the most expensive asphalt shingle option at $8 to $17 per square foot. For many homeowners, though, these roofs are well worth the investment for a long-lasting, durable roof that mimics the timeless aesthetic of slate roofing!
Synthetic Roof Shingles
Synthetic roofing shingles are a newcomer on the roofing scene. First hitting the market around the year 2000, these shingles have quickly left their mark on the roofing industry. Unlike asphalt shingles, these shingles are made from specialized polymers and recycled materials. In other words, they’re hardened plastic shingles.

That may not sound like the kind of durability you want on your roof, but nobody can deny that synthetic shingles are hardy and long-lasting. Depending on the type of synthetic roofing shingle you choose, these roofs can withstand winds between 110 and 150 mph. Given this kind of resilience, it’s no wonder that synthetic shingles last for around 50 years in Florida.

Synthetic shingles also have a very different look from other types of roofing shingles. That’s because these shingles are made to replicate the look of cedar shake or slate. This way, you can get the elegant look of a shake or slate roof at a fraction of the cost!

When it comes to cost, synthetic shingles are priced competitively compared to the other roof shingle types. Synthetic shingles cost $7 to $14 per square foot. While this is more expensive than most asphalt shingle options, it’s much more affordable than real cedar shake or slate!
Metal Roof Shingles


Many homeowners are surprised to learn that metal shingles are readily available for their next roof replacement. But it’s true — metal shingles are an increasingly popular type of shingle roofing in Florida. Made with stone-coated steel, these shingles combine the strength of metal roofing with the curb appeal and comfort of asphalt shingles.

Metal shingles work using an exposed fastener roofing system. This means that roofers drill rows of metal shingles straight down into your roof. While this all but ensures that a storm won’t be able to remove your roof, it does come with drawbacks. Namely, your roof’s exposed fasteners will face wear and tear, which shortens the overall life of your roof.

Metal shingle roofs last for about 30 years on average. While this is not especially long compared to other roof shingle types, you can rest assured that your home will enjoy 30 years of reliable protection. In Florida, that’s nothing to sneeze at!

Metal roofing shingles are fairly affordable, especially if you’re comparing them to other metal roofing options. Metal shingles cost $5 to $11 per square foot, which makes them a readily available metal roofing option for most homeowners. If you want the strength and resilience of a metal roofing system without losing the classic curb appeal of shingles, this could very well be the best type of shingle roof for your home!

### How to Get the Look of Slate Roof Tiles at a Lower Cost

Slate roof tiles are a classic roofing material. Slate roofs have been in style since the Roman Empire, although they have been limited to the very wealthy because of the high cost of slate. What Are Slate Roof Tiles & Why Do Floridians Love Them?


Florida is famous for its tile roofing. But while you’ll see plenty of roofs with clay or even concrete tiles, slate roof tiles are much rarer in the Sunshine State. That’s because, even compared to clay tile roofing costs, slate is expensive.

Roofing costs vary, but slate roof tiles can cost anywhere from $10 to $30 per square foot. With this kind of price tag, the fact that these roofs are still so highly sought after speaks volumes to the quality of the material. So what do people love about slate roof tiles that makes them willing to pay such high prices?

For one thing, slate roofs last for a long time. Like clay roofing tiles, slate can last for 50 to 100+ years, depending on if you get hard or soft slate. It’s important to note, however, that slate roofs rarely come with manufacturer warranties. This means if you want long-term protection, you’d need to get a lifetime warranty from your contractor — and they’d need to have been in business for a long time, too, since a lifetime warranty is only good if the company backing it up still exists.

Form is just as important as function when it comes to slate roof tiles, though. Slate roofs have been highly desirable for millennia because of the sleek, gorgeous look of slate tiles. An Alternative to Slate Roof Tiles


When you think of shingle roofing, you probably think of asphalt shingles. While asphalt shingle roofs are durable and reliable, they’re a little plain and common. Synthetic shingles, on the other hand, offer the best qualities of slate roof tiles without the off-putting price tag.

Synthetic shingles are made from specialized polymers and recycled materials. In other words, manufacturers make them using hardened, durable plastic. This may not sound as glamorous as slate roof tiles, but the end result is something all but indistinguishable from the real deal.

That’s because manufacturers shape synthetic shingles into near-perfect replicas of slate roof tiles. In fact, manufacturers use the same molds as the ones used in shaping slate roof tiles when creating synthetic shingles. This enables synthetic slate shingles to mirror the aesthetic of slate. As a result, you can enjoy the classic look of slate roofing and save money in the process.

S.ynthetic shingles can’t last as long as slate. However, you can still expect to get 40 to 50 years of life out of synthetic shingles. And with the ability to withstand high winds, humidity, and UV rays, synthetic shingles offer robust protection that’s far beyond that of conventional asphalt shingles.

How much do these alternatives to sate roof tiles cost, though?

For one thing, synthetic shingles routinely get warranties from their manufacturers.
