Before agreeing to a roof replacement, be sure to discuss your warranty options with your roofers!

Synthetic shingles are also cheaper to install because they’re lighter. Slate is one of the heaviest roofing materials on the market, and not all structures are built to take that kind of weight. Often, homes need to have additional supports installed during a slate roof replacement. By skipping this cost, synthetic shingles can save you even more money!

### When to Get Water Damage Roof Repair Services

No homeowner is happy to see that there’s a leak in their roof. And without professional help, today’s minor leak repair can be next month’s roof replacement. The risk is especially high in the summer months when hurricanes can turn minor roof damage into roofing catastrophes. Signs of Roof Water Damage


If you see water coming from your ceiling, you already know you have a leak. But sometimes the damage to your roof isn’t as clear-cut. Oftentimes there are early warning signs before you start seeing water dripping into your home or commercial property. By acting before water starts falling, you can minimize water damage to your home and lower your water damage roof repair costs.

In our line of work, these are the early signs of roof water damage that we look out for:

 	Ceiling Stains: Even if you don’t see any moisture, discolorization on your ceiling means it’s very likely that water is intruding into your roof. Look for dark stains in an irregular pattern.
 	Musty Attic: Most roofing problems will appear in your attic before you notice them throughout your home. If you access your attic and notice a musty smell or mold growth, there’s a very good chance that water is getting into your roofing system.
 	Mold on Exterior Walls: Finding mold and mildew in your home is never good. If you see it on an exterior wall, it could mean that you have a leak. Mold means that there’s condensation from where your exterior wall meets the interior of your structure, which indicates a roofing problem.

Whether you see an early warning sign or water coming from your ceiling, the important thing is to stay calm and take steps to minimize the damage. Let’s talk about what you can do if you’re experiencing a roof leak!
What to Do When You Have a Roof Leak in Florida
If you think that you need water damage roof repair services, there are several key steps that you’ll need to take to minimize the damage. Let’s take a look at what Central Florida residents can do to reduce the risk of severe water damage!
1. Stop the Water Damage from Spreading
If you notice water damage in your home, the most essential step is stopping it from getting worse. Conventional wisdom is to place a bucket under dripping water to prevent it from harming your floors, but this is only a partial solution. Water is still going to be damaging your roofing system this way.

That’s why it’s best to place a bucket in your attic to catch any water before it reaches your ceiling. While this can’t prevent damage to your roof decking, it will stop your ceiling from developing mold or other issues, which will help lower your water damage roof repair costs!
2. Identify the Source of the Leak
If you want to lower your water damage roof repair costs, it’s a good idea to find the source of the leak. While roofing contractors will be happy to find the cause for you, the longer they spend looking for the source, the more they’ll have to charge you for their time. That’s why it pays to identify the source yourself, if possible.

If you can access your attic, try to find where the water is coming from. In the vast majority of cases, you’ll be able to see the cause within a foot or two of where you see water dripping in. If you’re able to find the area where water is coming in, take a photo. This will help your contractors start there immediately and be as efficient as possible!
3. Call in the Contractors
When you’ve taken steps to mitigate the damage and identify the source, your next step is calling in the professionals. During this process, you’ll be able to let them know where the water is coming in and the current extent of the water damage to your roof. If you have photos of the damaged parts of your roof, this step will be a great time to pass those along!

From there, you should be scheduled for a roof inspection and estimate. Pricing water damage roof repairs can be tricky, which is why contractors need to see the damage firsthand before they can give you a bill. If you need urgent repairs, most contractors will be able to bump you up their lists to accommodate you.

### Mobile Home Roof Repair Tips & Cost Guide

Life as a mobile homeowner in Florida can be tough. While there are certainly many advantages to owning a mobile home, hurricane season can be a scary time. Signs You Need Mobile Home Roof Repair Services


For many people, it can be hard to tell when a roof needs repairs. While a leak is a clear sign that you need mobile home roof repairs, not all of the signs of damage are as obvious. To make sure you know when to get help, we’re going to review some of the most common signs of mobile home roof damage.

Mobile home roofing materials typically come in two types: shingles and flat roofing materials. Depending on which type of material your roof is made of, your roof will show damage in different ways. For that reason, let’s break down signs your roof needs repairing into two different sections.
Signs Mobile Home Shingle Roofs Need Repairs
Most of the time, a mobile home will have a flat roof. But with certain newer models, shingle roofs are becoming increasingly popular. This change in roofing style vastly reduces the risk of leaks forming due to standing water. On the other hand, shingle roofs can struggle to withstand the high winds that Florida’s hurricane season is infamous for.

As experienced Florida roofers, these are the signs of damage we look for on mobile home shingle roofs:

 	Missing Shingles: After a storm, it’s common to find shingles strewn throughout your yard. While asphalt shingles can withstand high winds, Florida’s hurricanes can be too severe for them, which can leave your roof exposed to water damage and even pest infestations.
 	Cracked or Curled Shingles: Not all mobile home roofing problems are caused by hurricanes. UV rays can dry out your shingles and crack or curl them, which weakens their ability to protect your home.
 	Bruised Shingles: When struck by hail or storm debris, shingles can become “bruised,” meaning they have a darker color and may have round indents from where they were hit. You may also notice patches of missing granules.

As veteran Florida roofers, the crew at PITCH Roofing has fixed more than their fair share of shingle roofs. If you find yourself needing mobile home roof repairs, entrust your roof to local pros who know how to set your roof up for long-term success and protection!
Signs Mobile Home Flat Roofs Need Repairs
While mobile home flat roofs hold up better against wind damage than shingles, they have their own issues. Pooling water is a much more common issue for flat roofs, which is why flat roofing materials have great water resistance. But if your materials get damaged, then you could be looking at serious roofing troubles.

Some of the most common signs that you need mobile home roof repairs for a flat roof include:

 	Splitting or Separating Seams: A flat roof’s seams are the places where one roll of material ends and another begins. During installation, these are sealed to create a water-tight barrier. But if you notice the edges of your roofing material lift up or slacken, it’s only a matter of time before water enters your roofing system.
 	Tears or Puncture Damage: During a storm, high winds can whip branches or other debris up onto your roof. With enough force, these flying projectiles can puncture or tear your roofing material, which leaves an entrance for water to get to the most vulnerable parts of you roof.
 	Moss and Mold Growth: If you notice moss or mold developing on top of your roof, there’s a good chance you also have pooling water. These microbes need a lot of moisture to grow, so they’re an early sign that something is wrong with your roof.

Even if you haven’t started noticing leaks or other signs of roof damage, having any one of these issues is a problem. Your home deserves the best protection possible, and the best way to get that is through timely mobile home roof repair services.

### Pros and Cons of Composite Roof Shingles in Florida

When you think of shingle roofing, asphalt shingles are probably the fist thing that comes to mind. While these are a timeless, classic option, they have new competition on the roofing market. Composite roof shingles have a lot to offer Florida homeowners, including many features that asphalt shingles simply can’t replicate.

But are they a good idea for Florida homeowners? That’s what we’re here to cover. We’re PITCH Roofing, and as local roofing professionals, we understand which roofing materials are viable for Florida roofs. Stick with us as we cover the good and the bad of composite roof shingles in Florida!
What Are Composite Roof Shingles?


Before we start weighing the pros and cons of composite shingle roofing in Central Florida, let’s first establish what these shingles are. Also called synthetic shingles, these roofing shingles are made from recycled materials and synthetic polymers. These shingles feel like hardened plastic with a durable, textured surface.

However, what sets composite roof shingles apart isn’t the way they feel, but the way they look. Synthetic shingles mimic the look of slate and cedar shake shingles. Slate and cedar shake are both highly expensive shingles that don’t last for an especially long time, so many people prefer composite roof shingles as a way to generate curb appeal without a large price tag for a roof that won’t last for very long.

Roofing is a highly localized industry, though. A great roofing material in Florida might be an awful material for a roof in Colorado. And even within the Sunshine State, different areas have different roofing needs. With that in mind, let’s talk about the good and the bad of composite shingle roofing in Central Florida and see if these shingles could be right for your home!
Pros & Cons of Composite Roof Shingles in Central Florida
Over the years, we’ve seen growing interest in composite roof shingles across Pinellas, Hillsborough, and surrounding counties. Before making any roofing decisions, we always encourage our customers to look at the good and bad sides of a given material. Let’s help you do that by looking at the pros and cons of composite roof shingles!
Pro: Durable and Hurricane-Ready
No roof is truly “hurricane-proof.” But composite roof shingles are about as hurricane-ready as a roofing material can get. Synthetic shingles are rated for winds of up to 130 mph, so when you add in their great water resistance, these shingles are ready for even major hurricanes.

Of course, Florida’s weather is tough on roofs even outside of hurricane season. But composite roof shingles are just as ready for the rest of Florida’s tough weather factors. UV rays, humidity, and severe heat can all damage roofs. But synthetic shingles are made of resilient, reinforced plastic that can stand up to all of these without budging!
Con: Composite Roof Shingles Are New
In some ways, it’s a good thing to enjoy the protection of a new, cutting-edge roofing material. But it has its drawbacks. Because synthetic shingles are relatively new to the market, nobody knows for sure what kinds of problems these shingles could present with as they age. It is technically possible that composite shingles could have issues that we don’t yet know about.

While this is a downside, it’s not quite as bad as it sounds. Most manufacturers offer limited lifetime warranties on their synthetic shingles. So if your shingles do develop some kind of unexpected problem decades after your roof replacement, you would still be under warranty and able to get help with any necessary repairs or shingle roof replacements.
Pro: An Improvement on Classic Roofing Materials
Slate and cedar shake shingles are old-school roofing materials that a lot of people love. But they just aren’t affordable for many homeowners. Additionally, they’re not right for every climate — for example, wood shingles are a bad idea in Florida because our humidity can lead to water absorption, which weakens the overall structure of the shingles.

Composite roof shingles are a solution to both of these problems. In terms of roofing costs, composite roof shingles are about half that of slate or cedar shake. And while other materials may not be suited to Florida’s climate, synthetic shingles are more than capable of withstanding the worst that Florida has to offer!
Con: Limited Resale Value
There is no reason that a potential buyer wouldn’t want a home with a composite shingle roof. However, while synthetic shingles can replicate the look and style of luxury roofing materials, they don’t get the same prestige. This means that your composite roof shingles won’t generate the same interest or value as real slate or cedar shake.

While you won’t see the same value in your home, you also won’t have to pay exorbitant roof replacement costs, so most homeowners still consider this investment a net positive. And while synthetic shingles may not generate the same value as cedar or slate, they do create the same visual interest and curb appeal, which can be just as important for attracting potential buyers!
Pro: Long-Lasting Protection
When you buy a new roof, you want it to last for a long time. And that’s exactly what you can count on with composite roof shingles. Even with Florida’s many adverse weather conditions, composite roofs last 40-50 years on average.

While they don’t have the long lifespans of slate, which can last for 100+ years, synthetic shingles far outlast asphalt shingles and even cedar shake. If you want to invest in a gorgeous roof that will last in Florida, composite roof shingles are an excellent option to consider!

### A Guide to Metal Roof Maintenance in Florida

As strong hurricanes become more common in both the Atlantic and the Gulf of Mexico, an increasing number of Florida homeowners are turning to metal roofing to protect their properties. Whether you’ve already got a metal roof or are still on the fence, though, you’ll need to know about metal roof maintenance to get the most life out of your new roof!

We’re PITCH Roofing, your local metal roofing partner. Today, we want to cover the routine maintenance that will keep your metal roof performing at its best for decades to come. Let’s start by covering some of the fundamental best practices for metal roof maintenance!
Metal Roof Maintenance in Florida


With Florida’s humidity and seasonal storms, proper metal roof maintenance is essential to protecting your investment in your home. Not only does maintenance protect your roof, but it also saves you money by avoiding costly metal roof repairs. So what do you need to do to safeguard your metal roof?

Conventional wisdom is to get a metal roof inspection about once every year. Most of the time, your inspection will come back clean and there will be nothing further to work on. But by getting regular roof inspections, you can stay ahead of any roofing damage and fix it before the problem spreads. Let’s talk about some of the most common issues your inspector will find while checking your metal roof for damage!
Cleaning Off Dirt and Debris
Between tropical trees and storm debris, it’s easy for dirt and other detritus to build up on your roof. That’s why an essential part of metal roof maintenance is having your roof cleaned when you start to notice dirt or debris gathering. Not only is this unsightly, but it can provide a home for pests and weaken the overall structure of your metal roof.

While you technically can clean off your own roof, we don’t recommend it. Metal panels can be treacherous to walk on, especially if you don’t want to damage your roofing system. By leaving roof cleaning to the professionals, you can guarantee a great result without endangering your own safety or that of your roof.
Cleaning and Maintaining Gutters
Gutters are a key part of any roofing system. This is doubly true with metal roofs, which can rust and degrade if water starts to pool along the panels. That’s why cleaning your gutters twice a year is an essential part of metal roof maintenance!

Keeping clean gutters isn’t the only way to protect your metal roof, though. You should also keep an eye on your downspouts to make sure that water is draining properly. As gutters age, they can start to move or develop holes that prevent them from carrying water off your roof and through the downspouts. If this happens, both your roof and your home’s foundation could be in danger.

If you suspect that there’s an issue with your gutters that cleaning can’t solve, it’s best to call in the professionals. Gutter repairs and replacements can go a long way in saving you money on more costly metal roof repairs!
Re-Applying Sealants
A good roof sealant is worth its weight in gold on a metal roofing system. Metal panels fit tightly together, but they’re not usually watertight. To prevent water from getting to the more vulnerable parts of your roof, your installers will apply a sealant to create a water-tight seal and protect your structure.

Sealants don’t last forever, though. And in most cases, they won’t last as long as your metal roof. UV rays and water can gradually break down your sealant, leading to leaks and other pervasive roofing problems. When performing routine metal roof maintenance, your inspector may recommend having sealant re-applied along your roof’s seams to ensure that you don’t start developing leaks or other expensive metal roofing problems.
Exposed Fastener Metal Roof Maintenance
Exposed fastener metal roofing, also called 5V roofing, is a popular, affordable metal roofing option. With this style of metal roof, your panels are installed by drilling them straight down into your roof. This results in a secure metal roofing system, but it also requires some unique metal roof maintenance.

With 5V metal roofing, your fasteners sit on top of the metal panels. This allows them to cover up the drill holes in your panels and prevent water from intruding. Over time, though, having fasteners exposed to the elements can lead to problems. In our experience, fasteners will slowly start to rust or loosen over a period of about 7 years or so.

When this happens, it can allow water to access the most vulnerable parts of your roof. Over time, it can even lead to your panels loosening and starting to shift on your roof. That’s why inspecting and repairing your fasteners is an essential part of exposed fastener metal roof maintenance!
Standing Seam Metal Roof Maintenance


Unlike 5V metal roofing, standing seam metal roofing has hidden fasteners. This means that your metal roofing panels slot perfectly together and attach underneath the panel. As a result, your fasteners are “hidden” safely beneath your roofing panels, which prevents rusting and other issues that we see with exposed fastener roofing.

Standing seam roofs have their own unique metal roof maintenance quirks, though. With standing seam, the integrity of your metal roofing system hinges on your panels fitting together and protecting your roof. When your roof is installed, your panels will fit together perfectly. Over time, though, panels can separate and become misaligned, especially if your metal roof installation wasn’t performed correctly.

Contrary to popular belief, metal roofing panels don’t sit still once they’re on your roof. Instead, they expand and contract with the heat of the sun. This can lead to problems with panels not lining up as neatly as they used to, which could require adjusting your panels’ placement on your roof. When performing metal roof maintenance, your roof inspector will ensure that your panels are still slotted together and capable of protecting your home!
Reach Out for Metal Roofing Help
Whether you need metal roof maintenance or you’re looking to get a metal roof replacement, PITCH Roofing is ready to help. As veteran local roofers, we know what it takes to set up a Florida roof for long-term success. If you’re looking for roofing help from roofers you can trust, all you have to do is ask!

### Are Wood Shingles a Good Idea for Florida Homes?

When you think of shingle roofing in Florida, you probably think of asphalt shingles. While these are the standard roofing option, there is still considerable demand for wood shingles in the Sunshine State. But are they a good idea for Florida homeowners?

We’re PITCH Roofing, and as your local roofing partner, we’re here to help you plan your next roof replacement. Today, that means looking at wood shingles and how they hold up against Florida’s unique weather patterns. Keep reading to see if these unconventional roofing materials are right for you!
What Are Wood Shingles?


When you think of shingles, asphalt shingles are probably the first things that come to mind. However, shingles can be made of nearly anything — asphalt, slate, and yes, even wood. Specifically, wood shingles are normally made from cedar wood, which is why they’re also known as cedar shake shingles.

Unlike asphalt shingles, cedar shake is made to order. This means that there isn’t a warehouse somewhere that’s full of wood shingles. Instead, when you hire a roofing company to replace your roof, they will contact a manufacturer on your behalf to chop down a certain number of cedar trees and shape the material into wood shingles. As you might expect, this is an expensive process, which is why cedar shake is considered a luxury roofing material.

For many homeowners, the high cost of wood shingles is offset by their distinctive aesthetic. Cedar shake roofs are famous for giving homes a rustic, natural look that asphalt shingles simply can’t replicate. If you want a home that stands out, cedar shake shingles are an excellent option.

This covers the basics of what wood shingles are and why they appeal to so many homeowners. But how do they appeal in Florida’s unique environment?
How Wood Shingles Perform in Florida
Roofing is an incredibly localized industry. The best practice for a roof in Michigan could lead to a catastrophic roof failure in Florida. Between tropical storms, humidity, and UV exposure, Florida roofs have unique challenges that need to be addressed in order to keep your home safe. With this in mind, let’s look at how wood shingles stand up to the worst that Florida weather has to offer!
Hurricane Resistant
Everyone wants a roof that can stand up to a hurricane, and wood shingles are more than up to the challenge. Cedar shakes have been found to withstand winds in excess of 170 mph. This means that even in a Category 5 hurricane, your roof will be ready for the worst!

It’s important to note that no roof is 100% hurricane-proof. A direct hit from a major storm will always do damage. But having a roof with higher wind resistance minimizes the risk of substantial damage to your roof and the underlying structure of your home, which is valuable assurance to have in the middle of a major storm!
Vulnerability to Moisture
If you’ve lived in Florida for any amount of time, you’ve probably noticed that we live in a pretty wet place. In the summer, it’s normal to experience spots of rain at least once a day for weeks on end. Surprisingly, this rain is not a problem for wood shingle roofs. The issue is the humidity.

Because they’re made of wood, cedar shake shingles can retain ambient moisture. In a humid place like Florida, this means your shingles can end up waterlogged fast. Not only does this discolor the shingles, but it can lead to mold growth and rot. While you technically can have wood shingles in Florida, they will require a lot of regular maintenance to keep them clear of rot and other issues from moisture absorption.
30 Year Lifespans
While wood shingles do a great job at protecting your home, they don’t last as long as other luxury roofing materials. While cedar shake shingles can cost as much as $30 per square foot, they only last for 30 years on average. This is comparable with asphalt shingles, which last for about 25 years in Florida but come at a fraction of the cost.

For many homeowners, this short lifespan is a problem. Even worse, it’s not guaranteed that your roof will last this long. While wood shingles hold up well to wind, their vulnerability to moisture can shorten their lifespan even further. This makes wood shingles a tough sell for homeowners who want a long-lasting roof.
An Alternative to Cedar Shake Shingles


While there are many things to appreciate about wood shingles, they just aren’t the best option for most Florida homes. This doesn’t mean you can’t have the distinctive aesthetic of cedar shake in Florida, though. All that you need is an alternative roofing material.

As veteran Florida roofers, we highly recommend synthetic wood shingles. Made out of synthetic polymers, synthetic shingles look like classic wood shingles but have a lot of advantages over traditional cedar shake.

Because of their resilient composition, synthetic shingles are much better at withstanding Florida’s year-round humidity. This means you can expect your synthetic wood shingle roof to age well, even with Florida’s harsh conditions. In fact, synthetic shingles do so well in Florida that they last for 40 to 50 years on average!

The best part is the price. Unlike cedar shake, synthetic wood shingles cost $7 to $14 per square foot. This means you’re paying half the price (or less) for a roof that looks just as good and is even more durable. While you certainly can choose to go for real cedar shake shingles, in our experience, synthetic shingles are a much more reliable way to get a great, long-lasting roof.

### Pros, Cons, and Alternatives to Slate Shingles

Slate roofing shingles are a classic, timeless material. Famous both for their great aesthetics and their durability, slate shingles are popular for historical buildings as well as residential structures. In Florida, though, they are not always the most accessible or durable of roofing materials.

We’re PITCH Roofing, and we’re here to answer all of your questions about your different roofing material options. Today, that means explaining the good and the bad of slate shingles. Stick with us as we cover everything you need to know about slate roofing in Florida!
Pros and Cons of Slate Shingles


In nature, slate doesn’t start off as slate. Rather, it starts off as clay, which weight and pressure compress into shale, and then compress even further into slate. This makes slate shingles even tougher and more durable than clay tiles, which are famous for their durability and longevity!

Once the slate has formed, it’s then mined from the earth in large slabs that manufacturers then shape down into the slate shingles you’re familiar with. With their distinctive profile and extreme durability, it’s no wonder that slate roofs are so sought after. While these shingles are desirable, though, you may notice that few homeowners actually have slate roofs, especially in Florida.

There are good reasons that slate shingles are highly sought after, just as there are good reasons that few people have a slate roof. Let’s talk about both sides of this issue by covering the good and the bad about slate roofing shingles in Florida!
Pro: Slate Shingles Last a Long Time
If you want a roof that’s built to last, there is no better option than slate roofing. Because slate is so durable and resistant to water damage, it is extremely difficult for the environment to damage your roof so long as you’re keeping up with regular roof maintenance. And since these are heavyweight shingles, they can often resist the winds of even Category 5 hurricanes!

As a result, it’s no surprise that slate shingles last 75 to 100 years on average. With this kind of longevity, a slate roof will usually be the last roof that you need to install on your home. For comparison, an asphalt shingle roof will rarely last more than 25 years at the very most.
Con: Slate Roofs Are Expensive & Hard to Come By
The biggest reason that not everyone has a slate roof is the price tag. Mining and manufacturing slate requires a lot of labor and expensive equipment. As a result, slate shingles cost $12 to $33 per square foot in Florida. This means that in addition to being the longest-lasting material on the market, it’s also the most expensive.

And slate shingles aren’t just pricey; they’re also rare. Most roofing contractors don’t offer slate roof replacements. Instead, you’ll have to find a contractor who specializes in slate roofing. This can be challenging, and it limits your options if and when you need occasional roof repairs.
Pro: Slate Roofs Generate Curb Appeal
When getting a roof replacement, a durable roof is a must. But durability isn’t the only thing that you should be looking for. For many homeowners, the way that a roof looks is just as important. This is especially true if you plan to sell your home one day.

Slate roofs have a unique look that offers mass appeal. This means that not only will your home be protected by a slate roof, but slate shingles can offer increased value by improving the aesthetics of your property. Curb appeal isn’t just an issue of vanity — when selling a home, curb appeal translates to a favorable return on your investment!
Con: Slate Shingles Are Brittle
While slate shingles are durable and hardy, they do have one glaring weakness. When it comes to impact damage, it is very easy for slate to shatter. This means that nobody should be walking on a slate roof without extensive training, because one small mistake could do serious damage to your shingles.

Walking on the roof isn’t the only way to break a slate roof, though. In Florida, some of the most common ways that slate shingles break are from hail and storm debris. When hurricane winds whip up branches and other debris and throw them onto your roof, there’s every chance that your shingles will shatter. This means replacing damaged shingles after the storm, which can be expensive given the high cost to manufacture and install these shingles!
An Alternative to Slate Roofing Shingles


While slate roofs have good and bad qualities, at the end of the day, most homeowners are not choosing to get these roofs. More often, if a homeowner wants the distinctive look of slate roofing, they’ll choose a synthetic slate shingle option.

Instead of expensive slate, synthetic shingles are made from synthetic polymers. This makes them much less expensive than real slate shingles! In fact, synthetic slate shingles cost $7 to $12 per square foot. That’s a tough number to beat when talking about the iconic look of slate roofing.

Despite the greatly reduced price, synthetic shingles look just like the real thing. While there are some slight differences that seasoned roofers will be able to spot, the average person cannot tell the difference between synthetic and slate shingles. This means you get the full value of a slate roof’s curb appeal without the intimidating price tag!

While synthetic shingles do not last as long as slate, they still last for a good, long time. Synthetic slate roofs average about 40 to 50 years of life, which is still much higher than the average lifespan of asphalt shingles. And in some respects, synthetic shingles are even better than real slate. For example, synthetic slate shingles are much more resistant to impact damage, which makes them a better fit for Florida homes.

Slate shingles might not be for everyone, but synthetic slate roofing is widely available and well-suited to Florida’s weather patterns. If you love the look of a slate roof but don’t want your roof to cost an arm and a leg, synthetic slate shingles are the best of both worlds. Why Are Roofing Costs Always Increasing?


If it seems like roofing costs are always on the uptrend, that’s because they are. In large part, this is because of increases in manufacturing costs. Materials like wood, metal, stone, and others are always rising in price. Since your roof uses multiple types of materials, from the wood of your decking to the asphalt of your shingles, roofing costs trend especially upwards.

This begs the question, though, of why material costs keep increasing. In 2025, there are three main reasons that roofing material prices continue to get steeper:

 	Increased Demand: An active housing market means that there is extreme demand for building materials. Since there is more demand, the price will continue to increase to whatever the market will tolerate.
 	Inflation: Inflation continues to increase year over year. While this is a normal economic force, it has been especially steep for years, and the roofing industry continues to feel the effects of the dollar’s decreased buying power.
 	Labor Costs: Creating shingles or tiles requires workers to harvest raw materials and shape them into usable roofing supplies. To keep up with inflation, workers will need an increasing amount of money for their labor, which in turn drives up the costs of roofing services.

These are the biggest reasons that roofing prices will increase yet again this April. But is there anything you can do about it?

That’s because roofing is a relatively small industry, especially when you look locally. While roofing contractors in California and New York might have different suppliers, one geographic area usually gets its roofing materials from the same handful of manufacturers. So if one roofer says that prices are going up in your area, it’s likely that those price increases will extend to other roofers in your county.

That doesn’t mean that you have no options, though. By knowing when a price hike is coming, you can get ahead of it and schedule your roofing services now. The price of roofing is always increasing. ### The PACE Program & Other Roof Financing Options

In roofing, money shouldn’t be everything. You should pick the roofers that have demonstrated their ability to do right by you and your property. Realistically, though, we understand that roofing costs are always going to impact the final decision. With the Florida PACE program, though, you can cover roof replacement and repair costs with no hassle and no money down.

It may sound too good to be true, but the PACE program is a government-operated loan service that makes roofing services much more accessible to the average Florida homeowner. We’re PITCH Roofing, and as your local roofing partner, we consider it our job to explain your roof financing options. Stick with us as we walk you through everything that the PACE program has to offer!
How Does the Florida PACE Program Work?


The PACE program allows homeowners to pursue home improvements even if they don’t have the money for a major project right now. PACE (Property Assessed Clean Energy) was created in 2010 to allow homeowners to get up-front financing for hurricane hardening and clean energy improvements to their homes.

What sets this program apart from other lending options is that PACE does not require a down payment. This makes roof financing much more available to low-income homeowners who may not be able to afford a large up-front cost when the time comes to repair or replace their roofs. Additionally, there is no credit score requirement for the PACE program.

Rather than looking at your credit score, PACE eligibility depends on your home equity and income. Without steady income, it is unlikely that a homeowner will qualify for a PACE loan due to lending concerns about paying off the loan. However, by basing the requirements in income rather than credit score, PACE loans are available to more homeowners than a home equity line of credit (HELOC).

This covers the rough idea of how the PACE program operates. But what can it do for your roof?
What Home Improvements Qualify for PACE Funding?
The PACE program is very broad in the types of home improvements it will fund. These include things like HVAC units, new windows, water heaters, etc. When it comes to roofing services, the PACE program provides funding for:

 	Roof replacements
 	Roof repairs
 	Roof insulation
 	Cool roofing features
 	Skylight installation
 	Gutter repairs and installation
 	Attic ventilation
 	Energy-efficient roofing upgrades

In addition to this wide variety of services covered, the PACE program allows you to choose your own roofers. This means that you can choose roofers you trust and make your own decisions about who works on your property.

As you can see, there are very few limitations when it comes to using the PACE program to fund roofing services! No matter what roofing problem you’re experiencing, you can get relief from PACE funding. If you’re feeling like this is too good to be true, you’re not alone. Many Florida homeowners are wary of any new program that claims to offer easy, accessible funding. Let’s talk about the potential downsides of the PACE program to make sure you know what to expect when signing up!
What Are the Downsides of the PACE Program?
The Florida PACE program doesn’t have any downsides in the sense that the program is exactly what it claims to be: a readily available loan service provider for home improvements. It provides exactly what it claims and is not a scam. However, there are a few important things to know before signing up for PACE funding.

PACE program loan rates range from 6% to 12.99%, with most homeowners paying somewhere between 6 and 8 percent. When repaying your loan, you pay through your property taxes. This means that, like with any HELOC, failure to pay could cost you your home. For this reason, it is extremely important that you completely understand the terms and interest rate of your loan so that you can be certain that you will be able to repay this loan.

Another potential “downside” of this program is that it’s not available everywhere. To receive PACE funding, your property must be in a county or city that has approved use of the PACE program. You can check out their service areas to see if PACE funding is available in your area.

To qualify for the PACE program, a homeowner must meet all four of the following requirements:

 	Be up-to-date on property taxes and not have been delinquent on property taxes in the past 3 years
 	Be up-to-date with mortgage payments
 	Have received no notices of default in the past 3 years
 	Have no involuntary liens on your home

While the PACE program is perfect for some, it simply isn’t right for others. At PITCH, our concern is always with getting you high-quality roofing services, not with who services your loan. To make sure you’ve got great roof financing options available, let’s talk about your other options!
Roof Financing Alternatives to the PACE Program


Whether PACE funding isn’t available where you live or it just isn’t the right fit for you, you still have great roof financing options available. In Florida, there are two main ways that people get roof financing: through their chosen roofing company and through a HELOC.
PITCH Roofing Financing
At PITCH, we proudly provide low-interest roof financing. In fact, we even offer 0% roof replacement financing for the first year of your loan. This allows local homeowners to get essential roofing services and pay them off on a more comfortable timetable!

To qualify for a loan through PITCH, you don’t need a huge down payment or perfect credit. Most of our financing plans don’t even require upfront payment! While it’s important not to take out a loan that you can’t pay back, roofing services are a necessity that we want to provide to as many people as possible.
Home Equity Line of Credit
A HELOC is a great roof financing option for some homeowners. With low interest rates, these are some of the most sought-after loans for financing roof replacements. The only drawback is that HELOCs have some of the highest requirements to qualify.

For a HELOC, you’re borrowing directly against the equity that you have in your home. This means that if you don’t have equity, or not enough to cover the costs of your roofing project, you won’t be able to use a HELOC. Additionally, HELOCs require good credit. While lower credit scores may qualify for a HELOC, to get the best rates, you will want a credit score of at least 650.

### A Guide to Roof Flashing Types in Florida

Roof flashing is the unsung hero of your roofing system. While shingles and tiles get a lot of the focus, your roof flashing plays an essential role in keeping your roof safe. The best way to make sure you have the right protection for your home is to familiarize yourself with the different roof flashing types.

We’re PITCH Roofing, and helping you better understand your roof is what we do. In our decades of roofing, we’ve seen underhanded roofers try to leave out flashing on an estimate to provide a lower number and get a job. By making sure you understand the different types of flashing and how they work, we want to ensure that you’re never taken in by this kind of scam!
What Is Roof Flashing


Before we delve into the different roof flashing types, let’s talk about roof flashing in general. Flashing is a strip or section of metal on your roof, usually galvanized steel. Contractors will install this material wherever your roof connects with another surface, be that a chimney, a skylight, or a valley in your roof.

But what does roof flashing do? In the simplest terms, it guides whatever off your roof. That’s why it’s strategically placed where your roof needs protection most. By preventing water pooling, flashing protects the most vulnerable parts of your roofing system. And when there’s a problem with your roof flashing, your roof is at significant risk of developing a leak.

Without functional roof flashing, water has a tendency to pool and seep into your roof decking. For starters, this causes headaches like roof leaks or even roof sagging. And over time it can endanger your entire roofing system. That's because your shingles sit on top of your decking. If water eats away at it, you could need a roof replacement instead of a roof repair.

But the experts at PITCH aren’t going to let that happen. To make sure you’re ready to take care of your roof and discuss your options with contractors, let’s talk about the most common types of roof flashing in Florida!
Florida Roof Flashing Types


Remember how we said that roof flashing goes around any place where your roof meets another surface, like chimneys or roof vents? Well, which type of surface your roof meets will determine what kind of flashing it needs in that area. There are many different roof flashing types in Florida, so it’s important to be aware of everything that your roofing system needs to stay safe and secure!
Step Flashing
Step flashing is ideal for any place where your roof runs into a wall. This roof flashing type uses a piece of metal that’s bent at a 90-degree angle. With this method, several layers of flashing are installed with the shingles to ensure that water moves seamlessly away from the wall and off your roof.
Apron Flashing
Apron flashing is also sometimes called continuous flashing because it uses a single, long piece of metal installed at the base of a roof penetration. Long pieces of metal like this used to have issues with aging because they couldn’t expand and contract with the rest of the roof in response to heat. Thanks to built-in expansion joints, though, this is now one of the most durable roof flashing types!
Base & Counter Flashing
Major roofing features like chimneys don’t just have one piece of flashing. Instead, they use two roof flashing types to ensure maximum protection. This way, when rain moves along your roof, it won’t start to seep into the chimney.

The base flashing in this system is actually a piece of apron flashing. In other words, it’s a long, continuous piece of metal flashing. Roofers call it base flashing, though, because it’s combined with a second layer of protection: counter flashing. This second layer of protection is installed opposite or above your base flashing, which ensures that water can’t penetrate your roofing system no matter where it’s coming from.
Valley Flashing
As the name implies, roofers install valley flashing in the valleys, or low points, of your roof. Without this type of roof flashing, water would be able to pool in your roof’s valleys and slowly eat through your shingles. That makes valley flashing especially important for complex, multi-story roofing systems!
Drip Edge
This is one type of roof flashing that gets a lot of use during Florida’s rainy season. This piece of metal goes along the perimeter of your roof and directs water into your gutters. As a result, it also protects your shingles, which could otherwise have water forced beneath them during a storm or hurricane.
Kickout Flashing
Roofing systems are unique. That means that sometimes, you have to get creative with how and where you apply flashing. Kickout flashing exists for when other roof flashing types can’t get the job done alone. Specifically, contractors install kickout flashing to connect the space between your step flashing and your gutters. This way, there is no gap and no way for water to become trapped on your roof!

### Average Rain Gutter Prices in Florida

In Florida, gutters are often an essential roofing feature. In the summer, our seasonal rains can lead to water draining slowly from your roof. Rain gutters allow that water to move seamlessly off your roof without doing damage. Despite the great work that gutters do, however, many homeowners still have a lot of questions about rain gutter prices in Florida.

Luckily, PITCH Roofing is here to answer any and all of your roofing question. As real Florida roofers, we know that pricing information is always changing. That's why we've compiled the latest information on gutter installation costs! Keep reading for our rain gutter cost guide for Florida homeowners.
Average Rain Gutter Prices in Florida


On average, rain gutters cost between $700 and $1,800. But many homeowners end up with gutter installation costs that are very different from the average cost. To find out where your rain gutter prices will fall, it's important to consider the many different factors that affect your gutter installation costs. Keep reading for a breakdown of how you could end up with more affordable or more expensive rain gutters!
Roof Size and Elevation
Naturally, the larger your roof, the more gutter material you will need, which in turn drives up rain gutter prices. But size isn't the only way that your roof can affect how much your new gutters cost. Multi-story homes often come with higher gutter installation costs because roofers may need to use special equipment to access the different tiers of your roof. Additionally, roofs that are more complex, with multiple hills and valleys, can require more work when installing gutters, which further increases costs.
Types of Gutters
Many homeowners are surprised to learn that not all gutters are the same. And which type you choose will have a lasting impact on your rain gutter prices. Let's talk about the three most popular types of guttering in Florida:

 	Half-round gutters: These are the most common type of rain gutters for older homes. They’re great at moving water off your roof, but they’re also vulnerable to clogging if they don’t have gutter guards or another means to prevent trapped debris from accumulating. In terms of cost, these are the most affordable type of rain gutters.
 	K-style gutters: These rain gutters get their name from their unique design, which looks a little like a K on its side. They’re easier to install because of their flat back, and they’re better at keeping debris out than half-round gutters. In terms of cost, these are comparable to half-round gutters but might be slightly more expensive.
 	Custom-fit fascia gutters: Unlike other types of gutters, these are not made in bulk. Instead, they’re tailored specifically to your roof. This does increase the total cost of your rain gutters, but it also ensures that your gutters are perfectly suited to your home!

Rain Gutter Material Costs
What your gutters are made from is just as important as the style they’re made in. As you can imagine, material costs have a huge bearing on total rain gutter prices. Let’s take a look at the most popular guttering materials in Florida and how much they cost!

 	Aluminum: $3 to $14 per square foot
 	Vinyl: $3 to $7 per square foot
 	Wood: $20 to $34 per square foot
 	Galvanized Steel: $5 to $18 per square foot

Downspouts
Downspouts are an essential part of your guttering system. While rain gutters carry the water off your roof, downspouts make sure that that water doesn’t end up near your home’s foundation. Like gutters, though, downspouts come with many different material options that will impact rain gutter prices.

Here’s how much you can expect to pay for downspouts in Florida, by material:

 	Vinyl: $5 to $9 per linear foot
 	Aluminum: $6 to $10 per linear foot
 	Steel: $9 to $13 per linear foot

### Cedar Shake Shingles & Alternative Options in Florida

For centuries, cedar shake shingles have been an attractive luxury roofing material. With the distinctive look of wood shingles, these wooden shingles offer an unconventional aesthetic that many homeowners love. In Florida, however, it can be difficult for cedar shake shingles to perform their best.

We’re PITCH Roofing, and as veteran Florida roofers, we know what materials can and can’t stand up to Florida’s severe weather patterns. And in many ways, wooden shingles just can’t keep up with other roofing materials on the market. That doesn’t mean you have to give up on your dream of having a roof with wooden shingles in Florida, though. Keep reading to see why cedar shake shingles may not be the best option for Florida roofs and what your alternatives are!
Why Cedar Shake Shingles Don’t Work in Florida


Nobody can deny that cedar shake shingles are gorgeous and have a timeless beauty to them. However, wood shingles do not perform their best in Florida. And when you compare wooden shingles to other roofing materials, even standard asphalt shingles, it becomes clear that wooden shingles just aren’t a good fit for the Sunshine State.

For one thing, Florida is famous for its humidity, especially in the summer. This excess moisture will then seep into your shingles, which prematurely ages them. Wooden shingles are already in danger of losing their vibrant color as they age, and this will only happen faster in a humid place like Florida.

This is a lackluster result considering how expensive cedar shake shingles are. Unlike other roofing materials, manufacturers don’t keep a backlog of wood shingles. Instead, cedar trees are cut down and shaped into shingles for every job. This means you’ll wait longer for wooden shingles and have to pay their high manufacturing costs, which can range from $14 to $30 per square foot.

The final nail in the coffin is wooden shingle warranties. Unlike other roofing materials, wooden shingles usually have no manufacturer warranty. This means that if your roof fails because of a problem with your shingles, you’ll have nobody else to foot the bill. While you would still have your contractors’ workmanship warranty to fall back on, many homeowners are rightfully wary of a roofing material that not even the manufacturers will stand by.

All in all, cedar shake shingles are very rarely worth the investment in Florida. That doesn’t mean you can’t enjoy the look of cedar shake shingles, though. In fact, there is an alternative roofing material that offers the best of cedar shake shingle roofing without the considerable drawbacks!
An Alternative to Cedar Shake Shingles in Florida


Synthetic cedar shake shingles are a superior alternative to real wooden shingles. Made from resilient synthetic polymers, these shingles are shaped specifically to emulate the look of cedar shake. This allows homeowners in Florida to enjoy that classic, timeless aesthetic without sacrificing long-term protection.

Here are some of the biggest ways that synthetic wooden shingles are better than the original!
Synthetic Shingles Are Built Florida-Ready
Unlike real cedar shake shingles, synthetic shingles have no problem dealing with Florida’s weather patterns. Because they’re made of a synthetic polymer, these shingles don’t take on water the way that wooden shingles do. This means you won’t have to worry about your roof getting old before its time.

In terms of aesthetics, synthetic shingles even hold up better than the real deal. That’s because the polymers in synthetic shingles age much better than the wooden fibers of cedar shake. So instead of growing dark and dull over time, synthetic shingles retain their original coloring.
Synthetic Shingles Need Less Maintenance
Getting a cedar shake roof means paying for regular maintenance. While every roof needs occasional maintenance, the needs of wooden shingles are significantly higher than average. As your wooden shingles curl and crack with age, they will need to be replaced, which can take time since each shingle is made according to orders, not in bulk. As a result, expect slow and expensive roof repairs with any wooden roofing material.

Synthetic cedar shake offers a very different experience, though. Since these synthetic shingles hold up better against the Florida elements, they do not require as much maintenance. Any roof can develop problems, but these shingles are much less likely to give you issues. And since manufacturers create synthetic wooden shingles in bulk, you’ll be able to replace any damaged shingles much faster and for less money.
Lower Roofing Costs
A synthetic polymer will almost always be cheaper than harvesting real wood. Even in areas where cedar shake shingles are more well-suited to the local climate, this is a big part of the appeal of synthetic wooden shingles. But how much do these roofing options really cost?

As we mentioned, cedar shake shingles cost $14 to $30 per square foot. On the other hand, synthetic cedar shake costs only half as much. Synthetic shingles cost between $7 and $14 per square foot. By choosing these machine-made shingles, you can get a roof that both lasts for a long time and is reasonably priced!
Synthetic Shingles Last as Long as Cedar Shake Shingles
Part of the appeal of wooden shingles is their long lifespans. While they don’t last as long in Florida, wooden shingles have been known to average between 40 and 50 years of life. This is much better than the 25-year lifespan of asphalt shingles!

Synthetic shingles can last as every bit as long, though. And because they’re better suited to the Florida climate, they can do it while looking even better than real wood. When comparing cedar shake shingles and synthetic shingles, there is no reason not to choose the synthetic option as a Florida homeowner!

### How Much Does a Metal Roof Replacement Cost in Florida?

Year after year, metal roofing becomes more popular in Florida. As strong hurricanes become more frequent, more Floridians are turning to metal roofing as a means to protect their homes and commercial properties. While these roofing materials have become more popular, there are still many common questions about how much metal roof replacement costs.

We’re here to answer those questions! We’re PITCH Roofing, and as your local metal roofing partners, we’re here to demystify metal roofs. Today, that means covering all the latest pricing information that you’ll need to know for your metal roof replacement. Keep reading for our guide to metal roofing costs!
Metal Roof Replacement Cost by Material


One of the biggest factors when calculating your metal roof replacement costs is which material you choose. While all metal roofs are hardy and durable, each metal roofing material is unique in both its advantages and price point.

As we look at the different metal roofing materials in Florida, these are some of the most popular:

 	Galvalume Steel: This is a popular roofing material across the Sunshine State, known for its strength and durability. After installation, a galvalume steel roof replacement costs between $10 and $19 per square foot.
 	Aluminum: This lightweight, durable metal is popular along the coasts for its unmatched rust resistance. In Florida, expect to pay $10 to $21 per square foot for an aluminum roof replacement.
 	Stone-Coated Steel: As the name implies, this material is roofing steel coated in a layer of protective stone granules. The result is a metal roof that mimics the look of tile or shingles. On average, these roofs cost $7 to $15 per square foot.
 	Copper: Copper is as luxurious a roofing material as they come. While copper roofs offer unmatched longevity, they are not for everybody with a price point between $15 and $30 per square foot.

While there are other metal roofing options on the market, like zinc or tin, these options are not popular. With new advances in roofing technology, these old-school materials simply haven’t been able to keep up with the times. This is good news for homeowners, though, since it means your readily available options are truly the best of the best!
Metal Roof Replacement Cost by Type


There are many types of metal roofs available in the Florida market. Which type you choose will impact your metal roof replacement costs just as much as your material choices, if not more. To better understand why this is and how much each option will cost, let’s look at these roofing styles one by one!
Hidden Fastener Metal Roofing
Hidden fastener metal roofs are the gold standard. These metal roofing sheets are carefully crafted so that they connect together beneath your metal panels. Since the fasteners are beneath your metal panels, they are protected against wear and tear from the Florida elements.

Hidden fastener metal roofs, also called standing seam, have a sleek, modern exterior that is perfect for homes. And the benefits of these roofing systems are not just aesthetic. Since the hidden fasteners allow your roof to freely expand and contract with the sun, you can expect your metal to hold up well in the long run. In fact, these roofs last 40-70 years on average.

As you might imagine, these high-quality roofing systems are far from cheap. Exact figures will vary depending on your roof and materials, but generally, a standing seam metal roof replacement costs between $10 and $28 per square foot. Despite these high costs, many Florida homeowners are happy to make this long-term investment in protecting their homes!
Exposed Fastener Metal Roofing
Exposed fastener metal roofing is another popular style of metal roofing in Florida. These roofs have corrugated metal panels that are drilled straight down into your roof. As a result, your fasteners are “exposed” on the top of your roof, which means you’ll need to keep an eye on them as they age and get occasional repairs.

Because installers drill your metal panels straight down into your roof, the panels cannot expand and contract as they heat up. This means that your roof will undergo extra stress and prematurely age. As a result, exposed fastener metal roofs rarely last longer than 30-40 years in Florida. Still, this is significantly better than the life expectancy of an asphalt shingle roof, which is closer to 20-25 years!

While exposed fastener metal roofs may not last as long, they have their own upsides. For one thing, they’re much more affordable than standing seam. They are cheaper to manufacture because of the panels’ simple designs, and they’re faster to install because they can be drilled down directly instead of carefully interlocked together.

As a result, exposed fastener roofs are your best bet for affordable metal roofing. In Florida, an exposed fastener metal roof replacement costs $7 to $12 per square foot. For this reason, these roofs are extremely popular among homeowners who want to get their homes hurricane-ready without breaking the bank!

### What to Know About New Build Roof Constructions in Florida

Building a new structure is an exciting time, and Florida is always full of new developments. When planning your new build, though, it’s important to know that new build roof construction is significantly different from a roof replacement. And your new roof construction will have an even larger impact on the long-term health and protection of your structure.

We’re PITCH Roofing, and as veteran Florida contractors, we’ve mastered new roof construction and roof replacements. Today, we’re explaining the biggest differences between these two services so you know what to expect and which roofers to trust with your property’s protection.
New Build Roof Construction vs. Roof Replacement


While both new build roof construction and roof replacements will give you a new roof, they go about it in very different ways. While some roofers might be great for a roof replacement, that doesn’t necessarily mean you want to trust them with your new roof construction. Let’s look at the biggest differences between these roof installation jobs!
1. New Build Roof Construction Has a Unique Scope of Work
New build roof construction differs from roof replacement in key ways. For one thing, you don’t have to tear off an old roof before installing a new one. Even more essentially, building a new roof from scratch requires much more planning and designing.

When planning your new build roof construction, roofers will consider your structure’s location, your preferences, and market conditions. They will also need to account for the structure as a whole. For example, if you’re building a multi-level property, your roofers will need to consider how any upstairs rooms affect the potential shape and design of your new roof.

As you might imagine, this takes a lot of skill and know-how. While roof replacements are not easy or simple, they are much more direct than new roof construction because you only have to tear off the old roof and install the new materials. If a roof replacement is coloring in a picture, then new build roof construction is drawing something from scratch.
2. You Need to Be Picky When Choosing Contractors
When it comes to a roof replacement, we always encourage our local community members to be choosey. You’re investing a substantial amount of money into your home, after all! But the stakes are much higher with a new build roof construction.

If something goes wrong with a roof replacement, you’re looking at a problem that could cost thousands of dollars to fix. But if something goes wrong with a new roof construction, fixing it could cost tens of thousands of dollars, and solving the problem will likely take much more time. That’s why it’s in your best interest to be very choosey with your roofers.

When evaluating potential roofers, look at things like reviews, credentials, and experience. At PITCH Roofing, for example, we were founded by veteran Florida roofers with a combined 60 years of experience. You can’t buy that kind of expertise, and we’re ready to use it for your new roof construction!
3. Building a New Roof Offers More Material Options


When replacing your roof, you certainly have a lot of material options. If you have a shingle roof, for example, you could upgrade to a metal roof. However, you’ll have many more roofing material options when planning your new build roof construction.

That’s because you can build any type of roof you want. Whether you want a standard sloped roof, a flat roof, or a mix of the two, the world is your oyster. As long as it’s structurally sound to do so, you can have nearly any kind of roof.

This goes beyond just the pitch of your roof or its hills and valleys. You’ll also be able to make decisions about what kind of roof your new structure can support. For example, concrete tiles are a popular material in Florida, but they’re extremely heavy. Many roofs need additional support installed to sustain this type of weight. But with new build roof construction, you can ensure that your roof starts off with enough strength to support heavier roofing materials and set up your new build for long-term success!
4. New Build Roof Construction Costs More
Roof replacements aren’t cheap, but they’re certainly more budget-friendly than a new build roof construction. As we’ve covered, new roof construction is much more involved than a roof replacement, and that extra time and labor will be reflected in your total roofing costs.

There is no reliable way to say how much a new build roof construction will cost. There are simply too many competing factors at play. What we can say, however, is that your total costs will depend on:

 	The size of your roof
 	Your roof’s pitch
 	The complexity of your roofer

### Everything You Should Know About Luxury Asphalt Shingles

Everyone knows asphalt shingles. They're affordable, come in a variety of styles, and are the most popular roofing material across North America. In Florida, we also associate these shingles with wind damage since it's normal to find asphalt shingles scattered in the yard after a storm. But with luxury shingles, you can enjoy better weather protection and enhanced aesthetics for your roof.

We're PITCH Roofing, your local shingle roofing partners. And today we want to cover all the great things that luxury asphalt shingles can do for your roof. This includes looking at luxury shingle protective features, curb appeal, and longevity. But first, let's cover the basics and discuss what luxury shingles are and what makes them so special!
What Are Luxury Asphalt Shingles?


Luxury shingles (also called premium or designer shingles) are made of the same materials as other asphalt shingles: a fiberglass base board, asphalt, and stone granules. This doesn't mean that luxury shingles are like other types of shingles, though. For one thing, they're made up of much thicker layers of asphalt. This ensures that they're much hardier and better able to resist Florida's severe weather patterns.

That isn't the most notable thing about luxury shingles, though. The first think that homeowners notice about these roofs is that they look very different from architectural asphalt shingles. That's because luxury shingles mimic the look of slate tile. They can do this thanks to their thicker consistency, which creates the smooth, raised texture of slate.

The difference this makes is more than skin deep. Having a roof that looks like slate tiles isn’t just something to brag about; it can considerably increase the value of your home. Curb appeal is worth a lot when selling a home, which is why homeowners choose luxury shingles both for the great, long-term protection and the favorable return on their investment.

This covers the basics of asphalt shingles. But if you're considering these shingles for your next roof replacement, you've probably got more questions. Let's start answering them by discussing how luxury shingles perform in Florida!
How Do Luxury Shingles Perform in Florida?
When you make a major investment in your home with a roof replacement, you want to pay for a high-quality roof. And with luxury shingles, that's exactly what you'll get. As we mentioned, these shingles are built using thick layers of asphalt. And because of this thicker composition, luxury shingles are much more durable than other shingle products on the market.

As we've established, luxury shingles have much higher wind resistance than other shingles. But how much higher? Well, old-school 3-tab shingles can only withstand winds up to 70 mph. Architectural shingles improved on this and are rated for winds up to 110 mph, but with proper installation, luxury shingles can resist winds up to 130 mph. This means that these dupes for slate shingles can withstand even a major hurricane!

Wind resistance isn't the only leg up that luxury asphalt shingles offer. Because of their thicker layers of asphalt, they're much more water-resistant than other types of shingles. As a result, you won't have to worry about water eating its way through your shingles! This, on top of their coating of UV-resistant stone granules, makes luxury shingles a fantastic option for homeowners who want a strong, durable roofing system.

What does all of this great protection come to? Well, traditional architectural shingles last for 20-25 years in Florida. While this isn’t bad, it’s considerably less than the 40 years of protection that you can get on average with luxury asphalt shingles. And with a bit of luck and proper maintenance, your luxury shingle roof could last for up to 50 years.
How Much Do Premium Shingles Cost in Florida?


While it's great to know how your new roof will look and perform, we understand that price is always going to be an important factor in planning your roof replacement. The bad news is that luxury shingles are, as you might expect, significantly more expensive than other asphalt shingle options. The good news, though, is that they're much more affordable than a new slate roof.

In Florida, a new slate roof can run you anywhere from $10 to $30 per square foot. While luxury shingles are expensive for a shingle product, they have much more reasonable costs of $8 to $15 per square foot. In other words, a luxury shingle roof could be literally half the price of a slate roof!

Many homeowners don't know how many square feet their roofs are, so these numbers can be a little difficult to apply to your situation. So let's put them into context. In Florida, the average roof is around 1,700 square feet. In other words, a luxury shingle roof costs between $13,600 and $25,500. This makes these roofs especially expensive by shingle standards, but closer to average when compared to other roofing materials in Florida.

We know that not everyone has the budget for a new roof, even when they need one. That's why we offer 0% interest roof replacement financing. With this great way to pay off your roof on your schedule, there's no barrier between you and a high-quality luxury shingle roof!

### Roof Maintenance Tips to Make Your Roof Last Longer in Florida

Taking care of your roof can make the difference between a roof that lasts 15 years and a roof that lasts for 25 years. But for many homeowners, it’s hard to know what kind of upkeep your roof needs. That’s why we’re sharing five simple roof maintenance tips to make your roof last longer!

We’re PITCH Roofing, and we want you to have the strongest, most durable roof possible. Sometimes that means shelling out for roof repairs, but often, it just means taking care of your roof. Keep reading for our tips on how to keep your roof Florida-ready!
5 Roof Maintenance Tips for a Long-Lasting Roof


In Florida, a lot of things are working against your roof. Hurricane-force winds, extreme UV rays, and high humidity can all do a real number on your roof. While your roof is already designed to withstand these conditions, you can get a lot more life out of your roofing system by taking care of it. Let’s cover the five roof maintenance tips that will help you do just that!
Keep Your Gutters Clean
In the summer, Florida sees more than its fair share of rain. And having clean, healthy gutters is an important part of keeping your roof ready. That’s why one of the most common roof maintenance tips you’ll find is making sure that your gutters are free of debris.

When gutters get clogged and backed up, they can no longer transport water off your roof. In fact, they suddenly become a kind of dam that keeps water trapped on your roof. This can lead to water eating away at your roofing material and causing leaks and other roofing headaches.

That’s why an essential roof maintenance tip is keeping up on regular gutter cleanings. In Florida, experts advise that you clean out your gutters at least twice a year unless you have gutter guards, in which case you only need to clean them once a year. If your gutters aren’t blocked but still aren’t working properly, it’s important to schedule timely gutter repair services to get them back in working order before the next storm arrives!
Trim Nearby Tree Limbs
Your roof is in extreme danger during hurricane season. And this danger only increases when you have tree branches hanging over your roof. That’s because during a major storm, these branches can be sent flying onto your roof, which can damage shingles and even crack tiles.

In Florida, palm fronds cause a lot of problems for homeowners. While these branches aren’t especially heavy, they can be whipped up by high winds to damage your shingles over and over again. Our roof maintenance tip is to trim any overhanging tree branches at least twice a year. Additionally, one of those times should be at the start of hurricane season to ensure your roof is ready for the difficult summer months!
Watch Out for Moss & Algae Growth
In humid Florida, moss and algae can grow almost anywhere. Roofs are a popular location for moss and algae because they’re often damp, but as they grow they can weak your shingles and leave your roof vulnerable to various kinds of roofing damage.

If you invest in high-quality Owens Corning shingles, your roof will come with small zinc deposits to prevent algae development. This isn’t foolproof, though, especially if your roof has been around for 15 years or more. If and when you notice algae or moss on your roof, it’s important to act quickly.

Our third roof maintenance tip is to get your roof cleaned as soon as you see signs of algae staining. You can choose to have this done professionally or do it yourself with an algae-killing cleaner. Either way, the important thing is to kill anything living on your roof so that your roofing system doesn’t prematurely age!
Check Your Attic for Moisture
If you have a roof leak, then the earliest signs will appear in your attic. That’s because your attic has the underside of your roof decking, which is only two layers below your shingles. So if water starts getting into your roofing system, the attic will be the first place you can notice the changes.

When performing roof maintenance in your attic, there are a couple of signs of water damage to look out for. The first is a musty smell. As water penetrates your decking, your attic will become more humid, which can allow mold growth. For this reason, you’ll likely smell a leak in your attic before you see it!

You should also look out for discoloration in your roof decking. Discolored or rotting wood is a surefire sign that there’s a leak somewhere in your roof. Our roof maintenance tip is to inspect your attic for leaks every six months! You can also do this as-needed if you ever suspect that you may have a leak.
Clear Your Roof of Debris
In Florida, one of the most important roof maintenance tips is clearing debris off your roof after a storm. High winds can take tree branches and deposit them on your roof, even if you’ve been keeping overhanging branches trimmed. While this isn’t itself dangerous, it can lead to a lot of roofing problems down the line.

That’s because pests love to make homes in branches and other debris on your roof. Additionally, these can degrade your roof and shorten its lifespan by weakening your shingles. These two factors are a surefire recipe for a pest infestation on your roof, which will take the combined efforts of an exterminator and contractor to fully fix.

In our opinion, it’s best to skip this hassle. That’s why we recommend giving your roof a visual once-over after every major storm. You don’t have to get on your roof to look, but walking around your home and visually inspecting your roof is an essential way to stay ahead of roofing problems in Florida!

Following these roof maintenance tips is a great way to get your roof a longer life and minimize repairs. But sooner or later, every roof runs into problems. When this happens, the best thing you can do is get timely roof repairs before the damage can get worse.
