### Can I Replace My Own Roof in Central Florida?

A roof replacement is a major investment. As a result, more than a few Florida homeowners have found themselves wondering: Can I replace my own roof in Florida? And the short answer is yes, it is perfectly legal for you to replace your own roof. However, not everything that’s legal to do is a good idea for everyone to try.

We’re PITCH Roofing, and as your local roofing partners, we’re here to answer all your questions about DIY roof replacements. As experienced contractors, we know the common obstacles and pitfalls that homeowners run into when trying to replace their own roofs. Keep reading for our guide on whether or not you should replace your own roof in Florida!
Can I Replace My Own Roof in Central Florida?


As we’ve established, yes, you can replace your own roof in Florida. Thanks to Florida Statute 489.103(7)(a), every homeowner has the right to work on their own roof, including replacing it. But before you start planning your own roof replacement, it’s a good idea to look at the full process involved.

That’s what we’re here for! Stick with us as we look at the many steps involved in replacing your own roof.
Talk With Your Insurance Company
In theory, you have the right to work on your own roof. But that doesn’t necessarily mean that your insurance will honor your policy if you do. While some insurers will accept any work that passes a final inspection with the county, others only cover work performed by licensed Florida contractors. To make sure you don’t accidentally violate your policy, it’s a good idea to have a quick chat with your insurance agent.

You should also know that your insurance company may not offer coverage for roofing-related injuries to you or anybody else on your policy. This provision is specifically outlined in Florida Statute 489.103(7)(a), so you’ll want to verify what coverage (if any) you can expect to have if you or someone is injured during your DIY roof replacement.
Schedule Your Replacement
While you work on your roof, it’s essentially exposed to the elements. That’s why you want to carefully pick a time when you and anyone else working on your roof can safely work on your roof without rain slowing down the project or a storm hitting in the middle of your replacement. For this reason, we don’t recommend replacing your own roof during hurricane season.

You’ll also want to work around people’s schedules. You, as the homeowner, will have to be on-site at all times that work is being completed, so you’ll need to choose a time when you can take several days off work. Additionally, you’ll want to plan for an extra day or two to replace your roof since the process often takes longer than DIY roofers expect. This means you’ll need to plan roughly a week where both you and anyone working on your roof can focus solely on this project.
Collect Your Roofing Permits
Whether you choose a roofing company or to replace your own roof, permits are a necessary part of any roof replacement. Normally your roofing contractors would handle the bureaucracy for you, but if you’re replacing your own roof, you’ll also have to file your own paperwork. It’s important to be thorough here, as missing an essential form could be the difference between keeping or losing your homeowners insurance policy.

Unfortunately, we can’t tell you exactly what permits you’ll need. While we work across Florida, each county has its own specific rules and requirements. If you want to learn more about what permits you’ll need when replacing your own roof, you should check out your county building department website to see what the local regulations are where you live.
Buy Your Roofing Materials


Once you have your permits, the only thing left to do is buy your roofing materials. If you’re going to replace your own roof, we strongly recommend sticking with asphalt shingles. These are the easiest roofing materials to install, so they’re the most friendly to first-time roofers.

You’ll need more than just shingles, though. A roof is a complex, multi-layered thing. That’s why, in addition to your shingles, you’ll also need:

 	A water-resistant underlayment
 	Venting materials
 	Sealant
 	Ridge caps
 	Flashing
 	Soffit and fascia materials
 	Drip edge

Replace Your Roof
After you’ve completed all this legwork, you’ll finally be ready to replace your own roof. If you’re an experienced contractor, then you’ll know how to install a shingle roof. If not, then there are guides online on how to tear off your old roof and install your new one.

One thing that many of those guides overlook, though, is your roof decking. In the best-case scenario, there will be no damage to this layer of wood support that holds up the rest of your roof. But living in Florida, the best-case scenario is often not what you see with local roofs. More often, there will be at least some water damage to your decking.

As a DIY roofer, you’ll need to know how to identify damaged decking and how to replace it. If not, your roof could end up failing final inspection or, even worse, experience a partial collapse further down the line. This is just one of the many pitfalls that can ruin a DIY roof replacement, so it’s best to only work on your roof if you’re 100% confident in your ability to identify and address roofing concerns like these.
Alternatives to Replacing Your Own Roof
If this sounds like a lot of work, that’s because it is. People dedicate their entire careers to learning how to properly install roofs, so it’s not something to be undertaken lightly. And in most cases, replacing your own roof doesn’t come with many benefits.

While replacing your own roof can save you money if you’re an experienced contractor with a good crew, that isn’t the case for most DIY roofers. More often, you end up paying more in the long run because of problems in your roofing system. And DIY roofs don’t get much in the way of warranties, so we wouldn’t expect any coverage for future repairs.

Additionally, replacing a roof is dangerous, especially if you don’t have the right experience and training. In addition to the physical risk of danger, there is also the risk of financial ruin. The state of Florida requires roofers to carry at least $300,000 in general liability insurance. Without that coverage, you could find yourself in a very uncomfortable position if somebody is seriously injured while replacing your roof.

For all of these reasons, it’s usually easiest just to leave replacing a roof to the professionals. You have the legal right to replace your own roof in Florida. But you also deserve a high-quality, easy roof replacement, and the best way to get that is through professional contractors.

### Is Terracotta Roofing Worth It in Florida?

For Floridians, terracotta roofing is a timeless, luxurious option. These high-quality roofing tiles are renowned for their durability, longevity, and enduring beauty. But are these high-end roofing materials worth all the hype?

We’re here to help you find out. We’re PITCH Roofing, and as veteran Florida roofers, we know terracotta tile roofing better than most. Today, we’re reviewing the pros and cons of terracotta roofing to help you plan your next roof replacement. Keep reading for a complete guide to terracotta tile roofing for Florida homeowners!
What Is Terracotta Roofing?


A terracotta roofing system is surprisingly complex. On the surface, you have your terracotta tiles, which are made of natural clay that has been heat-treated and hardened to ready them for Florida’s harsh weather conditions.

Below this surface layer, you also have a water-resistant underlayment. When installed properly, terracotta roof tiles should be carefully arranged to help water flow seamlessly off your roof. This doesn’t catch every drop, though. For the small amounts of water that can sneak their way through, your underlayment serves as a secondary barrier and protects your vulnerable roof decking.

Your decking is the base layer of your roof, and it’s what everything rests on. With terracotta roofing, decking may sometimes need to be reinforced to hold up the heavy tiles. But as long as the other parts of your roofing system work, there should be no way for the Florida elements to access your decking or damage it.

The final result is a complex, multi-layered roofing system. And while this can offer fantastic protection for your home or commercial property, it has its flaws, too. So before you commit to anything for your next roof replacement, let’s talk about the good and the bad of terracotta roofing in Florida.
Pros of Terracotta Roofing in Florida
No roofing material is “perfect,” but terracotta roofing has plenty of great features. If you’ve lived in Florida for any amount of time, you’ve probably seen more than a few clay tile roofs. Let’s look at why Florida homeowners keep picking this roofing material!
Great Hurricane Resistance
In Florida, everyone is worried about how their roof is going to hold up against the next hurricane. If you want peace of mind, there aren’t many options better than terracotta roofing. With shingle roofs, it’s normal to find a shingle or two in your yard after a major storm. But tiles are sturdier and heavier, which allows them to resist winds of up to 180 mph!

These aren’t just great against the wind, though. Terracotta tiles are also Class A fire-resistant, UV-reflective to minimize sun damage, and highly resistant to rot and pest infestations that can plague shingle roofs. In short, these tiles do a great job protecting you against the worst that Florida’s weather pattern has to offer!
Unmatched Longevity
Terracotta roofing tiles are, bar none, the longest-lasting tiles in Florida. Thanks to all their protective features, terracotta tile roofs last for about 50 years on average. But with proper maintenance and care, terracotta roofing tiles can last for as long as 100 years!

Compare that with asphalt shingle roofs, which only last 20-25 years in Florida. While there’s no denying that terracotta tiles are a high-end roofing material, you can at least make this investment knowing that you won’t need a new roof for a long, long time!
Color and Style Options
A big part of getting a new roof is finding the right one to protect your home. But you’ll also want to consider how your roof contributes to your home’s aesthetic and curb appeal, especially if you plan to sell one day. Luckily, terracotta roofing tiles come with plenty of opportunities for customization.

To start, tiles come in many different colors. Whether you like natural earth tones, the classic red of terracotta tiles, or zanier colors, there is definitely something out there for you. And with options in the style and cut of your tile as well, you can create a pattern that is 100% unique to your home!
Low Maintenance Needs
Every roof will need occasional maintenance and repairs. But compared to other roofing materials, terracotta tiles don’t need much. Aside from the occasional cleaning, there shouldn’t be many occasions when you need to fix an issue with your terracotta tile roof.

There is one potential exception. While it’s by no means common, during a hurricane storm debris can sometimes shatter tiles. The good news, though, is that this is a quick and easy tile roof repair, so you don’t have to worry about a large surprise bill.
Cons of Terracotta Roofing in Florida


While terracotta roofing comes with a lot of upsides, it has its downsides, too. Whether or not the cons outweigh the pros, though, will be for you to decide. So let’s look at the cons of terracotta roofing that you should know before scheduling a roof replacement!
High Installation Costs
We’ve certainly proven that terracotta tile roofs are high-quality. But that quality comes with an equally high cost. In fact, the biggest reason that more homeowners don’t choose terracotta roofing is the high roof installation costs.

So how much will a terracotta tile roof run you? Well, that depends in part on the size and state of your roof. But if you’re looking for a price range, you can expect to pay $12 to $21 per square foot for a terracotta tile roof. Those are high roofing costs, but you also have to consider the quality you’re paying for. Does the protection and longevity of a clay tile roof justify the high cost to install it? Only you can answer that question for yourself.
Replacing Underlayment
Earlier we informed you that terracotta roofing tiles can last for 50 to 100 years or more, and that’s still true. But not every part of your roofing system has that kind of longevity. Specifically, your roof underlayment will probably need replacing every 20 years or so.

That means that every 20 years, you’ll likely need to have your tiles removed and re-applied so that roofers can replace your underlayment with a new one. Thankfully, you won’t need to buy tiles again, so your total roofing costs will be much lower than that of a roof replacement. Still, this process can cost thousands of dollars, so it’s an expense that you should know about before committing to anything.

### Metal Shingle Roof Replacements for Florida Homeowners

For decades, shingles have been the most popular roofing material in North America. Now, as metal roofing is quickly gaining popularity, homeowners are starting to wonder if they can keep the classic look of shingles with the modern protection of steel roofing. And with high-end metal shingles readily available, homeowners can have exactly that.

But what are metal shingles? And do they come with the downsides of regular shingles? We’re PITCH Roofing, and as your local roofing partner, we’re going to answer these questions and more. Stick with us as we tell you everything you need to know about metal roof shingles!
What Are Metal Shingles?


If you’ve ever thought that you’d like a metal roof that looks like shingles, you’re not alone. A lot of homeowners were clamoring for the great durability of metal roofing without the distinctive look. As a result, the roofing industry released a new kind of roofing material: stone-coated steel roofing.

Manufacturers make this material by taking regular metal roofing sheets and coating them in a rust-resistant alloy. Once that has been applied, they then coat the sheets in stone granules. Not only does this provide additional protection, but it also replicates the look of asphalt shingles! And with granules coming in a variety of colors, metal shingles come in almost as many colors as asphalt shingles do.

For years now, Florida homeowners have raved about metal shingles as a way to protect their homes without dramatically changing their aesthetic. But are they really as good as the hype?
Metal Shingles vs. Asphalt Shingles
To see if metal shingles are really worth the investment, it’s worthwhile to compare them to old-school asphalt shingles. But roofing is complicated, so it’s important to compare across different areas. Let’s see how metal shingles and asphalt shingles stack up when compared apples to apples!
Weather Resistance
Asphalt shingles do a fine job standing up against the Florida elements. They’re water-resistant, fire-resistant, and can withstand winds of up to 120 mph when you invest in high-quality architectural shingles. While it’s common to lose a shingle or two in a major storm, your roof should overall hold up well to the Florida elements.

Metal shingles are even better at withstanding Florida’s weather patterns, though. Like asphalt shingles, they’re resistant to water damage and fire. Unlike asphalt shingles, though, metal shingles can resist winds up to 170 mph. And thanks to their protective stone granules, they’re also resistant to impact damage from hail and storm debris!
Roofing Lifespans
Everyone wants a roof that will last for a long time. In recent years, asphalt shingle roofs have achieved new longevity thanks to architectural shingles. Up from the 15-year lifespan of 3-tab shingles, this new roofing technology can last for up to 25 years, even in Florida’s challenging climate!

That’s a great number, but it’s not quite as impressive as metal shingles. Metal roof shingles last between 40 and 50 years on average. This makes them ideal for homeowners who want to go a long time before needing a new roof!
Maintenance
In many ways, metal shingles need less maintenance than asphalt shingles. With these, you don’t have to worry about mildew, mold, or pest infestations like you do with asphalt shingles. But that doesn’t necessarily mean that metal roofs don’t have any maintenance requirements.

In general, metal shingle roofs are very low maintenance. Over time, however, they may need a few repairs to remain in top shape. This includes restoring and repairing their exposed fasteners as well as re-applying paint that may begin to fade over years of UV exposure. In general, though, metal shingles require much less maintenance than asphalt shingles, especially during hurricane season when asphalt shingles tend to end up in the yard!
Energy Efficiency
Having an energy-efficient roof is important both for the planet and your wallet. After all, the more heat that your roof can remove from your home, the less your AC system has to work, which means less power drawn from your home and a lower monthly energy bill!

So are metal or asphalt shingles more energy efficient? In general, asphalt shingles absorb more heat and UV rays than metal, which heats your home. This is because metal shingles are better at reflecting UV rays away from your property. While the color of your shingles is also a factor, metal is just generally a more reflective material.
Installation Cost


At PITCH, we know that everyone is concerned about their roof replacement costs. And if you’re committed to getting the most affordable option, then asphalt shingles are probably the roofing material for you. Architectural shingles average between $5 and $9 per square foot, making them an affordable roofing material that still delivers on quality.

There’s no way around it: metal shingles are significantly more expensive. You’ll usually pay between $7 and $15 per square foot for metal roof shingles. However, it’s important to put this number into context. Yes, metal shingles have a higher up-front cost than asphalt shingles. But when you consider the enhanced protection, longevity, and value added to your property, many homeowners think that metal roof shingles are well worth the higher installation costs.

### Is There a Metal Roof That Looks Like Shingles?

Metal roofs are popular for their longevity and durability, which makes them great at facing off against hurricanes. Unfortunately, not everyone loves the look of metal roofing. Shingle roofs, on the other hand, are popular for their familiar, comforting aesthetic. At the same time, though, these roofs are not nearly as hurricane-ready as metal roofs. These issues have led many homeowners to ask: Can I get a metal roof that looks like shingles?

The good news is that yes, you can. We’re PITCH Roofing, and we know all about metal roofs, shingle roofs, and metal roofs that look like shingles. Keep reading as we fully explain what this option is and how to get it for your Florida roof replacement!
What Type of Metal Roof Looks Like Shingles?


When you want the reliable protection of metal with the welcoming look of shingles, there’s really only one answer: stone-coated steel. With the enduring protection of metal, these roofs can protect against the worst that Florida has to offer without disrupting your home’s aesthetic.

Stone-coated steel roofs combine multiple layers of protection. Manufacturers start by creating metal roofing sheets and then coating them in a rust-resistant alloy, usually one made of aluminum and zinc. This ensures that your metal roof won’t rust, even in Florida’s humid climate!

From there, the metal sheets then get covered in a thick layer of stone granules. The final result is a roof that has the classic look of shingles, but the modern protection of metal. Is a stone-coated steel roof right for your home, though
Pros and Cons of Stone-Coated Steel Roofing
No roofing material is entirely positive or entirely negative. But looking at both sides will give you the information you need to make right decision for your roof replacement. So to make sure you’re ready to choose, let’s talk about the good and the bad of metal roofs that look like shingles!
Pros of Stone-Coated Steel Roofing
There’s a lot to love about stone-coated steel roofing. Some of the biggest advantages that Florida homeowners appreciate include:

 	Longevity: Stone-coated steel roofs last for about 50 years on average. This makes them twice as long-lasting as a shingle roof!
 	Impact Resistance: The protective stones on these roofs aren’t just there to make your roof look like shingles. They also serve as an additional layer of protection. Specifically, these stones are great for standing up against hail or storm debris without denting!
 	Home Value: A metal roof is already going to raise your home’s value. But a metal roof that looks like shingles will raise property values even more, making these one of the best roofing investments you can make!
 	Wind Resistance: Stone-coated steel roofing is a great way to get a roof that can stand up to hurricane-force winds. A metal roof that looks like shingles can withstand winds up to 170 mph!

All of these are great reasons to invest in a stone-coated steel roof. But now that we’ve looked at the good side, we have to ask: What’s the bad side?
Cons of Stone-Coated Steel Roofing
While stone-coated steel roofs are great, they’re not perfect. And Floridians have several key complaints that you should know about before choosing this material. Let’s look at the negatives so you can make an informed choice!

 	Regular Maintenance: In most ways, these roofs require minimal maintenance and hold up well. There is one exception, though: their paint. The paint binds the granules together, but over the years, it may need to be re-applied to prevent degradation.
 	Difficult Installation: Stone-coated steel roofs are much harder to install than shingles. This doesn’t create problems for you as a homeowner, but it does mean that you need to be especially careful about which roofers you choose. Inexperienced roofers could turn your new metal roof into a disaster!
 	Exposed Fasteners: Stone-coated steel roofs are drilled down into your roof during installation. This secures the roof but leaves the fasteners exposed. Over time, the fasteners can get worn down and may need occasional repairs to keep your roof secure.

While there are definitely downsides to a metal roof that looks like shingles, most homeowners find that the good outweighs the bad. There is still one important factor that we haven’t talked about yet, though: cost.

And with the increased value to your home, you could even end up making some of that money back if you decide to sell during the lifetime of your stone-coated steel roof!

### 5 Causes of Roof Leaks Florida Homeowners Need to Know

A leaking roof can be a big headache to deal with. Depending on your specific leak, you could be looking at anything from a quick roof repair to a full roof replacement. This kind of uncertainty is scary, but by knowing the common causes of roof leaks, you can identify your issue and get some peace of mind.

PITCH Roofing is your local roofing partner. Made up of experienced contractors, we’ve fixed our fair share of leaks over our years as Florida roofers. As a result, we know the common causes of roof leaks in Florida and what you can do about them. Keep reading for our guide on identifying the source of your leaking roof!
The 5 Most Common Causes of Roof Leaks in Florida


The cause of your roof leak can tell you a lot about how serious the issue is. While all roof leaks need quick resolution, there’s a world of difference between having new shingles hammered onto your roof and replacing the whole thing. To help you anticipate what kind of roofing services you might need, let’s take a look at Florida’s biggest causes of leaks!
1. Broken/Missing Asphalt Shingles
Asphalt shingles are one of the most popular roofing materials on the market. That’s thanks to their low cost and great durability. But these roofing materials aren’t perfect. In Florida, it’s common for shingles to crack under the sun or be blown off entirely by high winds. Coincidentally, these are also some of the biggest causes of roof leaks in Florida.

Your shingles help keep water moving of your roof without allowing it to damage the more vulnerable parts of your roofing system. But when they’re damaged, they can’t perform that job anymore. As a result, your underlayment has more pressure on it, and when that fails, it’s normal for leaks to develop.

The good news is that this is a fairly easy repair if you move quickly and don’t let the water damage spread. It’s also easy to check for — just take a look at your roof and see if you can spot any missing or damaged shingles. If you don’t want to get on your roof, binoculars are great for this task!
2. Chimney Roof Leaks
If your home has a chimney, this could be where water is entering your structure. When working properly, your chimney shouldn’t let in any light. But a storm or wear and tear can break it down and allow water to enter your home, making chimneys one of the most common causes of roof leaks in Florida.

There are five clear signs of chimney roof leaks:

 	A musty smell from your fireplace
 	Rust on your firebox
 	Ceiling water stains near your fireplace
 	White stains on your chimney
 	Gaps or cracks in your chimney’s bricks

How much fixing your chimney roof leak will depend on the type and extent of damage to your chimney. Generally speaking though, these repairs can be as cheap as $150 or as expensive as $2,000. For a more accurate figure, your best option is to start collecting roofing quotes!
3. Problems with Vent Boots
A vent boot is a kind of protective flashing that helps waterproof pipes that come out of your roof. However, over time this waterproofing can fail, and the pipes become the perfect avenue for water to enter your roofing system. Vent boots rarely stay water-tight for more than 10 years at the most, which makes them a very common cause of roof leaks.

Most often, damaged vent boots will show via water stains on the ceiling and walls just below the pipe. If you suspect that your leak could be caused by an issue with a vent boot, you can verify this by safely getting on your roof and inspecting any pipes. If the vent boot has been damaged, you’ll likely see gaps or cracks around your pipe.

The good news is that fixing these issues is usually quick and easy. If there’s no major water damage, this should be an affordable repair that prevents any more water from entering your home.
4. Full or Damaged Gutters


Your gutters play a crucial role in moving water off your roof efficiently. By carrying water off your roof and depositing it away from your foundation, they keep your roof dry and your home secure. But when gutters get clogged or damaged, they can’t function as normal.

When water isn’t removed by your gutters, it can take longer to drain from your roof. This gives water time to sneak its way into cracks and crevices, which is a common cause of roof leaks. If your gutters are full, then the solution is as simple as clearing out any debris so that water can flow through them again.

If a storm has damaged them, though, you’ll need to have them professionally repaired. The signs of gutter damage are usually easy to spot, and include twisted gutters, sagging gutters, or gutters that are pulling away from your home.
5. An Old Roof
Unfortunately, among all of the causes of roof leaks, this may be the worst one. Why? Because there’s nothing that can be done to fix it. The only solution to leaks caused by a roof reaching the end of its life is to get a new roof.

If your shingle roof is leaking and it’s more than 20 years old, there’s a good chance that it’s time to replace your roof. In some rare cases, you might be able to get a patch for the leak. But in all likelihood, another leak will spring up shortly, and the only way to stop this pattern is to invest in a shingle roof replacement.

### Signs You Need a New Roof

When it comes to roof replacements, timing is everything. Getting one too early is a waste of money, but getting one too late could endanger your home and lead to problems with your homeowners insurance. That’s why you need to know the signs you need a new roof!

The veteran roofers at PITCH Roofing have been handling Florida roof replacements for a long time. Thanks to our experience, we know when to repair roofs and when to replace them. Keep reading for our complete guide to telling if your Florida roof needs replacing!
7 Signs You Need a New Roof


There are a lot of ways you can tell if it’s time to replace your roof. Not all of these signs mean that you have to replace your roof immediately, but if you have more than one, it could mean that it’s time to invest in a roof replacement to keep your home protected against the unpredictable Florida weather.

Now, let’s talk about the biggest signs you need a new roof!
Age of Your Roof
Remember how we said having one of these signs doesn’t necessarily mean you need a new roof? This is the exception. If your roof has reached the end of its lifespan, then you need a new roof. Waiting too long could lead to risking your insurance coverage, not to mention the risk of your roof failing.

But how do you know when your roof is at its maximum age?

That depends in part on the roof. The average lifespans of different roofing materials are:

 	Asphalt shingles: 20-25 years
 	Corrugated metal roofing: 20-25 years
 	Standing seam metal roofing: 40-70 years
 	Concrete tiles: 50 years
 	Clay tiles: 50-100 years

If your roof is at the end of its life, there’s no amount of repairs that can make it safe for your home. The best thing you can do is follow this sign you need a new roof and invest in a roof replacement!
Many Missing Shingles
Having a shingle or two fly off during a storm is not necessarily a sign you need a new roof. However, missing a large section of your roof is more than roof repairs can handle. So how many shingles can your roof lose before it needs replacing?

The rule of thumb is 25%. If your roof is missing more than a quarter of its shingles, then your best bet is to replace the whole thing. Bear in mind that your roof could need replacing even if you’re missing a smaller number of shingles, though. This is especially likely if your roof has significant leaking and water damage. If you’re unsure whether or not your roof needs replacing, a roof inspection is a great way to get a clear, dependable answer!
Neighbors Getting Roof Replacements
When a neighborhood is constructed, many of the homes are built at the same time. This means that neighbors often have roofs of similar ages. So if you start seeing shingles stacked up on your neighbors’ homes, it might be time for your roof to be replaced.

Use your best judgment with this sign you need a new roof, though. Different materials can last different amounts of time, so having one neighbor replace their roof isn’t necessarily a sign that you need to replace yours. But if all the homes around you are getting new roofs, it’s at least worth checking the age of your roof to see if you’re due.
Cracked or Curled Shingles


Missing shingles aren’t the only sign of damage to your roof. When large sections of your roof have cracked or curled shingles, it could be time to get a new roof. Shingles crack or curl as a result of baking under the hot Florida sun, and as they break down, they lose their ability to protect your home.

Like with missing shingles, 25% is the general number of damaged shingles before you need a replacement. So while replacing a small number of these shingles is easy, you don’t want to ignore a larger section of damage, since this is a clear sign you need a new roof!
Granules in the Gutters
Shingles aren’t just made of asphalt. They also have a coating of protective stone granules. As shingles age, though, these granules can fall off your shingles. Most often, you’ll find them in your gutters or collecting near your downspouts.

This is a serious sign you need a new roof because it shows that your shingles are breaking down. They only do this at the end of their lifespan, so it’s important to act quickly before they degrade further and your home loses the protection it needs to get through hurricane season.
Roof Sagging
A lot of things can cause roof sagging, and none of them are good. Poor roof installation can lead to problems evenly distributing weight, which causes sagging, or trapped water can weigh down part of your roof and lead to sagging. Regardless of the cause, this is a major structural concern.

In most cases, the only cure for roof sagging is a roof replacement. However, it’s best to contact a professional and have them look at your roof to determine if this is a sign you need a new roof or not. In some cases, you may only need a roof repair, which will be much cheaper!
Water Damage
A leaking roof is a serious problem. While not all leaks require roof replacements to fix, extensive water damage can weaken the entire structure of your roof. As water eats away at your roof decking, your home may no longer be able to support the weight of your roof.

If your home has a leak, call a contractor ASAP to take a look and identify both the cause and the extent of the damage. If your leak has been letting in water for a long time, this is probably a sign you need a new roof. But if the damage is new and minimal, you will likely only need a quick repair!

### Should You Call Contractors or Handyman Roofers?

Sometimes, a handyman roofer is just what you need. Other times, though, your situation calls for more experience than a handyman can offer, and you’d be better served by calling a roofing contractor. But how do you tell which you need? And what’s the difference between what a handyman roofer can do vs. what a contractor can do?

We’re PITCH Roofing, and we’ve got answers. As roofing contractors, we know where handyman roofers shine and where a different set of skills is needed. To help you tell which one you need, let’s start by covering the difference between handymen and contractors!
Handyman Roofers vs. Roofing Contractors


Handyman roofers are just that — handy. They have solid, generalized knowledge of roofing systems and how to help maintain them. This makes them well-suited to a variety of roofing tasks. And since they’re usually individuals rather than companies, they also usually have lower overhead costs, which lets them offer lower prices than most contractors.

A roofing contractor is slightly different. We also work on roofs, but contractors have more in-depth knowledge and experience with roofing. This means we're able to handle larger or more complex roofing jobs. On the flip side, though, you can expect to pay more for a roofing contractor to work on your roof.

So which one do you call when you have a roofing problem: handyman roofers or contractors? Well, that depends on your problem and on your roof. Let’s look at when you should call a handyman and when to call a contractor!
When to Call Handyman Roofers or Contractors
There are a lot of factors that determine who’s right for your roof repair job. These include the scope of the work, your timeline, and the state of your roof. To make sure you’re calling in the right pros, we’re going to talk about each of these important areas and who to call to fix your roofing problems!
Scope of Work
Handyman roofers are great at minor repairs. Think of things like replacing a couple of missing shingles or re-adjusting your gutters after they’ve been knocked down by high winds. These are tasks that handyman roofers excel at because they require some roofing knowledge without needing total expertise.

For other roofing jobs, though, you may need more help. Contractors have more specialized training, which makes them better able to handle larger roofing problems. These include roof leaks, damage to your decking, and any large-scale repair work.

In short, handyman roofers are great for when you have a small problem. That’s not just because their experience is ideal for minor issues, either. Thanks to their lower overhead costs, they’ll probably be able to offer you a better deal than a contractor.

For bigger jobs, though, there’s no substitute for a contractor’s experience. That’s why we don’t recommend calling a handyman roofer just to save money. While you might pay lower up-front costs, hiring the wrong person for your roof repair is one of the most costly mistakes a homeowner can make.
Timeline
Another advantage of handyman roofers is that they can work quickly. Sometimes, roofing contractors book up weeks in advance, especially after a major hurricane when many homeowners have major roofing damage. So if you lost a shingle or two in a storm and need a quick repair, handyman roofers may be your best bet for quick service.

Just like we don’t recommend choosing a handyman only to save money, it’s not a good idea to pick handyman roofers solely for quick service, either. Having someone out to quickly fix a repair that’s within their wheelhouse is great. But having someone out to fix a repair that’s beyond their skill set could lead to even more damage to your roof, which will make it cost even more when you eventually call a contractor to fix the source of the issue.
Your Roof


In most cases, handyman roofers are best suited to shingle roofs. That works out great since asphalt shingles are the most popular roofing material in North America. But if you have a tile or metal roof, you’d probably get better service from a contractor.

Part of what makes shingles so popular is how simple they are. While every roof has different layers and parts, shingles are the easiest to work with since they’re simple to install. This means that picking handyman roofers for a shingle roof repair can make a lot of sense.

For metal and tile, though, the installation and repair process is more complicated. Additionally, getting materials can be harder for handymen who don’t have the same relationships with manufacturers as contractors do.

Finally, you also need to consider the state of your roof. Roof sagging is a common problem that indicates your roof is not structurally sound. If you call out a handyman roofer, they could try to access your roof and hurt themself. When you suspect that your roof could be dangerous to access, it’s time to call in qualified roofing contractors. We know how to handle serious, structural damage like this, which is well outside the scope of handyman roofing.
Get a Free Estimate from Experienced Roofing Contractors
We’re contractors, but we freely admit it — handyman roofers do great work and in some situations, they could be exactly what you need. But if you’re dealing with a major roofing issue, there is no substitute for experienced Florida roofing contractors.

Whether you’re committed to going with a contractor or you want to explore your options, your next step is getting a free, no-obligation estimate. All you have to do is call us at (727) 677-4824, or you can even schedule your free estimate online! PITCH is made up of friendly professionals, so we’ll be happy to answer all of your questions and help you find the best solution for your roofing woes.

Choosing between handyman roofers and contractors is tough. But with roofing problems, the worst thing you can do is wait for the damage to get worse. Reach out to PITCH today, and we’ll show you how veteran contractors like us can go above and beyond to earn your business!

### Pros and Cons of Exposed Fastener Metal Roofs

With Florida’s hurricane seasons only getting stronger, more and more homeowners are looking for affordable metal roofing options. In recent years, one option has stood out among the rest: exposed fastener metal roofs. Homeowners still have questions though, primarily about performance and costs.

That’s what we’re here for. PITCH Roofing is your local roofing partner, and today we’re using our roofing know-how to answer all of your questions about exposed fastener metal roofing. Many people know this name without knowing exactly what it means, so let’s start with answering the biggest question!
What Is an Exposed Fastener Metal Roof?


An exposed fastener metal roof uses metal roofing sheets just like any other metal roofing system. These sheets are most often made of galvanized steel, but aluminum is also a common option for its improved rust resistance.

These roofing systems are also called crimped roofing or 5V roofing because of the ridged pattern used in the metal roofing panels. But what really makes these roofs stand out how they adhere to your roof.

Exposed fastener metal roofs drill down directly into your roof. This ensures that your roof is firmly attached and won’t go anywhere even during a major hurricane. However, having exposed fasteners has its downsides as well.

To get some clarity on the good and bad of exposed fastener metal roofing, let’s talk about how these roofs perform in Florida!
Does Crimped Metal Roofing Work in Florida?
An exposed fastener metal roof gives you all the things that you love about metal roofing. You’ve got a superior lifespan to shingles, with these roofs lasting about 30 years on average. These roofs also offer increased durability, with wind resistance up to 140 mph. That means your roof will be capable of withstanding a Category 4 hurricane!

This is the kind of performance that asphalt shingles just can’t match. But are there any downsides to getting an exposed fastener metal roof?

In some ways, having your metal roofing sheets drilled onto your roof is a good thing. After all, what better way to be sure that your roof isn’t going anywhere in a storm? But there are downsides to this approach. Specifically, your roof’s fasteners are exposed to the elements. This means they can wear and rust, which can lead to premature aging of your roof.

Additionally, your metal roofing sheets can’t move once they’ve been drilled down. This sounds good, but metal naturally expands and contracts with heat. Sitting under Florida’s hot sun all day, your roof will want to expand but won’t be able to. This is why exposed fastener metal roofs don’t last as long as standing seam roofs, which can last for 40-70 years.

It isn’t all bad, though. Exposed fastener metal roofs are still strong and durable; they just aren’t the strongest or the longest-lasting metal roof option. They are, however, one of the most affordable. So how much does an exposed fastener metal roof cost?
The Cost of an Exposed Fastener Metal Roof in Florida


Talking about roofing prices is always tricky. After all, how much you pay will come down to your roof’s size and unique features, the roofers you choose, and the ever-changing manufacturing prices. But when getting an exposed fastener metal roof, it’s safe to say that you’re getting the most affordable metal roof on the market.

On average, installing an exposed fastener metal roof costs between $7 and $12 per square foot on the Florida market. At the same time, the average size of a roof in Florida is around 1,700 square feet. This puts the average cost of an exposed fastener metal roof between $11,900 and $20,400!

Now, is this the cheapest option on the market? Of course not — asphalt shingles are substantially more affordable. However, this is definitely the most affordable option for a metal roof in Florida. If you want the strength and durability of a metal roof, there is no more affordable option!

However, installation costs aren’t the only things you should consider. At the end of the day, exposed fastener metal roofs need maintenance. In Florida, we usually find that fasteners may need replacing after roughly 7-10 years, so it’s a good idea to keep up on your roof inspections. Roof leaks are a common sign that your roof’s fasteners are damaged, which means you should expect your roof to need repairs at some point in its lifetime.

At this point, we’ve covered the big stuff: what exposed fastener metal roofs are, how they perform, and how much you’ll pay for one. Now it’s time to clear up any lingering questions!

### FAQs About Missing Shingles on Your Roof

After a hurricane, missing shingles are one of the most common problems in Florida. But while this problem is common, Florida homeowners still have a lot of questions about it. Are missing shingles a serious problem? Can they lead to leaks? Should you try to fix them yourself?

Today, we’re answering all of these questions and more. We’re PITCH Roofing, and as veteran Florida roofers, we know shingle roofs better than anyone. Today, we’re covering the frequently asked questions that we get about shingles. And we’re starting with the one we get most often: Why did my shingles get blown off my roof?
Why Did the Wind Blow Shingles Off My Roof?


When you find missing shingles in your yard, you might think that there was a failure in your roofing system. After all, you paid good money for your roof to be installed, so if you see missing shingles, it’s natural to think that something went wrong with your materials or roof installation.

But the truth is that shingles just aren’t built to withstand certain winds. Even for top-of-the-line Owens Corning products, it’s rare to find shingles that can withstand winds exceeding 130 mph. So while nobody likes to find missing shingles in their yard, this isn’t usually a sign that there’s an overall problem with your roof.

This leads to another common question that we get. Does losing shingles in a storm mean I have to replace my roof?
Do I Need to Replace a Roof With Missing Shingles?
Since your roof can lose shingles without having any structural flaws, the good news is that missing a few shingles doesn’t mean that you need a roof replacement. Notice that we said a few, though. While losing shingles is normal, losing too many of them could put your whole roof in jeopardy.

As a rule of thumb, if your roof still has more than half of its shingles, then there’s no need for a replacement. While replacing a larger amount of missing shingles will take more time and money, it should still be a far cry from the cost of a roof replacement.

The amount of shingles you lose isn’t the only factor here, though. Time is also extremely important. If you wait too long to get repairs, water could damage your decking and other parts of your roof. In cases like these, you’ll need a roof replacement to remove the water-damaged sections. Thankfully, however, moving quickly is usually enough to keep the job limited to just a repair.
Can I Replace Missing Shingles Myself?
DIY roof repair can be a good way to save money, but it isn’t always the best choice. So can you replace your own missing shingles? Well, that depends on a few factors.

A few of the considerations you should make include:

 	Number of Missing Shingles: Replacing one or two missing shingles is much easier than replacing entire sections of your roof.
 	Water Damage: If your roof has sustained water damage after losing shingles, it will require professional help. If you can’t identify water damage on a roof, then it’s best to let experienced contractors handle the job.
 	Roofing Experience: Have you done professional work on roofs before? Do you know that replacing shingles involves more than just hammering new shingles into place? If so, replacing your own missing shingles could make sense in your case!

Whether or not you should replace your own missing shingles is a case-by-case decision. But if you’re at all unsure of your ability to do the job successfully, it’s best to leave the work to professionals. The last thing that you need when handling a roof repair is to make a mistake that voids your warranty or, even worse, risks your homeowners insurance coverage!
How Can I Prevent Missing Shingles in the Future?


As we’ve established, losing a few shingles isn’t uncommon. If a strong enough hurricane hits your area, there isn’t much you can do about losing a few shingles, especially if your roof is getting on in years. But that doesn’t mean you have to accept losing shingles as a fact of life.

As a homeowner, you have plenty of ways to minimize your risk of losing shingles. Some of these strategies are:

 	Investing in Quality Shingles: We almost never recommend 3-tab shingles. Instead, most homes benefit from architectural shingles, which are much better at resisting high winds. As a bonus, they also look a lot better than 3-tab asphalt shingles!
 	Replacing an Old Roof: Losing a shingle or two in a major hurricane isn’t strange. But if your roof is 20 years old or older and you’re losing shingles in seemingly every storm, then it may be time for a roof replacement. New roofs are much better at withstanding high winds, so this could save you money in roof repairs over the long term!
 	Keep Up on Roof Repairs: Sometimes, unaddressed roofing problems can lead to losing shingles. These include things like UV damage, mold, and pest infestations. If you’re consistently losing shingles and can’t figure out why, it could be because you’re not keeping up with your roof maintenance!

There is no way to prevent losing shingles 100% of the time. But by investing in your roof and taking care of it, you can greatly lower your risk and save yourself a lot of money on roof repair costs.

It often takes time for roofers to inspect a roof, provide a quote, and start on a job, especially if you plan on comparing estimates. ### How to Compare Roof Estimates in Florida

Collecting estimates isn’t the most fun part of getting roof work done, but it’s arguably the most important. Whether your roof sustained damage in a hurricane or it’s just getting too old, knowing how to compare roof estimates is key to getting reliable workmanship at a fair price.

We should know — we’ve been working on roofs across Florida for years. We’re PITCH Roofing, your local roofing partner. Today, we’re reviewing how to compare roofing estimates to make sure you’re getting the best price without sacrificing quality. To start, let’s look at what should be included in a good roofing estimate!
What’s in a Roofing Estimate?


If you ask for a roofing quote and all the contractor sends back is a price, run. Real, experienced contractors know that a roofing estimate is much more than just a repair or replacement price.

At the bare minimum, a good roof estimate will include:

 	The overall cost of the job
 	Payment terms, such as when payment is due and how much of a deposit is required
 	A list of materials to be used during the job
 	The cost of cleanup and debris removal, including the cost of renting a dumpster
 	Licensing and permitting information
 	Estimated dates for the beginning and end of the job

With all this information, a good roofing estimate tends to be fairly long. At a minimum, it should be about a page in length, if not several. Once you’ve got this estimate in hand, it’s essential that you know how to compare roof estimates to make sure you’re getting the best possible deal.
How to Compare Roof Estimates
As we’ve established, roofing quotes come with a lot of information. This can be helpful since you need to know what you’re paying for, but it also makes it complicated to compare two estimates apples to apples.

To help you identify the important information, let’s talk about the different areas to look at when considering how to compare roof estimates!
Scope of Work
At PITCH, we help our customers compare estimates all the time. And one of the biggest points of confusion we see is with the scope of work on each estimate. Often, customers will say that they’ve been offered a better price by another contractor. But when they send over the estimate for us to take a look, the price quoted is for an entirely different, much smaller project!

When comparing roof estimates, always look closely at the scope of work. On each estimate, there should be a clear definition of the work to be completed. This itemized list should include everything from tearing off your roof to replacing sections of your decking to cleaning up after the job.

Sometimes, an estimate will be missing a key part of the job. Roofers sometimes do this to lower their costs and out-bid their competitors. But you’re the one who ends up paying the price since your roofing work is only partially completed. That’s why it’s essential to compare roof estimates by their total scope of work, not just the cost!
Roofing Materials
Alongside the scope of work, your roofing materials are a key part of any estimate. This doesn’t just mean your shingles or tiles, though. A roofing system is complex, with many moving parts. And a good roofing estimate will include all the materials that your contractors will use for your roofing project.

To give you an idea of what you can expect to see, let’s talk about one of the most common roofing jobs in Florida: installing a new shingle roof. For a project like this, your roofing materials list should include:

 	Shingles (including brand and color)
 	Drip edge
 	Water-resistant underlayment
 	Roof vents
 	Flashing
 	Pipe boots
 	Ridge caps

When comparing roofing estimates, you should be concerned if any one of these materials is absent. It’s also important to consider the quality of the materials when comparing estimates. For example, high-quality Owens Corning shingles often cost more than generic, less prestigious shingles. They also perform better, though, so it’s important to account for more than just the price listed on your estimate!
Workmanship & Material Warranties


The value of a roof isn’t just in the installation. Your warranties will affect your roofing costs for years to come. And when learning how to compare roof estimates, there are a lot of advantages that come with understanding workmanship and material warranties.

A workmanship warranty is just what it sounds like — a warranty on the work done by your contractors. This applies to issues with installation, so having strong, long-lasting workmanship warranties is one way that roofers can offer peace of mind in their abilities. Usually, workmanship warranties are only backed by the contractor.

A material warranty applies to, you guessed it, the materials. The manufacturer offers these warranties so that the customer can be confident that they’re being sold quality, durable materials. If your shingles were to fail due to a manufacturing issue, for example, you could have the manufacturer pay for new shingles to be installed.

Different contractors can offer wildly different warranties. For example, as Owens Corning Preferred Contractors, we can offer long-lasting workmanship and material warranties. This ensures that your roof is protected from all sides for years to come!

### What Is the Best Type of Roof for Hurricane Season?

Hurricane season 2024 has been an especially active one, especially for Central Florida. With Helene and Milton causing substantial amounts of destruction, many homeowners are asking themselves what the best type of roof for hurricane season is.

If you’re looking to keep your home safe by getting a high-quality roof, PITCH Roofing is ready to help. As experienced Florida roofers, we’ve seen it all. And we know which roofs do and don’t have what it takes to stand up against hurricanes. Today, we’re using that knowledge to help you prep for the worst that Florida’s weather has to offer!

First, though, let’s talk a bit about how Florida’s hurricane season can affect your roof.
Types of Hurricane Roofing Damage in Florida


Did you know that high winds aren’t the only way that a hurricane can damage your roof? While it’s true that major hurricanes can tear the shingles from your roof, there are plenty of other ways for a hurricane to be dangerous. And if you want to find the best type of roof for hurricane season, then you’ll need to know what your roof is up against.

To that end, let’s talk about how a hurricane can pose a danger to your roof!
Wind-driven Rain
You probably aren’t shocked to hear that hurricanes are wet. But more than that, the way that rain works in a hurricane is uniquely dangerous. Hurricane-force winds give the rain extra force, which helps it penetrate into your roofing system. This is why you may find your roof leaking during a hurricane even if it doesn’t normally.

Even if your roof isn’t normally prone to leaks, though, this is still a problem. That’s because this wind-driven rain is still doing water damage to your roof decking. If you see water coming through your ceiling during a hurricane, it’s a good idea to talk to a roof repair pro after the storm has passed. And when planning for the best type of roof for hurricane season, it’s important to prioritize water resistance!
Standing Water
As we established, hurricanes have the potential to deposit a lot of water onto your roof. And if your roof isn’t equipped to drain properly, you could find yourself with water trapped on your roof. This could be due to improper roof installation or storm damage to your gutters.

In either case, it’s going to cause a problem. Standing water can slowly eat through your roof — even water-resistant flat roofing materials. In the worst-case scenario, trapped water could become too heavy and lead to roof sagging, which is a sign of severe structural damage to your roof.

In many cases though, you won’t see signs of standing water until long after the storm has passed. That’s why it’s important to get a roof inspection after major storms and keep an eye out for water stains on the ceiling and other signs of roof leaks!
Storm Debris
High winds can do a lot more than just tear shingles from your roof. They can also turn branches and everyday trash into deadly projectiles. When high winds blow into town, they can send this storm debris flying into your roof, which can knock shingles loose, crack tiles, and dent metal roofs.

As you can see, this issue can affect nearly any type of roof. That makes finding the best type of roof for hurricanes especially difficult! However, while no roof is immune to damage from storm debris, you can prioritize roofing materials with great impact resistance.
The Best Type of Roof for Hurricane Season in Florida


Figuring out the best type of roof for hurricane readiness is tricky. After all, “best” applies to a variety of different categories, like durability, longevity, and price. And even if you don’t pick the very best roofing material for hurricane resistance, you can still pick a strong, resilient version of your chosen material.

To show you what we mean, we’re reviewing the three best types of roofs for hurricane season and which sub-types offer the best protection!
3. Asphalt Shingles
Asphalt shingles are the most popular roofing material in North America. There are plenty of reasons why — they’re hardy, affordable, and last for 20-25 years on average. They are not, however, the best type of roof for hurricane season.

That has a lot to do with their wind resistance. Traditional 3-tab shingles rarely had wind ratings higher than 80 mph or so. This made them completely incapable of standing up against hurricane-force winds, and many homeowners found themselves replacing their roofs after even Category 1 hurricanes.

There is a better option, though. New architectural shingle technology has made asphalt shingles thicker and much hardier, with popular shingles able to withstand winds of up to 130 mph. This is due to their being multi-layered with fiberglass and asphalt, which makes them weightier and harder to remove via wind. While asphalt shingles may not be the best type of roof for hurricane season, architectural shingles are definitely the best shingles for hurricane resistance!
2. Tile Roofing
Tile roofs are among some of the most popular in Central Florida. Spanish roof tiles have a long history in Florida, and even today tile roofing reflects luxury, beauty, and long-term protection. In fact, tile roofs last more than 50 years on average! So why don’t they have the number one spot as the best type of roof for hurricane season?

One reason: impact damage. While roofing tiles are strong and resistant to wind, they’re also very brittle. So when high winds knock a tree branch into tiles, they can crack or even shatter them. This then creates an opportunity for wind-driven rains to damage the more vulnerable parts of your roofing system.

Other than that, though, tile roofs do a great job holding up against hurricanes. If you want the best protection, we recommend clay roofing tiles. Not only are they beautiful, but they’re also durable enough to last for 70 to 100 years or more!
1. Metal Roofing
Metal roofs are the gold standard for hurricane resistance. They’re long-lasting, for one thing, with lifespans of 40-70 years on average. But they’re also capable of withstanding severe hurricane winds, including winds exceeding 140 mph.

If you want the best of the best when it comes to protecting your home against hurricanes, two options stand out. The first is standing seam metal roofs. These roof panels adhere beneath the panel, which means there are no exposed fasteners that can be worn down by the elements. This means your protection will last for a long time and you’ll need minimal repairs, even after major storms.

The other top contender is stone-coated steel roofing. By coating steel roofing in protective stone granules, manufacturers greatly increase the impact resistance of metal roofing. This means no dents from storm debris! And if you want the protection of metal roofing without the distinctive look, this option offers the best of both worlds!
Get a Free Quote for the Best Type of Roof for Hurricane Season in Florida
No matter what the best type of roof for hurricane season looks like for you, you always have good, durable options. And if you want to know how much your new, hurricane-resistant roof could cost you, PITCH has your back.

### How to Pay for a New Roof: The 4 Best Options

Whether your home or business has recently gone through a hurricane or just gotten too old, you need a new roof. But roof replacements aren’t always in the budget. That’s why we’re here to cover how to pay for a new roof in Florida, and how to make sure you’re getting a great deal.

We’re PITCH Roofing, and as Florida roofing veterans, we know a thing or two about financing roof replacements. We’ve worked with customers across Central Florida to help them pay for necessary roof replacements promptly so their homes didn’t have to go unprotected. Today, we’re sharing what we know to help you get a new roof on terms that make sense for you and your wallet!
How to Pay for a New Roof in Florida


Technically, there are plenty of ways to pay for a new roof in the Sunshine State. But rather than taking out a high-interest, short-term loan, there are four viable strategies to pay for a new roof. These include:

 	Paying cash
 	Financing with your roofers
 	Using your homeowners insurance
 	Getting a home equity loan

Let’s take a look at each option individually so that you can find how to pay for a new roof in a way that works best for you!
1. Cash
If you’re lucky, you might have the funds to pay for your roof replacement up front. And in some ways, this is the best way to pay for a roof. You don’t have to worry about interest rates, there’s no payment plan, and you’ll likely end up paying the least overall since you don’t have a loan accruing interest over time.

But not everyone with the money to pay for a new roof should pay in cash. Some of the reasons that a homeowner may choose not to pay in cash include:

 	Saving Emergency Funds: If your savings are roughly equal to the cost of your roof replacement, paying in cash may not be a good idea. If you have a real emergency, you’d have no funds left over to handle it. That’s why you should only pay cash if you will still have a comfortable emergency fund after paying for your roof replacement.
 	Leveraging Financing: Sometimes you can get low- or zero-interest roof financing. This means you’ll pay the same amount of money over a more comfortable schedule without additional costs!
 	Tax Advantages: Depending on how you finance your roof, you could end up saving on your taxes by not paying cash. This is especially common with home equity loans.

Any of these reasons could be motivation enough to not pay cash. While paying cash is sometimes the easiest and simplest option, it isn’t always. So when considering how to pay for a new roof, it’s important to think carefully and not just pay in cash because you technically can.
2. Roof Financing
Often, the easiest way to get financing is through your roofing company of choice. Most roofers offer these loans, and they’re usually easy to qualify for. But not all roofers offer the same deals on their roof financing.

At PITCH, we make roof financing one of the best ways to pay for a new roof. We do this by offering 0% interest on your new roof for one year. This means that if you can pay your loan off within 12 months, you won’t pay any extra interest! If you need a longer financing schedule, then you’ll still enjoy a year of no interest before it becomes a low-interest loan.

For homeowners who have not lived in their homes long enough to build up great sums of equity or especially high credit scores, this is the most accessible way to finance your roof. If you decide to finance your roof with your roofing company, just make sure to know the exact terms that you’re agreeing to. And if you don’t feel like you can trust roofers to give you a fair deal on financing, then you probably shouldn’t trust them to replace your roof, either!
3. Homeowners Insurance


In some cases, you may be able to use homeowners insurance to pay for a new roof. And Florida homeowners know that when considering how to pay for a new roof, insurance is the cheapest option. However, you can only use homeowners insurance to pay for a new roof in select circumstances.

So how do you know if you can use homeowners insurance to pay for your roof replacement? You should always check your policy or talk with your agent if you’re not sure whether or not your insurance will pay for your roof. But in general, your roof must have been damaged in a severe weather event to qualify for insurance coverage.

This means that insurers will generally pay for roof replacements due to issues like:

 	High winds
 	Water damage from a storm
 	Hail damage

If you think that your roof qualifies for a payout of your homeowners insurance policy, check out our guide to getting insurance to pay for a roof replacement. This covers the process of how to make an insurance claim that will be accepted!
4. Home Equity Loan
If none of the above options feel right to you, you may be able to take out a home equity loan. Also known as a home equity line of credit (HELOC), the way these loans work is fairly simple. By using your home as collateral, you can receive an amount of money equal to your equity in your home. This option isn’t available to all homeowners, though.

For one thing, you have to have a substantial amount of equity built up in your home. So if you’ve only been living there a short time, this may not be available to you. You’ll also need to have a fairly high credit score. To qualify for these loans at all, you usually need a credit score of at least 620. However, a credit score of 700 or higher will get you the best rates.

If you qualify for a HELOC, this could be a great option. In terms of how to pay for a new roof, HELOCs offer some of the lowest interest rates on the market. On the other hand, your home is put up as collateral, so you have to be completely sure that you will be able to pay off the loan no matter what. That, coupled with the high requirements to qualify, is why a home equity loan is great for some but not right for everyone.

### What to Do After a Hurricane: Protecting Your Property

For Floridians, hurricanes are simply a fact of life. That’s why we have to stay informed of how to handle these natural disasters while safeguarding lives and property as much as possible. There have already been many great guides on what to do before a hurricane, but what are you supposed to do after a Hurricane passes?

We’re PITCH Roofing, and as your local roofing partner, it’s our job to tell you that the danger to your home may not pass with the storm. How you respond after a hurricane is just as important as how you prepare for one. That’s why we’re here to share what to do after a hurricane to keep your home or business safe!
What to Do After a Hurricane


Before anything else, the most important thing to do after a hurricane is to stay safe. We’re going to focus on how to handle storm damage to your roof, but at all times, prioritize your own safety and the safety of those around you. Roofs can be expensive, but people are irreplaceable!

With that said, let’s talk about what to do after a hurricane to protect your roof and your property!
Take a Look at Your Roof Once the Storm Has Cleared
You should never step onto a heavily damaged roof. If you see visible sagging or other signs that your roof is structurally unsound, do not try to access it. You can inspect your roof for damage from your yard, and binoculars can help you see up close to inspect your shingles. While getting on your roof is more thorough, there is never a reason to endanger yourself by getting on a roof when you’re not 100% confident in your ability to stay safe.

If you can safely get onto your roof, start looking around for damage. The most common problems you’ll see after a storm are missing or bent shingles, warped flashing, and damage to your soffits or fascia. Make sure to note any damage and take multiple photos — you’ll need proof of the damage when you go to make your insurance claim. This is one of the most important things to do after a hurricane since your insurer will need proof that a storm caused the damage, so taking pictures ASAP is a great idea.

While you’re on your roof, take a look around for any storm debris. It’s extremely common for branches and even trash from other people’s yards to end up on your roof during a hurricane. Make sure to carefully remove any debris from your roof — over time, it can make a home for pests, and it’s much easier to prevent that problem than fix it.

If you don’t feel comfortable or safe getting on your roof after a hurricane, then don’t. You can always schedule a roof inspection once the storm has cleared. This way, you’ll be able to get professional roofers to take a close look at your roof and identify any damage from the Hurricane!
Tarp Damaged Sections of Your Roof


In a perfect world, what to do after a hurricane would only include calling your preferred contractors. You’d be able to call roofers the day after a Hurricane and get someone out to your house to fix the storm damage within 24 hours. But the truth is that roofers are usually swamped with calls after a major storm. It can take time for us to help everyone, and in the meantime, it can do your roof a world of good to tarp over any missing or damaged shingles.

If you can safely get on your roof, then you shouldn’t have too much trouble tarping any damaged sections. To tarp your roof, follow these instructions:

 	Cover any areas with missing shingles with thin wood; plywood works well for this purpose.
 	Attach the top edge of the tarp to the roof using nails or screws, placing them every 1-2 feet. Make sure to leave at least 4 feet of tarp around the damaged section to ensure that no water can get in.
 	Lay a 2x4 along each edge of the tarp and nail it down for extra security.
 	Pull the tarp tight and repeat the process for the remaining sides, ensuring it’s snug and won’t flap in the wind.

By tarping your roof, you’ll minimize the risk of water damage to your roof. But tarping your own roof isn’t achievable for every homeowner. If at any point you feel unsafe or like you’re not completely confident in how to tarp your roof, the best thing is just to leave it. Preventing water damage is important, but it’s even more important to make sure you don’t injure yourself or your roof while attempting to install a tarp.
Call Roofers and Your Insurance Agent
If you have roofing damage from a Hurricane, then you’ll want to start making phone calls. Perhaps the first person you should call is your insurance agent so that they can tell you exactly what you’ll need to submit a claim. Some insurance policies have strict stipulations with which roofers you have to use, so it’s best to check for these requirements before calling in contractors.

Once you’re all set with your insurance agent, the next thing to do after a hurricane is call in the roofers. You don’t have to give them every detail right away, a brief description of any damage you’ve noticed should be plenty. They’ll then schedule a date to have someone out to look at your roof and draw up some solutions for you.

The big thing to note here is that you should be reaching out to the roofers. If you see a roofer going door to door after Hurricane Helen, this is a big red flag. We call these people storm chasers because they blow into town after a hurricane and start offering dirt-cheap roof repairs and replacements. Unfortunately, they can charge so little because they’re inexperienced, use shoddy materials, and often aren’t even real roofers.

Storm chasers cause more problems than they solve, so stick with the local professionals. When you choose PITCH Roofing for your storm damage restoration services, you’re investing in local expertise, workmanship guarantees, and the long-term protection that comes with hiring professionals to do what they do best. That’s exactly what your home needs after a hurricane!

### Can You Put Solar Panels on a Metal Roof in Florida?

Two roofing innovations are experiencing a surge in popularity across Florida right now: solar and metal roofing. This has led many homeowners to wonder if they can or should combine these two technologies. But should you put solar panels on a metal roof?

We’re PITCH Roofing, and today we’re going to answer all your questions about solar panels on metal roofs. But before we get too far into how these systems work together, let’s first talk about each individually so you can know the value of solar and metal roofing in Florida.
Why Floridians Love Solar and Metal Roofing


Before we discuss putting solar panels on metal roofs, it’s important to make sure you know everything you need to about solar roofing and metal roofing. Let’s take a brief look at each one of these roofing technologies to make sure you’re up to speed!
Solar Roofing
Solar roofing is more than just popular right now — it’s a $9.6 billion industry and growing. You probably know the gist of how it works; installers adhere solar panels to your roof where they can capture sunlight and convert it to electricity via photovoltaic cells.

Florida is the Sunshine State, so there’s no better place for investing in solar energy for your home. And when properly mounted by professional roofers, solar panels can safely adhere to your roof even through tropical storms and hurricanes.

Of course, cost is always a concern for solar panels. And we won’t lie — they’re not cheap, with the average solar panel installation costing $20,000 to $25,000 in Florida. There are some important things to know about the cost of solar panels, though:

 	Thanks to the federal tax credit, you can cut 30% off the total cost of your solar panel installation
 	Solar panels pay for themselves in 6-12 years on average
 	Having solar panels on your home greatly increases its resale value and makes your property much more attractive to buyers

For all of these reasons, solar roofing panels are only getting more popular in Florida. But should you put solar panels on a metal roof? To answer that, we first have to look at the state of metal roofing in Florida.
Metal Roofing
Florida has seen more and more major hurricanes in recent years. Homeowners, tired of waking up to shingles in their yard, have been making the upgrade to metal roofing. And in general, it’s been working out extremely well for them.

While asphalt shingles can only rarely handle winds exceeding 110 mph, metal roofs have been known to withstand winds above 140 mph. That’s a big difference in your protection during a hurricane! When you add on the much longer lifespan of 40-70 years, compared to the 20 years of shingles, it’s not surprising that Floridians love metal roofing.

Like with solar roofing, though, cost is a big concern for homeowners thinking of getting a metal roof. And it’s true: Metal roofs are more expensive than shingle roofs. But there are plenty of affordable metal roof options on the market, and when you consider the long-term value of reliable protection and added resale value, many homeowners find that metal roofs are worth the investment.

Now that we’ve covered both solar and metal roofing, it’s time to answer the big question. Is it a good idea to put solar panels on a metal roof?
Should You Put Solar Panels on a Metal Roof in Florida?


Good news: Experienced contractors should have no problem adhering solar panels to your metal roof. This applies to standing seam metal roofs as well as corrugated metal roofs, and across all metal roofing materials as well. Thanks to modern solar panel mounts, you can apply solar panels to virtually any kind of roof!

That answers the question of if you can apply solar panels to a metal roof. But should you?

In a word, yes. There are no major downsides to installing solar panels on your metal roof. Thanks to the mounting system used for solar panels on standing seam metal roofs, no new holes or perforations are added to your roof during solar panel installation. This means that your roof isn’t any more likely to be damaged by weather in the future. Additionally, you don’t have to worry about losing your sleek, smooth aesthetic!

The mounting process is slightly different for corrugated metal roofs but still viable. With solar panels on corrugated roofs, the mounting system does drill down into the metal sheet. However, corrugated roofs are already drilled into place. So while this creates new holes in your roofing system, they are no more dangerous or unreliable than the ones that are already there.

In addition to there not being downsides, installing solar panels on a metal roof comes with many benefits that are unique to metal roofing. Some of these include:

 	Because metal roofs last longer than solar panels (which last about 20-25 years), you don’t have to worry about needing a roof replacement and having to pay for your solar panels to be uninstalled and reinstalled
 	Metal roofs reflect heat away from your home, which helps solar panels function since they work best in cooler weather
 	A metal roof with solar panels is a chance to double-down on being eco-friendly since metal roofs can be almost 100% recycled at the end of their lives

Clearly, there are a lot of great reasons to put solar panels on a metal roof. So where do you get started?
