### How Much Roof Flashing Repairs Cost in Florida

In roofing, many essential components of your roof are easy to overlook — especially roof flashing. This is an integral part of nearly any roofing system, but many homeowners don’t know what it is. As a result, they struggle to tell when it’s time to repair or replace roof flashing.

That’s what we’re here for. PITCH Roofing is your local roofing partner, and today we’re using our Florida roofing experience to cover what roof flashing is, when to replace or repair it, and how much those services cost. Naturally, though, we’re starting with the biggest question: What is roof flashing?
What Is Roof Flashing and Why Is It Important?


If you’ve ever noticed any metal strips on your roof, these were probably flashing. Usually made of aluminum for its rust resistance, the most common place that you’ll find flashing is along the valleys of a shingle roof. Plenty of other places have these metal strips, though, including along skylights, chimneys, and other unique roofing features.

So what’s the point? Roof flashing helps direct water off your roof. With damaged flashing, your roof may not naturally drain the way that it should. The result is pooled water, which can slowly soak through your shingles and lead to roof leaks or, even worse, roof sagging.

That’s why you’ll usually find flashing along the valleys of your roof and exterior ridges of roofing features. By directing water toward the edge of your roof, your flashing protects areas that would otherwise be vulnerable to water damage.

As we mentioned, most flashing is made of aluminum. This works well because aluminum is slow to rust, so the water won’t corrode your flashing (at least not quickly). There are drawbacks, though. Aluminum is a lightweight, malleable metal, so storms can easily damage it. That vulnerability is why homeowners need to know the signs that it’s time to repair or replace their flashing.
Signs of Roof Flashing Damage
Like other parts of your roofing system, any number of things can damage your flashing. Whether these issues require repairs or a full flashing replacement, though, it’s important to take them seriously. Any one of these issues means that your flashing isn’t working properly, which could put your whole roof at risk.

In Florida, the most common signs of damaged roof flashing that we see are:

 	Bends or Cracks: It can be easy to dismiss a bend or small crack in your flashing as a minor issue. But these problems disrupt the natural direction of water off your roof and reflect serious damage to the metal. Both of these issues will cause you headaches over time, so your flashing will either need to be bent back into place, re-sealed, or replaced.
 	Corrosion: While aluminum and other flashing materials are resistant to rust, they’re not immune to it. If you see signs of rust on your flashing, it means that your flashing can no longer repel water and needs either replacing or repairing.
 	Ceiling Water Stains: Sometimes the first sign you have of a problem isn’t on your roof at all. Water stains on your ceiling or walls could indicate you have a leak caused by damaged flashing.
 	Damaged Shingles: Are you noticing shingle granules collecting in your gutters or bending shingles? If so, it could be due to water damage, which indicates that your roof flashing isn’t functioning properly.

These are the roof flashing problems that we see and handle every day. But the best course of action will be completely unique to your situation. For example, sometimes cracked flashing can be re-sealed and continue working on your roof, whereas other times you’ll need a flashing replacement. The specifics will largely come down to the extent of the damage, where it’s located, and the unique features of your roof.

As you might imagine, this makes it hard to figure out how much roof flashing replacement or repair costs. But at PITCH, it’s our job to do hard work for our customers. So let’s take a closer look at how much your roof flashing might cost.
How Much Does Roof Flashing Repair/Replacement Cost?


When buying new flashing, you can expect to pay $15 to $25 per linear foot. More goes into your total costs than just this figure, though. You’ll also need to factor in the labor to install it as well as other material costs, like sealants and caulk. In many cases damaged roof flashing comes alongside other issues with your roof, so these may need repairing before any issues with your flashing can be fixed.

Other factors that can influence the cost of your roof flashing repair or replacement include:

 	What part of your flashing needs work (flashing in valleys, flashing near chimneys, etc.)
 	What material your flashing is made from
 	The extent of the damage and amount of new flashing materials needed
 	Your roofing material
 	The slope and accessibility of your roof

All told, most roof flashing repair jobs fall somewhere in the $300 to $600 range. Replacing an entire section of your flashing will likely be more expensive, both because you need to purchase more flashing and because the damage to address is more severe. On average, we find that roof flashing replacement costs around $1,500 in Florida.

We can do better than just giving you an average, though. In fact, with just a few easy steps, we can tell you exactly how much your new roof flashing will cost.

### How Much Does a Metal Roof Cost per Square Foot in Florida?

Metal Roof Pricing: What to Expect in 2025Estimated Price Range: $10,000 – $50,000If you're considering a metal roof, understanding the cost is key to making an informed decision. In 2025, metal roofing installation costs generally range between $5 and $25 per square foot, depending on the type of metal and style you choose. Budget-friendly options, like corrugated metal, start at approximately $5 per square foot, while high-end selections—such as standing seam metal—fall between $10 and $25 per square foot.Though metal roofing requires a larger upfront investment compared to asphalt shingles, its long-term benefits make it a smart choice, especially in areas prone to severe weather. With superior durability, energy efficiency, and longevity, a metal roof can provide lasting protection while increasing your home's overall value.																															
				FULL ARTICLE				
				In Florida, more and more homeowners are considering upgrading to metal roofs to protect against storms. But while people are generally interested in metal roofing, they still have some questions. Specifically, homeowners want to know the average metal roof cost per square foot in Florida.
Well, we’re here to answer exactly that! We’re PITCH Roofing, and as some of Florida’s best contractors, we’ve got the latest metal roofing price information for a variety of systems. Keep reading for a total cost breakdown of your metal roofing options in Florida!
How Much Different Types of Metal Roofs Cost per Square Foot

There is always a price range with roofing, but metal roofing has an especially high number of options that will drastically change your total roofing costs. One of the biggest cost factors is the type of metal roof used in your roof’s construction.
So let’s take a look at the different types of metal roofing materials and how much they cost per square foot!

 	Steel: Galvalume is among the most popular types of steel roofing in Florida due to its improved rust resistance. Galvalume metal roofs cost $6 to $12 per square foot on average.
 	Aluminum: If you live on Florida’s coasts, aluminum is likely the best option for your metal roof. Because aluminum is very resistant to rust, it can handle the saltwater air. This protection comes at a premium though, with aluminum roofs costing $7 to $15 per square foot in Florida.
 	Zinc: This is very much a luxury metal roofing material. Zinc is “self-healing,” meaning it sheds damaged parts to protect the integrity of the whole. This long-lasting protection isn’t cheap, coming in at $8 to $16 per square foot.

These are the most popular metal roofs in Florida and how much they cost in Florida. Unfortunately, this will not be enough to tell you how much your metal roof replacement will cost. To find that number, you’ll also need to account for your metal roof’s fasteners.
Hidden vs. Exposed Fasteners Metal Roof Cost per Square Foot
Many homeowners are surprised to learn this, but it’s true, your metal roofing material only makes up a part of your total material costs. How that metal is shaped will also greatly affect both manufacturing and installation costs.
To better understand how much different types of metal roofs cost per square foot, we have to review hidden vs. exposed fasteners.
Cost of Exposed Fastener Metal Roofing
Exposed fastener metal roofing, also called 5V or corrugated metal roofing, works in a simple, direct way. During the manufacturing process, they shape your chosen type of metal into corrugated sheets. Then, when it comes time to install your roof, your contractors drill the sheets down into place.
Like we said, simple. And that simplicity has some benefits. For one thing, exposed fastener metal roofs are easy and quick to install. This helps keep labor costs down and limits the time it takes to replace your roof. Your material costs also stay low thanks to the easy manufacturing process.
There are also drawbacks, however. Because your roof’s fasteners sit on top of the roof, they’re exposed to the elements. This means that they can get worn down, especially with Florida’s year-round humidity. Additionally, since your roof can’t freely expand and contract with the sun’s heat, it may undergo premature aging. For these reasons, exposed fastener metal roofs only last 20-30 years.
If you want a low metal roof cost per square foot, though, there is no better option. Exposed fastener metal roofing costs $5 to $12 per square foot on average, depending on your material choices and the specifics of your roof. This makes it the most viable option for affordable metal roofing!
Cost of Hidden Fastener Metal Roofing

Hidden fastener metal roofs work very differently. Also called standing seam, these roofs adhere together beneath the panel thanks to an interlocking mechanism. This requires specialized manufacturing to create the interlocking shape and overlapping design, but the final result is a smooth, sleek metal roof.
Because your fasteners are safely protected by your metal roofing sheets, you don’t have to worry about premature aging. And because your roof can expand and contract slightly with the heat, it doesn’t experience the same premature aging that 5V metal roofs do. That’s why standing seam metal roofs last for 50 years or more!
That kind of longevity comes with a high price tag, though. Hidden fastener metal roofs cost much more money to manufacture because of their unique, detailed design. They even cost more to install because of the time and experience required to slot these metal roofing sheets together.
So how much does a hidden fastener metal roof cost? In Florida, metal roof costs per square foot range from $10 to $35 for standing seam, although they average closer to $20. While this makes standing seam roofs a luxury, there is no better option if you want dependable, long-term protection!

We know what to look for and how to find out if you need roof repairs after a hurricane. Keep reading as we go over the most common signs of storm damage and what they could mean for your home!
Signs of Storm Damage to Roofs in Florida


No state does storms quite like Florida. As a peninsula situated between the Gulf of Mexico and the Atlantic Ocean, we’re uniquely vulnerable to hurricanes. That’s why both protecting against and resolving storm damage takes local know-how!

As experienced Florida roofers, we’re sharing the real, most common signs of storm damage that we see after every major storm!
1. Interior Signs of Roof Leaks
Sometimes you don’t even have to leave your home to find signs of storm damage. The morning after a storm, it’s a good idea to take a look for leaking water inside your home.

The problem is not always as obvious as water pouring from your ceiling, though. Other interior signs of roof leaks include:

 	Water Stains: After a storm, you might notice water stains on your ceiling or walls. These stains will look brown and tend to spread out over time, and they’re a sign that water is seeping into your roofing system through your roof.
 	Musty Odors: Immediately after a storm, you don’t have to worry about mold developing. But you may smell something musty, especially in your attic or other elevated parts of your home.
 	Sagging Ceiling: If your ceiling is sagging the morning after a hurricane or tropical storm, it means you have major damage to your roof. Specifically, sagging roofs mean that your roof is not structurally sound and could start draining into your home.

You may notice these issues immediately after a storm. But it’s also possible that these issues will take several days to appear. Be sure to keep an eye out for signs of leaks and water damage in the days after a hurricane or tropical storm!
2. Missing Shingles
This is perhaps the easiest sign of storm damage to spot, so it’s one of the first things you should look for. The morning after a storm, take a look at your roof from the ground and see if you have any missing or partially lifted shingles. If you have a pair of binoculars, they can help you take a closer look.

If you see any missing shingles, call your preferred roofers for repairs immediately. Missing shingles aren’t much of a problem the day after a storm, but as it starts to rain again in the coming days and weeks, they can lead to serious damage to your roof decking. This can weaken the entire structure of your roof, so it’s best to act quickly!
3. Loose Shingle Granules


Your asphalt shingles are made of three parts: a baseboard, asphalt, and stone granules. These granules both make your shingles more durable and help them reflect UV rays away from your home. During a storm, high winds can loosen these granules and scatter them across your roof.

There are two ways to check for missing shingle granules. The easiest way is to check your downspouts. If your gutters are working properly, then shingle granules will be funneled directly to your downspouts, where they should start to accumulate in your yard. Look for small stone granules, usually in colors similar to those of your shingles.

The other way to check for this sign of storm damage is to hop on your roof and take a closer look at your shingles. Note that you should never get on your roof if you think that it is structurally unsound or if you’re not completely confident in your ability to get on and off your roof safely. If you can access your roof, you’ll be able to see whether your shingles are bare or still have a coating of protective granules.
4. Damaged Flashing
Flashing is easy to overlook, but it does essential work in keeping your roof secure. Your flashing is a piece of thin metal that surrounds vulnerable parts of your roof, like vents, chimneys, or any other roof perforations. As a result, damaged flashing is a serious sign of storm damage.

So how do you tell if your flashing is damaged? Lok around any roof perforations — binoculars are a good place to start if you can’t physically access your roof. There will be a thin sheet of metal around each roofing feature. If you see any bending, warping, or signs of rust, then it means that you have damaged flashing and will need roof repair services.
5. Gutter Damage
Don’t let looking for signs of storm damage stop at your roofing materials. Your gutters are an essential part of your roofing system, so you’ll want to make sure they’re still secure and functional once the storm has passed.

Some of the most common signs that your gutters need repairing or replacing include:

 	Sagging in your gutters
 	Leaks from your gutters or water spilling over the edges
 	Cracks or splits in gutters
 	Free-hanging gutters or gutters that aren’t firmly attached to your roof
 	Water pooling around your home’s foundation

All of these signs of storm damage should be taken seriously. If you suspect that your gutters are damaged, it’s best to call gutter restoration professionals to either replace them or get them back to helping water move safely off your roof!

### Trailer Home Roof Repair Services for Flat & Shingle Roofs

Florida roofs have a lot to stand up against, especially during hurricane season. But the danger is doubled for mobile homes, which are much more vulnerable to storm damage. That’s why you need reliable trailer home roof repair professionals who can get your roof back in working order and protect your home!

That’s us: We’re PITCH Roofing, a local roofing company based right here in Pinellas County. Today, we’re talking to you about roofing for mobile homes and how you can get high-quality roof repair services on any budget. Let’s get started and talk about the different ways that we can fix your roof!
Trailer Home Roof Repair in Florida


There are a lot of reasons that you may need trailer home roof repair services. Not only can storm damage cause very different problems from normal wear and tear, but the kind of roofing material you have will also play a big role in which repairs your roof needs.

Mobile home roofs are usually either flat with TPO or modified bitumen or sloped with shingle roofs. Let’s talk a bit about what kind of repairs your roof might need depending on which material your roof has!
Mobile Home Flat Roofing Repair
Because of these roofs’ low slopes, flat roofing materials are all about keeping water from pooling on your roof or causing leaks. That’s why they’re made of water-resistant materials like TPO (a waterproof, rubberized polymer) and modified bitumen (rubberized asphalt).

With TPO, some of the most common trailer home roof repairs we see are:

 	Punctures and Tears: TPO roofing systems are single-ply roof membranes, so they’re vulnerable to impact damage from fallen branches, hail, and storm debris.
 	Shrinkage: As the sun’s UV rays cause your TPO roof to expand and contract, the roof’s seams can start to give way and may need re-sealing.
 	Pooling Water: On a functional mobile home flat roof, water should slowly drain off your roof. But if it’s started to pool, you will need to call in roofers ASAP before water starts to leak through your roof.

Modified bitumen roofs, on the other hand, tend to have different issues. While both mod bit and TPO are flat roofing materials, their different compositions mean they sometimes need different repairs. Some of our most common modified bitumen repairs are:

 	Blistering: Sometimes during installation, air gets trapped between your modified bitumen and roofing substrate. Over time, heat from the sun makes these gases expand, causing blistering throughout your roof that is both unsightly and could lead to leaks.
 	Granule Loss: Like shingles, modified bitumen has a fine layer of protective granules. If your roof starts shedding these, the sun can rapidly start aging your roof, shortening its overall lifespan.
 	Splitting Seams: Over time, the seams between rolls of modified bitumen can crack or separate, requiring resealing or applying additional layers of membrane.

If you’re experiencing any of these issues with any flat roofing material, it’s important to get trailer home roof repair services ASAP. Your mobile home has unique needs, and you deserve to work with contractors who know how to help!
Mobile Home Shingle Roofing Repair
Most mobile homes have flat roofs. But for some newer models, you might have a sloped roof with asphalt shingles. This brings a completely different set of roofing concerns since water will more easily move off a sloped roof. On the other hand, Florida’s high winds become much more of a concern.

The most common trailer home roof repair jobs we see for shingle roofs include:

 	Missing Shingles: Asphalt shingles can withstand high winds, but sometimes hurricanes can overwhelm them and tear shingles from your roof. If this isn’t fixed, water damage could mean more widespread damage that eventually needs a roof replacement to solve.
 	Curled or Cracked Shingles: Over the years, the sun can do a real number on shingles. Classic signs of sun damage are shingles that are curled or cracking, which will need to be removed and replaced.
 	Worn Vent Pipe Seals: If the seals around your vent pipes give out, you’ll need to have them re-sealed to protect your roof’s structural integrity. Surrounding shingles may also need replacing as part of this process.

No matter what kind of shingle roof repair you need for your mobile home, PITCH can handle it. As experienced local contractors, we’ve seen the worst that Florida has to throw at shingle roofs. Our hands-on experience and know-how will be invaluable in fixing your roof and keeping your home safe!

There is still one big question to answer, though. Cost is a big concern for everyone, so many homeowners want to know: How much do trailer home roof repairs cost?

But your costs will also change drastically depending on whether you have a TPO, modified bitumen, or shingle roof.

On average, mobile home roof repairs cost between $1,500 and $3,000. Of course, your number could end up coming in below or above this range depending on your circumstances. Part of what makes up this cost is roofing material costs, which are:

### What Are Composition Shingles?

It’s normal for homeowners to struggle with the terminology and jargon of the roofing industry. Not only are there many terms to learn for the different parts of a roofing system, but sometimes multiple terms refer to the same thing. This is the case with composition shingles, which are more commonly known as asphalt shingles.

Whether you call them composition shingles or asphalt shingles, they’re one of the most popular roofing materials in North America. And even in Florida with our hurricanes and humidity, these shingles do a great job at keeping homes safe. As your go-to guide on all things Florida roofing, PITCH Roofing is here to walk you through everything you should know about composition shingles!
What Are Composition Shingles?


Before we get into the nitty-gritty of how much composition shingles cost in Florida and if they’re well-suited to your roof we first need to talk about what these shingles actually are. Sure, they’re made of asphalt, but what does that really mean?

In the manufacturing process, shingles start with a baseboard, usually one made of fiberglass. This fiberglass then gets coated in a thick layer of protective asphalt to make it durable and capable of repelling water. Then the manufacturers sprinkle protective granules over each shingle to improve its impact resistance against hail and storm debris.

With old-school composition shingles, this is where the process stops. But modern roofing has come a long way. Nowadays, shingles are double-layered with asphalt to make them thicker and heavier. These new, improved shingles are called architectural shingles, and their extra weight makes them much harder for wind to blow off a roof. As a bonus, the thicker design also leads to more interesting designs that create depth on your roof.

That about wraps it up for composition shingles 101. Now, let’s start answering some of your biggest questions.
Composition Shingles: Longevity, Durability, and Cost


As experienced Florida roofers, we spend a lot of our time talking to people about their options when installing a new roof. In these conversations, we see a lot of the same questions pop up. How long do composition shingle roofs last? What kind of wind resistance do shingles have? How much do composition shingles cost?

We’re here to answer all of these questions and more. Keep reading for our complete breakdown about what you need to know for your composition shingle roof replacement!
Longevity
When compared to other roofing materials, the truth is that composition shingles don’t last for an especially long time. But that doesn’t mean you can’t get a good, respectable life out of your composition shingles.

On average, composition shingles last for 20-25 years in Florida. That number will very, very rarely go up, but it can easily go down if you’re not taking care of your roof. Take, for example, a roof leak. If a leak goes untreated, the water damage could soak into your decking and cause much more widespread damage throughout your shingles and the rest of your roof. This kind of problem can drastically lower your shingle roof’s lifespan!

That’s why we recommend biannual roof inspections to make sure that you’re staying on top of any potential damage. By treating issues as soon as they arise, you can give your roof the best possible chance at a long life. Nobody wants to replace their roof sooner than they have to, so it’s important to take care of yours!
Durability
You’ve probably noticed that Florida weather can be pretty tough on roofs. We aren’t just referring to hurricanes and tropical storms either — even Florida’s everyday weather is hazardous for roofs. Think of the humidity and UV exposure that your roof has to face every day! When installing a new roof in Florida, it’s important to invest in high-quality materials that can roll with the punches.

Composition shingles are great at standing up against Florida’s unique weather patterns. Let’s look at some of their biggest protective features:

 	Wind resistance of up to 110 mph thanks to hefty weight and strategic nailing positions
 	Many composition shingles have time-released zinc deposits to prevent mold
 	Ability to shed water because of multiple layers of asphalt
 	UV reflection via stone granules and light colors, which help reflect sun away from your home

As you can see, shingles stand up against the worst that Florida has to offer. Despite their ability to stand up to Florida’s weather, shingles aren’t invincible. They can crack, curl, or even be removed by gusts of wind. Staying on top of maintenance is the best way to keep your composition shingles in place and functioning at their best!
Cost
Finally, the big question: How much do composition shingles cost? The truth is that architectural shingles only cost a few dollars to make per square foot of shingles. But that’s not the number you need to know. For your roof replacement, you need to know how much you can expect to pay for a composition shingle roof installation — including labor costs and other pricing factors.

We have that number. When getting your roof replaced with composition shingles, you can expect to pay $5 to $9 per square foot of your roof. The average roof in Florida is around 1,700 square feet. So you could say that, on average, composition shingle roof replacements cost $8,500 to $15,300 in Florida.

This isn’t cheap, certainly, but it is one of the best prices you’ll get for a new roof. In fact, that’s a big part of why composition shingles are so popular — they’re the most affordable roofing material on the market. So if you’re on a tight roof replacement budget, there’s no better option than shingles!

### What Is the Best Roofing Material for Your Florida Home?

When getting a new roof, “good enough” isn’t good enough. You don’t deserve an okay roof — you deserve the best roof for your home. As your local roofing partner, PITCH Roofing is here to make sure that that’s exactly what you get.

But what makes something the “best” roof? Does it come down to the best protection, the best price, the best look, or some combination? Ultimately, the only one who can decide on what is or isn’t the best option for your home is you. We’re here to give you the information to make that choice, so keep reading for a complete overview of the best roofing materials in Florida!\
The Best Roof Options in Florida


Every climate has its own unique roofing issues and challenges. In Florida, we need roofs that can handle hurricane-force winds, humidity, and a lot of UV exposure. Over the years, three roofing materials have stood above the rest as especially well-suited to Florida’s unique climate.

Let’s take a look at the best roofing materials for Florida homeowners!
1. Asphalt Shingles
Whether they’re the best roof or not, asphalt shingles are certainly the most popular roofing material in Florida. Made of a fiberglass baseboard that’s then covered in asphalt and topped with protective granules, shingles are easy to install, come in a wide variety of colors, and don’t cost much to manufacture.

But do they make the best roofs in Florida? Let’s consider some of their pros:

 	At $5 to $9 per square foot, asphalt shingles are one of the most affordable roofing materials in Florida. Part of the reason they’re so popular is their low costs!
 	Shingles are easy to repair and replace, which keeps roof repair bills low over the years.
 	You can accomplish nearly any look with shingles thanks to their wide range of color and style options.
 	With high impact resistance, shingles are some of the best roofs for withstanding damage from hail and storm debris.

It isn’t all positive, though. Shingle roofs also come with notable downsides that you should carefully consider. Some of the less positive qualities of shingle roofs include:

 	Asphalt shingles have short lifespans of 20-25 years on average.
 	Shingles are generally only rated for winds of 110 mph. This means they can be damaged or even removed by major hurricanes.
 	Shingles aren’t very eco-friendly because they often end up in landfills after being removed from your roof.

2. Clay & Concrete Tiles


Tiles have a long, rich history in Florida. Originally brought over by Spanish colonists, tile roofs remain one of the best ways Floridians can protect their homes against tropical storms.

Roofing tiles come in one of two materials: clay and concrete. Clay is the classic option, but concrete is a more modern, affordable take on a tile roof. Both options come in a variety of colors, from classic red or brown to more unique colors like blue or green.

But are tiles the best roof material in Florida? They certainly have a lot going for them, for example:

 	In terms of longevity, tiles are tough to beat. Concrete tiles last 40-50 years, but clay tile roofs have been known to last 100 years or more with proper maintenance!
 	Tile roofs also only require minimal maintenance. This is thanks to their wind resistance of roughly 140 mph and their ability to resist rotting even in wet, humid climates like Florida!
 	Tiles, especially in lighter colors, help reflect UV rays away from your home thanks to anti-UV coatings. As a result, tile roofs often come with reduced energy bills.

While tile roofs are excellent roofing materials, there’s no such things as perfection in roofing materials. Some of their biggest downsides include the following:

 	High up-front costs are a major barrier to getting a tile roof. Clay tile roof replacements cost between $12 to $21 per square foot, and even concrete tile roof replacements cost between $10 to $19 per square foot.
 	While strong, tiles can be brittle. For this reason, one of the most common tile roof repairs is replacing a tile that has been cracked by hail or fallen branches.
 	Tile roof colors can fade over time, especially with concrete tiles. For this reason, you may need to have your tiles professionally re-painted over the course of its life, which can be a significant expense.

3. Metal Roofing
Whether or not metal is the best roof material, it’s at least the one enjoying the biggest upswing in popularity lately. Every day more and more Floridians are upgrading to metal roofs, which are hitting the market in a variety of styles and materials.

Metal roofing is complicated, which makes it hard to talk about whether or not metal roofing in general makes for the best roofs. To make this easier, today we’re just talking about the two most popular kinds of metal roofs: standing seam and corrugated metal roofs.

With that in mind, let’s look at the biggest pros of metal roofing:

 	Metal roofs have great lifespans, ranging from 40 to 70 years on average. Standing seam roofs generally last longer than corrugated metal roofs.
 	Metal roofs are the best roofs for wind resistance. Wind ratings for metal roofs range from 140 – 180 mph!
 	Roofs made of metal can reflect sunlight away from your home, reducing your energy bills in the summer.
 	Most types of metal roofing are recyclable, which makes them much more environmentally friendly than shingles.

Even metal roofs have their drawbacks, though. If these aren’t the best roof option for your home, it’s probably because:

 	Metal roofs are expensive. Corrugated metal roofing is more affordable at $7 to $12 per square foot, but standing seam will cost between $15 and $35 per square foot!
 	Rust can be a problem with metal roofs, especially if you live on one of Florida’s coasts. For these homes, we recommend aluminum metal roofing for its unmatched rust resistance.
 	Denting is a common issue for metal roofs in Florida. While these dents are rarely structural concerns, they can disrupt the look of your metal roof, especially on standing seam.

How to Tell if You Need a Guttering Replacement


Nobody wants to pay for new gutters if they don’t have to. So how can you tell if you need new gutters vs. gutter repairs? There are a few telltale signs that your gutters are at the end of their life. Some of the biggest ones we see in Florida are:

 	Cracking: Water will escape from virtually any cracks in your gutters, so once you see this issue, you can be sure that it’s time for a guttering replacement.
 	Rust: Corrosion is a surefire sign that your gutter materials are at the end of their life.
 	Peeling Paint: If the paint on or around your gutters begins to peel, it’s time for a replacement. Paint is made to withstand moisture and humidity, so peeling means that it’s being exposed to an extreme amount of moisture, likely from water trapped in your gutters.
 	Pooling Water: Puddles around your home’s foundation mean that your gutters are failing. If cleaning them doesn’t fix the problem, then it’s time to replace them.

All of these are signs that it’s time to invest in a gutter replacement. But that doesn’t necessarily mean that you should go with the first roofers you find. Your gutters do important work, and that work could be jeopardized if they’re installed by inexperienced contractors.

### 5 Steps to Handling a Leaking Roof

When you have a leaking roof, it’s normal to feel panicked or unsure of what to do next. But taking just a few simple steps can help protect your property and ensure the safety of your structure.

We’re PITCH Roofing, and we’re here to let you know what you should do when you have a leaking roof. Whether water is pouring from your ceiling or you’ve got ceiling water stains, we’ve got tips to make sure you can handle your roof leak while minimizing damage to your home!
5 Things to Do When You Have a Leaking Roof


With a roof leak, time is everything. Over time, water can eat away at your decking, lead to mold growth, or even become an electrical hazard. By acting quickly, though, you can greatly reduce the damage.

With that in mind, let’s talk about the first steps you should take after you notice that your roof is leaking!
1. Move or Cover Items Near the Leak
When your leaking roof is dripping water into your home, the first thing you should do is secure your belongings. This means placing a water-resistant tarp over heavy objects and furniture. For items that can more easily be moved, you’ll want to relocate them to a dryer part of your home.

Keep an eye on your leak in the coming days as you get ready for a roof repair. In rare cases with severe damage, a roof leak can expand. You’ll want to watch out for this so that you can move more of your belongings if new parts of your ceiling start to leak.
2. Try to Catch the Water
A leaking roof will damage more than just your ceiling. If the water isn’t caught and disposed of, it can do a real number on your floors. In some cases, fixing water-damaged floors could cost even more than fixing your leaking roof! That’s why you’ll want to set up whatever you can under the leak — trash cans, buckets, towels, whatever you have on hand.

When you’re already dealing with a leaking roof, the last thing you need is another type of damage to repair. By being proactive and catching the leaking water, you can save yourself a lot of time and headaches!
3. Call Professional Roofers
Once the inside of your home is dry and secure, it’s time to call in the professionals. It can be tempting to DIY your roof leak repair, but tracking down and addressing the cause of a leak isn’t always easy. So if you want to be sure that your leaking roof is fixed and won’t cause problems again, going with experienced contractors is your best option.

Sometimes roofers can come out and fix your leaking roof right away. But just as often, schedules fill up and you may have to wait a few days to a couple of weeks. That’s why it’s important to call your preferred roofers ASAP, so you can get on their schedule and get your leak fixed right away.
4. Tarp Any Roof Damage
If you’re going to have to wait a few days to get your leaking roof fixed, then the next best thing is tarping your roof. Specifically, you just need to tarp the area that’s letting in water. In Florida, this usually means tarping over a section that’s missing shingles or has visibly curled or cracked shingles.

Once you find the damage, place a tarp over it. The tarp should be thick enough to keep water out — at least six millimeters. You’ll want the tarp to cover any damage and several feet around it to make sure that water can’t continue seeping into your roof. This way, you can prevent long-term damage while waiting for repairs!
5. Take Photos for Insurance


We get it — roof leak repairs probably weren’t in your monthly budget. Thankfully, if your leak was caused by a severe weather event like a storm or hurricane, then there’s a good chance your insurance will cover your leak repair costs. But you’ll need photos of the damage for your claim.

Start by taking photos of the leak from the inside (if visible) and any damage that you can see on your roof. Additionally, include photos of anything ruined by the leak, such as a television or other device that was unlucky enough to be caught under the leak. By showing the extent of the damage, you greatly increase your odds of being compensated.

If your leak was caused by a passing storm, it can also be helpful to include news articles about the weather event. These become harder to find over time, so the sooner you save them, the easier it’ll be to get your insurance claim approved!

As veteran Florida roofers, we know our local community and how to help. ### Chimney Roof Leak

Homes with chimneys face a higher risk of leaking. In Florida, where the summers come with near-daily rain, this problem can be especially pronounced. But if you’re a homeowner who isn’t sure how to spot the signs of a chimney roof leak, it can be hard to act quickly enough to prevent permanent damage to your roof.

We’re PITCH Roofing, and as local roofers, nobody knows Florida and its roofing problems better than we do. If you’re concerned that you may have a leaking chimney, keep reading for our foolproof tips on spotting signs of a leak!
5 Ways to Spot a Chimney Roof Leak


Because of the way your chimney rises from your roof, it needs additional protection to keep water from entering where it attaches to your roofing system. Normally, these protections are handled during a roof installation. But when they are poorly installed or damaged over time, it’s likely to see a chimney roof leak in your home.

Now, let’s talk about the signs that you’re dealing with a leaking chimney.
1. Musty Smell from Your Fireplace
Many homeowners are surprised to learn that they may smell a chimney roof leak before they see it. But as water accumulates inside your chimney, it increases the humidity and can even cause mold growth. The result is a distinctive, pungent odor that may be stronger near your fireplace.

Even without the issue of a chimney roof leak, mold growth can be a major health hazard. If you suspect that your chimney is growing mold due to a leak, you’ll want to act quickly to minimize the effects of mold spores in your home.
2. Rusting Firebox
Noticing rust on the metal elements of your chimney is a classic sign of a leak. As the metal oxidizes, the overall structure of your chimney weakens. In this way, even a minor chimney roof leak can pose a serious threat to the safety of your home.

If you notice signs of rust near the firebox or damper, call a professional to assess the damage. Identifying the extent of the rust is the first step in determining how to fix your problem and how much your chimney roof leak repair will cost.
3. Ceiling Water Stains
Brownish splotches on your ceiling are a common sign of leaks. There are other causes of ceiling stains, but there are a few ways to tell if you’ve got a chimney roof leak. Some of the things to watch out for are:

 	Water stains that originate near your chimney and then spread
 	Stains that grow over time
 	Peeling paint or wallpaper

Any part of your roof can develop leaks and stains. But a chimney roof leak is even more concerning since it could affect the structural stability of your chimney and lead to a collapse. For this reason, it’s essential to act quickly if you suspect a leak in your chimney.
4. White Stains on the Chimney
Sometimes you may notice a problem on the exterior of your chimney before there’s a problem inside your home. White staining on your chimney’s exterior is one common example. Also called efflorescence, this discoloration appears when water evaporates off your chimney and leaves surface stains of minerals.

Once you see these stains, you’ll want to schedule a chimney inspection right away. Stains may not seem so bad when dealing with a chimney roof leak, but they can weaken the mortar holding your bricks together. Over time, this deterioration can collapse your chimney.
5. Gaps or Cracks in Your Bricks
If you find this issue on your chimney, then the water damage is likely already extensive. Loose or missing mortar is often the result of water eating away at your chimney over time. And if it erodes enough mortar, your entire chimney could be at risk.

Often, homeowners notice missing mortar as a second or third sign of a chimney roof leak. Regardless, getting a prompt chimney repair is the best thing that you can do to protect both your home and your chimney.
How Much Does a Chimney Roof Leak Repair Cost in Florida?


When we talk to homeowners about their chimney roof leaks, the cost of repairs is a common concern. And we get it — roofing problems probably weren’t in your monthly budget, and nobody wants to be surprised by a large bill. So what can you expect to pay to fix a chimney roof leak?

On the Florida market, chimney roof leak repairs average between $150 and $2,000. That’s a wide range, right? This price gap exists because there are so many different problems that could cause a leak, and how much it costs to repair your issue depends on both the cause and the extent of the damage.

For example, damaged or warped chimney flashing is a common cause of leaks. Replacing and reapplying new flashing will probably cost more than replacing a damaged chimney cap because of the higher labor and material costs. The price of the job can go up even further if there is widespread water damage as a result of your leak, which your roofers will have to repair to keep your home secure.

As you can see, how much you pay for leak repairs will come down to your unique situation. But that doesn’t mean you just have to guess at the price until you have a bill in front of you. The best way to get a personalized chimney roof leak repair cost is to sign up for a free roofing estimate.

### Should You Invest in a Solar Attic Fan?

When you buy a new roof, you don’t have to settle for the same old same old. Replacing or repairing your roof represents an opportunity to upgrade your roof’s performance. And if you, like many homeowners, are looking for a roof upgrade that will keep your home safe while saving you money, a solar attic fan is an excellent addition.

We’re PITCH Roofing, and as your local roofing partners, we’re here to make sure you get the most out of your roof. Today, we’re sharing what a solar attic fan can do for you. But before we get into the many benefits, let’s answer the most obvious question: What’s a solar attic fan?
What Is a Solar Attic Fan?


As the name implies, a solar attic fan is a solar-powered fan that, you guessed it, goes in your attic. By using a small, personal solar cell, these fans operate without raising your energy bill. And by dissipating hot, trapped air in your attic, a solar fan can help cool your entire home.

Of course, your attic already has ways of cooling itself. In fact, it has two important factors that contribute to its passive ventilation: vents and insulation. Insulation helps keep the hot air out of your attic, while vents help dissipate hot air while letting in cooler, fresher air. Together, they work to keep your attic cool and prevent it from overheating.

But these are imperfect systems. With active ventilation like what you’ll get with a solar attic fan, you can much more efficiently cool your attic and dissipate hot, trapped air. This will have many benefits for your home, but we’re going to discuss the biggest motivators that draw local homeowners toward upgrading their homes with solar attic fans.
Benefits of a Solar Attic Fan in Florida


Florida has more than a few chronic roofing issues, and it’s great to have high-quality products like solar attic fans to help mitigate them. Let’s look at the benefits you can expect from having an active form of ventilation cooling your attic!
Less Work for Your HVAC System
In the summer months, we all feel the spike in our energy bills from our AC working overtime. Even with a new, efficient HVAC system, having to cool your attic is a tough job. That’s partly because HVAC systems are only rated for 77°F. When your HVAC system gets above this temperature, it works less efficiently and needs more support. That’s where a solar attic fan can help.

By dissipating the heat in your attic, a solar fan makes the job of your HVAC system much easier. Without the added burden of cooling your attic, you can expect consistently lower energy bills in the summer. That’s a huge win for any homeowner in Florida!
Longer Life for Your Shingles
Did you know that a solar attic fan can actually make your roof last longer? That’s because shingles, while good at resisting heat, are not immune to high temperatures. Over time, too much heat can cause your shingles to crack, curl, and become more brittle. All of this results in a weaker roof that is less likely to last its full lifespan.

Unfortunately, having hot air trapped in your attic can make this issue even worse. Normally, a shingle dissipates some of its heat by transferring it to your attic. But if your attic is already full of hot air, it will take longer for that heat to transfer. This means your shingles spend more time at high temperatures, which can drastically shorten their lifespan.

That’s the beauty of a solar attic fan. By cooling your attic, they make it easier for your shingles to transfer heat and keep cool. This means less damage to your roof over time and a longer lifespan overall!
Federal Tax Credit for Your Wallet
We’ve already covered two ways that a solar attic fan can save you money. But thanks to a federal tax credit, you can even recoup some of the money spent on installing your new solar attic fan. Thanks to federal solar incentives, high-quality solar attic fans qualify for a 30% tax credit!

And at PITCH, we only install the best solar attic fans. We proudly work with Attic Breeze, whose third-generation solar attic fans meet the high standards to qualify for this tax credit. By investing in quality products for your roof, you can save money on your installation costs while improving your roof’s overall performance. And with Attic Breeze’s lifetime warranty, you can look forward to enjoying the benefits of your solar attic fan across your roof’s life!

### Replace My Own Roof

Even a cheap roof replacement isn’t that cheap. For many homeowners, having to spend thousands of dollars on a roof replacement is a serious blow to their finances. This leads many homeowners to ask themselves: Can I replace my own roof to save money?

The short answer is that yes, it is possible to replace your own roof. But whether or not that will actually save you money is a bit more complicated. We’re PITCH Roofing, your local roofing partners, and we’re here to de-mystify what it’s like to replace your own roof and what the perks are. Keep reading for a full guide on replacing your own roof in Florida!
Can I Replace My Own Roof to Save Money in Florida?


Florida weather has become especially devastating to roofs in recent years, so more and more homeowners are looking into DIY roof replacements as a way to reduce total roofing costs. And the good news is that there is legal precedent for this. According to Florida Statute 489.103(7)(a), homeowners have a legal right to replace their own roofs.

Replacing a roof is complicated, though, with many moving parts to manage. Let’s take a quick look at some of the logistics you’ll need to handle when replacing your own roof in Florida.
Acquire the Proper Roofing Permits for Your County
Every county has its own unique roofing requirements that will depend on the area you live in and the type of roof you’re installing. While it can be a lot of legwork to find and acquire all of the proper permits, this step is a crucial part of replacing your own roof.

Without proper permitting, you could be seriously fined by the county. Even if you aren’t fined, though, you’ll likely run into problems with your homeowners insurance. Insurance companies like to be sure that they’re insuring safe, well-installed roofs, and there’s no way to be sure of that without permits. By skipping this step, you could make your home uninsurable, which is a very risky position to be in as a Floridian.

If you decide to replace your own roof, you can start by looking into your county’s building department to see what permits are required for a homeowner working on their own roof. Make sure to plan a couple of days for running around, since you’ll likely have to make in-person appearances for these permits.
Plan Around Weather
Florida’s unpredictable weather is part of the reason many roofs need replacing, and it even gets in the way of installing a new roof. When you’re replacing your roof, you need dry conditions to protect the more vulnerable parts of your roofing system.

That’s why it pays to plan for a dry couple of days when replacing your own roof. If it starts to rain while your decking is exposed, you’ll need to quickly tarp over your roof and wait for the rain to pass. This can extend the timeline of your roof replacement, so it helps if you can plan to miss a week or more of work.

We also don’t generally recommend replacing your roof in the summer. Not only are thunderstorms an almost daily occurrence, but a tropical storm could do major damage to your roof if one rolls in before the installation is complete and approved by an inspector. To make matters worse, the heat can be hazardous, so it’s important to carefully choose when you do your DIY roof replacement.
Start Your DIY Roof Replacement
Once you’ve done some planning, you’re almost ready to start replacing your own roof! This is a complicated process, though, with many steps. The general outline of replacing your own roof will look like:

 	Purchasing roofing materials, including flashing, shingles, replacement decking, waterproof underlayments, vents, and other essential parts of your roofing system.
 	Ordering a dumpster and having it delivered to your property so that you can dispose of your old roof.
 	Supervising all work done by anyone who isn’t a licensed contractor. This is a legal requirement, so there’s no way to avoid being present on your roof throughout the length of the replacement.
 	Undergoing final inspection through a county-approved inspector. If the inspector finds any safety issues with your roof, you will have to fix these issues before being able to prove to your insurance company that your home has a new, insurable roof.

If this all sounds like a lot of hassle, that’s because it is. Replacing roofs is an industry full of people who undergo years of training to handle all of the logistical issues, and that’s before you account for the workmanship required to properly install a roof.

In short, it's complicated to replace a roof. And it's even harder for non-contractors. That’s why, even though you can replace your own roof, it’s usually a better idea to let the professionals handle it.
Should I Replace My Own Roof to Save Money in Florida?


The truth is that very few people should replace their own roofs. If you’re a former contractor who knows the permitting process and has a reliable crew of people to help out, then yes, it could make perfect sense for you to do a DIY roof replacement. For most other people, though, the truth is that replacing your own roof won’t save you a cent.

When factoring in the time required to take off work, it often costs more to replace your own roof. On top of that, you’ll probably end up paying more for your roofing materials since you don’t have connections with manufacturers to get discount rates for buying in bulk.

And all of this is before we even consider the quality of your roof. DIY roofs are much more likely to need multiple inspections before approval, and plenty of homeowners have tried to replace their roof only to have to hire professionals to do it again anyway. This is a waste of both your time and money, and it’s easy to skip it.

At PITCH, we understand that roof replacements are expensive and rarely come at a convenient time. And just because we don’t think most people should do DIY roof replacements doesn’t mean we don’t care about making roofing affordable for our customers. Let’s look at some more reliable ways that you can save money on your roof replacement!

### 7 Signs That You Should Replace Your Gutters

Your gutters, like your roof, will experience wear and tear as they age. Eventually, this means needing to get new gutters installed. But for many homeowners, it’s hard to tell when to replace gutters, and nobody is eager to make that investment before they have to.

That’s what we’re here to help you decide. We’re PITCH Roofing, and if you’re wondering when to replace your gutters, we’ve got the tell-tale signs. Keep reading for our personalized advice tailored to Florida homeowners!
When to Replace Gutters in Florida


Gutters are important wherever you live, but they’re especially crucial in Florida. With as much rain as we get, especially in the summer, gutters do the necessary work of moving water off your roof and away from your home’s foundations.

That’s why it’s essential to replace gutters as soon as they can no longer function properly. Now, let’s look at the ways you can tell when to replace gutters in Florida!
1. Cracks or Separation in Your Gutters
This is, hands down, the biggest sign that you need to replace your gutters. Unfortunately, it’s also the most likely issue that you’ll find. The spot where sections of your gutters connect is structurally the weakest part of your gutter system, and when a gap appears here, it disrupts the natural flow of water toward your downspouts.

As a result, the water can fall freely and eat away at your foundation and/or disrupt your landscaping. In either case, it’s important to get new gutters installed ASAP. Cracks and splits only get worse with time, so the longer the issue is left unaddressed, the more damage it could do to your home!
2. Eroding/Thinning Soil
You don’t always have to see damage in your gutters to tell that it’s time to replace them. One sign that you should replace gutters is the thinning of soil in your yard. This erosion is a sign that water is escaping your gutters before reaching your downspouts and destroying your landscaping.

This isn’t just an aesthetic issue, either. Your soil plays an important role in protecting your home’s foundation. As the soil gets thinner, your foundation can deteriorate faster and faster, eventually leading to major (and expensive) structural problems.
3. Gutter Sagging


Your gutters aren’t meant to hold much weight. So one sign to replace gutters is when you notice them sagging or pulling away from your roof. Most often, this is because they’re not draining properly and the weight of trapped water is damaging your gutters.

The good news is that this issue doesn’t always require a gutter replacement. It can also be caused by blocked gutters, so take a look at yours and determine if there’s any debris blocking the flow of water. If there isn’t, or if removing the debris doesn’t let the water drain, then it’s likely time to replace your gutters.
4. Peeling Paint
It can be tempting to dismiss peeling paint as an unimportant aesthetic problem, but it could point to a serious issue with your gutters. Peeling paint is often the result of extreme moisture — even more than the usual Florida humidity. So if your gutters or parts of your home surrounding them start to peel, it could be because your gutters aren’t draining properly.

Another sign of this issue is rust. Rust develops in areas where paint has peeled away, and if you see them, it’s important to replace your gutters ASAP. When rust isn’t addressed quickly, it can cause your gutters to develop holes. These will worsen your problem and could lead to rainwater eating away at your home’s foundation.
5. Pooling Water Around Your Home
When you think of pooling water, you might first be concerned about water collecting on your roof. But a sure sign that it’s time to replace gutters is when you notice water pooling around your home’s foundation. That’s because pooling water here clearly indicates that your gutters are no longer able to direct water away from your home.

Another sign that you need to replace your gutters is finding water pathways around your home. Even if the area is dry, channels for water to pass through mean that your gutter is failing to stop rainwater from accumulating around your home. If you see either of these signs, act quickly to get gutter replacement services!
6. Nails in Your Yard
Are you finding nails or screws seemingly at random in your yard? If so, it could be time to replace your gutters. In Florida, our hurricane-force winds can do a real number on gutters. Over time, these high winds can start to loosen the screws that attach your gutters to your home.

If you act quickly, you may be able to get away with a simple gutter repair, which will be much more affordable than a full replacement. Having contractors re-attach your gutters can fix this issue for a time, but you’ll want to keep an eye on your attachments in the future, especially during hurricane season.
7. Leaks or Ceiling Stains
In extreme cases, gutter problems can lead to leaks inside your home. That’s because water remains trapped on your roof and, over time, can start to penetrate into your roof. This is the most serious item on this list because, in addition to needing to replace your gutters, you may also need roof repair services to replace any damaged shingles and undo water damage.

If you have a leaking roof and other issues on this list, then there’s a good chance that your gutters are to blame. In addition to replacing gutters, you’ll also want to employ leak detection services to make sure you’re stopping the leak at its source and fixing any damage to your shingles and roof decking.
Get a Free Estimate to Replace Gutters on Your Home

While it can be helpful to look at gutter installation costs, the only way to get a 100% accurate number is to get a free roofing estimate. These essential parts of your gutters direct water away from your home’s foundation and landscaping features, protecting both the security and the beauty of your property. Still, installing them does add to your total gutter installation costs.For one thing, it takes time to carefully place downspouts around your property. This increases the total labor costs of your project.Downspouts themselves aren’t free, either. While their costs are low at about $30 to $75 per downspout, between four to five downspouts per home, this does contribute to higher gutter installation costs. ### Soffit Repair Services in Central Florida

Most of the time, soffits are an afterthought for homeowners. But when your soffits are damaged, you’ll quickly notice just how many problems can be avoided by having healthy, properly installed soffits. If you’ve recently noticed problems along the trim of your roof, then it’s time to get soffit repair services.

We’re PITCH Roofing, your local roofing partners. To help you keep your home safe and protected, we’re covering repair costs, the value of DIY soffit repairs, and how to pick the best roofing contractors near you. To get started, let’s answer one of the biggest questions we get: Should I replace my soffits on my own?
Is DIY Soffit Repair a Good Idea?


Many homeowners consider DIY roof repairs as a way to minimize their roofing costs. And we get it — roofing is often expensive. Still, there are a few things to know before you decide to handle your own soffit repair.

If you have experience as a roofing contractor, then it could make sense to replace your soffits yourself. However, many homeowners underestimate how difficult it is to repair or replace their soffits. Rather than just swapping out soffit boards, you’ll have to inspect the surrounding area for water damage and then attach a new cleat to the rafters, carefully apply your roof sealant, then re-install your roof’s molding. In other words, this process is anything but simple.

This isn’t the only reason that you should think carefully before doing any DIY soffit repairs. Another important issue is your homeowners insurance and roof warranty. Since soffits help keep water from penetrating into your home, any mistakes with installation could jeopardize your entire roofing system. That’s why insurance policies and warranties often have strong language about only allowing licensed contractors to work on any part of your roof, even your soffits.

So by attempting to save money replacing your own soffits, it could actually end up costing more in the long run by voiding your coverage. In short, DIY soffit repair can be a good idea for some people, but in most cases, it’s easier and safer to leave the job to the professionals.

Of course, if you’re going to hire contractors for your soffit repair, it’s natural to have questions about how much it will cost.
How Much Do Soffit Repairs & Replacements Cost?
In roofing, it’s always difficult to guess how much the job will cost without seeing your roof. That’s also true for soffit repair. While we know what factors can raise or lower your total roof repair costs, there’s no way to give you an exact figure without inspecting your roof ourselves.

But that doesn’t mean we can’t help. When replacing damaged sections of soffits, what you replace them with will largely determine how much you pay. Let’s look at the costs of different soffit materials:

 	Wood soffits are the most affordable option at $1 to $3 per square foot.
 	PVC soffits are reasonably priced at $3 to $7 per square foot.
 	Vinyl is just a bit more expensive at $5 to $8 per square foot.
 	Aluminum is the most expensive option at $8 to $20 per square foot, though many homeowners feel it’s worth the investment.

When you get your soffit repair cost estimate, your roofer will explain to you the pros and cons of your options to help you decide on the right material for your roof. But material costs aren’t the only factors that affect total repair costs. How much you pay for soffit repairs will also be influenced by:

 	Accessibility: The easier it is for roofers to work on your soffits, the less you’ll have to pay in labor costs.
 	Overhead: How much your contractors charge depends, in part, on their business model. Larger, national roofing companies have more overhead (national marketing campaigns, larger staff, etc.), so they generally have to charge more than small, local roofers.
 	Damage: The more widespread damage to your soffits is, the more you’ll be charged to fix it. This is because of roofers having to buy more materials and spend more time working on repairs.

These are the biggest factors in determining how much your soffit repair costs. But how do you get a real, reliable number?

FAQs About Soffits & Fixing Them in Florida


Q: How do soffits work?

A: Soffits, along with fascia, help keep water and pests out of your roofing system. That’s why soffit repairs are so essential. If you see rotting or other signs of deterioration on your soffits, then your entire roofing system could be at risk of water damage or a pest infestation.

Q: How do I know if I need soffit repairs?

A: Some of the biggest signs that your soffits need repaired or replaced include:

 	Cracks in your soffits
 	Visible water damage inside your home or on the soffits themselves
 	Peeling or chipping paint on your soffits
 	Signs of pest infestation in your roof

Q: What causes soffit damage?

A: In Florida, plenty of things can damage your soffits. Humidity, poor roof ventilation, and high winds are some of the most common causes that we see, largely due to Florida’s distinctive weather patterns.

Q: How long do soffit repairs take?

A: In most cases, replacing damaged soffits with new materials doesn’t take long. Unless you have large sections of damage, you can expect soffit repairs to take one day of work or less.

Q: How do I prevent soffit damage in the future?

A: To prevent future damage, ensure your gutters are clear and functioning properly, regularly inspect your roof and soffits for signs of wear, and address any leaks or pest issues promptly. Periodic maintenance and painting can also extend the life of wood soffits.

### Asphalt Shingle Repair Guide for Florida Homeowners

In Florida, there could be an issue with your shingle roof for any number of reasons. High winds could remove shingles from your home, UV rays can crack and curl your shingles, humidity can lead to mold growth, etc. So as a homeowner, it’s safe to assume that sooner or later you’ll need asphalt shingle repair services.

We’re PITCH Roofing, and as experienced Florida contractors, we’ve seen it all. So no matter what issue your shingle roof is having, you can count on us to fix the issue for you. Keep reading for a step-by-step guide of what to do when you think your shingle roof might be damaged!
Verify the Extent of Your Roof’s Damage


Missing a shingle or two after a major storm isn’t that big of a deal, usually. You might need new shingles installed, but the repairs can usually be done quickly and without spending much money. If the damage is more severe, though, you could be looking at a shingle roof replacement. This is both much more time-consuming and more expensive.

So how do you tell whether you need asphalt shingle repair services or a complete roof replacement? A good first step is to hop on your roof and take a look. Some of the signs that your roof needs repairs include:

 	A small number of missing or cracked shingles
 	Small water stains on your ceiling
 	Finding shingle granules in your gutters
 	Damage or twisting of your flashing
 	Early signs of mold or algae growth on your roof

All of these are fairly minor issues that, in most cases, won’t require a complete roof replacement. On the other hand, these signs could mean that it’s time to replace your shingle roof:

 	More than 25% of your roofing shingles are missing or cracked
 	Large sections of water damage, especially if interior damage is severe
 	Roof sagging
 	Shingles missing almost all their granules, leading to “bald patches”
 	Any minor signs of roofing damage on a shingle roof that’s over 20 years old

If you aren’t sure of the extent of your roofing damage, that’s okay. At PITCH, we offer roof inspections to determine the exact cause of your roofing issues. Whether you need asphalt shingle repair services or a full roof replacement, we’ve got the perfect crew for the job!
Apply a Patch to Prevent Further Damage
If you’ve confirmed that your roof needs repairs, then it’s important to act quickly. Once your roof is damaged, it will be much more vulnerable to more damage over time. Even a minor asphalt shingle repair job can quickly get worse if weak points are left exposed to the elements, so applying quick patches is a great way to keep your roof safe while you hash out the details with your roofers.

The goal of these patches is not to fix the core issue. In fact, trying to do your own asphalt shingle repairs could void your warranty and lead to issues with your homeowners insurance. Thankfully, you can apply most patches and sealants without violating any of these policies.

If you find a damaged section of your roof, buy a patch kit or sealant to prevent further damage. Patch kits come with new pieces of asphalt that you can apply over the damaged area to keep it protected and prevent damage from spreading. Sealants, on the other hand, are made of liquid rubber and can be applied over water leaks to prevent more water from making its way into your roofing system.

Whichever solution you choose, the important thing is to act quickly before Florida’s unpredictable weather worsens your roofing damage. From here, the only thing left to do is call in the professionals.

Otherwise, you could end up with a broken roof and no insurance coverage, which is a scary situation in Florida.

FAQs About Asphalt Shingle Repair in Florida


1. Q: Should I do my own asphalt shingle roof repairs?

A: Even if you have the skills for the job, we don’t recommend doing your own roof repairs. In addition to risking doing further damage, your warranty and homeowners insurance policy probably don’t allow for you to work on your own roof. So if you do your own repairs and then later a hurricane damages your roof, you could find yourself without coverage. This actually makes DIY repairs more expensive in many cases!

2. Q: How do you apply a patch kit to a shingle roof?

A: You can apply a patch kit over a damaged section of your roof by following these steps:

 	Clean the roof surface: Remove debris, dirt, or loose granules around the damaged area to ensure the patch adheres properly.
 	Apply roofing cement: Spread roofing cement under the surrounding shingles to help hold the new patch in place.
 	Insert the patch: Place the patch in the exposed area, aligning it with the existing shingles.
 	Seal with roofing cement: Apply roofing cement or another sealant over the edges of the patch or shingle to prevent water infiltration.
 	Press and secure: Press down on the patch or new shingle firmly, ensuring a good bond with the cement.
 	Allow time to set: Give the patch time to set and adhere, following the manufacturer’s instructions for curing time.

3. Q: Will my roof need replacing if I get it repaired?

A: No, in most cases getting asphalt shingle repairs doesn’t mean that your roof is nearing the end of its life. Most shingle repair jobs will last for the full life of your roof. However, if your roof needs many repairs, it could be a sign that it’s nearing the end of its life.

4. Q: When should I schedule asphalt shingle repairs?

A: The best time to repair your roof is always ASAP. Even minor damage can quickly grow out of control, so it’s important to act quickly if you think that your roof needs repairs.

5. Q: How much do shingle roof repairs cost?

A: In most cases, repairing asphalt shingles is very affordable. General asphalt shingle repair costs range from $500 to $1,500 or more for most repairs, but the number could be higher for bigger jobs. ### Are Shingle Roof Coatings Good for Florida Homes?

If you have a shingle roof, you probably wish that it lasted longer. High-quality shingle roofs can last for up to 25 years, but in the world of roofing, that isn’t much time. As a solution, many homeowners have tried shingle roof coatings that promise to make your roof last longer and better resist Florida’s tough weather conditions.

But do these coatings really work? We’re PITCH Roofing, and as veteran local roofers, we’ve seen plenty of homes with these coatings. Today, we’re sharing our findings with you to help you make the best decision for your home!
How Do Shingle Roof Coatings Work?


Shingle roof coatings generally come in one of two materials: silicone or acrylic. In either case, the general idea is the same: You coat your roof in the mixture with the hopes of it extending your roof’s lifespan.

Usually, the person selling you a shingle roof coating will pitch it one of two ways. If your roof is old, then they’ll tell you that a roof coating will extend the life of your roof thanks to the extra durability added by another layer.

If you have a new or undamaged roof, then the selling point will be that shingle roof coatings can prevent damage from rain or wind. In this way, the idea is that a shingle roof coating will keep your roof functional for longer and save you on repair costs.

In short, no matter what the state of your roof is, someone will be willing to sell you an expensive coating for your shingle roof. But does it really work?
5 Issues With Shingle Roof Coatings
In theory, a protective coating for your roof sounds like a great way to prevent problems. The reality, unfortunately, is a little more complicated. Let’s talk about some of the biggest pitfalls that homeowners run into with these “protective” coatings!
1. A Good Shingle Roof Is Already Protected
When reading claims of what a shingle roof coating can do, you’ll hear it all. These include claims that the coatings will make your roof waterproof, improve their wind resistance, etc. There’s just one problem with these claims, though: your roof should already be able to resist the Florida elements without a problem.

Asphalt shingles are made from a baseboard of fiberglass, a thick coating of asphalt, and protective stone granules. With proper installation, shingles won’t have any trouble keeping water out of your home or resisting winds of 110 mph or more.

If your roof does struggle to hold up against wind and rain, that’s a serious problem. But the solution to roofing problems isn’t to cover your roof in a new coating. Rather, you should address the structural issues so that your roof can function as it was always intended to.
2. Shingle Roof Coatings Cause New Damage


Not only do shingle roof coatings not offer much in the way of protection, but they can actually damage your roof. When trapped under a thick coating of silicone or acrylic, your shingle loses all ability to dissipate heat. This can lead to premature curling or cracking of your shingles. As a result, your roofing system will not last as long.

For this reason, many insurance companies take issue with shingle roof coatings. Whether getting one of these coatings will void your roof’s coverage depends on your specific insurer and policy. But given that these coatings can already do more harm than good, we don’t recommend risking your coverage in Florida, where a major storm could destroy any roof, regardless of whether or not it has a coating.
3. Coatings Distort Aesthetics
When you invest in high-quality architectural shingles, part of what you pay for is their distinctive patterning. Also called dimensional shingles, these roofing materials create depth and dimension on your roof. Unfortunately, all of this beauty goes away once you add on a shingle roof coating.

Shingle coatings are generally one color, most often black or white. Not only does this obliterate that visual interest that architectural shingles create, but it also rarely looks even. That’s because shingles weren’t made to be coated in another material, and applying that coating evenly on a sloped roof can be almost impossible. As a result, most roofs with these coatings look uneven and patchy.
4. Coatings Don’t Fix Major Problems
If your roof is old or damaged, you’ve probably been told that a shingle roof coating can make it last longer for less than the cost of roof repairs or a roof replacement. But this simply isn’t true. If your roof has a real problem, then a coating won’t be able to fix it.

In some cases, coatings make the problem even worse. Take a leak for instance. If your roof has water trapped under the shingles, then applying a coating doesn’t resolve the issue — it just traps water in your roof. This can lead to rot or mold growth, both of which will be harder to fix with your shingles covered in a coating. So in the end, you can bet that your protective coating won’t actually end up saving you money!
5. Coatings Are Not Cheap
On top of all the problems above, shingle roof coatings aren’t even especially affordable. They are cheaper than roof replacements, but they’re far from cheap. This is because applying these coatings takes a lot of time and effort, so your labor costs will be substantial.

Without knowing the specific brand of shingle roof coating you’re considering or who’s offering to apply it, we can’t say exactly how large the price difference will be. In our experience, though, these coatings tend to cost around 60% of the cost of a shingle roof replacement.

So if your roof had a major issue and needed replacing, it might cost around $10,000 to get a new shingle roof (depending on many unique factors). This new shingle roof will last 20-25 years. Or you could spend around $6,000 for a shingle roof coating that may, at best, extend your roof’s lifespan by a couple of years or, at worst, damage your roof further and make your roof replacement even more expensive.

For our money, we know which one we’d pick.
