### Causes of Ceiling Water Stains

Finding ceiling water stains in your home or business can be alarming. In addition to being unsightly, these stains often indicate a larger problem in your structure. Unfortunately, there are so many different causes of ceiling water stains that it can be hard to know what to do or who to call.

Luckily, there are ways to determine the cause of your ceiling water stains. We’re PITCH Roofing, your local roofing partners. Today, we’re putting our roofing expertise to use and helping you take the first steps to resolve the cause of your water stains. Keep reading for our complete guide!
Determining if You Have Ceiling Water Stains


When you see discoloration on your ceiling, your first thought is probably water damage. However, there are other causes of ceiling stains, and determining if you really have ceiling water stains is the first step in fixing the problem.

One common cause of ceiling discoloration is smoke. Whether from cigarettes, candles, or something else, this can create a brownish color that looks very similar to water damage. There are some notable differences between the two patterns, though.

Size is the best way to determine if your stain is from water or smoke. Smoke stains tend to have smaller areas of discoloration. Water stains, on the other hand, spread in amorphous shapes and may even appear damp (though not all water stains do). Water stains are also often darker in color, especially if they’re left for significant lengths of time.

If you think that your home or business has ceiling water stains, then it’s important to get help before the issue gets worse. However, knowing who to call can be tricky, which is why it’s important to be able to identify the cause of your ceiling discoloration.
How to Find the Cause of Your Ceiling Water Stains


Generally, you can attribute ceiling water stains to roof damage or a problem with your pipes. Knowing which one is behind your problem is key — after all, you wouldn’t call a plumber to do a roofer’s job, or vice versa. To help you know which services you need, let’s look at how you can tell the cause of your water stains!
Roofing Leaks
Roof leaks are a common cause of ceiling water stains, especially on older roofs. While a functional roofing system can keep water out, even minor damage can weaken the structural integrity of your roof and allow for water to sneak in. So how do you know if this is the cause of your issue?

The location of the water stain can tell you a lot about the cause. If your stain is near a skylight, chimney, or other roof perforation, this is a good indicator that the problem is a leak. Contractors seal roof perforations when they install your roof, but over time the seals can wear down, which leads to leaks.

If you really want to be sure that it’s a roof leak, getting on your roof and taking a look around can be a good idea. If you see damaged or missing shingles, then that is probably the cause of your ceiling water stains. The good news, though, is that fixing or replacing a handful of shingles is a quick and easy repair!
Leaking Pipes
Just as common as roof leaks, leaking pipes can easily cause ceiling water stains. This is an even more urgent problem than a leak in your roof since your roof at least won’t be damaged when it’s not actively raining. With a leak in your pipes, however, the damage is constant. That's why you need to act quickly to determine the cause and prevent further harm to your home or business.

Like with roof leaks, location can give you an idea of whether or not your stains were caused by a plumbing issue. Specifically, if your leak happens near a sink or a toilet, then there’s a good chance that the issue is with your plumbing. Plumbing problems are also especially likely causes in homes with newer roofs. If your roof is under five years old, there’s a very low chance that a roof leak is the cause of your stains.

If you suspect that leaking pipes are your problem, turn off the water immediately. More water escaping into your ceiling means more damage and more expensive repairs. Once you’ve shut off the water, call a plumber to come fix your pipes. If you catch the problem early enough, there’s every chance that the necessary repairs will be minimal and won’t break the bank!
Poor Roof Ventilation
If you don’t think that a roof leak or a plumbing issue caused your ceiling water stains, then problems with your roof ventilation could be the culprit. Healthy roofs are able to release hot air and moisture while allowing in small amounts of fresh air to keep your attic dry and safe. When these systems fail, though, you can start noticing issues like ceiling water stains due to condensation.

The best way to identify a ventilation problem is to take a peek at your attic. Once you’re up there, look for signs of moisture or mold growth. If you find that it’s humid and has mold, especially if you can’t see a clear sign of a leak, then there’s a good chance that poor ventilation is causing your ceiling water stains.

If ventilation is your issue, then call in roofers to fix whatever issue is causing these stains. Most often the solution is as simple as replacing old, damaged vents. Additionally, they may add extra insulation to your attic to help keep hot, humid air outside.
Get a Free Estimate for Repairing Ceiling Water Stains
If you think that your ceiling water stains were caused by a roofing problem, then you need reliable contractors to handle your repairs. That’s us. PITCH Roofing offers dedicated leak detection and restoration services, so even if you’re not sure exactly what the cause is, we’ll be happy to figure it out and provide a long-lasting solution.

We’ll inspect your roof, have a quick chat with you about what we’ve found, then prepare a detailed estimate that covers the full scope of work for your leak repair. ### The Best Home Addition Roofing Contractors Near You

A home addition is a fantastic way to expand your living space. However, as you probably know, this is a major investment in both time and money. For the best, highest-quality addition to your space, it’s essential not to skimp on home addition roofing.

Common Problems in Home Addition Roofing


In many ways, home addition roofing is much more complicated than getting a roof replacement. With a roof replacement, you’re mostly just replacing the outside-facing materials and updating what’s already there. With a home addition, however, your goal is to build a new roof from scratch. This is a much larger enterprise, which means much more can go wrong.

Here are some of the biggest issues with home addition roofing that you’ll want to watch out for!
Proper Insulation and Ventilation
Without proper insulation or ventilation, you can feel a temperature differential between the main house and the addition. This is especially apparent in the summer when the rest of your home might be crisp and cool, but the addition is several degrees warmer.

Not only is this unpleasant, but it can also have larger ramifications. Poor insulation or ventilation in your addition’s roof means that your air conditioning system will have to run more or less constantly to try to keep it at the temperature of the rest of the home. This can both run up your energy bill and shorten the lifespan of your AC system!
Roofline Integration
Home addition roofing is not just about creating a strong roof for your addition. You also need your contractors to ensure that your new roofline meets your existing roofline in a way that’s natural and seamless.

This isn’t just an aesthetic issue, either. While proper roofline integration does give your home a great profile, there are more pragmatic concerns. Namely, failing to match the rooflines can lead to issues with water drainage, which in turn can cause persistent leaks. A problem like this isn’t quick or cheap to fix, either, so it’s important to choose roofers who will get the job done right the first time.
Matching Materials
If your home addition’s roof is made of the same material as the main structure, then you probably want a perfect match. This is often easier said than done, though. Not only can manufacturers struggle to find the exact right type of roofing material, but age and weathering can leave a visual marker between your old roof and your home addition.

Solving issues like this requires expert know-how and relationships with roofing material manufacturers. For your home addition roofing project, look for qualifications like being an Owens Corning Preferred Contractor to ensure that your roofers can reliably source materials that will perfectly blend your two roofs together.
Structural Load Balancing
It’s easy to forget just how heavy a roof is. Even with relatively lightweight architectural shingles, you’re looking at 60-80 pounds per bundle, and that’s before you add in decking, underlayments, and other essential parts of your roofing system.

With home addition roofing, you have the weight of two roofs to worry about. And without proper planning, the point where these two roofs can be improperly balanced. When this happens, it can lead to extra weight being put on one of your roofs, which can lead to roof sagging and, over time, massive structural damage.
Picking the Best Home Addition Roofers in Florida


Above are just a few of the things that can go wrong with home addition roofing. That’s why it’s essential that you pick experienced contractors who know how to avoid these issues and deliver a high-quality, new roof.

### Roof Replacements vs. New Roof Construction: 3 Crucial Differences

If you’ve gotten a roof replacement for your home or business before, it’s easy to think that your experience with new roof construction will be more or less the same. And it’s true that there are similarities — they both put on a new roof, after all. These two processes have many differences, however, and you’ll want to be aware of them to properly plan your new roof construction.

That’s what we’re here for! PITCH Roofing is your local roofing partner for all things roof replacement and new roof construction. Today, we’re discussing the differences between these services and what you should know before hiring contractors. Whether you’re planning a unique new structure or want an addition to your home, keep reading for everything you’ll want to know in advance!
1. Roof Replacement & New Roof Construction Are Different Jobs


Both roof replacements and new roof construction have different scopes of work. For one thing, a roof replacement naturally requires removing your old roof, something that isn’t necessary when building a new roof from scratch. This is essentially the only way in which a roof replacement is less work than a new roof construction.

In all other areas, new roof construction requires much more time and effort. With a roof replacement, your contractor is just building a roofing system on top of what’s already there. New roof construction, on the other hand, requires designing your unique roof according to a building or addition that is being built. This requires in-depth analysis of your structure to determine what type of roof will best suit its long-term protection!

For this reason, you can generally expect new roof construction to cost more than a roof replacement. Your total new roof construction costs will depend on the size, slope, and materials of your new roof, but a good rule of thumb is that building a new structure’s roof will cost more than adding a roof to an addition, which will, in turn, cost more than a regular roof replacement. For more concrete cost estimates, it’s best to get a quote from your chosen roofers!
2. New Roof Construction Gives You More Options
When getting a roof replacement, you have your pick of roofing options. More or less. But with new roof construction, you can truly get any kind of roof that you want since you can alter the structure to support virtually any type of roof.

For example, tile roofs are extremely popular in Florida. However, some homes can’t support them because of their heavy weight. If you were getting a roof replacement and your structure couldn’t take this weight, the only solution would be to add additional support to your home — a slow and expensive process. With new roof construction, though, you can plan ahead and install those supports now to get you your ideal roof.

With the whole world of roofing materials open to you, you’ll be able to pick from Florida’s favorites, like:

 	Asphalt shingles
 	Composite (synthetic) shingles
 	Concrete and clay roofing tiles
 	Standing seam and corrugated metal roofs
 	Flat roofing materials like TPO and modified bitumen

When choosing materials for your new roof construction, you’ll want to have several factors in mind. These include the aesthetic that you want for your new construction, how often you want to have to repair or replace the roof, and your budget. A new roof construction is a unique opportunity to get the perfect roof, but with all of these competing factors, it’s especially important that you work with reliable roofers who can answer your questions along the way.
3. Picking Quality Roofers for New Roof Construction Is Essential


When planning a roof replacement, you need experienced roofers who know how to install your chosen roofing material. This is an important job, but it simply isn’t as involved as planning and executing a new roof construction.

As we mentioned, planning a unique roof for your structure or addition requires in-depth analysis of the property. This means that not only is new roof construction more work than a roof replacement, but it also has much more serious consequences if you choose the wrong roofers.

Think of it this way: If roofers make a mistake during a roof replacement, this can put your entire roofing system in jeopardy. Fixing the problem will probably be expensive, but you should be able to resolve the issue within a number of days once crews start working on it. In the best-case scenario, it won’t require another roof replacement.

Things are very different with the construction of a new roof. Since it encompasses so much more work, a mistake during this crucial stage could be disastrous. In all likelihood, fixing the problems this creates (which could take months to show signs) will require removing your roof entirely and addressing structural issues with your property. You can count on this being both slow and expensive, even before they have to install a new roof to cover the structure.

For this reason, you cannot be too careful when picking reliable roofers. Make sure to pick contractors who have both local roofing experience and great reviews to back them up. At PITCH, we never expect our customers to take it on faith that we’re reliable roofers. Instead, we show them our commitment to quality workmanship and customer service through our actions.

FAQs About New Roof Construction in Florida


1. Q: How long does it take to complete a new roof installation in Florida?

A: How long it takes to install your new roof will depend on the size of the building, the roofing material you’ve chosen, and how cooperative the weather is. In some cases, a new roof can be installed in a day or two, but other jobs may require several weeks. To get a better idea of how long your new roof installation may take, it’s a good idea to ask the roofer who comes to prepare your estimate.

2. Q: Are there specific codes for new roof construction in Florida?

A: Yes, the Florida Building Code has many specific provisions. These ensure that new roofs meet high standards for design, materials, and installation. For this reason, you’ll want to work with experienced roofers who know the regulations inside and out and can ensure that your new roof is compliant with local rules!

3. Q: How can I ensure that the new roof is hurricane-resistant?

A: When hurricane-proofing your roof, you’ll first want to choose wind-resistant roofing materials like metal or tile. Additionally, it’s always a good idea to invest in strengthening features like hurricane straps to reinforce roof-to-wall connections.

4. Q: How much does new roof construction cost?

A: How much it costs to install your new roof will depend on a wide variety of factors. These include your chosen roofing materials, the size and slope of your roof, roof accessibility, and unique roofing features. That’s why the cost range for a new roof installation is wide, ranging from $10,000 to upwards of $40,000 depending on the specifics of the job.

5. Q: What roof materials are best for new roof construction?

A: “Best” is subjective, but there are especially popular roofing materials in Florida. Asphalt shingles remain the top choice for new residential structures, whereas metal and flat roofing materials are the norm for low-slope commercial roofs.

### Membrane Roof Cost Guide for Floridians

Whether or not you should get a membrane roof is a complicated question. Issues like roofing needs, your structure’s location, and your budget all play a big role. That’s why you need up-to-date information on single-ply roofing membrane costs and considerations!

We’re PITCH Roofing, and as your local roofing partner, we make it our business to keep you informed on local roofing issues. Florida has plenty of flat roofs that need protecting, and sometimes a membrane roof is the perfect solution. Other times though, there are better options for unique situations. Let’s talk about the latest information on membrane roofing in Florida so you can make an informed decision!
How Much Does a Membrane Roof Cost in Florida?


Roofing prices are always changing, which is why you need the most current numbers. Generally speaking, flat roofing materials tend to come in at a similar price point. But when trying to plan a major investment like a flat roof replacement, it helps to have the most accurate information possible.

Right now, TPO membrane roofs cost between $4 to $10 per square foot. Put another way, a membrane roof replacement for a 1,500-square-foot building would cost between $6,000 and $15,000. This is a wide range, but it includes both manufacturing and installation costs. If you want to get a better idea of where your roof replacement costs will fall on this spectrum, let’s talk about the different pricing factors that will affect the cost of your flat roof replacement.
Membrane Roof Cost Pricing Factors
The size of your roof and your material of choice aren’t the only factors that determine your roof replacement costs. This is why roofing companies encourage getting personalized estimates instead of giving out flat rates — there are simply too many variables. That said, by looking at the different factors affecting membrane roofing costs, you can get a sense of whether you should expect to pay on the higher or lower end of the spectrum.

Here are the biggest factors affecting membrane roof costs in Florida!
Unique Roofing Features
The more features affecting your roof, the more you can expect to pay for a membrane roof replacement. These include any and all roof perforations like skylights, chimneys, vents, HVAC units, etc.

The price increase comes, in part, from increased time and labor costs. A fast, simple membrane roof replacement only requires roofers to roll out the membrane and adhere it to your roof. These roof perforations, however, require them to stop and seal the areas around each and every roofing feature to ensure that water can’t get in.

Material costs are another reason for this price increase. Sealing roof perforations requires extra materials, which will further increase the total cost of your flat roof replacement. For these reasons, the fewer unique roofing features your flat roof has, the lower you can anticipate your membrane roofing costs to be.
Previous Roofing Damage


Good roof maintenance doesn’t just prevent damage and make repairs cheaper. It can also go a long way in keeping your membrane roof replacement costs down. That’s because the state of your flat roof has everything to do with how much you’ll pay for a new one.

When getting a membrane roof, that roof sits on top of your roof decking. Without proper maintenance, your decking can receive water damage that weakens the overall structure of your flat roof. So when getting a membrane roof replacement, your roofers will replace any damaged sections of decking. Thankfully decking isn’t very expensive, but it does represent an increase in both time and labor costs to replace it before starting on the rest of your flat roof replacement.
Roof Slope
Many people believe that flat roofs are exactly that — flat. While this confusion is understandable, very few flat roofs are actually flat, and the few that are were installed a long time ago. Nowadays, almost every “flat” roof is, in reality, a low-slope roof.

Modern roofing codes generally require that all roofs have at least a slight slope to them. This is to help with drainage and prevent water pooling on your flat roof. But if your flat roof hasn’t been replaced in a while, it may not comply with these updated standards. That means that when you get your new membrane roof, you can expect to pay extra to have this slope added and keep your roof in compliance with local ordinances.
Flat Roof Accessibility
Many property owners overlook the importance of making sure that it’s easy to get on and off your roof. Issues like overgrown landscaping or inaccessible patios can make it harder for contractors to access your roof. And the harder it is to access your roof, the more you’ll end up paying for a membrane roof replacement.

This is because accessibility issues make the entire job take longer. So that extra time getting on and off your roof both slows down the project and increases your labor costs. There is no way to say exactly how much this could increase your total costs, but if it causes a major slowdown in labor, then you can expect the cost different to be significant. That’s why it pays to clear your yard and make things as easy for your roofers as possible!
Find Out How Much Your Membrane Roof Will Cost
All of these factors will influence how much your membrane roof costs. And by being aware of them, you can guestimate roughly where you roofing price might fall. There is only one way to be sure of how much you’ll pay for a new flat roof, though, and that’s to get a personalized roofing quote.

### Guide to Tile Roof Repairs in Florida

Tile roofs are famous for their longevity and durability. This doesn’t mean that you’ll never need tile roof repair services, however. When your roof does eventually need repairs, picking the right roofers is an essential step in getting your roof back in top shape.

That’s where we come in. PITCH Roofing is your local roofing partner with plenty of Florida roofing experience. Today, we want to talk about common tile roof repairs and how we can help if your roof is having problems. We’re starting off by covering the most common tile roof repairs in Florida!
The Most Common Tile Roof Repairs


Whether you have clay or concrete tiles, your roof is going to last for a long time. Despite this longevity, though, occasional repairs are all but unavoidable. That’s because tile roofs, while strong, have vulnerabilities that lead to occasional issues.

Let’s talk about some of the most common tile roofing problems that we fix every day!
Cracked Tiles
It takes a lot of force to break a roofing tile. Unfortunately, a lot of force is exactly what you can expect during a hurricane or hailstorm. Either hail or storm debris can slam into your roof, cracking a tile or two and opening the way for future water damage.

Thankfully, you can avoid larger problems by moving quickly. When we get called out for this tile roof repair, we quickly replace the broken tile(s) and re-seal your roof to make sure that it’s completely waterproof and structurally sound. This is among the cheapest tile roof repairs, so all things considered, it’s not a bad problem to have!
Fasteners Uplifting
When installed correctly, a tile roof should be securely nailed into place. Unfortunately, tile roofs are not always installed correctly. Inexperienced contractors may accidentally misuse their nail guns and not drive the nail as deep as it needs to go. Over time, this can lead to your nails starting to uplift as they’re exposed to the elements, putting your entire roofing system in jeopardy.

The best way to avoid this headache is to carefully choose your tile roof installers. But if the damage is already done, you can still count on tile roof repair professionals to fix this problem. Our crews remove any lifting nails, resolve any water or wind damage that they’ve caused, and then re-install the tiles so they’re stronger than ever before. When it comes to tile roof repairs, this is the kind of comprehensive restoration that you should look for!
Damaged Flashing
There are plenty of ways that your roof’s flashing can be damaged. Storm debris or hail can cause impact damage, poor installation can cause it to function incorrectly, and it can even just get too old to work. But your flashing protects your vents, which are an essential part of your roofing system. So if your tile roof has flashing damage, it’s essential to get repairs ASAP.

How we handle your flashing repair will depend on how it was damaged. Sometimes the original material can be salvaged, but in other cases we may have to completely remove it and reinstall new flashing. Either way, you can count on the tile roof repair pros at PITCH to resolve the issue and get your roof back to its full strength.
Picking Tile Roof Repair Professionals


Whether you’re experiencing one of the issues above or something totally different, you need tile roof repair contractors that you can trust. The problem is that every roofing company claims to be the best in the area. Let’s look at some ways you can find real, reliable tile roof repair pros near you!
Excellent Roofing Reviews

### Should You Get a Roof Overlay for Your Home or Business?

A roof replacement is a major investment. But did you know that it’s not the only option available if your roof is at the end of its life? Getting a roof overlay could be a way to cut down costs while giving your roof a new layer of protection. However, this solution isn’t right for every case.

We’re PITCH Roofing, and as Florida’s most trusted roofing company, we’re here to help you decide if a roof overlay is right for you. Keep reading as we cover the good and the bad of installing a second layer to your roof!
What Is a Roof Overlay?


Roof overlays are, in the simplest possible terms, when you install a new roof over top of your old one. This is usually done with old shingle roofs, but that doesn’t mean your new roof has to be made of the same shingles. For example, if your shingle roof has reached the end of its life, you could get a roof overlay of new shingles or upgrade to a metal roof.

Either way, the result is a strong, resilient roof installed on your roof without the need to remove your old one. For this reason, roof overlays are sometimes called re-roofing jobs, since the roof is being layered over instead of replaced.

But is re-roofing a good idea in Florida? Well, that depends. Florida roofs need to withstand some of the most adverse weather conditions in the country. In some cases a roof overlay is more than capable of meeting these high standards, but in other cases, you’re better off going with a roof replacement.
Pros & Cons of Roof Overlays in Florida
To help you decide if a roof overlay is right for you, let’s discuss the upsides and downsides of this roofing option!
Pro: Faster & Cheaper Than Roof Replacements
The biggest draw of getting a roof overlay is the time and money saved. Without the need to remove your old roof, the entire job goes much faster. On average, removing a roof takes 4-6 hours. This isn’t a huge amount of time, but when you’re factoring in labor costs for roof replacements, 4-6 hours is a significant amount of time and money.

How much money does getting a roof overlay save you, though? Compared to roof replacements, roof overlays are usually about 25% cheaper. Given that roof replacements cost, on average, around $13,000, this means you could save around $3,250 by getting a roof overlay for your old shingle roof. For many homeowners, this price difference makes getting a new roof much more affordable!
Con: Doesn’t Fix Existing Issues
One of the great things about getting a roof replacement is that it gives your roof a clean slate. With a full roof replacement, everything is removed and newly installed, including damaged decking and ventilation systems. This means that if your old roof has any leaks or other common roofing problems, the damaged parts will be replaced with brand-new, functional pieces.

This isn’t the case with a roof overlay, though. Since a new layer is added onto your old roof, the old problems are still there. That said, getting a roof overlay should still fix issues like leaks because water won’t be able to reach your old shingles.

However, any water damage will remain. This means that if your roof decking has water damage from a leak, it will remain damaged. This can lead to a lack of support for the two roofs now on your structure. For this reason, a roof overlay is often not a great idea if you know that your roof has significant water damage or other structural issues that a roof overlay can’t fix.
Pro: Extra Insulation
During the hot Florida summers, the more insulation you have on your roof, the better. Many homeowners pay good money to get extra insulation that will help keep the cool air inside their homes and keep out the sweltering heat of summer. With a roof overlay, you can get extra insulation while saving money.

Since you essentially have two roofs on your home, you enjoy twice the insulation. While shingle roofs are not normally known for their fantastic insulation, having two layers of shingles is enough to provide significant cooling. This has the bonus of lowering monthly energy bills since your AC won’t have to work as hard!
Con: You Can’t Get a Roof Overlay More Than Once


A roof overlay is an affordable alternative to roof replacements, but it’s not something that you can repeat on the same roof. In most cases, there is no danger in having the weight of two roofs on your structure. However, that doesn’t mean you can keep adding weight forever.

Reliable roofers will not offer a roof overlay more than once on the same roof. This means that when your roof eventually needs replacing, you will have to have your two roofs removed so that a new one can be installed. In this way, the savings of a roof overlay are only temporary. However, this can still be a great solution if you think you’ll have more funds in the future or don’t plan to still be in the home.

That eventual roof replacement may come sooner than you think, too. Shingle roof overlays last a long time, but rarely more than 15 years or so. On the other hand, a shingle roof replacement averages around 25 years in Florida. This doesn’t mean that you can’t enjoy the advantages of a roof overlay, but it’s important to know what you’re signing up for when you make this investment in your property.
Pro: Less Disruptive
If you own an apartment complex or other multi-family dwelling, then you probably want to minimize disruption to your residents. If this sounds like your situation, then a roof overlay could be exactly what you need. Since contractors won’t need to tear off your roof, they also won’t need to haul in a dumpster to store the old roof.

And since the entire job will go faster, that means less time with your residents’ lives being disrupted. Keeping residents happy is always ideal, so this time-saving method could be best for your wallet and your residents!
Get a Free Estimate for a Roof Overlay or Roof Replacement
Clearly, getting a roof overlay has both considerable advantages and drawbacks that make it not right for every situation. But whether you decide to go with re-roofing or a traditional roof replacement, PITCH has you covered. With either choice, the next step is getting a free, no-cost roofing quote.

At PITCH, our estimates are second to none. They’re detailed, thorough, and give you all the information you need to make an informed decision. For your free roof overlay or replacement estimate, call us at 727-677-4824 or sign up for your estimate online. As experienced roofers with great reviews and elite status as Owens Corning Preferred Contractors, we’ll be happy to explain your options and help make sure your roof is perfectly suited to your needs!

Price will always be a deciding factor in roof replacements. Unfortunately, it can be tricky to get reliable information about the average cost of a new roof in Florida. Average Cost of a New Roof Video

What’s the Average Cost of a New Roof in Florida?


Part of the reason it’s so hard to find accurate roof replacement cost information is the sheer number of variables. How much your roof costs will depend on the slope of your roof, the state of your decking, and your roof’s complexity, among a host of other factors. But above all, which roofing material you pick will have a huge impact on the cost of your new roof.

That’s why we’re going to look at the average costs of Florida’s favorite roofing materials! By breaking it down material by material, we’ll help you plan for your roof replacement costs. Keep reading for a comprehensive look at Florida roofing costs!
Price of Asphalt Shingle Roof Replacements
Asphalt shingles are by far the most popular roofing material in North America. That’s not shocking — they’re reliable, have respectable wind resistance, and suit a wide variety of styles and tastes. But another big part of their popularity is their low roofing costs.

At PITCH, we generally recommend choosing architectural asphalt shingles. These cost marginally more than 3-tab shingles, but they can give your roof 25 years of protection, whereas 3-tab shingles would be lucky to last 15 years on a Florida roof. And if you’re worried about the average cost of a new shingle roof, we’re happy to report that you can still get a great bargain with architectural shingles.

On average, architectural asphalt shingles cost between $4 and $8 per square foot. So for a 2,000-square-foot roof replacement, you’re only paying $8,000 to $16,000. In the world of roof replacements, that’s a fantastic price for a high-quality roof, so we strongly recommend this for homeowners on a tight budget!
Price of Tile Roof Replacements
In Florida, tile roofing comes in two popular materials: clay and concrete. In addition to significant cost differences, these roofs also perform very differently. While both are excellent luxury roofing options, concrete tiles last about 50 years on average, while clay tile roofs have been known to last for upwards of a century!

The average cost of a new concrete tile roof ranges from $10 to $19 per square foot. On a 2,000-square-foot roof, that puts your total roof replacement costs between $20,000 and $38,000. This is far from a cheap roof replacement, but it’s certainly more budget-friendly than clay tiles.

Clay tile roof replacements average between $12 and $21 per square foot. A $2 difference may not feel like much, but spread across a 2,000-square roof, that’s $24,000 to $42,000, so the difference is actually thousands of dollars. Still, if you want the longest-lasting roof possible, clay tiles are an excellent choice!
Price of Metal Roof Replacements


There are many different types of metal roof replacements. But in Florida, three in particular are especially popular. Let’s look at the average cost of a new metal roof:

 	Corrugated Metal Roof: These exposed fastener roofing systems have the shortest lifespan at around 50 years. However, they’re also the most affordable metal roofing option. On average, these roofs cost $5 to $9 per square foot. Or, on a 2,000-square-foot roof, $10,000 to $18,000.
 	Stone-Coated Steel Roof: These roofs offer classic metal roof strength without the distinctive look. They also enjoy long lifespans of 50-70 years. And with roof replacement costs between $7 and $15 per square foot, you can get a stone-coated steel roof replacement for a reasonable $14,000 to $30,000 on average.
 	Standing Seam Metal Roof: Standing seam is the gold standard of metal roofing. Sleek, durable, and with a lifespan of 50-70 years, these roofs exemplify the best that metal roofing has to offer. They’re also expensive though, with total roofing costs between $10 and $35 per square foot, or $20,000 to $70,000 for a 2,000-square-foot roof replacement.

Metal roofs are never the cheapest option on the market, but they’re always strong and reliable. And with Florida’s hurricane seasons becoming more and more active, paying a bit over the average cost of a new roof could be worth the investment!
Price of Flat Roof Replacements
Florida is somewhat unique in its approach to flat roofing. While in many cases flat roofs are synonymous with commercial roofing, both residential and commercial structures in Florida can have flat roofs. In our experience, whether it’s for a home or business, TPO roofing and modified bitumen are the two most popular flat roofing options.

TPO is a rubberized, single-ply roofing membrane. In other words, it’s what people call a “rubber roof.” This new roofing technology is estimated to last for about 30 years, which is a long time in the world of flat roofing. TPO  also has a reasonable price point between $3 and $8 per square foot, or $6,000 to $16,000 across 2,000 square feet of flat roofing.

Modified bitumen is a more classic option, made up of asphalt, rubberized polymers, and a fiberglass base. It doesn’t age quite as well, though, so you can only expect around 20 years of protection. Still, with modified bitumen average roofing costs of $3 to $5 per square foot, or $6,000 to $10,000 per roof, this is a great option for people who want a low-cost option that will still perform well.

### What Is Considered an Old Roof? Guide for Florida Homeowners and Buyers

In Florida, it’s important to know when to get a roof replacement. Having your roof replaced too early could waste your money, but waiting too long could put your home or business in danger when the next storm blows through. This begs the question: What is considered an old roof in Florida?

There are a lot of factors that go into determining your roof’s lifespan, and we’re here to explain all of them so you can plan your roof replacement. As your local roofing partner, PITCH Roofing has the experience and know-how to accurately judge how long a Florida roof will last. Keep reading for our guide on when a roof is considered old in Florida!
What Is Considered an Old Roof?


To a certain extent, what counts as an “old” roof depends on who you ask. For example, you may have heard that insurance companies won’t insure a roof that’s been around for more than 20 years. While this isn’t exactly true, it’s not far off.

You’re probably aware of Florida’s homeowners insurance crisis. As a result of the crisis, homeowners insurance providers are picky about what homes they will and won’t ensure. And most insurers are indeed hesitant to insurance a roof that’s 20 years old; in some cases, a 15-year-old roof might even be a risk that many insurers aren’t willing to take.

But it’s not quite true that you can’t insure a 20-year-old roof. While insurance companies see these roofs as old, you can usually still qualify for coverage if you get a roof inspection. As long as a licensed contractor can inspect your roof and not find any immediate problems, then your roof probably isn’t “too old” to insure.

That said, many 20-year-old roofs will have reached the natural end of their lives. But when trying to figure out what is considered an old roof, it’s important to remember that your roofing material has a big impact on how long your roof will last. That’s why we’re going to take a look at what counts as “old” for Florida’s favorite roofing materials!
Lifespan of Roofing Materials in Florida
When determining if a roof is too old or not, insurers have very different requirements for different materials. Often, these requirements fall well short of the actual natural life of your roof. To take a look at this discrepancy, let’s first cover how long a roof lasts in Florida:

 	Architectural shingles: 20–25 years
 	Concrete roofing tiles: 50 years
 	Clay roofing tiles: 50–100+ years
 	Standing seam metal roofs: 50–70 years
 	Corrugated metal roofs: 40–50 years
 	Modified bitumen flat roofs: 15–20 years
 	TPO flat roofs: 20–30 years

When looking at what is considered an old roof, it’s important to keep all these differences in mind. As we can see, a 20-year-old shingle roof is fairly old, whereas a 20-year-old metal roof is just getting started.

However, insurance companies don’t look at these materials the same way that roofers do. By the standards of most insurers, a shingle roof is old at 20 years old, as are most flat roofs. On the other hand, materials like tile and metal are considered old after 50 years.

So when determining if a roof is old, it’s important to look at both of these numbers. For example, we know that a 15-year-old shingle roof is somewhat old, but still has years of life left and can most likely be insured. On the other hand, a 50-year-old concrete tile roof will be harder to insure.

Even if your roof is considered old, though, it may still be possible to get insurance. Remember those roofing inspections we mentioned earlier? If your roofing inspection comes back saying that your roof has at least 3 years of life left, you will probably be able to qualify for Citizens Insurance. However, once a roof gets near the end of its lifespan, Citizens will probably be your only option.
FAQs About Older Roofs in Florida


1. Q: Should I buy a home with an old roof in Florida?

A: Using the information above, you should have a good idea of when a roof is “old.” But ultimately, determining whether or not a roof is “too old” for you to buy a home depends on you. If you’re comfortable having a Citizens policy and potentially having to replace your roof within the next few years, then there’s no reason not to buy a home with an older roof. On the other hand, if you want to have as many insurance options as possible, then you’ll want a roof that’s at least 5 years away from being considered old by insurance companies.

2. Q: Should I get a roof replacement before selling my home?

A: If your roof is near the end of its life, getting a new roof installed can make your home much more appealing to potential buyers. On the other hand, roof replacements are a big investment. Ultimately the right choice depends on your needs, but replacing your roof could be a good idea if your shingle roof is 20+ years old and you need your home to sell quickly.

3. Q: Is it bad to have a home insurance policy with Citizens?

A: Citizens is an excellent insurance option. In fact, because of the homeowners insurance crisis, it’s currently Florida’s largest insurer. However, it is not always the cheapest option. As a result, many homeowners prefer to have other options rather than being stuck with the insurer of last resort.

4. Q: Can I repair an old roof to help my home sell?

A: If your roof is currently experiencing leaks or has other signs of roofing damage, then yes, fixing those issues can make your home more appealing to buyers. However, there is no way to “fix” a roof being considered old. So if your problem is only your roof’s age, a roof replacement is the only real solution.

5. Q: Can I get insurance to replace my old roof before I sell my home?

A: Check your policy for the specifics of what your insurance will and won’t cover. But generally speaking, most insurers will only replace a roof if it has been damaged during a storm or other natural event. That means that your roof being too old is not usually enough to get insurance to pay for a roof replacement.

Apartment Roofing Materials

 	Synthetic and asphalt shingles
 	Concrete and clay roofing tiles
 	Standing seam and corrugated metal roofing
 	Flat roofing materials (TPO & modified bitumen)

While we’re happy to provide your preferred roofing material, the two most common options for Florida apartments are asphalt shingles and flat roofing. With that in mind, let’s talk about what you should know about these materials before getting a roof replacement!
Asphalt Shingles for Apartments
In Florida, many apartments are protected by architectural asphalt shingles. That’s because of three important factors: dependable durability, great aesthetics, and low roofing costs. Let’s talk about each of these factors in more detail!

Architectural shingles are both thicker and hardier than old-school 3-tab shingles. As a result, they’re typically rated for winds of up to 110 mph. Just as importantly, these asphalt shingles have protective coatings and time-release formulas that both keep them protected from water damage and prevent mold from developing on your roof. In humid Florida, this can make all the difference in how long your roof lasts!

That’s why architectural shingles enjoy long lifespans of about 25 years on average. In addition to their durability, though, these shingles also look great and boost curb appeal. With distinctive shading that generates visual interest on your roof, architectural shingles are a great apartment roofing material in part because they help attract new residents to your complex.

Undeniably, though, low roofing costs make up a big part of these shingles’ popularity. Architectural shingles cost between $4 and $8 per square foot. And when you’re paying for a large apartment roof replacement, these lower per-foot costs can make all the difference in your total bill. For this reason, architectural shingles are popular among apartment owners who want to keep roof replacement costs low.
Flat Roofing for Apartments
Shingles are the most popular material for sloped apartment roofs. But for apartments with flat roofing, modified bitumen and TPO reign supreme. With two extremely different approaches to protecting your home, both of these options can protect your apartment’s flat roof for decades.

To help you compare these apartment roofing materials side by side, we’re going to look at how each one works and their performance on your roof. Let’s get started with TPO!

 	How It Works: TPO is a single-ply, water-resistant membrane that keeps your roof dry thanks to its rubberized polymers.
 	Performance: TPO is a top-of-the-line flat roofing material. While it can be vulnerable to puncture damage, TPO generally holds up well to Florida’s weather, especially UV rays that could otherwise wear down your roof. For this reason, TPO apartment roofs last about 30 years on average.
 	Cost: TPO roofing costs between $4 and $8 per square foot.

TPO is an excellent option for any low-slope apartment roof. But in some situations, a modified bitumen roof could be what you’re looking for:

 	How It Works: This multi-layered roofing material combines protective asphalt with polymerized rubber and a strong fiberglass base.
 	Performance: Modified bitumen is a staple in Florida flat roofing. In addition to resisting water, it also has high tensile strength to keep its form no matter what the Sunshine State can throw at it. On average, modified bitumen roofs last about 20 years.
 	Cost: Modified bitumen roofing costs between $3 and $6 per square foot.

Whether you choose TPO or modified bitumen, you’re still investing in a reliable flat roofing system. But the type of roofing material you choose isn’t the only factor in the quality of your apartment roofing services. You’ll also need to carefully choose experienced, local contractors.

### Getting a Great Metal Flat Roof in Florida

Flat roofs have very unique functions. A sloped roof’s biggest concern is wind resistance since water naturally slides off the roof. With a flat roof, though, you need extra protection against pooling or slow-draining water. Because of these differences, many locals are unsure whether metal flat roofs work in Florida.

As your local flat roofing experts, PITCH Roofing knows all about which materials work best as flat roofs in Florida. Today, we’re looking at metal flat roofs and discussing how viable they are for Florida homeowners and business owners. But before we get ahead of ourselves, let’s start with the big question: Are metal flat roofs even an option?
Can I Get a Metal Flat Roof in Florida?


In the Sunshine State, the most common flat roofing materials are TPO and modified bitumen. However, it is possible to get a metal flat roof. This makes metal roofing an extremely versatile option since other materials can generally only be applied to flat roofs or sloped roofs, but not both.

There are some limitations to when you can get a metal flat roof. Technically, many of the roofs that we call “flat” are actually low-slope roofs. This includes any roof with a slope under 4:12. Exactly how flat your roof is will matter, though, because different types of metal roofs have different slope requirements.

For example, a standing seam roof only needs a minimum slope of 0.25:12. This means that these metal flat roofs can work for virtually any structure. Corrugated metal roofing panels, on the other hand, require a slope of 3:12 or more, so they may or may not work for your particular flat roof.

This is the basic concept of how you can get a metal flat roof in Florida. For more details, though, let’s look at each of these flat roofing options individually.
Planning Your Metal Flat Roof Replacement
Choosing your flat roofing material is a major decision. For a metal flat roof, choosing between standing seam and corrugated metal roofing will affect your roofing costs, aesthetics, and the longevity of your roof. To help you plan your roof replacement, let’s look at your metal flat roofing options!
Standing Seam Flat Roofs
Standing seam metal roofs are sleek and modern. With mostly-flat roofing panels, these roofs function by fastening together beneath the roofing panel. This hidden fastener design protects your seams from the elements and provides a smooth, flawless finish.

When it comes to performing as a metal flat roof, standing seam is second to none. Metal flat roofs are extremely resistant to water penetration, so you don’t need to worry about slow-draining water wearing through your roof. Standing seam roofs are especially resilient. In fact, thanks to their hidden fasteners, these roofs have no weaknesses or penetrations for water to use to enter your structure.

With a lifespan of up to 70 years, standing seam is an excellent option for metal flat roofing. However, it is not cheap. Standing seam roofs cost anywhere from $10 to $25 per square foot on average. So if you’re looking for a budget flat roof, metal may not be the right option.
5V Flat Roofs
Corrugated metal roofs, or 5V, work very differently from standing seam. Where standing seam roofs adhere under the panel, 5V metal roofs are drilled down onto your roof. This has two big effects on your roof: First, it creates a more distinctive, almost industrial look. And second, it leaves exposed fasteners on top of your new metal flat roof.

Exposed fasteners are tricky when it comes to flat roofing. Normally, there is some risk of wear and tear on your fasteners from weather exposure. But this problem is even worse with metal flat roofs. Your exposed fasteners will have more water exposure, which could lead to them being worn down and providing an opening for water to start leaking into your home or business.

Thankfully, this can be managed by intermittently replacing the screws. For many property owners in Florida, however, this extra maintenance is a big downside. Additionally, corrugated metal flat roofs will likely not reach the full 50-year lifespan that they would have on a sloped roof due to this extra wear and tear on their fasteners.

Normally, the low cost of 5V roofing would be its saving grace. That’s because these panels cost $5 to $12 per square foot to install, so they’re much more affordable than standing seam. However, remember that these roofs need a slope of at least 3:12. If your slope is lower than that, you’ll also have to pay for a built-up roofing system to increase the slope. This may drive up your roof replacement costs so much that it would be either cheaper or the same price to go with standing seam.
Picking Your Metal and Flat Roofing Contractors


For all of the reasons outlined above, we recommend standing seam metal flat roofs in most circumstances. But whether you go with hidden or exposed fasteners, you’re going to need qualified experts to install your new roof.

That’s us.

Reasons You Might Need a Metal Roof Repair


Florida is famously tough on roofs. Between our humidity, sun exposure, and occasional hurricanes, there’s a lot that could go wrong with your roof. While metal roofs are extremely resistant to most of Florida’s roof killers, no roof is completely immune.

If the damage has already been done, then the only way to fix it is through professional metal roof repair services. However, knowing what your roof is up against is the first step in taking care of your roof across its lifetime.

Now, let’s review some of the most common causes of metal roofing damage in Florida:

 	Saltwater Corrosion: This issue is especially common along Florida’s coastline. While aluminum metal roofs can resist corrosion, other types of metal roofing may struggle in saltwater environments and need regular repairs.
 	Impact Damage: Hailstorms or storm debris can cause denting on your roof, although this is more of a visual concern than a structural problem.
 	Expansion Issues: Ideally, your roof would expand and contract with the sun’s heat. Sometimes this isn’t possible though, such as with exposed fastener metal roofs, and this problem can cause premature wear and tear.
 	Algae and Mold: If algae grows on your roof, cleaning it is essential to making sure your metal roof stays strong and healthy.
 	Major Hurricane Winds: Metal roofs do an excellent job withstanding hurricane-force winds. But in extreme circumstances where winds blow in excess of 170 mph, there are no guarantees, and your metal roofing panels could be removed or damaged.

These are some of the most common ways that your metal roof can be damaged. But how are you supposed to get help once you need metal roof repairs?

### Guide to Composite Shingle Roofing in Florida

Composite shingles are a great, affordable alternative to slate or shake shingles. Also called synthetic shingles, these roofing materials are starkly different from the asphalt shingles that you may be used to. This leads many Florida homeowners to have questions about how long composite shingles last, how they hold up to local weather, and how much they cost.

We’re here to answer all these questions and more. As your local shingle roofing partner, PITCH Roofing knows just about everything about composite shingle roofing in Florida. Keep reading for our comprehensive guide to synthetic shingles!
Composite Shingles 101


Composite shingles get their name from the various materials they’re made of. Namely, these include a combination of synthetic polymers and recycled materials. But while synthetic shingles are made of complex, top-of-the-line roofing technologies, they perfectly emulate the classic style of all-natural slate or shake shingles.

That’s because during the manufacturing process, fabricators make composite shingles using the same molds that shape shake and slate. This, combined with unique coloring that all but perfectly mimics the look of the real deal, makes synthetic shingles extremely effective at recreating these timeless aesthetics.

Technically, there are some visual differences between composite shingles and real slate or shake. But it would take a roofing professional closely examining your roof to find them. For neighbors and friends, though, composite shingles are all but indistinguishable from the real deal.

The end result is a luxurious roof without the luxury price tag. But in order to determine if this material will create a high-value roof for your home, we have to discuss how these shingles hold up to Florida’s weather.
Lifespan and Durability of Synthetic Shingles in Florida
Florida is famous for its beautiful views and warm weather. Unfortunately, these things also come with downsides. For your roof, some of the biggest weather events that it will have to endure include hurricane-force winds, UV rays, and extreme humidity. So how well do composite shingles perform against these everyday Florida roofing concerns?

Let’s look at the biggest concern first: high winds. Asphalt shingles are famous for coming off roofs during major storms. However, this problem is much less common with synthetic shingles. That’s because composite shingles have wind ratings of up to 150 mph. This means that your composite shingle roof will stay put even through major hurricanes!

Thanks to the protective features of composite shingles’ polymers, they’re also extremely good at resisting UV rays. This UV resistance is further improved by protective, anti-UV coatings that are common on these shingles. Normally, UV rays can prematurely break down your roofing materials. But with composite shingles, this is a very low concern.

Extreme humidity like Florida’s leads to a lot of roofing problems. In some cases, the mold and algae that develop can weaken your structure so much that your entire roof needs replacing. Thankfully, though, this is extremely unlikely with composite shingles. Thanks to the reduced porosity of composite shingles and their algae-resistant additives, algae is a very rare sight on these roofs.

As you can see, composite shingles stand up well to Florida’s three biggest roof killers. So with all this in mind, how long can they last?
How Long Do Composite Shingles Last?
Composite shingles, as we’ve covered, are extremely durable. That’s why they last much longer than traditional asphalt shingles. Even a high-quality architectural asphalt shingle roof will rarely last longer than 25 years at best. On the other hand, composite shingles last for 40-50 years in Florida.

There are some caveats to this number, though. First, you will need to make sure that experienced professionals install your roof. Shoddy roof replacements are a surefire way to sabotage your roof, so it’s best to avoid cheap, inexperienced contractors who can’t deliver a quality roof installation.

Your roof will also likely need maintenance over its lifespan. Granted, composite shingle roofs need less maintenance than the average roof thanks to all their protective features. Despite this, it’s a good idea to get regular roof inspections to get the maximum lifespan out of your roof. Most times they won’t find any issues, but when they do, getting roof repairs before damage can spread is the best way to maintain your roof.

The only final thing to keep in mind is that composite shingles are a high-value roofing system. This means that they require a significant up-front investment. While these roofs are less expensive than slate or shake, that doesn’t mean that composite shingles are cheap.
The Cost of Composite Shingles in Florida 2024


Both slate and shake shingles can cost as much as $30 per square foot in Florida. On the other end of the spectrum, asphalt shingles may cost as little as $5 per square foot. Synthetic shingles represent a middle point between these two extremes.

But just because that’s the average price doesn’t mean it’s what you’ll pay for your new roof. How much your new roof costs will depend, in large part, on what type of roof replacement you get.With that in mind, let’s talk about how much different types of roof replacements cost in Florida!Shingle Roof Replacement CostsIn Florida, there are two popular shingle roofing options: asphalt shingles and synthetic shingles. Architectural asphalt shingles are some of the most popular in Florida, capable of lasting for about 25 years. Synthetic shingles, on the other hand, mimic the style of slate or wood shingles and last for up to 50 years with proper maintenance.But how much does a new shingle roof cost in Florida? Well, architectural asphalt shingles cost between $4.50 and $8 per square foot. So let’s say that your roof is the average size for Florida, so around 2,000 square feet. That would mean your new roof costs would fall between $9,000 and $16,000 for a new asphalt shingle roof.Synthetic shingles, also called composite shingles, have very different roof replacement costs. Their price per square foot ranges from $7 to $14. On an average-sized roof, that’s $14,000 to $28,000 for a new synthetic shingle roof. This highlights the biggest difference between these shingle roofing materials; asphalt shingles are affordable and don’t last exceptionally long, whereas synthetic shingles have high up-front costs but last a good deal longer!Tile Roof Replacement CostsTile roofing has a deep history in Florida, and while some improvements have been made over the years, the core function of tile roofs remains the same. In other words, tile roofing is still a great way to protect your home from the Florida weather. And with two types of tiles, clay and concrete, you have a lot of variety in tile roof replacement costs.Concrete tiles represent your more budget-conscious choice, but they’re by no means cheap. With a lifespan of about 50 years, concrete tiles cost between $7 and $19 per square foot. On a 2,000-square-foot roof, that puts your total new roof costs between $14,000 and $38,000.Clay roofing tiles come with higher costs, but they’re also capable of lasting for a century or longer! If your first priority is a long-lasting roof, there’s truly no better option. A new clay tile roof will cost $12 to $21 per square foot. With an average-sized Florida roof, that means you’re paying $24,000 to $42,000 for a clay tile roof replacement. This puts clay roofing tiles firmly in the “luxury roofing” category!For more information on how much the different types of tile roofs costs (like barrel tiles vs. flat tiles, for example), check out our full tile roofing cost guide.Metal Roof Replacement CostsMetal roofing is one of the best ways to protect your roof against Florida’s infamous storms. If you want to get your home hurricane-ready, then you’ll have to choose between three of Florida’s most popular metal roofing options. Let’s talk a bit about each option and how much they could cost you!Corrugated roofs, or 5V metal roofs, use an exposed fastener system that drills the roof into place. This is secure, but the exposed fasteners can lessen your roof’s lifespan as they get worn down, which is why corrugated metal roofs last around 50 years. They’re also the most affordable metal roofing option, however, with new roof costs between $5 to $12 per square foot, or $10,000 to $24,000.Standing seam metal roofing, on the other hand, uses hidden fasteners. These lock together beneath a flat, sleek roofing panel, which creates a smoother aesthetic and protects your roof from wear and tear. For this reason, standing seam metal roofs can last up to 70 years in Florida. Standing seam roofs come with high costs, though, between $10 and $23 per square foot. In other words, a new roof costs between $20,000 and $46,000 when you pick standing seam.Your final option is stone-coated steel roofing. Made with sheets of durable steel coated in protective stone, this option offers the unbeatable protection of metal roofing alongside a more conventional, homey aesthetic. Total roofing costs will usually fall between $7 and $15 per square foot. This puts it squarely in the middle of the price range, with average metal roof replacement costs between $14,000 and $30,000 on a 2,000-square-foot roof.Flat Roof Replacement CostsIn Florida, flat roofs are a staple for both homes and businesses. Because flat roofs have unique concerns, namely resisting pooling water, they also have unique roofing materials. And in Florida, two options stand head and shoulders above the rest.Your first choice is modified bitumen, which is a rubberized asphalt that resists both water and puncture damage. These affordable flat roofs only last for about 20 years, but they make up for it with low costs of $4 to $8 per square foot. So on a 2,000-square-foot roof, you’re looking at flat roof replacement costs between $8,000 and $16,000.TPO, on the other hand, is a single-ply roofing system. This means that it’s applied in one single sheet across your roof, and with its special blend of rubberized polymers, there’s no better option for water resistance. TPO roofing lasts for 20-30 years and costs $5.50 to $9 per square foot. So on an average-sized Florida roof, your new roof costs should be between $11,000 and $18,000.Other Factors in Calculating How Much a New Roof Costs in FloridaYou’ve probably noticed that there’s a lot of range in how much a new roof costs, even when using the same material. That’s because material costs, while important, aren’t everything. Keep reading for an overview of all the different factors that could affect how much your new roof costs in Florida!Roof Size and SlopeObviously, the larger your roof, the more it costs to replace. But did you know that your pitch can have just as big of an impact on how much your new roof costs? Most roofs have a pitch between 4:12 and 9:12. And the steeper the pitch of your roof, the more it can cost to replace. An asphalt shingle roof, on the other hand, may have lower labor costs since it is faster and easier to install.Replacing Roof DeckingThe decking beneath your roof will also contribute to total new roof costs. When getting a roof replacement, it’s normal for some parts of your roof decking to have degraded over the years. As a result, some or all of your decking may need replacing in order to support your new roof. Unfortunately, there’s no way to examine your decking without removing your roof, so this can lead to a small additional charge that can’t be covered by roof replacement quotes.Unique Roofing FeaturesAny distinctive features on your roof will increase how much your new roof costs. This includes skylights, chimneys, dormer windows, or sections with different slopes from the rest of the roof. All of these things take more time and effort to work around, so they’ll raise your total labor costs.Dumping FeesWhen all is said and done, your old roof needs to go somewhere. When paying for a roof replacement, included in that cost is the price to rent a dumpster and deposit your old roof into it. This is an essential part of getting a roof replacement, but it does increase your total overhead and labor costs when getting a new roof.Find Out the Exact Cost of Your Roof ReplacementAt the end of the day, this is all helpful information in guessing how high your new roof costs could be. The Best Roof Replacement Financing Options in 2025


If you’re not sure how to finance a roof replacement, this is the guide for you. There are many ways to pay for a new roof, and which one is right for you will depend on the specifics of your situation. Let’s look at how you can pay for a roof replacement in Florida!
0% Interest Roof Financing
When talking about roof replacement financing, it doesn’t get better than 0% interest. And that’s exactly what Pitch offers with our one-year no-interest roof loans. Because at Pitch, we don’t think that anyone should have to wait to get a new roof installed. With our 0% interest roof replacement financing, you’ll be able to get the new roof you need without having to wait to save up.

Of all the roof replacement financing options, getting a loan through your roofing company is certainly the most direct. Any lender will require a credit check, but it doesn’t take perfect credit to quality for these no-interest loans. In fact, many homeowners are surprised to find that they qualify for our best rates!

You don’t have to choose a loan through your roofing company to get a great roof financing option. However, as we’ll see in the other roof replacement financing options, this one is definitely the simplest and the fastest.
Home Equity Loans (HELOC)
Technically called a Home Equity Line of Credit (HELOC), home equity loans are a great way for some homeowners to finance their roof replacements. How this roof replacement financing option works is by allowing you to borrow against your equity in your home.

Since a HELOC uses your home as collateral, it’s a great way to get low-interest roof replacement financing. However, there are limitations to this option. For one thing, many homeowners won’t qualify for a home equity loan. That’s because you have to have 15-20% equity in your home, so it’s not always an option for people who have recently bought their homes.

There’s also the issue of credit. You can get a HELOC with a credit score of 620 or above. However, if your credit score is at or around 620, you won’t get the best rates. In order to get a low interest rate with a home equity loan, you will want a credit score of 700 or higher. Otherwise, you could find yourself paying high rates for the life of your loan.

Despite its limitations, a home equity loan is an excellent option for roof replacement financing. If you meet the qualifications, this could be a great way to pay for your new roof!
Personal Loans
If you don’t have the equity to qualify for a HELOC and don’t want to finance through your roofing company, getting a personal loan is the next best thing. You can get these loans from any bank, credit union, or other financial institution, and many come with credit score minimums as low as 500.

Like with a HELOC, a lower credit score will mean higher interest rates. The upside, though, is that since there’s no home equity requirement, this option is available for many more homeowners. And if you have a high credit score, you may qualify for lower rates. However, personal loans do not come with rates as low as a HELOC.

In most cases, it's better to choose roof financing over a personal loan. Personal loans have some of the highest interest rates in the industry, and while you may qualify for lower rates with a high credit score, the rates likely won't be better than what you get with traditional roof financing.
Homeowners Insurance Roof Replacement Financing


In a perfect world, your homeowners insurance policy would always cover the cost of a roof replacement. However, there are only specific situations where your insurance is a reliable option for roof replacement financing. So how do you know if you qualify for insurance to pay for your new roof?

The first hurdle is determining why your roof needs replacing. If you need a new roof because of normal aging or wear and tear, then your homeowners insurance policy probably won’t cover the cost of a roof replacement. If, however, your roof was damaged in a storm or hurricane, then you may be eligible for insurance-funded roof replacement financing.

Most homeowners insurance policies specifically cover "acts of God," or natural disasters like hurricanes and tornadoes. You'll need to review your policy and make sure that this is the case for your roof. Then your next step is submitting a claim to your insurance company. We have a full guide on getting insurance to pay for your roof replacement, but the short and sweet version is that you will need to include the following in your claim:

 	Photos of the storm damage done to your roof
 	Proof that the damage was caused by a storm
 	A roof inspection report from licensed Florida roofers saying that your roof needs replacing

This is the information that you’ll need to provide to have a chance at qualifying for this roof replacement financing. If they accept your claim, then the next step will be collecting roof replacement quotes and sending them to your insurance provider for approval.

### The Best Types of Metal Roofs for Houses

Metal roofing is a polarizing topic. While it makes some people think of old, rusted tin roofs and loud rainstorms, others see it as a to-of-the-line roofing material for hurricane resistance. As more and more Florida homeowners change their way of thinking about steel roofing, there’s a growing interest in the different types of metal roofs for houses.

As your local roofing partner, PITCH Roofing is here to give you all the information you need about residential metal roofing in Florida. Keep reading for our comprehensive breakdown of the best types of metal roofs for houses in the Sunshine State!
Is Residential Metal Roofing a Good Idea?


Many people are hesitant to make the leap to metal roofing. If this sounds familiar, you’ve probably heard references to industrial-looking metal roofs, rust, and loud rain. But the truth is that, with all of the different types of metal roofs, there are plenty of great options for residential metal roofing.

Before we talk about metal roofs for houses, let’s cover some general facts about metal roofing in Florida. For one thing, metal roofs routinely come with wind ratings as high as 150 mph. Even the best shingle roofs top out at around 110 mph, so this is a massive upgrade in home protection. And with an active hurricane season this year, there’s no better time to get ready for the next big storm.

In addition to wind resistance, metal roofs are also resistant to water damage and algae, two common problems for shingles. While rust is possible, modern metal roofs are formulated with zinc and aluminum to minimize the risk of corrosion. In short, metal roofs offer great humidity and water resistance.

Now, the final big concern is noise during rain. We won’t lie: Yes, metal roofs can sometimes be slightly louder than shingle roofs in the rain. But people tend to overestimate how big the difference is. Modern metal roofs come with more insulation than older versions, which tampers down the noise considerably. And if you’re concerned about noise levels, you can always get extra insulation during your metal roof replacement.

As you can see, metal roofs are a great option for Florida homeowners. With the basics covered, let’s talk about the different types of residential metal roofing and what they can offer you!
The 3 Best Types of Metal Roofs for Houses


In Florida, what makes the “best” metal roof for a home depends on what you’re looking for. To help you make the best decision for your roof, we’re covering the three most popular types of residential metal roofing!
1. Corrugated Metal Roofing (5V)
Corrugated, or 5V, metal roofing is much-loved in Florida. Made with corrugated metal sheets, this roofing system uses an exposed fastener system. In other words, roofers drill it into place when they install your roof. Some homeowners see 5V roofs as looking too “industrial,” but others appreciate the unique aesthetic and reliable protection of corrugated panels.

There is a downside to corrugated metal roofing, though. Because the fasteners are “exposed” to the elements, they can experience a lot of wear and tear over time. Additionally, these roofs can’t expand with the sun’s heat because they’re drilled into place. Because of these limitations, 5V metal roofs rarely last longer than 50 years — a fairly short life for a metal roof.

But if you’re looking for affordable metal roofs for houses, corrugated roofs are second to none. On average, residential 5V roofs cost $5 to $12 per square foot. This is still more expensive than shingles, but much more affordable than other types of metal roofs for homes. Their low price point is a large part of what has made corrugated metal roofs increasingly popular throughout Florida!
2. Standing Seam Metal Roofing
Think of standing seam roofs as the go-to metal roofs for houses. Made with flat, ridged panels, these roofs use a hidden fastener system. This means that the panels interlock under your roof. This keeps them in place without disrupting the sleek, smooth aesthetic that many homeowners love.

Because the panels lock together from the underside, there is no increased risk of wear and tear. They can also expand and contract freely with heat, which keeps the roofs functional for longer. As a result, standing seam roofs have been known to last as long as 80 years with proper maintenance.

This longer lifespan and more residential aesthetic come with a high price tag, though. Standing seam roofs cost between $11 and $18 per square foot, which is a much more substantial up-front investment. However, if you want a roof that stays strong over the years, looks great, and requires minimal maintenance, standing seam roofs are worth the extra cost.
3. Stone-Coated Steel Roofing
If you want the protection of metal roof without the distinctive appearance, stone-coated steel roofing could be a perfect fit. These roofs are made of exactly what you’d think — resilient steel roofing panels coated in stone granules for increased protection. The result is a roof that blends in anywhere but offers the unmistakable protection of metal roofing.

These metal roofs for houses enjoy many unique benefits, including increased resistance to denting from hail and storm debris thanks to the layer of protective stone. You also don’t have to worry about oil canning, which can cause unsightly (though not damaging) patterns on other types of metal roofs.

Stone-coated steel roofing offers a mid-point for residential metal roofing costs. With prices ranging from $8 to $14 per square foot, stone-coated steel roofing offers a great balance of cost and performance. With this residential roofing material, you can count on getting a lot of bang for your buck. In fact, stone-coated steel roofs last between 50 and 70 years on average!
