### Get the Best Flat Roof Repair Services in Florida

Whether you need your flat roof repaired after a storm or due to normal wear and tear, you want the best crew possible on your roof. But if you’re like many homeowners, you’re also concerned about flat roof repair costs. The key is balancing quality roof repair services with fair, honest pricing.

We’re PITCH Roofing, and as veteran local roofers, we know all about great workmanship and roof repair costs. Today, we’re covering everything you need to know to get your flat roof back in great shape without breaking the bank. Keep reading for our guide on repairing your flat roof in Florida!
Can I Repair My Own Flat Roof?


DIY flat roof repairs seem like a great way to save money. After all, you don’t have to pay for roofing contractors or overhead! But while it may technically be possible for you to repair your own flat roof, it’s not something that we generally recommend.

There are a few reasons we advise against DIY flat roof repair. First, there’s the danger that you won’t be able to fix the issue correctly. And we emphasize correctly — it’s possible to fix a leak or tear in your flat roof for now, but leave a lasting problem going forward. When this happens, it can be even more dangerous than just having a leak, since you may not be watching out for signs of damage in the future.

But even if you’re a roofing expert and know exactly what you’re doing, it still usually isn’t a good idea to repair your own roof. Without proper permitting and a valid contractor’s license, you’re likely voiding your flat roof's warranty. So if there’s a larger problem down the line, you won’t be able to depend on your coverage.

The final reason not to repair your own roof is homeowners insurance. Generally, homeowners insurance providers don’t like to see people working on their roofs. If you do try to repair your flat roof, and your insurance company finds out about it, it could lead to problems insuring your roof or canceling your policy completely.

For all of these reasons, we strongly recommend hiring reputable local roofers for your flat roof repair.
Finding the Best Flat Roof Repair Company Near You


If you’re going to have to pay someone to repair your flat roof, you may as well hire the best. But if you’re not familiar with the local roofing scene, it can be hard to tell which roofers are right for you. Luckily, we’ve got a full breakdown of what to look for in flat roof repair contractors!

### Find & Address Roof Storm Damage After a Hurricane

Roof storm damage is a major concern in Florida. With Hurricane Debby hitting Florida on Monday August 5th, there’s no better time to check for and address damage once the storm has cleared. Unfortunately, many homeowners aren’t sure of what to do for their roof after a major storm passes through.

We’re here to give you all the crucial information you need to know. PITCH Roofing has deep roots as local roofers based in Hillsborough and Pinellas Counties, and that means we look out for our Florida residents. Keep reading for all of our advice on how to take care of your roof after a storm!
What Kinds of Room Storm Damage Should I Worry About?


In our conversations with local homeowners, we’ve found that many aren’t sure what roof storm damage really entails. They mostly think of missing shingles or storm debris landing on their roofs. And while these are some of the most common types of roof storm damage, they’re not the only things that you should look out for.

In addition to these common aftereffects of a storm, you should also keep an eye out for:

 	Damaged gutters, which may have been pulled from your roof
 	Standing water, especially on flat roofs
 	Debris that’s stuck on your roof, like branches or garbage
 	Cracked soffits or fascia

Any of these signs of roof storm damage are cause for concern. Now that you know what a storm can do to your roof, let’s talk about what you should do once a storm has left your area.
How to Identify Roof Storm Damage and What to Do
As we talk about inspecting your property for roof storm damage, we’re going to focus on how to identify signs of damage and resolve the issue(s). However, you may also need to contact your homeowners insurance to get coverage for any necessary repairs. For that, you can check out our guide to use your insurance coverage for roofing services.

With that said, let’s talk about your step-by-step list of what to do after a hurricane or tropical storm!
1. Inspect the Exterior of Your Property
The first step in finding roof storm damage is taking a look at your roof. If you can safely and confidently get on your roof for an inspection, break out your ladder and do that. If you’re at all unsure about being unable to do that, though, do not get on your roof. Instead, reach out to roofers in your area and see about getting a roof inspection. Many roofers will provide this service at minimal costs.

If you decide to go with professionals, they’ll handle inspecting your property and make recommendations on how to fix any roof storm damage. On the other hand, if you’re getting on your roof yourself, there are specific signs of damage to watch out for.

The first thing you should look for are missing, torn, or curled shingles. All of these mean that your roof decking could be exposed and vulnerable to water damage. You’ll also want to make sure gutters are securely adhered and free of debris as well as remove any storm debris that remains on your roof.

Once you’ve verified that everything looks good on your roof, your next step is to head back inside to see how the interior of your roofing system is holding up.
2. Check the Inside of Your Home for Roof Storm Damage


It’s a common misconception that storm damage is always visible from the outside. Often, however, the first signs of roof damage occur inside the home. To look for interior signs of roof storm damage, your attic is a great place to start.

Your attic is the first place that your roof should show signs of water damage. Take a look up there and see if you can spot any wet spots or leaks. Even if the exterior of your roof looked like it was in perfect condition, hurricane-force winds can still cause leaks that can lead to water damage or mold if they’re not addressed.

Whether or not you see signs of leaks in your attic, it doesn’t hurt to walk through your home and look at your ceiling. If you notice any new brown circles, it could mean that you have a leak that you couldn’t spot in your attic. Make note of where this circle is so that you can point it out to the roofer(s) who come to fix the storm roof damage.

If you find any signs of roof storm damage in or outside your home, you need to act fast to prevent the damage from getting worse.
3. Schedule Roof Repairs ASAP
Even if your roof storm damage looks minor right now, it will only worsen over time. A cheap job replacing a handful of shingles can turn into a partial roof repair in a matter of months. So when you see signs of storm damage on your roof, call your favorite local roofers ASAP.

When you call your roofers of choice, you’ll want to request a roof repair cost estimate. This way, they’ll send a professional to your home to inspect the damage personally and write up a personalized quote that’s unique to your roof and your repair needs. After that, they’ll schedule your roof repair job so that your roofing damage doesn’t get any worse.

### How Long Do Flat Roofs Last? Roof Replacement Guide

In Florida, flat roofs are an integral part of both residential and commercial roofing. But how long do flat roofs last in the Sunshine State? Well, that depends on a few factors.

We’re PITCH Roofing, and as your local roofing partners, we consider it our job to answer all of your roofing questions. Today, that means walking you through how long flat roofs last in Florida and the steps you can take to make sure you get a long life out of your roof! To start, let’s answer your biggest question and explain how much life you can expect to get out of your flat roof in Florida.
How Long Do Flat Roofs Last in Florida?


In the world of roofing, flat roofs serve a unique purpose. While a sloped roof’s biggest concern is withstanding wind damage, flat roofs have to be able to handle slow-draining water. This means that water resistance is the biggest factor in how long your flat roof lasts in Florida.

Different types of flat roofs do this in different ways. For example, TPO roofing is made of a rubberized membrane that’s applied to your roof in a single ply. Modified bitumen, on the other hand, is made of rubberized asphalt that’s built up on top of a fiberglass base. These different approaches to flat roofing mean that each roofing material has a slightly different lifespan.

Modified bitumen flat roofs last for about 20 years, whereas TPO roofing can last for 25-30 years with proper maintenance. This means that on average, flat roofs last 20-30 years in Florida. This is good information to have before your flat roof replacement, but it’s not everything you need to know.

When looking at your flat roofing options, it’s important to be aware of how you can get the most life out of your new roof. Let’s talk about the three biggest factors in how long your flat roof lasts!
How to Get the Most Life Out of Your Flat Roof


As a property owner, you have some power to control how long your flat roof lasts. By addressing three important factors, you can set your new roof up for a long life of protecting your home or business. So what do you have to do to make your flat roof last in Florida?
1. Pick Experienced Flat Roofers
Who you pick to install your flat roof will massively impact how long a flat roof lasts. Regardless of the type of flat roof that you pick, proper installation is essential to having a long-lasting roof. If there is an issue with your flat roof’s installation, it could cause a catastrophic, premature failure in your roofing system.

So how do you find reliable flat roofers? We have two tips. First, always look at roofing reviews. Most roofers will tell you that they’re the best in your area, but reviews are where you find out how well a roofing company really delivers on what it promises.

Our second piece of advice is to choose local flat roofing experts. Experience is everything in roofing, so you need a crew that both knows flat roofing and your local climate. Roofers who only have experience roofing in other climates or installing shingles simply won’t be prepared to give you a high-quality flat roof replacement.
2. Don’t Be Afraid to Invest in Your New Roof
At Pitch, we make it our business to provide affordable roofing services. But that doesn’t mean that you should always go with the cheapest roofing option available. In fact, cheap roofing often reflects low-quality roofing, either in the materials, the workmanship, or both. In short, if you try to cut corners, your flat roof won't last long.

For example, consider that you get two quotes. Company A can replace your flat roof for $12,000, but Company B can replace your roof for $6,000. If you only care about how much your roof replacement costs, then Company B seems like the best choice. But you have to ask yourself: How can Company A come in that far under Company B’s estimate?

It’s possible that Company A is over-charging for their services. But it’s also possible that Company B is using cheap labor or materials for their roof replacements, and that’s a recipe for a bad roof installation. This brings up an important question: How do you know when you’re getting a good deal vs. getting a low-quality roof?

The best way to know if you’re getting a fair flat roofing price is to look at other estimates. This way, if an offer is drastically lower than the others, you can confidently assume that the low price is due to cheap materials or labor. And in either case, it’s best to invest in your roof with a fairly priced roof replacement using quality materials and expert workmanship.
3. Commit to Keeping Your Flat Roof in Good Shape
Getting a long life for your flat roof doesn’t stop with your new roof’s installation. No matter who installs your roof or what they put on it, your roof will always require maintenance to get the longest life possible.

In Florida, you generally want to get a roof inspection once a year and after major storms. This way, if your roof develops an issue (as all roofs do sooner or later), you’ll be able to address it quickly before the problem worsens. For example, a small puncture in your TPO roof isn’t a big deal if you catch it early. But over time, the damage can spread, and what was a quick fix six months ago could suddenly require much larger flat roof repairs.

For this reason, it’s a good idea to stay current on your roof’s health. When you know that there’s an issue, you can act quickly to give your roof the longest life possible!

### The Best Types of Roof Underlayments in Florida

Getting a roof replacement involves much more than choosing between tiles or shingles. Your roofing system is complex, and it has many different layers and parts. One of the most important, but most overlooked, is your water-resistant roof underlayment.

When you need help understanding all of the different types of roof underlayments, PITCH Roofing has your back. With years of experience with Florida roof replacements, we’re experts on all parts of your roofing system, including your underlayment. Stick with us as we explain this crucial part of your roofing system!
What Is a Roof Underlayment and Why Does It Matter?


Your roof has many different layers, but one of the most vulnerable is your decking. Usually made of plywood, this is the base on which the rest of your roof sits. And while roofing materials like shingles and metal go a long way in protecting your roof, they can’t keep out 100% of the water that hits your roof.

That’s where your roof underlayment comes in. Available in a variety of different water-resistant materials, your underlayment keeps your decking dry and free of rot and mold. In other words, it keeps the base of your entire roofing system from falling apart, so it’s among the most important parts of your roof.

In addition to this massive boon for your roof’s water resistance, roof underlayments also offer a variety of secondary benefits. These include insulation for your home, keeping out the hot air during the summer, as well as soundproofing that can help your roof stay quiet during a rainstorm, which is especially helpful for metal roofs.
Types of Roof Underlayments in Florida
Now that we’ve covered the basics of what a roof underlayment is, it’s time to discuss your options when it comes time to replace your roof. In Florida, three materials in particular dominate the roofing scene: rubberized asphalt, felt, and synthetic roof underlayments. Now, let’s look at the good and the bad of each of these underlayments to help you pick which one is right for your home!
Rubberized Asphalt Underlayments
When you hear the phrase “peel and stick,” it’s referring to rubberized asphalt underlayments. And you probably will hear the phrase somewhere during your roof replacement, because these water-resistant protections are extremely popular in Florida right now. But what are they?

Rubberized asphalt can be across your decking or in specific sections, and its unique combination of tough asphalt and waterproof rubber makes it ideal for keeping your decking dry and secure. Some of the things that Florida homeowners enjoy about these underlayments is their:

 	Quick and easy installation, which helps lower roof replacement costs
 	Top-quality water resistance
 	Hardy durability and the potential to last for as long as 30 years or more
 	Thick insulation that helps cool your home in the summer

These are all great pros to see in a roof underlayment, but peel and stick has its cons too. For one thing, they’re extremely hard to remove. This is good news when you’re getting it installed and want protection, but bad news when you need to replace your underlayment. As a result, you may have to replace extra parts of your decking during your next roof replacement.
Felt Underlayments
For a long time, felt roofing was the gold standard in roof underlayments. With new advances in roofing technology, though, felt has largely fallen to the wayside. Still, it’s worth looking at felt underlayments at least to understand how far modern roofing has come.

Felt worked as an additional layer to protect roof deckings from water damage. However, unlike rubberized asphalt, felt isn’t really waterproof. Rather, it would absorb water with time, leading to mold and rot. To make matters worse, even in the best-case scenario, felt underlayments rarely lasted much longer than 10 years.

In 2024, very few roofers even offer felt underlayments, and you should probably be suspicious of those that do, outside of extremely unique circumstances. Between rubberized asphalt and synthetic roof underlayments, there are simply better options on the market.
Synthetic Underlayments


Nowadays, synthetic underlayments have become the go-to option for roof replacements. Made with a special blend of polypropylene fibers, this roof underlayment option is every bit as water-resistant as peel and stick. So what has made it so popular in Florida?

Synthetic underlayments offer a lot of benefits for local homeowners. Some of the biggest draws include:

 	Extreme durability that won’t break down when exposed to water
 	Being thin and lightweight so there’s no extra pressure no your roof decking
 	Lasting for 25-50 years, longer than any other type of roof underlayment
 	Required for some types of home warranties

In terms of durability, there’s simply no beating synthetic underlayments. If they have any cons, it’s that they cost more than other types of roof underlayments. But for the kind of long-term protection and reliability that they offer, they’re certainly worth the extra investment in your home.

### The Best Metal Roofing Materials for Florida Homeowners

If you’re considering a metal roof replacement, it’s a good idea to get familiar with the different metal roofing materials available in Florida. People often talk about “steel roof replacements” as a catchall, but the truth is that there are many different types of metal roofs. The trick is finding the right type for your home or business.

Today, PITCH Roofing is helping you do exactly that! As your partners in local roofing, we want you to have all the information you need to make an informed choice about your metal roof replacement. Stick with us as we walk you through all the different metal roofing materials available in Florida!
The Best Metal Roofing Materials for a Roof Replacement in Florida


Florida’s climate plays a huge role in how long your roof will last. This is especially true for metal roofs, which have some unique concerns and vulnerabilities thanks to Florida’s weather patterns: namely, rusting. But with the right metal roofing materials, you can get a sturdy, high-quality metal roof that’s built to last.

Let’s talk about how to make that happen.
Steel Roofing
Think of steel as your classic metal roofing material. It’s the most popular type of metal roofing panel and for good reason. Steel is strong enough to resist storm debris and hail while being flexible enough to withstand Florida’s extreme UV rays. However, steel is also extremely prone to rust, and that can be a big problem with Florida’s humidity.

That’s why modern metal roofs almost never have panels made entirely of steel. Instead, when roofers talk about steel roof replacements, we’re actually talking about a specific mixture of metal roofing materials. Usually, "steel roofing" refers to either galvanized steel or galvalume steel.

The idea of these types of steel roofs is to keep the hardy protection of steel while protecting it against rust. Galvanized steel does this with a zinc coating, which helps it prevent rust. While this protection works, it only lasts for as long as your zinc coating holds up, which probably won’t be the full lifespan of your roof.

Galvalume steel, on the other hand, offers even better protection with a mixture of zinc and aluminum, which both prevents rust and “heals” the metal when it’s damaged. This provides long-lasting rust protection that should keep your roof rust-free for decades.

And your steel roof will be around for decades — about 60 years on average, in fact. This makes it a great metal roofing material for homeowners who want a roof that’s built to last!
Aluminum Roofing
In most parts of Florida, galvanized or Galvalume steel is enough to prevent metal roof rusting. There is one exception, though: Florida’s coasts. Whether you’re on the Gulf of Mexico or the Atlantic Ocean, you’ll need to take extra steps if you want to keep your roof rust-free with all of that saltwater in the air. Thankfully, aluminum roofing is the perfect metal roofing material for coastal Florida.

Aluminum resists rust better than other metal roofing materials. In fact, it can even “heal” itself by shedding damaged parts of itself. This, coupled with it being sturdy and surprisingly lightweight, makes it essential for homeowners looking for a metal roof within a mile of Florida’s coastline.

Even with Florida’s challenging weather patterns, an aluminum roof can last from 50 to 80 years. If you need a long-lasting metal roof for your property near Florida’s coast, there’s truly no better metal roofing material on the market.
Stone-Coated Steel Roofing
Some homeowners like the protection and longevity of metal roofing but aren’t such big fans of the look. While metal roofs are available in sleek standing seam or corrugated panels, some prefer a more classic look for their homes. If this sounds like you, then stone-coated steel could be exactly what you’re looking for.

As the name implies, stone-coated steel is made by covering steel roofing panels in stone granules. The result is a look similar to that of shingles but with the protection and durability of steel. In many ways stone-coated steel is the best of both worlds; you get the wind resistance and longevity of steel roofing while enjoying the dent resistance provided by the stone granules.

Thanks to this multi-layered protection, these metal roofing materials can last for up to 70 years in Florida. That’s better than any shingle roof can offer, which makes stone-coated steel perfect for homeowners who love the look of shingles but want robust, reliable protection!
How Much Do Metal Roofing Materials Cost in Florida?


Up to now, we’ve covered the most popular metal roofing materials in the state. But there’s still one big question looming: How much does it all cost?

Calculating the costs for a metal roof replacement is a complicated process. Ultimately, your total roofing costs will depend on the size of your roof, what fasteners you use, and any unique roofing features. That said, we can tell you how much these metal roofing materials cost to give you an idea of what you can expect for your roof replacement.

The average costs of Florida’s top metal roofing materials are:

 	Galvanized Steel: On average, galvanized steel costs between $5.50 and $8.50 per square foot, making it among the most affordable metal roofing materials.
 	Galvalume Steel: Because it requires different types of metal and performs better, Galvalume steel costs just a bit more at $6 to $10 per square foot.
 	Aluminum: As a must-have metal roofing material for coastal areas, aluminum roofing costs between $8 and $12 per square foot.
 	Stone-Coated Steel: As a top-of-the-line metal roofing material, stone-coated steel costs $8 to $15 per square foot.

As you can see, metal roofing is not cheap. But with no-interest roof financing, Pitch makes metal roofing attainable for many homeowners who otherwise wouldn’t be able to afford this kind of high-quality protection. If you’re committed to your home’s safety, don’t let a high price tag talk you out of the unique protection that these metal roofing materials offer.

These are the average costs of Florida’s best metal roofing materials. But if you want to know how much you can expect to pay for your metal roof replacement in Florida, your best bet is to get a customized roofing estimate.

### How Long Do Tile Roofs Last in Florida? Clay and Concrete Tile Roofing Guide

Did you know that tile roofs have been used in Florida since the days of the first Spanish settlers? Over time, the way that tile roofing works has completely changed in some ways while staying almost exactly the same in others. This leaves a lot of people wondering: How long do tile roofs last in Florida in 2024?

We’re here to answer these questions and more. PITCH Roofing is a Tampa Bay roofing company with years of experience in tile roofing, so today we’re walking you through tile roof lifespans, costs, and more. Let’s get started by answering your biggest question!
How Long Do Tile Roofs Last in Florida?


When looking at how long a tile roof lasts in Florida, the answer can be simple: anywhere from 25 to 100 years. But a range like that is so wide that it’s not really helpful. So how do you find out how long your tile roof will last?

Well, that depends on a number of factors. To help you plan your tile roof replacement, let’s talk about the biggest factors that determine how long a tile roof lasts in Florida!
How Weather Affects Tile Roof Lifespans
Some weather phenomena in Florida will damage your roof in unavoidable ways. For example, Florida’s year-round humidity will wear on your roof no matter what you do or where in Florida you live. However, sometimes how the weather affects your roof is more luck-based.

This mostly includes things like tropical storms and hurricanes. If a major hurricane hits your home, there’s a chance that your roof will need replacing regardless of the type of roof that you chose. However, this doesn’t mean that tile roofs are completely defenseless against hurricanes. In fact, with wind resistance of up to 150 mph, tile roofs are some of the most hurricane-resistant roofs in Florida.

So where does this leave the lifespan of your tile roof?

With proper maintenance, you can minimize the negative effects of Florida’s everyday weather, like cleaning mold from your shingles to prevent it from spreading. But if the right storm hits your home, there’s no roofing material that is guaranteed to survive. This can be an uncomfortable truth, but it’s important to have realistic expectations for your new roof!

Of course, this doesn’t mean that tile roofs can’t or don’t last a long time in Florida. In fact, they’re one of the longest-lasting roofing materials in the Sunshine State, depending on the type of tile you pick.
How Long Different Types of Tile Roofs Last
When looking at how long tile roofs last in Florida, the type of tile roof has a major impact on the answer. Generally, there are two options for tile roofing in Florida: concrete tiles and clay tiles.

On the surface, the numbers are simple. Clay tiles last for 25 to 50 years on average. On the other hand, clay tiles last anywhere from 50 to 100+ years, making them the longest-lasting roofing material in Florida. But to make sure you have clear expectations, it’s important to take a closer look.

Concrete tiles don’t last as long as clay tiles in part because they’re more porous. With all of our summer storms and year-round humidity, this makes clay tile roofs especially vulnerable to mold. By keeping these roofs clean and mold-free, you can greatly increase your chances of your tile roof lasting closer to 50 years than 25.

At the same time, there are some important caveats to clay tile’s lifespan of 100+ years. For one thing, you can expect to occasionally have to replace individual tiles across your roof’s life. This is a quick, affordable repair, and usually follows storms when high winds can pull shingles loose or crack them with storm debris.

Additionally, your tile roof’s water-resistant underlayment will have to be replaced after 20 years. So while your tile roof can last for an extremely long time, you will still have to pay to have your roof removed and put back on every 20 or so years. This is much cheaper than paying for a roof replacement, but it’s still a good thing to be aware of!

Regardless of what type of tile roof you get, you want to consider not just how long tile roofs last, but also the total value of your overall roof.
The Value of Tile Roofing in Florida


How long tile roofs last is a big part of their overall value. But it’s not the only thing determining the total worth of this investment in your home. To determine the value of your tile roof, you have to know how much tile roofing costs in Florida.

For example, concrete tile roofing costs between $10 and $19 per square foot in Florida. On a 2,000-square-foot roof, that puts your tile roof replacement costs between $20,000 and $38,000. On the other hand, clay tile roofing costs anywhere from $12 to $22 per square foot. Using that same 2000-square-foot roof, a clay tile roof replacement will cost $24,000 to $44,000.

When determining if your roof is worth the investment for you, it’s important to keep both roofing costs and tile roof lifespans in mind. While clay tile roofing is more expensive than concrete, many homeowners consider the longer lifespan to be worth the up-front investment. However, you are the only person who can decide the right roofing material for your home.

As professional roofers, we strongly recommend prioritizing value over roofing costs to ensure you get a high-quality roof. While you should never overpay for a roof, getting too hung up on getting the cheapest possible roof is often a recipe for disaster. ### Soffit and Fascia Replacement

Soffits and fascia are often-overlooked sections of a roofing system. If you’ve noticed signs of damage in these parts of your roof, though, it’s imperative that you seek soffit and fascia replacement services ASAP. But how do you pick reliable contractors? And how much should you expect to pay for soffit and fascia repairs?

We’re PITCH Roofing, and as your local roofing partner, we’re here to answer all these questions and more. As licensed, veteran roofers serving the Greater Tampa Bay region, we’re more than qualified to answer all of your questions about soffits and fascia as well as your questions about how to get the best roofing services in Florida.

Now, let’s talk about the role your soffits and fascia play in protecting your roof!
Why Is Soffit and Fascia Replacement So Important?


We’ll start with a quick review of the role that soffits and fascia play. Fascia is the flat, vertical board along the lower edge of your roof. Your soffits are the horizontal boards that sit below your fascia. And together, these two come together to keep your roof dry and functional.

For one thing, they both protect your roof from leaks and water damage. Even during a mild summer storm, winds can whip rain into places that it couldn’t normally reach, like the underside of your roof. By keeping the water out, soffits and fascia protect your roof from serious damage.

Your soffits and fascia also help with the ventilation of your roof, which is just as important for keeping your roof healthy and functional. Soffit vents allow fresh air to filter into your roof and attic, whereas your roof’s exhaust vents filter out hot, humid air that could otherwise lead to water damage or mold development.

When your soffits and fascia are damaged, though, they can’t function properly. This can lead to issues with leaks, retaining water, mold, rot, and even roof sagging over time. In short, soffit and fascia replacement is not something that you want to wait for.

If you’ve noticed peeling paint, cracks in your soffits or fascia, or signs of pests in your roof, then it may be time to get a soffit and fascia replacement. But how are you supposed to pick reliable roofing contractors?
Picking the Best Roofers for Your Soffit and Fascia Replacement


Because replacing your soffit and fascia doesn’t require a full roof replacement, you might think that you don’t need to be especially choosy with your roofers. But as we’ve established, your soffit and fascia are critical to your roof’s health. If you want them to keep your roof safe, they must be worked on by experienced professionals.

Let’s talk about how you can find the best roofers in Florida for your soffit and fascia replacement!

### How Much Does Flat Roof Installation Cost in Florida?

In many places, flat roofs are primarily used by businesses and other commercial structures. But in Florida, flat roofs are a normal part of residential roofing. This has led many Florida homeowners and business owners to have questions about flat roof installation costs and options when the time comes to replace their roofs.

When trying to account for the many factors that go into flat roof installation, it helps to have expert insight. That’s what we’re here for — PITCH Roofing has mastered flat roof replacements during our time as Florida roofers, and today we’re passing on everything you need to know for your own roof replacement. Keep reading for your complete guide to flat roof installation in Florida!
Flat Roof Installation Costs and Options


On average, flat roof installation costs between $4 and $14 per square foot in Florida. But a range that big isn’t really helpful for planning your own roof replacement. For a more accurate number, we have to look at flat roof replacement on a material-by-material basis.

But there’s more to flat roof installation than just the price. So before we get into the nitty gritty of roof replacement costs, let’s discuss your options and the overall value that your new flat roof can offer.
Modified Bitumen Flat Roofing
Modified bitumen, or mod bit, is made with asphalt, specialized rubber polymers, and a fiberglass base. The result is a robust flat roofing material that can keep out water while also resisting the worst that Florida’s weather patterns have to offer.

Specifically, modified bitumen roofs are great at resisting impact damage. Protection like this can be a lifesaver since storm debris and hail could otherwise puncture your flat roof and lead to leaks. As a bonus, modified bitumen is quick and easy to install, which helps keep flat roof installation costs down.

While modified bitumen comes in various colors (black, grey, and white being the most common), it’s usually a black roofing material. This makes it a popular choice for hospitals and other structures where you can see the roof from inside the building since it helps hide dirt and signs of aging.

All in all, modified bitumen roofs last for about 20 years in Florida. For a flat roof in the south, this is a reasonable lifespan and makes mod bit a high-value roofing system for any homeowner or business owner.
TPO Flat Roofing
Thermoplastic polyolefin, TPO, is a membrane roofing system. In other words, it’s applied in a single ply to create a waterproof barrier across your roof. Since this is a rubber roofing system, you can count on it keeping water out better than any other flat roofing material.

In theory, a flat roof has a low slope to help water move off your roof. But when things go wrong, your roof can start retaining water. With a TPO roof, though, you can count on that waterproof membrane to keep your roof protected even during a major hurricane or tropical storm. Additionally, their white color helps reflect UV rays away from your structure to keep it cool and reduce stress on your roof.

TPO roofs have their drawbacks as well. For one thing, flat roof installation takes more time and expertise with TPO, which can drive up the cost. And because they’re a single-ply roofing membrane, they’re more vulnerable to puncture damage from storm debris or hail than modified bitumen.

TPO roofing lasts for a long while — up to 30 years. For a flat roof, lifespan doesn’t get much better than that, which makes TPO flat roofs an extremely popular option for homes and businesses in Florida.
Flat Roof Installation Costs in Florida


Now that we’ve covered the value of two of the most popular flat roofing options in Florida, it’s time to talk about the real flat roof installation costs that you can expect to pay.

A modified bitumen roof can cost anywhere from $4 to $8 per square foot. In other words, a 1,500-square-foot flat roof installation would cost $6,000 and $12,000. This low flat roof installation cost is thanks to both low-cost manufacturing and its ability to be installed quickly and easily.

On the other hand, installing a TPO roof costs between $9 and $15. Using that same measurement of a 1,500 square roof, you’re looking at flat roof installation costs between $13,500 and $22,500. While TPO has higher material and installation costs, many Floridians feel that it’s worth the extra investment for a roof that will last longer and better resist water damage.

Flat Roof Installation FAQs
Q: How much does it cost to install a flat roof in Florida?

A: Flat roof installation costs vary depending on your material, size of your roof, and unique roofing features like chimneys or skylights. That said, flat roof replacements cost between $5 and $15 on average.

Q: How long do flat roofs last?

A: Proper flat roof installation is essential in making sure your roof lasts as long as possible. When properly installed, most flat roofs will last between 15 and 30 years, depending on the material and how well it’s maintained.

Q: Do flat roofs require a lot of maintenance?

A: Flat roofs usually require more inspections and repairs than sloped roofs. That’s because they’re vulnerable to puncture damage and leaks, especially if there’s an issue with installation and the roof doesn’t drain properly.

Q: Are flat roofs energy efficient in Florida?

A: Depending on the type of flat roof, you can add reflective caps to help increase energy efficiency. If you’re interested in energy-efficient flat roofing options, be sure to mention this to your roofer when you consult with them for an estimate.

### Get Insurance to Pay for Your New Roof in 4 Steps

As a homeowner, you probably already know about Florida’s homeowners insurance crisis. Floridians pay a lot of money to safeguard their homes, and they expect support when their roof eventually needs replacing. Unfortunately, using your coverage can be difficult, especially if you’re not used to navigating insurance systems. That’s why we’re here to tell you how to get insurance to pay for a roof replacement in Florida.

We’re PITCH Roofing, your trusted local roofing partners. Over our years of providing high-quality roofing services, we’ve learned the ins and outs of getting your roof replacement covered by insurance. Keep reading for a complete breakdown of how to get your new roof covered by your homeowners insurance!
How to Get Insurance to Pay for a Roof Replacement in Florida


At first glance, the process of getting your roof replacement covered by insurance can seem daunting. The language on your policy may be confusing, you may not be sure who to contact, or you may just not know how to prove that you qualify for coverage. But with a bit of know-how, all of these hurdles become much easier to navigate.

See for yourself in these four steps to get your homeowners insurance to cover your roof replacement!
1. Review Your Policy and Roof Replacement Coverage
Many homeowners think that having insurance means you never have to pay for a roof replacement. Unfortunately, this is not the case. To get your insurance provider to pay for a new roof, you’ll likely have to meet specific criteria.

To find details on your own coverage, you’ll have to carefully read your policy. That said, most homeowners insurance policies only cover weather-related damage. This means that they probably won’t pay for a new roof if it has simply reached the end of its life due to normal aging.

However, you may be able to get insurance to pay for a roof replacement if your roof was severely damaged by:

 	High winds (missing shingles, impact damage from storm debris)
 	Water damage (stormwater damaging your decking)
 	Hail (impact damage, dents in metal roofs)

If your roof needs replacing because of these weather-related factors, then there’s a good chance you’re covered by your insurance policy. However, the burden is on you as the homeowner to prove your case.
2. Collect Evidence for Your Roof Replacement Insurance Claim
When you’re trying to get insurance to pay for a roof replacement, you have to prove two things: first, that your roof was damaged. And second, that your roof was damaged by a major weather event.

Proving that your roof sustained damage is the easy part. Take photos of your roof to show the damaged sections. If you’re not able to access your roof yourself, most roofing companies will be happy to snap a few pictures for you as part of conducting a roof inspection. Be sure to take photos of the damage close up and farther away so that your insurance company can see both the details of the damage and the big picture.

You’ll also need to find ways to document how and when the damage occurred. If your roof was damaged in a hurricane, it should be easy to find articles showing that your area was hit by a major storm. Or if your roof was hit by a falling tree, it can be helpful to take photos of the tree from the ground to show where it fell.

This is a lot of legwork, but it’s essential to getting the insurance coverage you deserve. Once you’ve taken steps to prove that your roof was damaged by weather, the next step is proving that it needs replacing.
3. Get a Roof Inspection to Prove Your Roof Needs Replacing


In a perfect world, your photos would count as proof that your home need a roof replacement. But insurance companies are finicky, and they’ll usually only accept proof from licensed contractors. That’s why your next step to getting insurance to pay for a roof replacement is scheduling a roof inspection.

During your roof inspection, a licensed roofer will get on your roof and create a detailed report determining whether it needs to be repaired or replaced. If they determine that it needs replacing, you’ll send in that report with the other parts of your claim.

When getting a roof inspection, it’s important to make sure you’re working with experienced professionals. For one thing, if they’re not licensed in the state of Florida, your insurer won’t take the report seriously. And it pays to go with roofers who have experience with this kind of documentation. A vague report on your roof is as helpful as not having one at all.

While roof inspections aren’t typically free, they’re fairly low-cost. Generally, you can get a quality roof inspection for under $200. This price may not be reimbursed by your insurance company. But compared to the cost of a roof replacement, it’s easy to justify this investment in getting your roof covered.

You won’t just need a roof inspection to get your claim approved, though. You’ll also need a roof replacement cost estimate.
4. Collect Your Roof Replacement Quotes
The purpose of getting a roof inspection is to prove your roof needs replacing. Once that’s done, your insurance company will want numbers for how much they can expect to pay if they approve your claim. For that, you’ll need to provide several roofing estimates, although they may not need to come from different contractors.

When scheduling your estimates, you’ll need to request quotes for several different types of materials, including the original material. For example, if your shingle roof was damaged in a hurricane, you’ll want to ask for estimates for shingle, metal, and tile roofs, just to cover your bases (although we wouldn’t recommend expecting your insurance company to upgrade your roof). This is because roofing companies need to know they’re getting a fair deal, so they’ll want to see their options.

Right now, insurance companies are especially wary of roofers in Florida. That’s because storm chasers rigged the system by providing extremely costly estimates with inflated prices and then delivering sub-par work. To make sure that your claim isn’t rejected, pick roofers with a great reputation for providing fair prices and quality workmanship.

How to Choose a Roofing Contractor in Florida


Unfortunately, when you’re looking to pick a roofer, it’s not enough to just go with whoever says they’re the best or claims to have the most experience. Many roofers either overstate their qualifications or outright lie about them. Despite this, there are still plenty of ways that you can find both the truth and reliable roofers.

1. Keep Your Search Local
There are some things you just don’t want a big, national corporation for, and roofing is one of them. It’s not that large, national roofing companies can’t be good — some of them are great. But a great roof in Ohio, one that’s designed to stand up to ice and snow, might not make it through even a single Florida hurricane season.

That’s why it pays to go with local roofing expertise. When you pick contractors who live and work in Florida, you get the benefit of all that local experience. But when considering how to choose a roofing contractor in Florida, the issue isn’t just the value of in-state experience. You also need to be aware of the dangers that traveling roofers can bring.

We call them “storm chasers” — roofers who blow into Florida after a major storm and go around offering dirt-cheap roof replacements to homeowners who took the brunt of the damage. Part of the problem with this is that they often use inexperienced subcontractors. But another part of the issue is that they don’t stick around. This means that if your roof runs into any trouble after being worked on by storm chasers, nobody is going to be there to be held accountable for the work.

When you pick local roofers, you can count on dependability and great roofing warranties. So between local roofers and storm chasers, there’s really no competition.
2. Check Out Online Reviews and Local Recommendations
Reviews are the first place that you should look when hiring a roofing contractor. Simply Googling “roofers near me” is a great place to start. When looking at results, don’t just go based on the average star rating, but instead, check for recent reviews in the last few months. This will make sure you’re seeing the latest information about your roofing company, since great reviews from five years ago don’t mean much if the recent reviews are mostly negative.

Of course, most roofing companies will have the odd negative review or two. Nobody can please everyone all the time. But watch out for patterns in the roofing reviews. For example, if multiple people in the past three months say that the work wasn’t done well or that the crew left nails in their yards, then you probably have good reason to expect that the same will happen with your job.

Don’t just limit yourself to online reviews, though. It also helps to get recommendations from neighbors and people on Nextdoor. After all, if your neighbor loves their new roof, then it makes sense to choose contractors with experience in your neighborhood. Just make sure to double-check any recommendations by investigating online reviews — it never hurts to be too careful when choosing a roofing contractor!
3. Collect Multiple Estimates


In addition to knowing how to choose a roofing contractor, everyone also wants to know how to get the best price on a roofing estimate. Luckily, the answer to both is the same: start collecting estimates. By being able to directly compare prices, you’ll be able to find the best rate for the job.

When you get multiple estimates, you’ll also be able to compare solutions. Different roofers may have different ways of solving your roofing issue. For example, if one roofer tells you that you need a roof replacement but two others tell you that you just need a repair, you can safely assume that your roof still has years of life left on it and save yourself the big payout.

So in addition to helping you get the best price, collecting estimates also gives you the chance to make sure that the right work is being done on your roof.
4. Prioritize Quality Roofing Over Low Costs
Comparing estimates is the best way to get a good price, but it’s important not to get blinded by a low number. Storm chasers offer low-cost roofing, but more importantly, they also offer low-quality roofing. And there’s no point in paying a reduced cost for roofing work that another contractor will have to redo any way.

Sometimes the lowest price is the right choice. But just as often, low roofing costs are a ploy to get your business, even if the roofers know they can’t provide quality workmanship. That’s why it’s important to not forget the other items on this list when you see low roofing costs. While you may save some money today, roofing costs are all about the long game, and cheap roofing always costs more in the long run.
5. Always Get a Roofing Contract
If you don’t remember any other step of how to choose a roofing contractor, remember this one. You always need a contract. Even if these roofers have great reviews, even if they’ve offered you the best price, even if someone you trust recommends them, always get a roofing contract.

Why is this so important? Because the contract exists to protect both parties. It guarantees that your roofing services will be done as agreed upon, and it gives the roofer some weight to demand payment for their services. That’s why you should be extremely suspicious of roofers who hesitate to provide a written, thorough contract.

Without a contract, the roofer can do whatever they want to your roof. And whether the job is completed according to what you agreed upon or not, there’s no written proof and thus no way for you to demand that the work be completed.

Generally, not wanting a contract is a sign of a scam roofing contractor. These roofers don’t insist on contracts because they don’t want to be held accountable. So if a roofer ever tries to start working on your home without a contract in place, that’s a surefire sign that you need to look elsewhere!

### Why Are Asphalt Shingles So Popular? Common Roofing Materials Explained

Asphalt shingles have been the most popular roofing material in North America for over a century. And even in Florida, where we have unique concerns like hurricanes and extreme humidity, asphalt shingles dominate the roofing industry. But why are asphalt shingles so popular in Florida?

There are many factors that contribute to the popularity of asphalt shingles. We should know — we’re PITCH Roofing, your veteran Florida roofing contractors. Keep reading for our breakdown of why people love asphalt shingles, from their performance to their price!
Why Are Asphalt Shingles So Popular in Florida?


Florida has unique roofing concerns. Unlike northern states, we don’t generally have to worry about ice or snow damaging our roofs. Instead, our roofs have to handle high winds, heavy rain, humidity, and the occasional hail storm.

Asphalt shingles have proven to perform well in all of these areas and more. Let’s talk about the five biggest ways that asphalt shingles have earned their great reputation in Florida!
Durability and Longevity
In Florida, everyone’s biggest priority is getting a roof that lasts. And with their unique composition of fiberglass, asphalt coating, and protective stone granules, asphalt shingles can handle the worst that the Sunshine State has to offer.

Their asphalt coating prevents water from penetrating your shingles and ruining them. And when you invest in quality architectural shingles, you can count on wind resistance of up to 130 mph. This won’t prevent shingle uplift during major hurricanes, of course. However, you’ll likely only lose a small number of shingles, and replacing them is both a quick and cheap repair.

On average, asphalt shingles last for 20 to 25 years in Florida. While this isn’t the longest possible lifespan for a roof, it’s nothing to sneeze at. And you can count on quality protection throughout your roof’s life when you choose reliable asphalt shingle roofers. For example, as Owens Corning Preferred Contractors, we can offer a 10-year workmanship warranty and a lifetime material warranty. This means that even if your roof is damaged, you’ll still have coverage thanks to the many great shingle roofing warranties available! This comprehensive protection goes a long way in making asphalt shingles so popular.
Diverse Color and Style Options
Why are asphalt shingles so popular? Well, their style versatility has a lot to do with it. For one thing, architectural shingles are famous for their great aesthetics. Thanks to their layered design and unique shading, they can create the appearance of texture and depth on your roof, which goes a long way in creating visual interest.

In addition to their excellent aesthetics, asphalt shingles come in nearly any color you could imagine. So no matter what style you’re going for with your shingle roof replacement, you’ll be able to find a perfect shingle color to match. That said, neutral colors like browns and greys are more abundant, so you may have to pay a little extra for especially bold colors.
Easy to Sell
Florida has one of the hottest real estate markets in the country, especially in and around Tampa Bay. If you’re a homeowner who plans to sell one day, asphalt shingles are an excellent choice. Why? Because these tried and true roofing materials make it simple and easy to sell your home. No wonder why asphalt shingles are so popular!

Most people are familiar with asphalt shingle roofing. So while a metal roof could raise some concerns for homeowners who aren’t familiar with this roofing option, you can count on any potential buyers being familiar with shingle roofs. And when you’re trying to sell your home, having a new, reliable roof makes a world of difference.
Florida-Proof Roofing


Technically speaking, no roof is 100% “Florida-proof.” But asphalt shingles come pretty close. While they are vulnerable to wind uplift during severe storms, these shingles can handle many of Florida’s biggest roof killers without a problem.
Some of the most common environmental factors that shingle roofs handle well include:

 	Impact Damage: Asphalt and stone granules create a strong, protective base. As a result, you can count on your asphalt shingle roof to easily handle hail and storm debris.
 	Mold: Mold and algae can grow on Florida roofs year-round. But thanks to advancements in roofing technology, asphalt shingles are protected. This is thanks to time-released copper in your shingle that prevents mold development over the years.
 	UV Rays: The Florida sun is no joke. But the glaze on shingles’ stone granules can help reflect UV rays away from your home, protecting both the shingle and your energy bill. This is especially effective with lighter-colored shingles, which absorb less heat.
 	High Winds: As we’ve established, shingles can be removed by extremely high winds. But with wind ratings as high as 130 mph, you can count on your asphalt shingles to stay put even through Category 3 hurricanes. This makes them a reliable roofing material, even in hurricane-prone Florida!

Handling Florida’s infamous climate so well is part of what makes asphalt shingles so popular in the Sunshine State. While no roof can go on forever without being damaged, asphalt shingles excel at keeping the Florida elements at bay for decades to come.
Low-Cost Roofing
In addition to their durability and style options, the low cost of asphalt shingles is a big contributor to why asphalt shingles are so popular. It makes sense — in addition to having low manufacturing costs, asphalt shingles are quick and easy to install. After all, it’s not time-consuming to nail shingles onto your roof. So how much can you expect to pay for an asphalt shingle roof?

Prices vary, and they always depend on what type of asphalt shingles you choose. For our purposes, we’ll use architectural shingles as an example, since they’re the most popular type of shingle. These shingles cost around seven dollars per square foot. So on a 2,000-square-foot roof, you can expect to pay roughly $14,000 for an asphalt shingle roof replacement.

This isn’t a hard and fast number, though. Your final price will depend on which brand of asphalt shingles you choose, your roof’s unique dimensions, and who you pick to install your roof. So while you can count on asphalt shingles being affordable, you’ll need to start collecting estimates to determine exactly how much your asphalt shingle roof will cost.

### The Most Popular Types of Roofs in Florida

If you haven’t gone through a roof replacement before, it’s normal to feel overwhelmed by the options. The pressure can be especially high here in Florida, where you know that your roof has to protect your home or business from UV rays, year-round humidity, and even hurricanes. So how are you supposed to know the good and the bad of all the types of roofs in Florida?

This is a good place to start. We’re PITCH Roofing, your local roofing partners. When you need information on the different types of roofs in Florida, there’s no better resource than veteran Florida roofing contractors like us. Stick with us as we cover the most popular types of roofs near you!
Types of Sloped Roofs in Florida


Most homes in Florida have a slope between 4:12 and 9:12. In other words, they’re angled in such a way that water will naturally move off your roof thanks to gravity. This means that your roofing materials need to focus more on resisting winds and impact damage and less on keeping out standing water.

There are plenty of roofing materials that do exactly this, so let’s talk about these types of roofs in Florida and which could be right for your home!
Shingle Roofing
Asphalt shingles are the most common type of roof in Florida. Made of a fiberglass baseboard, asphalt coating, and protective granules, these shingles can resist rain, hail, and winds up to 110 mph. As an added bonus, they’re also the most affordable sloped roofing option on the market.

When properly installed, asphalt shingles last for 20 to 25 years on average. This is a respectable length of time, but it’s also one of the shorter lifespans for sloped roofing materials. As a result, asphalt shingles may not be for you if you want a roof that will last for an exceptionally long time.

Composite shingles, or synthetic shingles, are a higher-end alternative. Made of unique rubberized polymers and recycled materials, composite shingles replicate the look of slate or shake shingles at a much lower cost. They’re also durable and able to resist the worst of Florida’s weather with wind ratings as high as 150 mph. As a result of this strength, these shingles last for about 50 years.

The one downside is the cost of synthetic shingles. Where asphalt shingles cost around six dollars per square foot, synthetic shingles cost closer to $12 per square foot. Still, if you want a durable roof with a luxurious aesthetic, synthetic shingles are one of the best types of roofs in Florida.
Tile Roofing
Clay tiles have been one of the most popular types of roofs in Florida for centuries. Made from natural clay, these tiles resist rain, rot, and even winds of up to 125 mph. Thanks to their hefty weight, they’re extremely difficult for wind to remove in a storm. However, this weight also means they put a lot of pressure on your roof, and not all structures will be able to hold up a tile roof. When you get a roofing estimate, your roofer should inspect your home to make sure that they can safely install a clay tile roof.

Where clay tiles really stand out, though, is their longevity. Clay tile roofs can last 50 to 100 years or more, making them the longest-lasting type of roof in Florida by far. This comes at a premium, though, with clay tile roofing sometimes costing more than $20 per square foot.

Concrete tiles are a more affordable alternative. With many of the same protective benefits, the main difference between these two is that concrete tiles only last for about 50 years. However, you can still expect similar protection and great aesthetics from a concrete tile roof.

So how much does concrete tile roofing cost? Prices vary, but you can expect to pay closer to $15 per square foot for a concrete tile roof replacement. While this isn’t “affordable” by everyone’s standards, it does represent a great way to get a classic Florida roof at a substantially reduced cost!
Metal Roofing
Metal roofing is the gold standard across all the types of roofs in Florida. These roofs are durable and able to resist winds of 140 mph or more, depending on the type of metal roof. And with lifespans ranging from 40-70 years, you can count on your metal roof to last for a long time. To give you a better idea of what you can expect from your metal roof replacement, let’s look at the two types of metal roofs in Florida.

Standing seam metal roofs are arguably the best option for metal roofing. With flat panels with raised edges, these roofs come together via interlocking under-panel connections. These hidden fasteners are then hidden and protected from the elements. As a result, standing seam roofs last closer to 70 years than 40. And their sleek, smooth exterior is perfect for a modern home. However, they’re also more expensive.

Corrugated metal roofs, on the other hand, are more affordable but don’t last as long. These corrugated sheets are drilled into your roof, which secures them but leaves their fasteners exposed where they can experience wear and tear from the weather. For this reason, they don’t last as long as standing seam roofs.

In terms of price, a standing seam metal roof costs around $18 per square foot. Corrugated metal roofing, on the other hand, costs closer to $12 per square foot. Whichever you choose, both types of roofs can offer great, long-lasting protection!
Types of Flat Roofs in Florida


A flat roof isn’t technically flat. Rather, it’s a low-slope roof, with a slope lower than 4:12. As a result, it has different issues than a sloped roofing material. For these types of roofs in Florida, the biggest priority is water resistance, since it can take longer for water to move off a low-slope roof.

With this in mind, let’s look at the most common types of flat roofs in Florida!
Modified Bitumen Roofing
Similar to asphalt shingles, modified bitumen is made from a combination of asphalt and fiberglass. Importantly, however, it has rubber added in to improve its water resistance. This creates a flat roofing material that’s both sturdy enough to resist impact damage while also being water-resistant enough to keep your structure dry.

Among the types of flat roofs in Florida, the lifespans are fairly comparable. Mod bit roofing lasts for about 20 years, making it a standard option. With low costs of only about six dollars per square foot, modified bitumen roofing is a popular option for people looking for budget-friendly roof replacements.
TPO Roofing
Thermoplastic polyolefin, or TPO, is a rubberized roofing membrane. That means it’s made primarily of rubber and is applied as a single layer across your roofing system. As a result, TPO roofing is lightweight, flexible, and unbeatable when it comes to water resistance.

A new arrival on the scene, TPO roofing has been protecting roofs since the 90s. Since it’s so new, though, nobody is sure exactly how long it lasts. Our best guess, though, is that TPO roofing will last for 20 to 30 years on average. This makes it slightly more durable than a modified bitumen roof.

This increased durability comes at a price, though, both literally and figuratively. TPO roofing is vulnerable to puncture damage, so it can sometimes be ruptured by hail or storm debris and need repairs. And in terms of cost, TPO roofing costs around eight dollars per square foot, making it just a bit more expensive than modified bitumen. Still, if you want to be sure that your roof is dry and protected for years to come, TPO roofing is one of the best types of roofs in Florida.

### TPO Roofing Costs Across the Lifetime of Your Roof

Picking out a flat roofing material is a big challenge. Low-slope roofs have their own unique challenges to live up to, and the type of flat roofing that you pick will have a big impact on how well your new roof performs. Rubber roofing like TPO is one of the best options on the market, but many homeowners have questions about how much TPO roofing costs.

At PITCH Roofing, we’ve repaired and installed more than our fair share of TPO roofs. That’s why we’re qualified to be your local TPO pricing experts. Stick with us as we cover the full costs of a TPO roof, from installation to maintenance to repairs!
How Much TPO Roofing Costs in Florida


TPO roof replacements cost around $8,000 to $14,000 on average. But that doesn’t really tell you how much you’ll pay in TPO roofing costs for your own installation, let alone across your roof’s lifetime. To get a complete look at how much your TPO roof will cost in Florida, we have to look at the costs of installation, maintenance, and repairs.
TPO Roof Installation & Replacement Costs
Replacing a roof is the most expensive part of roofing, with contractors having to both tear off and dispose of the old roof as well as install the new one. This can wrack up quite a bill between material and labor costs. With TPO roofing costing between five and nine dollars per square foot, you can expect to pay between $7,500 and $13,5000 for a 1,500-square-foot roof replacement.

For a membrane roofing system like TPO, this is a great value. In addition to being waterproof, TPO roofing lasts for 20 to 30 years. This makes it an extremely competitive flat roofing material, even when you account for TPO roofing costs.

But you’re not done paying for a roof just because it’s successfully installed. Keeping your roof healthy and functional takes time and effort, so you can count on paying TPO roofing costs for years to come. Let's talk roofing maintenance costs to get you a better idea of what you can expect to pay in upkeep.
TPO Roof Maintenance Costs
Homeowners sometimes overlook maintenance as a way to lower total TPO roofing costs, but this is not a good idea. Taking care of your roof is essential to making sure that it keeps working for years to come.

A good place to start with TPO roof maintenance is to get regular roof inspections. Conventional wisdom is to get a roof inspection twice a year and after major storms. Many issues can pop up on a TPO roof, from UV damage to weakening seams, and staying ahead of these problems is the best way to keep your TPO roofing costs down across the life of your roof. The price of a roof inspection can be anywhere from $200 to $500.

You’ll also want to invest in regular roof cleanings. There’s no set timetable for this, but when you start noticing algae or mold on your roof, it’s time for a professional cleaning. We don’t recommend DIY cleaning, since many cleaners and scrubbing techniques could damage your TPO roof. Paying for professional TPO roof cleaning services can cost between $300 and $700 depending on the size and state of your roof.

While maintenance can keep repair costs low, it can’t prevent wear and tear on your roof. That’s why it helps to know the rough costs of the most common TPO roof repairs.
TPO Roof Repair Costs


It's hard to nail down how much TPO roof repairs cost. That’s because the total roof repair costs will depend on what the issue is, the cause, and the extent of the damage. For this reason, TPO roof repairs can cost anywhere from $100 to several thousands of dollars, making them a significant portion of total TPO roofing costs.

But we know that a range that wide isn’t helpful. That’s why we’re sharing the most common issues that TPO roofs run into and how much they cost to fix!

 	Puncture Damage: As a rubber roof, TPO can be punctured by foot traffic and storm debris. Luckily, repairing this damage is usually quick and easy since you only need another piece of TPO to cover the punctures. For a repair like this, expect to pay anywhere from $200 to $800, depending on the size of the damaged portion of your roof.
 	Leaks: The cost of TPO leak repairs depends on what caused the leak. Causes range widely, from poor installation to wear and tear. Because of these diverse leak causes, fixing a leak can cost between $300 and $1,000.
 	Membrane Shrinkage: Over time, your TPO roof membrane can shrink. When this happens, it leads to cracks and strains across your roof. Fixing this requires completely replacing sections of your roof, so you can expect to pay between $1,000 and $2,500 for this labor-intensive repair.
 	Pooling Water: Trapped water can indicate either poor installation or some kind of damage to your roof. In general, it’s cheaper to fix new damage than an essential problem with your roof. To reflect this disparity, fixing this common issue with TPO roofing costs between $300 and $1,200 on average.

As you can see, TPO repairs aren’t cheap. To minimize repair costs, you’ll need contractors who know TPO roofing inside and out.

### Everything You Need to Know About Roofing Warranties in Florida

If you’re confused about roofing warranties, you’re not the only one. Between workmanship warranties, material warranties, lifetime warranties, and all the other types of protection available for your roof, it can be hard to tell what covers what. Thankfully, our experienced PITCH Roofing crew has the answers you need about how roofing warranties work.

As experienced Florida roofers, we know our stuff. And as an Owens Corning Preferred Contractor, we offer some of the strongest warranties in the state. That means we’re more than qualified to break down everything you should know about your roof’s warranties!
How Do Roofing Warranties Work?


In theory, we all understand warranties. They’re pretty simple, after all; they just mean that, if there’s a problem with your product, someone else pays to repair or replace it. And it works the same way with roofing warranties. But with so many different types of roofing warranties available, it’s normal to have questions about which warranties cover what.

To help clarify this murky area, let’s talk about the different types of roofing warranties one by one!
Workmanship Warranties
The better the workmanship warranty, the more faith your roofer has in their skills. That’s because these types of roofing warranties are centered around the quality of your contractor’s roof repair or replacement skills. In short, if something goes wrong with your roof due to poor installation, it’s covered under your workmanship warranty.

Almost every reputable roofing company offers a workmanship warranty. But the length of time can vary quite a bit. In our experience, we’ve seen everything from two-year workmanship warranties to warranties that last for 20+ years. There are even lifetime warranties that will cover your roof across the lifespan of your materials.

In general, though, 10 years is a good minimum amount to accept, although a longer warranty is a good sign that your contractors have faith in the quality of their work.
Material Warranties
A material warranty on your roof covers the products installed on your roof. For this reason, these warranties often come from the manufacturer rather than your contractor (although there are exceptions). For example, if you got a tile roof replacement but there was an issue with your tiles, your material warranty would cover replacing any defective materials and having the replacements installed.

Your material warranty may also have different rules for when it applies. For example, as Owens Corning Preferred Contractors, our shingle roofs come with a lifetime material warranty. However, they also have blow-off coverage for the first 15 years of your roof’s life. In this way, different types of damage may fall under different parts of your material warranty.
Who Pays for Roofing Warranties?
At first glance, you might think that it doesn’t matter who pays for a roofing warranty. After all, as long as someone else is covering the bill, does it really matter? The truth is that it very well could matter, because you’ll only have coverage for as long as the company backing your warranty continues to exist.

Many Florida homeowners have found themselves without the great warranties they were promised because the warranty was only backed by their contractors, and when a problem arose, the contractors had either moved on or left the business entirely. This leaves homeowners with no coverage and no real way to avoid paying for the necessary repairs out of pocket.

That’s why manufacturer-backed roofing warranties are especially valuable. Manufacturers like Owens Corning have been around for decades, so you can be confident they’re not going anywhere. Since Pitch is a Preferred Contractor, we can offer manufacturer-backed material and workmanship warranties. This offers enhanced peace of mind for customers who want to be sure that they’ll have coverage no matter what happens!
What Isn’t Covered by Roofing Warranties?


In an ideal world, your roofing warranties would apply in every situation. But the truth is that there are many scenarios where your coverage might not apply. Let’s look at some of the most common reasons that you can’t use your warranties to cover roofing damage:

 	Damage by Extreme Weather: Your roofing warranties exist to make sure your roof can handle everyday weather. But they almost never apply to damage from hurricanes, tornadoes, hail storms, etc. These are considered “acts of God” and beyond the scope of what roofers can reliably protect against, so your roofing warranties probably won’t apply.
 	New Roofing Work: Having another contractor work on your roof could void your workmanship warranty. Your material warranty would still be in effect, but many workmanship warranties come with clauses about not vouching for their work after someone else has been on your roof and had a chance to make their own changes.
 	DIY Roofing: If having another professional on your roof doesn’t void your workmanship warranty, you can bet that working on your roof yourself will. It’s normal to want to save money when a leak pops up or shingles get blown off, but attempting repairs on your own could mean that you have no coverage when the next big problem comes along.
 	Pressure Washing: In humid Florida, algae on roofs is a real concern. But the way to handle it isn’t with a pressure washer, since this will likely void both your workmanship and material warranties. If you need your roof cleaned, it’s best to reach out to a company that specializes in safely and gently cleaning your roof without risking damage to your materials.

With so many ways to void your warranty, you should pick reputable roofers with transparent warranties who do great work the first time!
