### The 7 Most Common Roof Problems in Florida

When you’re making decisions about your roof, it helps to know what you’re up against. The Sunshine State has more than a few roof killers, and some roofing materials are better at handling these than others. To help you make the right decision for your home, we’re sharing the most common roof problems in Florida.

As your local roofers based in Pinellas County, PITCH Roofing is more than qualified to explain the biggest roofing problems that homeowners face. Today, we’re putting our decades of local roofing experience to use and helping you make the best choices for your home!
The 7 Most Common Roof Problems in Florida


Roofs are complex things with a lot of different parts. For this reason, almost anything can go wrong with a roof, especially when you have weather like ours. That said, below are the biggest issues that we see all the time as Florida roofing contractors.
1. Shingle Uplift
Take a look outside the morning after a hurricane, and you’ll probably see more than a few shingles scattered around the neighborhood. That’s because high winds can easily remove shingles from your roof during a hurricane, especially if winds exceed 110 mph. And when this happens, it can mean serious problems for your roof. Specifically, this leads to leaks, one of the most common roof problems in Florida.

Missing shingles create a weak point in your entire roofing system. For example, having your water-resistant underlayment exposed can lead to wear and tear that lets water into your home. And an unchecked leak can put your entire roofing system in jeopardy.

That’s why we strongly recommend giving your roof a look over after major storms. By acting quickly to get roof repair services as soon as you notice missing shingles, you can prevent leaks and even worse storm damage.
2. Damaged Flashing
Your flashing plays a critical role in helping water move off your roof. If you’re not familiar, your flashing is a piece of galvanized steel that moves along the valleys of your roof and helps guide water toward the edge of your roof. But in Florida, there are plenty of things that can damage your flashing and lead to issues with your roof retaining water.

Your flashing can get worn out by temperature changes, damaged by flying debris, or torn off by high winds. Without it, you can experience ponding and, over time, roof sagging, two serious issues that could threaten the life of your roof.
3. Cracked Sealant
Many parts of a roofing system need sealing to protect against water intrusions. These include your vents, chimneys, skylights, and virtually all other roofing features. This sealant is made to last, but there’s only so much that can be done about the hot Florida sun. Over time, sealant breaks down due to UV rays. Once it does, your home could easily experience serious leaks and mold problems.

Unfortunately, there is no reliable way to prevent sealant from cracking. However, you can minimize your risk by getting regular roof inspections. An exprienced roofer will be able to look at all the nooks and crannies of your roof to ensure that your sealant is holding strong. And if it’s not, they’ll help you fix the issue and keep your home safe.
4. Impact Damage
In Florida, almost anything becomes a projectile in a storm. That, in conjunction with tree branches and hail, can lead to impact damage, an extremely common roof problem in Florida. When high-speed winds send branches and other storm debris into your roof, they can do a lot of damage. This is especially true for tile roofs, which are often brittle.

There’s no way to completely mitigate the risk of impact damage. But you can lower it by keeping your yard clear of debris. Additionally, keeping tree limbs over your roof trimmed is a good way to keep your roof safe. If you do notice damage to your roof from hail or debris, reach out to reliable local roofers to get your roof back in top shape.
5. Pest Infestations
As a Florida homeowner, you probably know that many pests are eager to enter your home. But did you know they’re just as eager to move into your roof? Termites, rodents, and bats are some of the most common roof problems in Florida, as far as pests are concerned.

One good step in preventing pest infestations is keeping your roof clean. This means somewhat regular washings and clearing any fallen branches or leaves off your roof, which would otherwise become a home for pests. It’s also important to make sure that your soffits and fascia are healthy, as holes in these can become highways for pests.

If your roof does develop an infestation, you’ll first need to work with an exterminator. Then, once the pests have been removed, a roofer will be able to fix your roof and stop more bugs and rodents from entering your roof.
6. Mold Growth
If you can count on one thing in Florida, it’s humidity. Unfortunately, all this moisture in the air makes it easy for mold to grow. This is especially true if your roof has areas that sit mostly in the shade. Over the years, this mold can eat away at your roofing materials and weaken your entire roof.

Having good ventilation in your attic is one way to prevent mold from developing. And if you start seeing mold on your roof, it’s important to clean it immediately to stop the damage from spreading. Mold is one of the most common roof problems in Florida, and it only gets worse when left unaddressed.
7. Poor Repairs and Installation
Of all the most common roof problems in Florida, this one is the easiest to prevent. When inexperienced roofers repair or install a roof, they can create more problems than they solve. Whether they’re using cheap, low-quality materials or using unreliable contractors, the result is a roof that isn’t ready to stand up to the Florida elements.

And as the homeowner, you’re the one who pays the price. That’s why it’s a good idea to be choosey when picking your roofers. You’ll want to prioritize local experience, quality workmanship, and customer service. And we’re proud to say that at Pitch, we’ve earned top marks across the board.

As Owens Corning Preferred Contractors, we’ve proven ourselves as masters in quality roofing and customer service. And as local roofers, we have the personalized experience to protect your home against the worst that Florida has to offer. If you need help keeping your roof working at its best, we’re the roofers to call.

### Pros and Cons of Barrel Tile Roofing in Florida

As a Florida resident, you’ve probably noticed how popular tile roofing is down here. It’s part of the local history, with Florida being one of the first places on the continent to have clay tile roofs. Today, barrel tile roofing is just as popular as it has ever been. But many homeowners still have questions about this tile roofing material.

What makes barrel tiles different from other tiles? How do I know if barrel tile roofing is right for my home? We’re PITCH Roofing, and today we’re answering all of these questions and more. Keep reading for a full breakdown and review of everything you need to know about barrel tile roof replacements in Florida!
What Is Barrel Tile Roofing?


Barrel roofing tiles get their name from their iconic shape — rounded like a barrel cut in half. In Florida, the two most common types of barrel tiles are Spanish tiles and Mediterranean tiles, which reflects the classic and timeless appeal of barrel tile roofing. But beyond great aesthetics, these tile roofs are some of the most durable in the state of Florida.

Barrel roofing tiles function by locking together on your roof. With an alternating face-up and face-down pattern, these tiles seamlessly move water off your roof and protect it from wind, pests, UV rays, and all of Florida’s other major roof killers.

Barrel tiles are available in a variety of materials, with the two most common options being clay and concrete. Clay is the classic tile option and offers a longer lifespan, whereas concrete barrel tiles are more affordable but may not last as long. In this way, you can get a barrel tile roof that meets your unique needs and preferences!
Positives of Barrel Tile Roofing in Florida
Barrel roofing tiles have been a staple for Florida homeowners for centuries. Let’s talk about some of the biggest features that have contributed to this popularity!
Unbeatable Longevity
Many homeowners want a roof that they can install and then forget about. If this sounds familiar, then tile roofing could be perfect for you. A well-installed clay tile roof can last for upwards of a century, even in Florida. And while concrete barrel tiles don’t last as long, you can still expect to get 50 years of life out of your concrete tiles!

A big part of this long lifespan is the great wind resistance of barrel tiles. Since they’re heavy and lock together, wind doesn’t have much of a chance to remove them from your roof. Many barrel tile roofs are rated for 150 mph winds, which means your home will be protected even through major hurricanes!
Variety of Styles
In addition to choosing between clay and concrete tiles, you’ll be able to completely customize the aesthetic of your new tile roof. For one thing, you’ll be able to choose your type of barrel tile. Spanish tiles are a classic option, especially for homes with white stucco siding, and Mediterranean tiles are designed for the lower-slope roofs of Mediterranean-style homes.

Spanish barrel tiles are a high-profile S-tile, which creates an S shape with large, sweeping curves. This is the type of tile that you probably think of first when you imagine a tile roof. Homeowners choose this type of barrel tile roofing when they want to add a classic, old-world feel to their home.

Mediterranean tile roofs, on the other hand, use medium barrel tiles. These have a gentler, more measured curve, which creates a more contemporary look and adds visual interest to your home while still providing the classic appeal of a tile roof.

In addition to choosing the types of tiles, you’ll also be able to select a color that suits your home and your tastes. While tiles traditionally come in neutral tones and the distinctive clay tile red, nowadays you can get a barrel tile roof in virtually any color that you like.
Great Aging in Florida
As time goes on, every roofing system gets weaker. But of all the roofing materials in Florida, barrel tile roofing arguably holds up the best. Because of Florida’s year-round humidity, rot is a big concern for local shingle roofs. But because of the way that roofing tiles are manufactured, they’re all but impervious to rot and stay strong over the years.

Insects and other pests are also a big roofing concern in Florida. But because of their makeup, tile roofs don’t attract termites, carpenter ants, or other annoying pests. By keeping your roof dry and pest-free, tile roofs age well without giving you headaches over the years.
Negatives of Barrel Tile Roofing in Florida


Barrel tile roofing is great, but it’s not right for everyone. Let’s talk about some of the biggest drawbacks to barrel roofing tiles to help you make a decision about your roof replacement!
High Roofing Costs
While the price of barrel tile roofs can vary, they’re never the cheapest option. When you account for both materials and labor, a clay tile roof can cost between $19 and $31 per square foot. While concrete tiles are more affordable, you can still expect to pay $14 to $28 per square foot for a concrete barrel tile roof.

If barrel tile roofing works for your budget, we encourage you to consider it. These roofs are durable, beautiful, and some of the most reliable in the state, so they’re well worth the up-front investment However, they’re simply not in everyone’s budget, and there’s nothing wrong with ultimately deciding that a roofing material isn’t right for your home.
Heavy Roofing Materials
Part of what makes barrel tiles so appealing is their heft — it makes them much more resistant to hurricane-force winds. But the weight of tile roofing can also be a problem. That’s because your roof has to support that weight, and not every home is prepared to handle the weight of a tile roof.

For this reason, before starting your roof replacement, experienced installers will inspect your home to make sure that your roof can handle the weight of clay or concrete tiles. If necessary, they may suggest ways to add extra support to your roof. This process will increase your total tile roofing costs, but when it’s necessary, it’s the only way to safely install a tile roof.

### How Much Do Roof Leak Repairs Cost in Florida?

A leaking roof is a hassle that no homeowner wants to deal with. But between Florida’s seasonal storms, heavy UV exposure, and year-round humidity, roofing wear and tear is a fact of life. If you’ve recently noticed a new leak or stains on your ceiling, then you need to know how much a roof leak repair costs in Florida.

We’re PITCH Roofing, your local roofing partners based right here in Pinellas County. We’ve been fixing leaks across Florida for a long time, and we know that every job and solution is unique. But that doesn’t mean we can’t help. Stick with us as we go over the average cost of roof leak repairs in Florida!
What Determines the Roof Leak Repair Costs for Your Home?


As a homeowner, it’s easy to get frustrated with the lack of transparent pricing in the roofing industry. But with so many unique factors to every leak repair, it’s impossible to give a flat rate for every leaking roof in Florida.

That doesn’t mean you have to go in blind, though. Let’s talk about some of the factors that can affect how much your roof leak repair costs!

 	Roofing Materials: The kind of material on your roof will play a big role in how much it costs to fix your leaking roof. For example, replacing a few damaged shingles is cheap and easy. Fixing a damaged section of standing seam metal roofing, however, can cost a lot more.
 	Cause of the Leak: A roof can leak for any number of reasons. A minor leak in your attic may not be a big deal, but if your decking has become soaked through, you could be looking at much higher roof leak repair costs.
 	Age of Your Roof: An older roof is much more likely to have a larger problem causing the leak. As a result, it will usually cost more to repair a leak in an older roof than a new roof.
 	Roof Accessibility: The easier it is to access your roof, the less you’ll pay for repairs. So if your roof has an especially high slope or there are plants or other obstructions to accessing your roof, you can expect to pay more for roof leak repair services.

All of these factors will affect how much it costs to fix your roof. With this in mind, let’s discuss the cost of common causes of roof leaks!
Cost of Roof Leak Repairs in Florida
As we mentioned, the cause of your roof leak will drastically change your total roof leak repair costs. To give you an idea of what you might pay, we’re covering the cost of some of the most common causes of roof leaks!

 	Missing Shingles: This is arguably the most common cause of roof leaks, especially during hurricane season. If you’re only missing a handful of shingles, expect to pay up to around $500 for your repairs. If you’re missing a larger section of shingles, though, you could be looking at a bill between $1,000 and $2,000.
 	Poorly Driven Nails: If your shingles aren’t nailed into place correctly, the nail can rise over time and create an opening for water to enter your home. Fixing this improper installation on a small handful of shingles will cost around $400. But if your entire roof was poorly installed, you could be looking at a much larger issue.
 	Leaking Chimney or Skylights: Chimneys, skylights, and other unique roofing features create vulnerabilities in your roof. Re-sealing the flashing can fix the issue for under $500 in many cases. However, if the entire thing needs re-flashing, you could be looking at roof leak repair costs of up to $5,000.
 	Poor Ventilation: Your roof’s ventilation system can crack over years of UV exposure. When this happens, replacing or re-sealing your vents can stop the water from getting into your roofing system. In general, fixing poor ventilation costs between $300 and $500.
 	Soffit and Fascia Leaks: Your soffits and fascia keep water from entering your home in a storm. When they become damaged, this protection is weakened and you can start noticing leaks. Repairing a section of soffits and fascia could cost as little as $300, but if it all needs to be replaced, your bill could be upwards of $2,500.

Keep in mind that these are general price estimates, so your specific situation could be different, even if the cause of your roof’s leak is listed here. But regardless of what’s causing your leak, it’s important to move quickly to keep your roof leak repair costs low.

### The Best Time to Get a Roof Replacement in Florida

Deciding when to replace your roof in Florida can be tricky. Nobody wants to pay for a roof replacement before they need to, but waiting too long could cause problems with your homeowners insurance or, even worse, leave your home vulnerable to a hurricane. So what’s the best time to get a roof replacement in Florida?

Ultimately, the best time to get a roof replacement will come down to the specifics of your roof. These include things like location, age, and any damage that it has sustained across its life. But that’s not specific, and it’s not enough information to plan your roof replacement. For that, keep reading as PITCH Roofing explains when you should replace your roof in Florida!
How Age Changes When You Should Replace Your Roof


While damage could require an early roof replacement, every roof will need replacing after a certain amount of time. So how long can your roof go before you need a roof replacement? That depends on the kind of roofing material that’s protecting your home.

To give you an idea of the best time to get a roof replacement, let’s talk about how long the most popular roofing materials in Florida can last:

 	Asphalt Shingles: Architectural shingles last for 20-25 years in Florida.
 	Composite Shingles: Synthetic shingles stay healthy and strong for about 50 years.
 	Concrete Tiles: These cost-effective tile roofs have an average lifespan of 50 years.
 	Clay Tiles: Clay tile roofs have a unique lifespan of 100+ years, so it’s usually best to base your decision to replace your roof on its performance rather than its age.
 	Metal Roofing: Depending on the type of metal roof you choose, your roof could last 40-70 years on average.
 	Flat Roofs: Most flat roofs need replacements after about 20 years.

When your roof reaches the end of its lifespan, it’s time to replace it. For example, the best time to replace an asphalt shingle roof would be after about 20 years of life. But if your roof is running into problems before it reaches its full age, it may need an early roof replacement.
Signs It’s Time to Replace Your Roof
If your roof is damaged, then the best time to replace your roof could be sooner than you think. Not all roof damage is a sign of a serious problem, though; often, you can get away with a simple replacement. So what types of roof damage indicate that you need to replace your roof?

Signs that your roof needs replacing include:

 	Missing, Damaged, or Cracked Shingles: If your shingles are showing signs of major wear and tear like cracking or curling, it may be time to replace your roof. A good rule of thumb is that if more than 25% of your shingles are damaged, you need a roof replacement ASAP.
 	Multiple Leaks: Having a roof leak is often a simple repair. But multiple leaks throughout your roof point to a larger problem that only a full roof replacement can fix.
 	Roof Sagging: If you notice your ceiling starting to dip or sag, it’s probably time to replace your roof. This is a major issue, so it’s important to move quickly before your roof fails and destroys property inside of your home.
 	Missing Granules: Your asphalt shingles should have a thick coating of protective granules. If you notice they’re missing or showing up in your gutters, then your shingles have reached the end of their life and need replacing.

Experiencing any of these major roofing problems is a sign that you need to replace your roof ASAP, regardless of the time of year. But if you have the luxury of picking your own schedule, when is the best time to get a roof replacement?
The Best Time to Get a Roof Replacement in Florida


The best time to get a roof replacement in Florida will always be whenever your roof needs replacing. But if we’re talking about the calendar year, there are a lot of advantages to scheduling your roof replacement in the fall or winter.

This has a lot to do with the local weather patterns. In the summer, you can expect popup showers just about every day. This can slow down progress on your roof replacement as sections of your roof need to be tarped off to prevent water damage, so many homeowners prefer to schedule their roof replacements during the drier seasons.

There’s also the matter of hurricanes. Florida's hurricane season runs from June 1st to November 30th, so it’s generally a good idea not to schedule a roof replacement during these times. Nobody wants a hurricane to hit their roof when it’s partially torn off and covered in tarps. On the other hand, if you know that your roof needs replacing ASAP, it’s better to get a roof replacement now, even during hurricane season, than let a hurricane hit your roof while it’s old and weakened.

Finally, scheduling your roof replacement also means better conditions for your roofers. A roof gets hot fast, and your roofers will probably be working from sunup to sundown for at least one day, if not several. By picking the best time to replace your roof, you can improve working conditions for the people replacing your roof, which isn’t a requirement but is certainly a nice thing to do for your contractors.

### The 5 Best Shingle Roof Colors for Florida

Asphalt shingles are the most popular roofing material and for good reasons. They’re strong, durable, and they’re affordable for most homeowners. In addition to all of these benefits, though, shingles also offer a lot in the way of style options. With a wide range of shingle roof colors to choose from, there’s truly something for everyone.

But how do you know which shingle roof color is right for your home? And do shingle colors matter when it comes to the quality of your roof? We’re PITCH Roofing, and as experienced Florida roofers, we’re here to answer all of these questions and more. Keep reading for the most popular shingle roof colors in your neighborhood!
What to Consider When Choosing Shingle Roof Colors


As a homeowner, there are several factors that should impact which shingle roof colors you’re considering. Personal taste is certainly one of them, but you’ll probably want to consider more practical concerns as well. As you weigh the pros and cons of different shingle roof colors, let’s talk about some of the main concerns that you’ll want to take into account.
Match Your Roof to Your Siding
When looking at shingle roof colors, it’s important to pick one that complements the color of your siding. Not only will this create a more cohesive visual that’s more enjoyable for you as a homeowner, but it will also increase your home’s curb appeal. This means that when the time comes to sell, you can expect to get more value from your home.

If your home’s siding has multiple colors, you may want to choose shingles that also contain multiple colors. This is very common with architectural shingles, which are made using multiple layers of fiberglass and asphalt. This creates a dimensional, textured look that can easily contain several colors.

Go for UV-Reflection
You may have heard that your shingle roof color affects how well your roof stands up to the sun, and that’s true. Darker-colored shingles will attract more heat, which could mean higher energy bills for you in the summer. Additionally, UV rays can crack your shingles over time, so choosing the wrong shingle roof color could shorten the lifespan of your roof.

That’s why we generally encourage customers to choose light shingle roof colors. While it’s not a night and day difference, Florida is already hard on roofs. Why not give your roof a break and lessen the amount of UV rays it has to withstand? In Florida, colors like light greys and blues are both beautiful and help keep your roof protected from the sun.
Consider Your Neighborhood
If you want to march to the beat of your own drum, there’s nobody stopping you from getting any shingle roof color that you like. But there are real benefits to looking around your neighborhood and noting the colors of the newest roofs.

Why? Property values. A visually cohesive neighborhood can seem more appealing to buyers and allow homeowners to set higher selling prices. This is why many HOAs have a short list of acceptable shingle roof colors. Even without an organization mandating certain colors, though, you can beautify your neighborhood by choosing shingle colors that match those of your neighbors.

Even if you’re not concerned with property values, following your neighbors’ lead can be a good idea. Your neighbors have to deal with the same weather conditions that you do, so take a look at how their roofs are holding up. If you see a roof that’s been there for a while and doesn’t show signs of cracking or algae, it could be a good indication that that color is well-suited to your neighborhood’s climate.

### Asphalt Shingles vs. Composite Shingles

Shingles are the most popular roofing option in North America. But determining which type of shingles are right for you depends on your roof, budget, and tastes. To help you make a decision about your next roofing material, today the experts at PITCH Roofing are sharing all the differences between asphalt shingles vs. composite shingles.

While both these options are shingles, there’s a world of difference between them. These differences extend across material composition, durability, and cost. But don’t worry — we’re covering it all in this comprehensive asphalt and composite shingles guide!
Roofing Materials: Asphalt Shingles vs. Composite Shingles


Shingles come in many different forms, but their base components play a large role in how well these materials can protect your roof against the infamous Florida weather. As you weigh asphalt shingles vs. composite shingles, keep in mind their material composition and what it could mean for your roof!
Asphalt Shingles
Asphalt shingles have a long history in Florida, and even today they’re the most popular roofing material in the Sunshine State. While they used to be flat and one-dimensional, today’s asphalt shingles have undergone many improvements in both durability and aesthetics.

But how are they made? Well, composition starts with a baseboard, usually one made of fiberglass. This is then coated in hot asphalt to provide impact resistance and waterproofing. Finally, the asphalt shingle is coated in protective stone granules, which help with both style and UV resistance.

For old asphalt shingles, that’s where the process stopped. But for high-quality architectural shingles, this process is repeated to give multiple layers. Not only does this offer double the weather resistance, but it also creates a dimensional, textured look that many homeowners love. And while we’re talking about aesthetics, asphalt shingles come in a wide range of colors, so there’s no limit to how you can customize your home.
Composite Shingles
Composite shingles are a newer arrival on the roofing scene, having first become popular in the 1980s. Nowadays, these shingles are famous for their ability to seamlessly replicate the look of shake or wood shingles without incurring sky-high roofing costs.

Also called synthetic shingles, composite shingles are made from a wide range of materials. These include recycled plastics, fiberglass, and various proprietary polymers. From there, the shingle usually receives various paints and coatings to make it match the exact color of whatever it’s trying to emulate. And since their base materials are much more affordable than cedar or slate, these shingles can offer the same luxurious aesthetics at a fraction of the price.

They’re not just pretty, though. Composite shingles are hardy and more than able to stand up to Florida’s storm season. In fact, their great UV resistance and wind resistance make them able to stand up to two of Florida’s biggest year-round roof killers.
Durability of Asphalt Shingles vs. Composite Shingles in Florida
Every environment brings its own challenges to roofing, and Florida has three big weather features that you’ll want to protect against: UV rays, high winds, and heavy rains. To help you plan your next roof replacement, let’s compare how asphalt and composite shingles hold up to local weather patterns!
Asphalt Shingles
As one of Florida’s favorite roofing materials, asphalt shingles do a great job standing up to the local elements. Some of their durability features include:

 	Wind Resistance: Quality architectural asphalt shingles usually offer wind ratings around 110 mph, which makes them able to withstand most storms and even hurricanes.
 	Fire Rating: Asphalt shingles have a Class A fire rating, meaning that they’re extremely unlikely to catch fire.
 	Water Resistance: Thanks to their thick asphalt coating, these shingles are very resistant to water. Thin, 3-tab shingles offer less protection, but with multiple layers, architectural shingles are unlikely to get soaked through even in the worst storms.
 	UV Resistance: Most modern asphalt shingles have a protective UV coating to help reflect the sun’s rays away from your home. However, this coating will likely break down with time, so older shingle roofs could be more vulnerable to sun damage. This can lead to cracking and breakage.

When you put all this together, you have a good, hardy shingle. But while these shingles are reasonably strong, they can’t last forever. Most asphalt shingle roofs will need replacing after 20-25 years. This is an important consideration when weighing asphalt shingles vs. composite shingles!
Composite Shingles
Thanks to their unique composition, composite shingles offer unmatched protection against the Florida elements. To prove it, let’s talk about some of their biggest weather resistance features:

 	Wind Resistance: Composite shingles have been approved for winds up to 130 mph. For reference, that’s equivalent to a Category 4 hurricane! In terms of wind resistance, there’s no better shingle roofing option.
 	Fire Rating: Like asphalt shingles, composite shingles also hold a Class A fire rating and do a great job resisting combustion.
 	Water Resistance: Thanks to the plastic and fiberglass in their composition, composite shingles are extremely unlikely to be damaged by rain. When installed properly, your rows of composite shingles should keep your roof safe and dry!
 	UV Resistance: Thanks to their protective coatings, composite shingles are well-suited to resist UV rays. However, like with asphalt shingles, this coating can degrade over time. Unlike asphalt shingles, however, composite shingles are unlikely to crack due to the sun’s rays and may instead lose some of their color. This can be somewhat unsightly, but it doesn’t usually ruin the shingle.

Thanks to all of these protective features, composite shingles are among some of the most durable roofing materials in Florida. When properly installed and maintained, they can last as long as 50 years. When it comes to longevity, there’s a clear winner between asphalt shingles vs. composite!
How Much Do Asphalt Shingles vs. Composite Shingles Cost?


We know that price is a big concern when comparing asphalt shingles vs. composite. While we don’t think that price should be the only factor when deciding on your next roof replacement, some roofing materials just aren’t in everyone’s budget. To help you make your decision, let’s talk about the cost of asphalt shingles vs. composite in Florida!
Asphalt Shingles
In addition to their great aesthetics and solid durability, there’s another factor that makes asphalt shingles the most popular roofing material in North America: its low price. In fact, across all roofing materials, asphalt shingles are one of the most affordable options.

So how much do they cost? Architectural shingles cost between four and nine dollars per square foot. So if your roof is 2,000 square feet, you’ll pay between $8,000 and $18,000 for your new asphalt shingle roof!

Technically, asphalt shingles can be even cheaper, with 3-tab asphalt shingles costing as little as two dollars per square foot. But these shingles are much more fragile, and since they rarely last more than 10-15 years in Florida, we don’t generally recommend them to homeowners.
Composite Shingles
Composite shingles are much more affordable than real cedar shake or slate roofing. But while they’re more affordable, there’s no denying that they cost substantially more than asphalt shingles.

In Florida, you can expect to pay between seven and fourteen dollars for composite shingles. Or, on a 2,000-square-foot roof, between $14,000 and $28,000 for a composite shingle roof replacement.

For homeowners who can afford it, composite roofing is a beautiful, durable roofing option. But sometimes it simply isn’t in the budget. That’s why knowing average shingle roofing costs is so important to deciding between asphalt shingles vs. composite!

### How to Prevent Storm Damage to Your Roof

Hurricane season is here, and while we haven’t had any major storms yet in 2024, meteorologists predict an active hurricane season for Florida. This news leaves many local homeowners wondering how they can prevent roof storm damage this summer. As your local roofing partners, PITCH Roofing has all of the expert tips and insights you need to keep your home safe!

When it comes to protecting your roof from hurricane damage, there’s a lot that’s under your control. Today, we’re reviewing what you can do to give your roof the best possible chance at standing strong against a hurricane. Keep reading for real advice from our roofing experts!
How to Prevent Roof Storm Damage in Florida


From the choices you make about your roofing material to regular maintenance, it all affects how your roof stands up to storms. But today, rather than focusing on which roofs are best for hurricanes, we’re talking about what you can do to protect your existing roof from storm damage.

With that in mind, let’s talk about the ways that you can prevent storm roof damage!
1. Get a Professional Roof Inspection
Homeowners often think that if their roof isn’t leaking or showing other issues, then there’s no problem. But the truth is that roofs are complex. As a result, you could have damage in one part of your roofing system that doesn’t cause any immediate, visible problems. When you’re trying to prevent storm roof damage, though, these issues can create serious weak points.

The best way to find these hidden roofing problems is through a professional roof inspection. By checking your roof’s ventilation and penetrations, a roof inspector can identify any problem areas and present you with solutions that will keep your roof strong. Nobody can control where storms go, but by keeping your roof as healthy as possible, you can greatly reduce your risk of roof damage during a storm.

Be sure not to wait until you hear about a hurricane coming your way to schedule an inspection. Repairs can take time to implement, and you don’t want to be waiting for work to be completed when the storm hits!
2. Clean Your Gutters
Clogged gutters aren’t just an eyesore — they’re hazardous to your roof. When properly installed, gutters become an integral part of your roofing system. Specifically, they direct water off of your roof and away from your home’s foundations. But when they’re clogged, gutters fail to function properly and can actually lead to water pooling on your roof.

That’s why keeping your gutters clean and free of debris is one of the best ways to prevent storm roof damage. And while you should be cleaning your gutters regularly, there isn’t really a “too late” with this option. This means that as long as the storm hasn’t hit yet, you can clean your gutters to help deal with the incoming rain and keep your roof healthy and functional.
3. Trim Your Trees and Clean Your Lawn to Prevent Storm Roof Damage


It may sound counterintuitive, but protecting your roof really does start from the ground up. During a storm, anything you leave on the ground can become a projectile. This includes trash cans, children's’ toys, furniture, etc. In Florida, wind speeds can exceed 140 mph during the worst storms, so it’s smart to clear your yard of all debris so there’s nothing nearby to get thrown at your home.

After cleaning your lawn, it’s time to make sure your trees aren’t endangering your roof. During a storm, anything touching or hanging over your roof is a danger. As winds increase, branches can either whip against your roof or be removed and become storm debris. In either case, one of the best ways to prevent storm roof damage is trimming your branches and making sure nothing is touching your roof and there are no dead or decaying branches looming over your home.
4. Invest in Hurricane Straps
In Florida, the best way to prevent major storm roof damage is to secure your wall-to-roof connections. Many people do this using hurricane straps, which reinforce your roof and make sure it stays put even during the worst storms.

Hurricane straps don’t just protect your roof, either. They’re also good for your budget. Installing hurricane straps leads to lower homeowners insurance premiums, making them an excellent way to prevent storm roof damage and help out your finances. The best part? In Florida, you can get these at a huge discount.

That’s thanks to the My Safe Florida Home program. This public fund allows you to install roof upgrades, like hurricane straps, and be reimbursed for two thirds of the cost. If you’re interested in preventing storm roof damage with hurricane straps, choose experienced contractors who know how to help you navigate this program!
5. Buy Tarps to Prepare for the Worst
Using the above strategies, you can minimize your risk of storm roof damage. But if Mother Nature decides to hit your roof hard during a storm, some damage might be inevitable. After a storm can be a difficult time to find tarps, so it helps to have some ready and on-hand.

Once the storm has passed and you can safely access your roof, it’s a good idea to give it a brief look over to make sure there’s no damage. If there is damage, you’ll want to tarp it up immediately. Missing a few shingles isn’t a big deal, but leaving a roofing vulnerability like this exposed can worsen the damage.

By tarping your roof after a storm, you can stop the damage from spreading or getting worse. In this way, one of the best ways to prevent storm roof damage actually happens after the storm has passed!

### How to Prepare for a Roof Replacement in Florida

Sooner or later, every roof needs replacing. But many homeowners find themselves in the position of not knowing what to do when it’s their turn. We’re PITCH Roofing, and today we’re clearing up the confusion and explaining how to prepare for a roof replacement.

This includes preparing both yourself and your roof! You probably already know that your home needs to be ready for the roofers. But many homeowners may not be aware of issues that arise during roofing that you’ll want to plan for ahead of time to make sure you’re comfortable and uninterrupted during your roof replacement.

With these different areas of concern in mind, let’s talk about how you can prepare for a roof replacement in Florida!
1. Get Your Home Ready for a Roof Replacement
There are several steps in preparing your home for a roof replacement. Some of them make things easier for roofers and some of them protect your property, but all of them are important.

First, make sure your driveway is clear of vehicles and obstacles before the day of your roof replacement. Your roofers will need that space both for their trucks and for the dumpster that will hold your old roofing system. If your vehicle is still there when they show up, it could slow down the entire roof replacement process.

To prepare for a roof replacement, you should also take anything fragile off of the shelves. If you’re getting shingles nailed onto your roof, that force can travel throughout your home. Oftentimes this force isn't enough to knock anything down, but there are always exceptions, and it’s better to be safe than sorry.

The final way to get your home ready is to make sure your attic is prepared for the roof replacement. If you’re storing anything in your attic, it may be a good idea to cover it with a tarp or plastic shielding. Replacing a roof can lead to a lot of loose sawdust and wood splinters in your attic, so covering your possessions is a good way to make sure they’re not damaged during your roof replacement.
2. Prepare for a Roof Replacement by Planning Your Time


Sometimes, a roof replacement is a simple, quick job that only takes a day’s work to complete. Other times, though, the process takes longer. In general, it’s safe to assume that your roof replacement will take between 2-4 days, assuming that the weather cooperates and doesn’t pause the installation.

When you prepare for a roof replacement, you need to think about where you’ll be during this time. Do you want to stay home while they replace your roof? Many homeowners do, and there’s no rule saying you have to leave your home. However, it’s important to know what to expect.

Roof replacements are loud. They’re not deafening, but they’re not quiet, either. So if you work remotely and have a lot of meetings, it may be a good idea to move somewhere else until the work is finished. You should also consider your pets. Many animals find ongoing loud noises upsetting, so it could be a good idea to find somewhere for your pet to stay even if you plan to stay at home.
3. Give Your Immediate Neighbors a Heads Up
Remember how we said that roof replacements are loud? Well, it’s safe to say that you won’t be the only one aware of your roof replacement. In all likelihood, your neighbors are also going to notice the extra noise. They also might not enjoy how early the noise starts — most crews get started very shortly after sunrise, especially during the Florida summer when crews are eager to work before your roof gets extremely hot.

There is no law saying that you have to warn your neighbors about your roof replacement. But to keep a good relationship with your neighbors, how you prepare for a roof replacement should include giving them a warning.
4. Get Ready by Taking Photos of Your Property


As one of the final steps in preparing for a roof replacement, it’s helpful to walk around your home and inspect it for damages. Watch out for things like the state of your gutters, window screens, and your soffits and fascia. Whether or not you see any signs of damage, take photos of the vulnerable parts of your roofing system and your home in general.

If you’ve chosen reliable roofing contractors, you probably won’t run into any issues with the crew damaging your property. But accidents happen, and you'll want to be ready for them. When you inspect your home after your roof replacement, let your contractors know if you find any damage that wasn’t there beforehand. If they’re really committed to customer satisfaction, then they should have no problem fixing the issue.

You should note, however, that your roofers may not be legally obligated to help. Some roofers include clauses in their contracts stating that they’re not responsible for any damages during the roof replacement process. For this reason, you can also think of carefully reviewing your agreement before signing as an important step in preparing for a roof replacement!
5. Prepare for a Roof Replacement by Picking the Right Roofers
The most important way you should prepare for a roof replacement happens long before any work is agreed upon. There is a wide range in quality when it comes to roofing contractors, so the best way to protect your home during a roof replacement is to make sure that qualified professionals are handling the job.

### Re-Roofing vs. Roof Replacement: Guide for Florida Homeowners

When buying a new roof, affordability is a big concern. One way that homeowners can save money is by choosing to re-roof instead of getting a roof replacement. But what does that entail, exactly? And what are the drawbacks? We’re PITCH Roofing, and today we’re going to help you choose between re-roofing and roof replacement.

Whether you’re not 100% sure what re-roofing is or you just want to know how to choose between re-roofing vs. roof replacement, we’ve got you covered. As experienced Florida roofers, we’ve seen it all and know both the installation costs and the long-term value of these roofing systems. Keep reading for our complete breakdown of re-roofing and roof replacements in Florida!
Re-Roofing vs. Roof Replacement: The Basics


A roof replacement is pretty simple. Someone tears off your old roof, replaces any damaged decking, then installs a new one. This is the most common thing to do when your roof reaches the end of its life, but it’s not your only option.

Instead, you could choose re-roofing, also called a roof overlay. With this method, roofers don't tear off your old roof. Instead, they install your new roof over top of the old one. This is most commonly done by installing shingles or metal over an old shingle roof, although other combinations are sometimes possible depending on the state of your roof.

Re-roofing is substantially cheaper than a roof replacement because you don’t pay for the labor to tear off and dispose of your old roof. But in roofing, there’s a lot more to these big decisions than just the price tag. So let’s talk about what you need to know to choose between re-roofing and roof replacement.
When to Choose Re-Roofing vs. Roof Replacement
There is no “best” option between re-roofing and roof replacement. Instead, both roofing services work best in different scenarios. So how are you supposed to know which one you need? Let's talk about the different situations in which you need re-roofing and which ones call for a roof replacement.
When to Pick Roof Replacement
The right thing to choose depends, in part, on the state of your old roof. For example, if your roof is leaking or showing other signs of water damage, this could indicate that your roof decking has been damaged. Adding another layer on top of that may not be structurally sound, so your best bet is probably to tear off the old roof and install a new one.

Roof replacements are also more widely available since they aren’t limited to any specific roofing materials. This means that no matter what your old roofing material is or what new roofing material you want, roof replacement is always an option, and many Florida homeowners appreciate that flexibility when deciding between re-roofing and roof replacement.

There are also cost considerations to make. A roof replacement usually costs more than re-roofing, but some exceptions could make your situation different. In some cases, your homeowners insurance may pay for all or part of a roof replacement, especially if it was damaged during a storm. Ultimately, whether re-roofing or roof replacement costs more will depend on your unique situation.
When to Pick Re-Roofing
In just as many situations, re-roofing could be a better option for your home. If you need a new roof because yours is getting older but hasn’t shown signs of weakening, then it could be safe to add another layer on top. If there’s no existing damage, the new layer should protect the older layer beneath it from further wear and tear.

Because all roofs have a weight limit, your material options are more limited with re-roofing than roof replacement. The most common re-roofing choice is to install new shingles over your old shingle roof. However, you can also install a lightweight metal roofing system over your old shingles. Generally speaking, though, heavier materials like tiles or slate are out of the question.

Of course, one of the biggest factors when choosing between re-roofing and roof replacement is cost. Floridians pick re-roofing when they need a new roof on a budget. As mentioned, getting a roof overlay is a great way to save on roof replacement costs. However, it may be better to think of it as just delaying those costs.

That’s because you won’t be able to install a third layer on your roof, so your next new roof will require a replacement. When that happens, you’ll have to pay to have both of your roofs removed and disposed of. Re-roofing could still be a good idea, especially if you plan to sell before the next roof replacement or to be in a better financial position, but it’s important to take this into account when figuring out total re-roofing costs.
Get Your Free Estimates for Re-Roofing and Roof Replacement
Both re-roofing and roof replacement are the right choice in different situations. In addition to using the information above, getting a free estimate is a great way to help you decide on what to do about your new roof. FAQs About Re-Roofing and Roof Replacement


We’ve covered when to pick re-roofing vs. roof replacement, but we understand that you may still have questions. As your local roofing partners in your corner, we want to do everything we can to help you make an informed decision. That’s why we’re answering the most common questions that we see about re-roofing and roof replacement!

1. Q: How much does re-roofing cost compared to a roof replacement in Florida?

A: Re-roofing is significantly cheaper than roof replacement because of the lower labor costs. However, there’s no way to say exactly how much it will cost. Your total roofing costs will depend on your new and old roofing materials, the size of your roof, its condition, and many other factors. For this reason, we strongly recommend getting an estimate if you’re interested in re-roofing!

2. Q: Are all roofs eligible for re-roofing?

A: No, sometimes a roof is not suitable for re-roofing and needs replaced instead. This includes roofs that have already undergone a roof overlay and heavily damaged roofs. Additionally, re-roofing is limited to lightweight roofing materials like shingles and some types of metal.

3. Q: Do roof overlays still have warranties?

A: In most cases, shingle warranties are only valid for total roof replacements. There may be exceptions, but generally speaking, choosing a roof overlay means foregoing any warranties on your roofing shingles.

4. Q: Does re-roofing help with energy efficiency?

A: Yes, by adding a new layer of materials to your roof, re-roofing can add insulation and improve energy efficiency. However, getting a roof replacement is also an opportunity to upgrade your roof and add more insulation, so this isn’t technically a leg up on roof replacements.

5. Q: How do I know if my roof needs replacing instead of re-roofing?

A: Signs that you need a roof replacement include multiple leaks, algae or mold in your attic from water damage, roof sagging, and large sections of missing shingles.

### Stone-Coated Steel Roofing Costs and Durability in Florida

If you’ve noticed an uptick in the number of metal roofs across Florida, it’s not just you. More and more, homeowners are choosing steel roofing to both lower homeowners insurance premiums and provide the best possible protection against hurricanes. But for some homeowners, the look of a metal roof simply isn’t their taste. Thankfully, stone-coated steel roofing is an excellent compromise between protection and aesthetics.

We’re PITCH Roofing, and we’re here to answer all of your questions about this metal roofing option. From how it performs in Florida to how much a stone-coated steel roof replacement costs, we’re covering it all. Stick with us as we get started by talking about the appeal of stone-coated steel roofing!
Is Stone-Coated Steel Roofing a Good Idea in Florida?


Metal roofing can be tricky depending on where you live in Florida. For example, coastal homes need metal roofs made from aluminum to prevent rust. So do stone-coated steel roofs have what it takes to handle the Florida elements?

The answer is a resounding yes.

Manufacturers create stone-coated steel roofing by taking metal sheets (usually Galvalume steel or a metal of similar quality) and covering them in protective stone granules. The result is a roofing system that carries all of the benefits of a metal roof without its drawbacks or distinct aesthetic. As a result, many homeowners who want a lower-profile look or a more traditional aesthetic choose stone-coated metal roofing.

It’s not just about aesthetics, though. These metal roofing systems perform well, too. Depending on your brand and metal roof installers, your stone-coated steel roof will be able to withstand winds of 120-170 mph. This means that you can count on your roof staying in place even through major hurricanes!

Even with everything the Sunshine State throws at your stone-coated roof, you can count on it lasting between 40 and 70 years. For reference, a great shingle roof won’t make it more than 25 years in Florida, and often it’ll be closer to 15-20 years. This makes stone-coated steel roofing a great investment in your home’s long-term safety.

That said, all of these great things are also true about regular metal roofs. So what makes stone-coated steel roofing stand out?
What Makes Stone-Coated Steel Roofing Different
We’ve already covered that stone-coated steel roofs have a timeless aesthetic. But looks aren’t the only leg up they have on other types of metal roofing. By adding protective stone granules on top of steel, these roofs mitigate some of the biggest drawbacks of metal roofing.

Some of the improvements that stone-coated steel roofing offers include:

 	Impact Resistance: One common downside to metal roofs is their tendency to dent. In Florida, storm debris and the occasional hailstorm can leave quite a mark on a metal roof. But the stone granules go a long way in minimizing this damage and keeping your roof looking its best!
 	Noise Reduction: In general, people overblow how much noise a metal roof makes. But it is true that, depending on the materials, a metal roof can make more noise during a rainstorm. With stone-coated steel roofing, though, there’s no sound of water hitting bare metal, so you don’t get that extra noise during storms.
 	UV Resistance: Over the years, UV rays can do a real number on your roof. Metal roofs are generally good at reflecting away some of the UV rays that hit your roof, but stone-coated metal is even better. That’s because the stone granules are usually coated in a UV-protective glaze, which prevents your roof from being bleached or weakened by the sun.

All of the above factors are ways that these roofs stand out. And normally, we would tell you about the cons of this roofing material next. But to be honest, these roofing systems don’t have a lot of drawbacks. In fact, the only factor that makes homeowners hesitate to choose stone-coated steel roofing is the price. So how much should you expect to pay for a stone-coated steel roof replacement?
How Much Does a Stone-Coated Steel Roof Replacement Cost?


When dealing with metal roofing, you know going in that it’s not going to be cheap. And this is very much the case with stone-coated steel roofing. But, at least when compared to other types of metal roofing, the costs of stone-coated steel roofing aren’t too scary.

In Florida, you can expect to pay between seven and 15 dollars per square foot for your stone-coated steel roof replacement. In other words, your average roofing costs will be between $14,000 and $30,000, and most Floridians pay somewhere around $20,000 for a new stone-coated steel roof.

These ranges are nice, but they don’t tell you how much you, specifically, will pay for your new metal roof. The only way to get that information is through a roofing estimate from experienced contractors!

### Deciding on a Roof Repair vs. Replacement

Having roofing troubles is stressful enough. But the situation gets even worse when you aren’t sure if your home needs a roof repair or roof replacement. With such different price tags, many homeowners are eager to get clarity on whether their roof is going to need a complete replacement or if it can get by with some quick repairs.

We’re here to help you figure it out. PITCH Roofing is your local roofing partner with decades of experience with both roof repairs and roof replacements. Thanks to this local expertise, we know how to tell if your home needs a roof repair or replacement. Keep reading for our simple ways to tell if you need a roof repair or replacement!
How to Decide Between Roof Repair vs. Roof Replacement


A roof is a surprisingly complicated thing. Many people think that the only important thing is what roofing material you choose, but a secure roof has multiple layers of protection, and it’s important to consider each of these as you try to decide between a roof repair vs. roof replacement.

Now, let’s look at how you can tell what your roof needs!
1. Inspect Your Attic for Roof Leaks
Leaks are the most common problem that homeowners notice with their roofs. But just having a leak isn’t a good indicator of whether you need a roof repair or roof replacement. If you’ve recently noticed a leak in your home, chances are that this isn’t the start of the water damage. But your attic could give you important clues as to what your roof needs.

Attics are an important part of your roof and help a lot with ventilation. But they’re also vulnerable to damage. For example, if a storm takes a few shingles with it, your attic will be the first place that you start to see signs of wear and tear.

So if you have a leak, it’s a good idea to see how your attic is holding up. Look for signs of water damage in your attic’s ceiling, such as dark spots or, even worse, mold. If you see substantial signs of water damage across a large section of your attic, this could mean that your roof decking has been soaked through. And in order to replace it, you may need a full or partial roof replacement.

On the other hand, if you don’t see signs of major water damage, it could mean that the damage hasn’t spread. If you call in professionals ASAP, you have a great chance of only needing a roof repair and saving yourself a lot of money.
2. Look at the Extent of the Damage
If you’re not sure whether you need a roof repair or roof replacement, it can help to hop on your roof and take a look around. Missing shingles are another common problem in Florida, so that can be our example.

A handful of missing shingles can be easily replaced without replacing your entire roof. However, if you’re missing an entire section of your roof, you may need more intensive help. A good rule of thumb is 25% — if you’re missing more than that, there’s a good chance that you need a roof replacement.

This isn’t a hard and fast rule, though. The time that your roof has been damaged matters too. That’s why it’s a good idea to call in roofers as soon as you see a problem so that they can act quickly before damage spreads and your roof repair becomes a roof replacement.
3. Consider the Age of Your Roof


Age isn’t just a number — at least not in roofing. In fact, age is one of the biggest considerations roofers make when deciding if you need a roof repair or roof replacement. That’s because a problem on an older roof could warrant a replacement, but that same problem on a newer roof could be handled with a repair. But why would roofers go from a roof replacement to a roof repair just based on age?

Think about it like this: A shingle roof can last for 20-25 years in Florida. So if your roof is only five years old when it gets its first leak, there’s still a lot of life left in that roof — the shingles are still strong, as are your wood decking and underlayment, so there’s no need to replace the entire thing.

That same leak looks very different on an old roof, though. If your roof is 22 years old when it gets a leak, many roofers will suggest replacing it. Not because they can’t just fix the leak; they probably could. But because your roof is only going to continue to present new issues like this as it approaches the end of its life, it often makes the most sense to get ahead of the problem and replace the whole thing so you’re not paying for multiple roof repairs just to replace your roof in a handful of years.
4. Think About Your Plans for the Future
Something that many homeowners don’t realize is that the choice to repair or replace your roof is yours. Granted, there may be times when a roof is truly ruined and no amount of repairs can fix it. But in general, whether you repair or replace your roof comes down to what makes the most sense for you.

For example, let’s say you plan to sell your home in the next few years. You may decide that it doesn’t make sense to invest that much in a home you’re leaving, so you just get a repair to fix the immediate issue. On the other hand, you could also decide to replace your roof to get the highest price when selling your home.

Ultimately, the decision to get a roof repair or roof replacement is yours. As roofers, our job is just to give you the best information, make our recommendations, and then help you get the roofing services that you need.

### How Dimensional Shingles Changed Roofing in Florida

If you walk through a residential neighborhood in Florida, most of the homes will probably have dimensional shingle roofs. That's because dimensional shingles completely revolutionized roofing in Florida. While Floridians were using asphalt shingles as early as 1935, dimensional shingles hit the market in the 1970s and changed local roofing as we know it.

But do dimensional shingles still hold up? We’re PITCH Roofing, and we’re here to help you decide if dimensional roofing shingles are right for your home. To do that, let’s talk about the core facts you need to know about these asphalt shingles and how they can protect your home.
What Are Dimensional Shingles?


You may already be familiar with how 3-tab shingles are made, and dimensional shingles aren’t that much different. Like with 3-tab shingles, you take a baseboard of fiberglass, drench it in asphalt, and then coat it with protective granules. But that’s where the similarities end.

Dimensional shingles (or architectural shingles) are made up of two layers of asphalt and fiberglass. This means they’re twice as thick, twice as heavy, and twice as durable as 3-tab shingles. In Florida, where hurricanes are just a fact of life, having shingles that stay adhered to your roof in a storm is invaluable. And since dimensional shingles have wind resistances of up to 110 mph, they’re ideal for protecting your home from passing storms on a budget.

The difference between dimensional and 3-tab shingles isn’t just functional, either. Thanks to their two-ply design and specialized manufacturing process, these shingles create visual dimension on your roof, hence their name. This contrasts with 3-tab shingles, which look flat and don’t add much visual interest to a home. As a result of this difference, dimensional shingles don’t just protect your home; they also create visual interest.

That’s the bare-bones summary of why Floridians love dimensional asphalt shingles. Now, let’s talk about some of their more specific appeals and why they could be the perfect fit for your home.
How Long Do Dimensional Shingles Last in Florida?
Longevity is a big concern with roofing anywhere, but especially in Florida. Between hurricanes, humidity, and sun exposure, your roof faces many challenges every day. But dimensional shingles can stand up to all of this for a long time.

Architectural shingles usually come with protective coatings to improve their resistance to wind and UV rays. This sets them up for long-term success, which is why dimensional shingles last for 20-25 years in Florida. For comparison, a 3-tab shingles roof would be lucky to make it 15 years in Florida and would definitely not be able to withstand a hurricane.

This is part of why Floridians have flocked to dimensional shingles; they’re just more reliable. But this isn’t the only reason that Floridians choose these asphalt roofing shingles. They also choose dimensional shingles for the price.
Cost of Dimensional Shingles


In addition to offering dependable protection, dimensional shingles also come at a great price point. In fact, they’re the most affordable roofing material on the market. But what does “affordable” mean when it comes to a roof replacement?

It’s important to keep in mind that roofing prices are not fixed; they change depending on the specifics of your roof and your local market. That said, dimensional shingles tend to cost between four and seven dollars per square foot. Thinking about it by the foot isn’t always helpful, though. So in other words, if your home is near the average size of 1,7000 square feet, you can expect to pay between $8,000 and $14,000 for your dimensional shingle roof replacement.

These low roofing costs make dimensional shingles especially appealing to many Florida homeowners. With high homeowners insurance rates and costs of living, many Floridians need to save money wherever they can. Dimensional shingles provide an opportunity to do that without sacrificing your home’s safety or looks.

### A Florida Homeowner's Guide to Roof Maintenance

Roof maintenance is important no matter where you are, but nowhere is it more important than in Florida. Hurricane season is especially roofs on worn, unprotected roofs. That’s why keeping up with roof maintenance is so essential for Florida homeowners.

Many people aren’t sure what’s included in maintaining a roof in Florida, though. That’s what we’re here for. As your local roofing partner, PITCH Roofing wants to help you get your roof hurricane-ready. That’s why we’re sharing our tips for easy things you can do to keep your roof strong. Keep reading for a full guide on roof maintenance in Florida!
5 Roof Maintenance Tips for Floridians


Every year, Floridian homeowners spend a lot of money on costly roof repairs. But in many cases, these repairs could have been avoided altogether if homeowners had kept up with their roof maintenance. To keep your roofing costs down, let’s talk about the easy things you can do to keep your roof in top shape!
1. Make Sure Nothing Is Touching Your Roof
A good rule of thumb is that if your contractor didn’t put it on your roof, it probably shouldn’t be there. In Florida, this includes things like palm fronds that can touch your roof, branches from any overhanging trees, and storm debris. Having any of these things on your roof could make it drastically more vulnerable to damage during a storm.

For one thing, these issues create a space for mold and pests on your roof. As these issues develop, they can weaken the overall structure of your roof and leave it vulnerable the next time there’s a storm.

That’s why we recommend keeping your roof clear of any and all debris and plant life as part of your regular roof maintenance. A good way to keep up with this is to give your roof a quick look over after major storms. Branches can make their way onto your roof even without overhanging trees, and this will allow you to stay ahead of any problems before they can do serious damage.
2. Verify the Health of Your Shingles
Most Floridians have shingle roofs. If you’re one of them, then it’s a good idea to check in on your shingles and make sure they’re not developing any issues. Because in Florida, there are a lot of problems that your shingles could develop.

For one thing, individual shingles can be blown off by high winds in a storm. But even on a peaceful day, your shingles could be drying out and getting baked by the sun. When conducting this bit of roof maintenance, you want to look for any missing or curling shingles. Once you’ve identified any issues, reach out to licensed professionals for shingle repair services.
3. Inspect Your Attic
Taking a look around your attic is an often-overlooked part of roof maintenance in Florida. But the truth is that your attic is the first spot in your home that may show signs of roofing damage. For example, oftentimes a leak will appear in your attic before you see water stains in your ceiling.

You should inspect your attic for leaks, discoloration, mold, and pests, all of which could be signs that there’s something wrong with your roof. If you notice any of these issues, it’s important to act quickly and call in your trusted roofing contractors. Problems that are visible in your attic have already spread to some extent, and moving quickly will help keep your repair costs as low as possible.
4. Clear Gutters and Inspect Soffits and Fascia
Many homeowners overlook their gutters, soffits, and fascia. But while they’re easy to overlook, caring for these parts of your roof is essential roof maintenance. You probably already know to clear leaves and other debris from your gutters, but there are other important roof maintenance steps that you should be taking as well.

You should also inspect your soffits and fascia for chipped paint or signs of rotting. These could mean that bugs are infiltrating your roofing system, and even little creatures can do a lot of damage to the interior of a roof. Your soffits and fascia also protect your roof from water damage, but they’ll be less effective at this if they’re growing weaker over time.

If you notice any issues with your gutters, soffits, or fascia, it may be worth calling in professional roofers if you’re unsure of how to resolve the issue. We especially recommend this if your gutters need replacing since any issues with your downspouts could lead to structural damage over time.
5. Check Your Roof for Perforations
You’d be surprised how many roofing features are structural weak points. Chimneys, skylights, and vents all serve a purpose on your roof, but they’re also an opportunity for openings in your roof. Since your roof is only as secure as its most vulnerable section, we strongly recommend inspecting your roof features as part of regular roof maintenance.

Things to look for include cracks in sealant, missing sections of mortar, and any odd holes that you see along the edges of your roofing feature. All of these could indicate that there’s a vulnerability in your roof, and if there is, you’ll want to get professional roof repair services before a storm comes by and worsens this weakness in your home.

### How Much Do Roof Repairs Cost in Florida? Roof Repair FAQs

Roof repair costs vary depending on where you are, what’s wrong with your roof, and who you hire to fix it. In general, roof repairs in Florida cost between $150 for handyman roofers and upwards of $5,000 for work requiring experienced contractors. So how do you know if your roof repair costs are going to be closer to the higher or lower end of that range?

You check with the experts. PITCH Roofing is your local roofing partner, ready to help with any and all local roof repairs. Today, we’re guiding you through average roof repair costs in Florida and what you can expect to pay when you hire professionals to fix your roof. To get started, let’s dive in and discuss how much you might pay for a roof repair!
Minor vs. Major Roof Repair Costs in Florida


Having a roof that needs repairing can mean a lot of things. You could be dealing with wear and tear or hurricane damage. Your roof may have interior or exterior problems. The damage could be brand new or have been going on for a while. And all of these factors will impact your total roof repair costs.

In roofing, we tend to think of repairs as either “major” or “minor.” These aren’t hard, objective categories, but they can be useful in thinking about how much time and money it will take to fix the issue. To help you plan for your own roof repair, let’s talk about what makes a major or minor roof repair.
Minor Roof Repairs
Minor roof repair jobs are usually pretty quick and painless. Repairs like these cost under $1,500 to fix and can be completed within a day of work. Some common examples of these minor repairs that we see in Florida include:

 	A small number of missing or damaged shingles
 	Cracked roofing tiles
 	Water pooling on your flat roof
 	New, minor leaks
 	Ventilation problems
 	Minor damage to your gutters

Any of these issues should be simple enough to resolve. But that doesn’t mean you should be completely relaxed. A minor repair will, with time, become a major problem. Think of a leak: A new leak is a minor nuisance, but a long-standing leak could mean serious water damage to your entire roofing system. That’s why it pays to move quickly before your roofing problems get out of hand and your roof repair costs increase significantly.
Major Roof Repairs
Major roof repairs include anything that you need a roofing contractor for instead of a handyman. These major roof repairs usually cost between $1,500 and $5,000, but they can exceed this number. In fact, some roofing damage can be so severe that it requires a full roof replacement.

When trying to determine if you’ll have high roof repair costs, watch out for any of these roofing issues:

 	Major water damage to your roof decking, especially if your attic is damaged
 	Missing a large section of shingles from your roof
 	Roof sagging
 	Heavily damaged flashing
 	Damaged roof trusses

While all of these roofing problems are less than ideal, they aren’t the worst-case scenario. The worst-case scenario is having to replace all or part of your roof. And that can very easily happen if you don’t get timely roofing services. For this reason, the best time to call roof repair contractors is as soon as you know there’s a problem.
