### Steel Roof Cost Guide for Florida Homeowners

How much does a steel roof cost? This is one of the most common questions we get from Florida homeowners. With hurricane seasons getting worse and homeowners insurance rates on the rise, a lot of people are looking to steel roofing as a way to protect their homes and save money. But with so many different factors affecting the price of steel roofing in Florida, it can be hard to get a clear answer.

That’s what we’re here for. As your local roofing partner, PITCH Roofing has all the information you need about the cost of steel roof replacements. Keep reading for a total cost breakdown of the average steel roofing costs in Florida and what you can expect when planning your roof replacement.
Steel Roof Costs: Material Considerations


When creating roofing materials, manufacturers almost never create roofing panels that are just steel. More often, they add other metals and protective coatings to their panels in order to offer better resistance to rust, UV, rain, etc. And which type of steel you get will have a big impact on how much your steel roof costs.

To give you an idea of what you can expect your steel roof replacement to cost, let’s look at the most common types of roofing steel.
Galvanized Steel Roofing
You’ve probably heard of galvanized steel, and if you know a lot about it, you are most likely not surprised to hear that it makes a great roofing material. Steel, by itself, is already great at standing up to impact damage and high winds, two serious dangers in Florida storms. But the galvanization process takes this protection to the next level.

When steel is galvanized, that means it’s coated in protective zinc. And zinc is one of the best metals in the world for corrosion resistance. This isn’t because it completely resists rust — aluminum is technically better in that area. What makes zinc special is that it has “self-healing” properties. This means that when parts of zinc do start to rust, it sheds them and protects the rest of the metal. That’s why galvanized steel is so much more resistant to rust than regular steel.

Naturally, it costs more to coat steel in zinc. But even with this additional protection, galvanized steel is still an affordable metal roofing material. Galvanized steel roofing panels cost two to four dollars per square foot to manufacture, which helps keep steel roof costs low.
Galvalume Steel Roofing
Galvalume was invented in 1972 by Bethlehem Steel, and it offers slightly different protection from galvanized steel. As the similar names imply, both of these steel roofing options have a zinc coating. But with Galvalume steel, the protective coating isn’t just zinc. Instead, it’s an alloy of 45% zinc and 55% aluminum.

This difference in the protective coating comes with several differences. For one thing, Galvalume steel is more resistant to rust because of the aluminum, so you can expect even better corrosion resistance. As a bonus, the smaller crystal structures are closer together than in galvanized steel, which creates a sleeker, smoother appearance.

There is a trade-off, though. Zinc is better at handling scratches and cuts than aluminum. As a result, galvanized steel is better able to take minor scrapes without showing any signs of damage. Still, many homeowners think this trade-off is worth it for the increased rust protection.

Because of the addition of aluminum and a more complicated coating process, Galvalume steel tends to cost more than galvanized steel. When calculating Galvalume steel roof costs, you can expect to pay anywhere from five to fifteen dollars per square foot for Galvalume steel.
Steel Roof Costs: Installation Considerations


Material costs are one thing, but steel roofing is complicated. Knowing the type of steel used isn’t enough to predict steel roof costs. To get a full picture, you also have to look at how the panels are fastened to your roof.

It may seem trivial, but the type of fastener will largely determine how much your steel roof costs. So to help you plan, let’s look at the costs of both hidden and exposed fastener steel roofs.
Exposed Fasteners
A steel roof with exposed fasteners is easy to manufacture and install. That’s because roofers adhere it to your roof by drilling it down into your decking. It’s simple, direct, and doesn’t take a lot of time or special manufacturing considerations. But these corrugated steel sheets may have a slightly negative impact on your roof’s longevity.

Don’t get us wrong — steel roofs with exposed fasteners last a long time, up to 45 years or longer. But because the fasteners sit on top of your roof, they’re exposed to the elements. This can lead them to weaken over time and need repairs, which are an extra roofing expense.

On the other hand, low installation costs help offset some of the downsides of exposed fasteners. Corrugated steel roofing costs five to 12 dollars per square foot. For the average roof size of 1,700 square feet, that puts total metal roofing costs between $8,500 and $20,400. This makes it a very popular option for homeowners who want to keep steel roof costs low!
Hidden Fasteners
Steel roofs with hidden fasteners are called standing seam. And the way that these roofs protect your fasteners is genius. The steel panels are mostly flat, but they have a ridge where they raise up. Beneath this ridge is the interlocking mechanism that allows your panels to slot together into a single roof. Since the adhesion is under a layer of steel, it’s much better protected against the elements.

That extra protection makes a lot of difference in roof performance. Standing seam steel roofs are the gold standard, and they’ve been known to last up to 70 years. That’s why they’re so popular with homeowners who want a roof they can put on and forget about.

While the protection is great, though, you definitely pay for it. A standing seam steel roof costs between nine and 21 dollars per square foot. Using the same 1,700 square feet as an average roof size, you’re looking at steel roof replacement costs between $15,300 and $35,700. This means that a standing seam roof isn’t affordable for everyone, but if it’s within your budget, it’s definitely a steel roofing option worth considering!

### Types of Roof Shingles Near Me: Expert Recommendations

Shingle roof replacements are one of the most common roofing jobs in the state of Florida. But there’s still a lot of variety to them. For one thing, there are many different types of roof shingles on the market. And knowing which one is right for your home is a key first step in getting a new shingle roof.

We’re PITCH Roofing, your local shingle roofing experts. As Owens Corning Preferred Contractors, we know shingle roofs better than anyone. That’s why we’re putting our expertise to good use and telling you everything you need to know about shingle roofing options in Florida. We don’t want to waste your time, so let’s dive right in!
Types of Roof Shingles in Florida


In Florida, there are two types of roof shingles on the market: composite and asphalt. And while these are both shingle roofing materials, they have major differences in aesthetics, longevity, and cost. So while asphalt roof shingles could be a great fit for one home, composite shingles might be a better fit for another.

That’s why we’re going to explain everything you need to know about both these types of roof shingles. Let’s get started by going over everything you need to know about composite shingles!
Composite Shingles
Composite shingles are also called synthetic shingles because of their unique makeup. Made from recycled materials and synthetic polymers, these shingles are famous for their ability to replicate the look of shake or slate roofing. This makes them a great option for people who want a shingle roofing system but don’t like the look of traditional asphalt shingles.

This type of roof shingle is also popular among homeowners who want a durable, long-lasting roof. For one thing, these shingles have protective coatings to help them resist UV and water damage. And with wind resistance of up to 150 mph, you can count on your composite shingle roof to stay in place even through a hurricane.

Thanks to all these protective features, composite shingle roofs last a long time. Even in Florida, where the weather is famously tough on roofs, we regularly see composite roofs last 40 to 50 years before needing a replacement. To sum it all up, these roofs are durable, long-lasting, and look like luxury roofing materials. So what’s the downside?

Well, a high-quality roof often comes with high costs. This is certainly true for composite shingles, which cost seven to 14 dollars per square foot. On an average 1,700-square-foot roof, that’s $11,900 to $23,800 for a shingle roof replacement. This is still much more affordable than actual shake or slate roofing, but it’s important to note that this is a high-cost shingle roof replacement.

With that overview, let’s talk about another type of roof shingles: asphalt shingles.
Asphalt Shingles
Asphalt shingles are made of a fiberglass base and coated in asphalt and protective granules. With this layered protection, the shingles are intended to hold up against high winds and heavy rain. But how well they do that really depends on the different types of roof shingles that you’re talking about.

Asphalt shingles come in two major types: 3-tab shingles and architectural shingles. To help you pick the best type of roofing shingle for your roof replacement, we’re going to discuss both these shingle options individually.
3-Tab Shingles
Years ago, 3-tab shingles were the default option for a shingle roof replacement. They were known for their flat look and their thin composition, which was made of a thin baseboard and a single asphalt coating. But new advances in the roofing industry have made them all but obsolete.

That’s because 3-tab shingles just can’t compete with other types of roof shingles. Their wind resistance almost never goes higher than 90 mph, which means they’re liable to come off even during a tropical storm, let alone a hurricane. And with minimal protection against Florida’s humidity, these shingles are just as likely to rot off your roof as be pulled up by storms.

So why did people use them for so long? Well, they’re cheap. Manufacturing costs are low because they’re light, thin shingles, and it doesn’t take experienced roofing labor to hammer these thin shingles onto a roof. That’s how you get roof replacement costs as low as two to four dollars per square foot.

Despite these low costs, though, we don’t recommend 3-tab shingles for homes in Florida. With an active hurricane season coming this year, it just isn’t a good idea to leave your home unprotected like that. Instead, consider upgrading to architectural asphalt shingles.
Architectural Shingles
Remember how we said that 3-tab shingles were replaced by modern roofing technology? This is that technology. Architectural (or dimensional) shingles are hardier, more durable, and look better than 3-tab shingles. In fact, of all the types of roof shingles in Florida, these are now the most popular option for shingle roof replacements.

It’s not hard to see why. Architectural shingles are twice as thick as 3-tab shingles, which increases their wind resistance to 110 mph. This is great wind resistance for an affordable roofing system, and it’s complemented by an extra layer of asphalt coating that keeps your shingles from soaking through. When you choose high-quality Owens Corning shingles, they even come with anti-algae properties to keep your roof looking and performing its best!

Dimensional shingles also stand out in aesthetics. They have a unique, textured pattern to them that creates depth and visual interest on your roof. So in addition to protecting your home, architectural shingles can vastly improve curb appeal and add visual interest to your roof.

And they do all of this at a great price. While more expensive than 3-tab shingles, architectural asphalt shingles have a great price point. On average, they cost between four and nine dollars per square foot. Using the average roof size of 1,700 square feet, that means $6,800 to $15,300. In other words, they’re a bargain when compared to composite shingles!

### Aluminum Roofing Pros: Roof Replacement Guide

If you live in coastal Florida, aluminum roofing could be the perfect material for you. But roofing services are often major investments in your home, especially if you’re looking for an aluminum roof replacement. That’s why it pays to get advice from the experts first.

In the state of Florida, nobody knows aluminum roofing better than PITCH Roofing. As experienced local roofers, we know the good and the bad of aluminum roofing, and today we’re passing along our knowledge to help you make the right decision for your home. That’s why we’re going to start off by answering a simple question: Who needs aluminum roofing?
Who Needs Aluminum Roofing in Florida?


Of all the types of metal roof replacements in Florida, aluminum roofing offers unique benefits. For one thing, it’s one of the most lightweight metal roofs on the market, and it doesn’t sacrifice strength or durability, either. In fact, aluminum roofs are just as good at resisting hurricane-force winds as other types of metal roofs!

People don’t generally pick aluminum roofing just because it’s lightweight, though. More often, homeowners choose aluminum because they live within a mile of the coast. Florida is surrounded by saltwater, and while most modern metal roofs have rust protection built-in, this isn’t enough to deal with the saltwater air directly on the coast.

Aluminum roofing, however, does not rust. Since it contains only trace amounts of iron, there simply isn’t anything there to corrode. This is its biggest selling feature, and it’s why aluminum roof replacements are popular in coastal parts of Florida.

In terms of cons, aluminum roofing doesn’t have many. It is a softer metal, so it’s a little more vulnerable to denting. However, this is mostly just a matter of looks and doesn’t affect structural integrity. As a result, this doesn’t often dissuade people from getting an aluminum roof.

The cost of aluminum roofing, however, can pose a problem for some homeowners.
How Much Does Aluminum Roofing Cost?
In roofing, talking about costs is always tricky. And that’s especially true with aluminum roof replacements. Roof replacements always have many unique factors that affect the total costs, but the cost of a new aluminum roof is doubly challenging because there are two types of viable roof replacements: corrugated and standing seam.
Corrugated Roofing


Corrugated aluminum roofing is a more budget-friendly option. This is due to both its simple manufacturing process and its simple, quick installation.

Corrugated roofing, or 5V, uses metal sheets with many hills and valleys. Since these sheets are drilled straight down into the roof, there is no need for a complicated fastening mechanism. And when it comes time to install your roof, experienced roofers should have no trouble quickly attaching your new roof. By keeping manufacturing and labor costs low, corrugated aluminum roofing remains an affordable metal replacement option.

The downside to these exposed fasteners is that they undergo wear and tear over the years. As a result, aluminum corrugated roofing will not last as long as standing seam. Still, an aluminum corrugated roof can last for about 40 years.

So how much is this roofing system going to cost you? On the Florida market, we see aluminum corrugated roof replacements cost between five and 12 dollars per square foot. This is more than a shingle roof replacement, but in the world of metal roofing, this price is quite affordable.
Standing Seam Roofing
Standing seam aluminum roofs use hidden fasteners. And while this makes them more durable, it also considerably raises the cost of a metal roof replacement.

Unlike corrugated metal roofs, standing seam uses panels that are mostly flat. The only spot where they raise is where the fastener sits beneath the panel, allowing them to slot together. And since the fasteners are hidden under the roof, they’re better protected against the elements. This also creates a sleek, smooth profile that many homeowners love.

However, it also drastically increases roofing costs. That’s because these panels are much more expensive to manufacture, and they take more time and experience to install. Many homeowners believe that they’re worth it, though, especially because standing seam roofs last 50-70 years.

The total costs of aluminum standing seam roofing range from $10 to $21 per square foot. This makes it a luxury roofing material. Still, for homeowners who can fit it into their budget, standing seam aluminum roofing is one of the best options for coastal Florida.

We also pride ourselves on offering timely roof replacement estimates that have no hidden fees and cover the full scope of your aluminum roofing job!

Aluminum Roofing FAQs
Q: Is aluminum roofing good for Florida’s climate?

A: Yes, aluminum roofing is an excellent choice for Florida homeowners. Not only is it lightweight and durable, but it’s also immune to rust. This makes it great for homeowners near the coast as well as homeowners further inland since Florida’s humidity can lead to metal roof rusting in virtually any part of the state.

Q: Do aluminum roofs hold up to hurricanes?

A: As a metal roofing material, aluminum holds up beautifully against hurricanes. It resists both wind and rain, and both hidden and exposed fasteners are capable of keeping your home in place. And unlike a shingle roof, you won’t find pieces of it in your yard the morning after a storm!

Q: Do aluminum roofs need a lot of maintenance in Florida?

A: Aluminum roofs need minimal maintenance. Since they don’t move and can’t rust, there isn’t much that can go wrong with them when they’re properly installed. Our advice is usually to get an inspection once every two years just to make sure there’s no mold or algae growth.

Q: How does aluminum roofing compare to other metal roofing materials?

A: Aluminum roofs tend to be more expensive than steel roofs. However, they also can’t rust and are extremely lightweight, so this lower risk of issues is well worth the slightly higher price tag for many homeowners.

Q: Are aluminum roofs energy efficient?

A: Yes, aluminum roofs are great with energy efficiency. Since they’re UV-reflective, they keep your home cool and lower the amount of work your AC has to do in the summer. As a bonus, you can also recycle your aluminum roof when it reaches the end of its life!

### How to Decide Whether to Repair or Replace Your Roof

Problems with your roof are never fun to deal with, but there’s a world of difference between getting roof repairs and a roof replacement. Hammering on a few missing shingles can easily cost under $500, whereas a roof replacement will cost thousands. So when your roof starts leaking, deciding whether to repair or replace your roof is one of the first questions you need to answer.

PITCH Roofing is here to help you make the best decision for your roof. As a homeowner, it can be tough to tell what’s causing your roofing issues. After all, a leak can be a minor inconvenience or a sign of major water damage. But there are ways you can tell whether you should repair or replace your roof in Florida.
Should You Repair or Replace Your Roof?


One of the biggest factors in repairing or replacing your roof is the extent of the damage. For example, missing a handful of shingles after a storm is almost never a reason to replace a roof. On the other hand, you may still have the option of getting a repair even if your roof has been severely damaged.

In most situations, you get to choose whether or not you should repair or replace your roof. You may have major damage that should be replaced, but most experienced contractors will be able to come up with a repair solution that can give your roof more time. So how do you know whether to bite the bullet and get a roof replacement or get a temporary fix? Well, that will come down to the specifics of your roof and your situation.
How the Age of Your Roof Affects the Decision to Repair or Replace
At a certain point, a roof gets so old that your only option is to replace it. But there is no definite line where you have to replace it. Instead, it’s about balancing the age of your roof with how well it’s protecting your home.

What kind of issues indicate that you should replace an old roof? There are many, but some of the most common signs it’s time to replace a roof include:

 	Recurring roof leaks
 	Interior water damage on your ceiling
 	Having missing or damaged shingles across more than 25% of your roof
 	Algae and mold developing on your roof

If your roof is getting on in years and shows these issues, replacing it is probably the right decision. You may be able to repair it and buy yourself more time, but another issue will come up, and repairing the same issues indefinitely will only cost you more in the long run.
Considering the Cost of Roof Repairs
One good way to decide whether to repair or replace your roof is to look at how much you’d have to spend on fixing your roof. For example, if your roof is about to get its third $2,000+ repair in the past handful of years, then this could be a sign that it’d be cheaper to just replace the roof and stop issues from recurring.

Roofing costs always vary, but in Florida, you can expect an architectural shingle roof to cost between $14,000 and $20,000. This is undeniably a major expense. But it’s still cheaper than the cost to keep replacing the same issues over and over again. For this reason, you may consider replacing a problematic roof even if it’s fairly young.

Unfortunately, even newer roofs can need replacing if they’ve been improperly installed. Issues with ventilation, underlayments, and properly distributed weight can all cause newer roofs to need replacing. While nobody wants to replace a roof that’s under 20 years old, it’s important to consider how much you’re spending on repairs. It’s also important to carefully choose your roofers to ensure that your new roof doesn’t run into these same issues.
Budgeting for Roof Repairs vs. Replacement


Roofing problems don’t come on a schedule. And if you don’t have the money available for a roof replacement, you may be tempted to go with the cheaper solution and get a repair as a band-aid. This can work as a temporary measure to give you more time to save, but if your roof needs replacing, then there’s no repair that can change that.

Putting money into repairs to buy time can add up quickly. This leads to a frustrating cycle where you’re trying to save up for a roof replacement but your money keeps going to repairs. Luckily, there is a way out of this vicious cycle: roof financing.

At Pitch, we proudly offer 0% interest roof financing to avoid exactly this problem. Whether you repair or replace your roof should come down to the right decision for your home, not just your budget. By getting the money up-front, you can get the secure roof you need now and pay it off on a more comfortable schedule. Additionally, this will likely be cheaper than having pay for repairs every few months as you try to save up!
Start the Roof Repair or Replacement Process

From there, the only thing left to do will be to pick your roofers!

At Pitch, we believe in the quality of our work. That’s why we’re not asking for anything special — just the opportunity to show you what our experienced roofers can do. If you’re on the fence about whether to repair or replace your roof, let our experts help you make the right decision for your budget and your home.
Deciding to Repair or Replace Your Roof FAQs
Q: When should I replace my roof?

A: Normally, you’ll replace your roof when it reaches the end of its life cycle. For shingle roofs, this is after 20-25 years. However, you may need to replace it earlier if your roof fails due to poor installation or because of hurricane damage.

Q: Can I just replace shingles instead of replacing the whole roof?

A: Yes, if your roof has lost a few shingles to a passing storm, you should be able to replace a handful of missing shingles without replacing the entire roof. There is one caveat, though. If your roof is missing large sections of shingles or has sustained structural water damage, you may need to replace your entire roofing system.

Q: How often should I get a roof inspection?

A: For roofs installed more than five years ago, get a roof inspection once every two years and after major storms. This will let you stay ahead of any damage and repair it as it comes.

Q: Should I replace my roof if I plan to move?

A: If you plan to sell your home in the next few years, you may be able to get repairs so that you’re not on the hook for a roof replacement. However, if your roof needs many repairs, it may be harder to sell, whereas selling a home with a new roof can give you a lot more bargaining power.

Q: Is it cheaper to repair or replace a roof?

A: In many situations, roof repairs are cheaper than roof replacements. But if you look at the lifetime of your roof, it may be cheaper to replace a damaged roof now. This is because continuing to pay for repairs indefinitely quickly adds up.

### Types of Flat Roofing Materials in Florida

Flat roofs are common for both residential and commercial structures in Florida. But did you know that these roofs are especially vulnerable to damage from the local elements? To get long-lasting roofing for flat roofs, it helps to know what kind of flat roof materials you need.

As your local roofing partners, it’s our job to make sure that you’re informed about your flat roofing options. That’s why today, PITCH Roofing is sharing our insights and tips for picking your flat roof materials. Whether a roofing membrane or a layered flat roof is right for your home, we have the know-how and the expert roofers to make sure you get a flat roof replacement that will last.

Now, it’s time to discuss the different options for flat roofing in Florida!
Types of Flat Roof Materials in Florida


First things first: let’s talk about why flat roofs need special roofing materials in the first place.

On a sloped roof, you can install shingles or tiles because the water will naturally slide off the edges of your roof. As a result, you don’t need anything especially water-resistant, since the water won’t be on your roof for long. Flat roofs work very differently, however.

While they’re not technically flat and are actually low-slope roofs, flat roofs can’t move water off your roof as efficiently as a sloped roof. While your roof should have a slight slope to help with drainage, you can still expect water to pool on your roof and take time to completely run off. To protect your roof during this vulnerable period, you need special roofing for flat roofs.

That said, there are very different approaches to flat roofing materials. Specifically, flat roofs tend to have either a rubber roof membrane or a layered roofing system. Now, let’s look at each of these options and how they protect your structure!
TPO Roofing
Thermoplastic polyolefin, or TPO roofing, is a rubber roofing membrane. In other words, this is a single-ply roofing system that covers your flat roof. While having only one layer of protection may seem risky, it’s very well-suited to what flat roofs need: water protection.

Because TPO is made of rubber, it creates a water-tight barrier around your home. This means that even if water is trapped on your roof for days or hours, TPO should keep it away from the vulnerable interior of your roof. And since it’s reinforced with fiberglass and carbon fiber, you can still count on it to be hardy and resilient, which makes for excellent roofing for flat roofs.

That said, TPO isn’t perfect. For one thing, it can shrink and become brittle as the sun ages it over the years. This can require additional maintenance over the lifetime of your roof. Additionally, it’s a fairly new material on the market, so roofers are still debating exactly how long it lasts on average since the chemical formulation of TPO has changed in recent years.

While we don’t know an exact number, there’s good evidence to suggest that TPO roofs average 15-20 years of life, even in Florida. This is a standard lifespan for a flat roof, but it could turn out to be even longer if new alterations to TPO sheets improve its heat resistance over the years!
Modified Bitumen Roofing
As a layered flat roofing system, modified bitumen (or mod bit) is hardy. Made from blending asphalt with rubber polymers and reinforcing the mixture with fiberglass, mod bit is an excellent alternative to a single-ply roofing membrane. With its many layers of protection, you can count on it to hold up against the worst Florida has to offer and keep its structural integrity intact.

Modified bitumen works much better than TPO in areas that see a lot of foot traffic. This makes it popular for commercial structures like hospitals. Since it’s built of multiple layers of sturdy protection, some light traffic shouldn’t cause problems for your modified bitumen roof!

Despite its strengths, there’s no such thing as perfect roofing for flat roofs. Modified bitumen still has flaws, like its weakness to ponding. While it isn’t likely to experience ponding, if it does, your asphalt protection won’t keep out water as well as a rubber roof would.

When it comes to lifespan, we know exactly how long this flat roofing material lasts. On average, modified bitumen lasts for about 20 years in Florida. And since it’s a low-maintenance roofing system, you can count on minimal repairs and low maintenance costs across these two decades of protection!

This is a basic look at two of the most popular types of flat roofs in Florida. But there’s still one important area that everyone has questions about: the cost of different flat roofing materials.
Affordable Roofing for Flat Roofs


When choosing a roofing material, we encourage roofers to consider more than just the cost. Of course we all have limits to our budgets, but it’s important to balance the cost with the performance of your new roof. With that disclaimer out of the way, let’s talk about the costs of different types of flat roofs!

On average, TPO flat roofs cost between five and 10 dollars per square foot. So if your roof is 2,000 square feet, your total roof replacement costs will probably be between $10,000 and $20,000. Keep in mind that other factors can impact this cost though, like the current state of your roof and any unique features on it!

Modified bitumen roofing is a more affordable roofing option for flat roofs. With costs ranging from four to eight dollars per square foot, you can expect a mod bit roof replacement to cost between $8,000 and $16,000 if you have a 2,000-square-foot roof. These low costs make mod bit flat roofs the most popular option in roofing for flat roofs.

### Shingle vs. Tile Roofing: Exploring Your Roof Replacement Options

In Florida, shingles and tiles are two of the most popular roofing materials that you’ll find. While both can protect your home and look great doing it, there are many differences between these shingles and tiles in terms of durability, longevity, and aesthetic options. With all of these many areas to consider, many homeowners aren’t sure how to choose between a shingle vs. tile roof.

Luckily, PITCH Roofing is here to help you make this decision. As seasoned roofing vets in Florida, we understand the ins and outs of both shingle and tile roofing systems. From installation to how your roof will look in 20 years, we’ll walk you through everything you need to know about these two roofing materials.

To start off, let’s cover the basics of what roofing tiles and shingles are.
Shingles vs. Tile Roofs: Material Differences


Living in Florida, shingle roofs are the most common roofing material that you’ll see. These roofing systems are usually made of asphalt shingles, which are a protective base board that is coated in asphalt and protective granules to protect your shingles against impact damage, wind, and heavy rains.

Alternatively, shingle roofing can also include composite shingles. Also known as synthetic shingles, these are made of rubber and other recycled materials to imitate the look of wood shake or slate roofing. This makes them popular among homeowners who want the aesthetic of luxury roofing materials without the high roofing costs!

There’s variety among roofing tiles, too. Tiles generally have a more elegant profile than shingles, but they come in two varieties: clay and concrete. Each of these materials performs slightly differently, but the end result is a long-lasting roofing system that protects your roof while also delivering on that classic Florida style.

Now that we’ve got the basics out of the way, let’s look at how to decide between a shingle vs. tile roof replacement!
Choosing a Shingle vs. Tile Roof in Florida


As Floridians, our roofs need to be ready for just about anything. To make sure your home is prepared for the next major storm, let’s talk about all of the differences between roofing shingles and tiles!
Longevity of Shingle and Tile Roofs
One of the biggest differences in shingle vs. tile roofs is in lifespan. For your average asphalt shingle roof in Florida, you can expect 20-25 years of life when you use reliable contractors and high-quality architectural shingles. This number jumps up considerably for composite shingles, which can last between 40 and 50 years.

The numbers are noticeably different for tile roofs, though. A concrete tile roof will average around 50 years, whereas a clay tile roof could last for a century or more. So while both shingles and tiles have a wide range in how long they can last, tiles are, generally speaking, your best bet for a roof that will last.
Roof Installation Costs
Calculating roofing costs is always tricky. That’s because your total installation costs will depend largely on your roof’s unique features and size. However, we can still cover the differences in the average costs of shingle vs. tile roofs.

The cost breakdown of shingle and tile roofing materials in Florida is:

 	Asphalt Roofing Shingles: Architectural shingles cost between four and eight dollars per square foot. This is partially what makes them so popular; they’re a great blend of durability and low roofing costs.
 	Composite Roofing Shingles: These long-lasting shingles cost between seven and 14 dollars per square foot in Florida. This is a significant price jump, but still cheaper than real shake or slate roofing!
 	Concrete Roofing Tiles: Including installation costs, concrete tile roofs cost between seven and 19 dollars per square foot. While more expensive than shingle roofing, this is still considered a more affordable tile roofing system.
 	Clay Roofing Tiles: This luxury roofing material costs between $12 and $21 per square foot, making it the most expensive option on this list. But with its classic Florida profile and unbeatable longevity, it’s not hard to see why!

Roofing costs vary depending on many factors, and there are always ways to get an affordable roof replacement. But these ranges should help you pick out which roofing material best suits your roofing budget.
Hurricane Resistance
While humidity and UV exposure do a number on local roofs all year round, hurricanes will destroy your roof all at once. So when choosing between a shingle vs. tile roof, it helps to know how your new roofing system stands up to major storms.

Generally, shingles are a little worse than tiles when it comes to standing up against hurricanes. For example, asphalt shingle roofs usually only get wind resistance up to 110 mph or so. This is a great figure that will protect against tropical storms and many hurricanes, but it simply can’t match the 150 mph wind resistance of clay tile roofs.

In short, you’re a lot more likely to find stray shingles in your yard after a storm than to find uplifted tiles. Thankfully though, both shingle and tile roofs can stand up to the heavy downpours that come with major storms!
Roof Maintenance Schedule
Both shingles and tiles can give you a roof that will last for decades. But how many repairs will your roof need over those decades? This is an important consideration for the cost of your roof across its lifetime.

Shingles will typically need more maintenance than tile roofs. This doesn’t mean that shingle roofs bring a lot of headaches, but rather that from time to time your shingles might get torn off by high winds or baked in the hot Florida sun. When this happens, it’s usually quick and easy to get a handyman to your home to perform these minor repairs.

Clay tiles are less likely to need much maintenance other than occasional washing to clear off algae. The one exception to this, though, comes from impact damage. Most tile roofs are fairly brittle, so when hail or storm debris strikes a tile, it can shatter it. This is more expensive than replacing broken or missing shingles, but the overall roof repair costs are still low, and simple repairs like these shouldn’t take much time for experienced roofers to resolve.

For both shingle and tile roofs, it’s a good idea to get regular roof inspections to ensure that your roof stays in top form throughout its life!
Get a Free Shingle or Tile Roofing Estimate
Above are some of the biggest considerations to make when deciding between a shingle vs. tile roof replacement. And whether you have lingering questions or you feel ready to make a final decision, the next step is collecting your free roofing estimate.

When you get your estimate, you’ll be able to talk with a roofing professional and get personalized answers to all of your questions. To get started, you can schedule your roof inspection by calling us at 727-677-4824 or scheduling your free estimate online.

And if you already know what you want, then we can help you speed through the roofing process. Get an online-only estimate and we’ll use satellite images to measure your roof and prepare a customized estimate using your chosen roofing material!

At the end of the day, deciding between a shingle vs. tile roof largely comes down to personal needs and preferences. Whatever roofing material you decide on is the right one. As experienced roofers, our job is just to help you make your decision and make sure that you get a great, long-lasting roof put on your home. ### How to Get Affordable Roofing Services in Florida

Across Florida, it seems like everyone is looking for affordable roofing. That’s why we’re sharing our tips for how to make sure that you get an affordable roof that doesn’t compromise on quality or durability!
5 Tips for Affordable Roofing in Florida


No matter where you go, roofing is never cheap. That’s because it requires expensive materials and highly skilled professionals to do most major roofing jobs. But just because roofing isn’t cheap doesn’t mean you can’t make it affordable.

Here are our five tips on how to make sure you get an affordable roof replacement!
1. Schedule Your Roof Replacement in the Off Season
Sometimes something catastrophic happens to your roof and you need a replacement ASAP. In cases like this, we never recommend putting off your roof replacement since damage could spread to your decking and cost you more in the long run. But if you’re looking at replacing a roof because it’s getting too old, it pays to plan ahead.

In Florida, summer is the busy roofing season thanks to the hurricanes and tropical storms that tear through the state. As a result, contractors are often tightly booked with little gaps in their schedules. Not only does this mean it’ll take longer to get your roof replaced, but you can also expect labor costs to jump in the summer due to the high demand. So if you can afford to wait, getting a roof in the winter is a great way to take affordable roofing into your own hands!
2. Invest in Quality Materials
It may be hard to believe, but choosing the cheapest possible roof is not the best way to pursue affordable roofing options. In fact, skimping on the essentials could cost you a lot more in the long run.

As an example, let’s look at shingles. 3-tab shingles are by far the cheapest shingles on the market, but they’re also the flimsiest. They’re thin, dry out under the sun, and can rarely handle winds in excess of 80 mph, so they’re unlikely to survive even a tropical storm, let alone a hurricane.

Architectural shingles, on the other hand, are only slightly more expensive and much more durable. They’re thicker, hardier, and much better at resisting wind uplift. So while the initial roof replacement might be a bit more expensive, this value pays off in saving you money on repairs in the future. When looking for affordable roofers near you, avoid roofers who promise cheap upfront costs at the expense of quality or longevity!
3. Explore Affordable Re-roofing Options


When you think about it, a roof replacement is a complicated job. Before installing your new roof, contractors first have to tear off your old one. This adds a lot of time to your project, and more time on your roof means higher labor costs.

One way to make roofing more affordable is to choose re-roofing instead of a roof replacement. With this approach, a new roof is installed on top of your old roof, so the old one never needs to be removed. This makes getting a new roof both faster and more budget-friendly!

Also called a roof overlay, this process is great for some but is not right for every structure. To see if re-roofing is a good idea for your home, ask your roofer about it when they come out to perform a roof inspection in preparation for your roofing estimate.
4. Collect and Compare Roofing Estimates
The best way to make sure you’re getting affordable roofing services is to compare prices. That starts with collecting estimates from licensed Florida roofing contractors. Common wisdom is that you should collect three estimates for the job, and we agree with that, but we don’t recommend taking the cheapest estimate every time.

Naturally, you shouldn’t go with an estimate that’s much more expensive than other quotes you’ve seen. But sometimes an estimate has a cheap price because the roof itself is cheap and of low quality. So by choosing the cheapest roof installation costs, you could end up paying for poor materials and even worse workmanship, which defeats the purpose of affordable roofing.

A good way to make sure you’re getting a good roof, in addition to comparing the price, is to compare the details in the estimate. Vague, general estimates don’t protect you because they don’t clearly outline the work that will be completed for the quoted price. A comprehensive, detailed estimate, on the other hand, protects you and ensures that you know exactly what you’re paying for.
5. Explore Affordable Roofing Discounts and Reward Programs
When you pick the right roofers, there may already be discounts and rewards programs available for you to take advantage of. For example, PITCH Roofing offers special discounts for teachers, veterans, and first responders. And when you’re talking about something as expensive as a roof, any percent off your roof will result in sizable savings!

If you don’t qualify for these programs, you still have options to make your roof more affordable. At Pitch, our Black Tie rewards program comes with perks like free inspections, preventive roof care, and high-priority roof services. This represents extra value across the lifetime of your roof, which is key to giving you a high-value roof replacement!

### Pros and Cons of a Spanish Tile Roof in Florida

If you’ve been considering getting a tile roof replacement, someone has probably recommended getting a Spanish tile roof. But while Spanish clay tiles have a long history in Florida, they’re not right for everyone. So how do you know if they’re the right choice for your roof replacement?

Well, this article is a great place to start. We’re PITCH Roofing, your team of local tile roofing professionals. Keep reading for our breakdown of Spanish tile roofs and the value they can bring to your Florida home. But to get started, let’s define exactly what Spanish roofing tiles are and how they’re made.
Spanish Tile Roof Manufacturing


 

Spanish roofing tiles are a type of barrel tile or S-shaped tile. These names come from their shape, which looks like half a barrel when installed but is actually S-shaped to allow for the tiles to lock together beneath your roof. Since the mechanism of adhesion happens below your roof, this vulnerable area is protected and will experience little wear and tear over the years.

This has always been the general shape of Spanish roofing tiles, but their composition has changed a lot over the centuries. These tiles were originally created using nothing but clay, water, and a kiln. While this produced strong, resistant tiles, modern roofing technology has made a lot of improvements.

For one thing, Spanish tiles are now made using machines that can create the perfect tile shape every time. This means drastically lower manufacturing costs, making a Spanish tile roof much more affordable for homeowners. Additionally, modern Spanish tiles have added protective coatings to better resist things like rain and UV rays.

In short, Spanish tiles used to be good in Florida, but now they’re great. But are they right for your home? The only way to know is to consider both the good and the bad of a new Spanish tile roof.
Pros and Cons of a Spanish Tile Roof in Florida


Spanish tile roofs have been popular in Florida for centuries. And with modern roofing improvements, that popularity has only gone up. But no roofing material is right for every home, so let’s talk about everything you need to know before scheduling your tile roof replacement.
Pro: Long Lifespans and Low Maintenance
If you want a roof that you can trust to last a long time without many issues, a Spanish tile roof is an excellent option. For one thing, clay roofing tiles last longer than any other roofing material, with lifespans ranging from 70-100+ years!

And during this long lifespan, it’s unlikely that your roof will have many problems. A Spanish tile roof can withstand high winds, heavy rains, and extreme UV exposure. So even with Florida’s unpredictable weather, you can still count on your tile roof to stay put!
Con: High Costs of a Spanish Tile Roof in Florida
Remember how we said that Spanish tile roofs have become more affordable thanks to modern roofing technology? That’s true, but “more affordable” is relative. Even today, Spanish roofing tiles are a luxury roofing material with a complex installation, so you can count on these roofs costing more than the average roof in Florida.

So how much does a Spanish tile roof cost in Florida in 2024? The latest numbers put the average cost between $15 and $22 per square foot for these clay tiles. Keep in mind that total tile roof replacement costs depend on the size of your roof, its unique hills and valleys, and its accessibility. But for most homeowners, it’s fair to say that a Spanish tile roof is a major property investment!
Pro: Local Charm and Aesthetics
Spanish tile roofs just make sense in Florida. This is especially true if you have a Spanish- or Mediterranean-style home. By adding a Spanish tile roof, you can give your home a look that’s tropical, modern, and distinctly Florida.

And on the Florida housing market, this kind of charm has a lot of value. Thanks to increased curb appeal and its many protective features, a Spanish tile roof will substantially increase the value of your home. This makes clay tile roof replacements a popular option for people who plan to stay in their homes forever as well as people who plan to sell one day.
Con: Brittle Roofing Tiles
In a lot of ways, clay tiles are hardy and resilient. But the way they handle impact damage could be an exception. While these tiles are resistant to the worst that Florida’s weather can throw at them, their brittleness means that shattering is an issue that homeowners commonly run into.

Now, it’s important to note that you won’t be dealing with shattered tiles every other month if you get a Spanish tile roof. But from time to time, storm debris or hail could crack a tile on your roof. The silver lining, though, is that replacing cracked tiles is a quick and easy repair, so it shouldn’t eat up much of your time or budget.
Pro: Eco-friendly Roofing
Whether you’re a committed environmentalist or you just want a lower monthly energy bill, Spanish roofing tiles can do a lot for you. For one thing, clay is an entirely natural material that’s easy to recycle. This gives tile roofing a big leg up on asphalt shingle roofs, which end up depositing about 107 billion shingles into landfills every year.

Additionally, Spanish clay tiles create excellent insulation on your roof. In the hot summer months, this means your roof will keep the cool air in and the hot air out. When you combine this with their UV-resistant coatings, Spanish tile roofs are able to reliably keep your home cool to help both the environment and your monthly budget.
Get a Spanish Tile Roofing Estimate
As you can see, there are both upsides and downsides to getting a Spanish tile roof replacement. Ultimately, the only person who can decide what’s right for your roof is you. We’re just here to make sure that you get the excellent roofing services that you deserve.

### Pros and Cons of Metal Roofs in Florida

When looking at roofing materials, you always need to consider the location. This is especially true for metal roofs in Florida. Given the local climate, metal roofs can be a huge advantage over tropical storms and hurricanes. But at the same time, you should also consider how year-round humidity and saltwater in the air could affect the longevity of your metal roof.

PITCH Roofing is here to give you a balanced look at metal roofs in Florida so you can make the best decision for your home or commercial property. As seasoned roofing professionals, we know the value of a metal roof across its lifetime. So let’s talk about the good and the bad so that you can get the roof that’s right for you!
Pros of Metal Roofs in Florida


If you’ve noticed more and more homes getting metal roofs lately, it’s not just you. Metal roofs have become more popular than ever in Florida, and that’s not just a coincidence. Let’s talk about some of the biggest reasons Floridians keep upgrading to metal roofs.
Wind Resistance
If you have a shingle roof in Florida, then you probably know that winds from tropical storms and hurricanes are tough on your roof. Shingle roofs in Florida often deal with winds uplifting shingles and need intermittent repairs after major storms. But it’s a very different story with metal roofs in Florida.

A well-installed metal roof can handle winds in excess of 140 mph. This means that even if a major hurricane directly hits your home, you can count on your roof to stay put and keep protecting your structure. This advanced level of protection is worth a lot to Floridians who just want peace of mind when the next storm hits!
Lower Energy Bills
Most metal roofs are extremely effective at lowering monthly energy bills. In addition to the insulation that you could expect from any roof, metal roofs are also good at reflecting UV rays. This means that when the hot summer sun is beating down on a home, metal roofs are able to reflect those UV rays away from the structure and keep it cool.

This isn’t just good for your budget, though. It also helps your roof last longer. The sun is extremely damaging to roofs, especially over decades. By deflecting some of these harmful rays, metal roofs in Florida can fight off wear and tear and protect your structure for longer.
Long Roofing Lifespans
Given these great protective features, it’s not shocking that metal roofs in Florida last for a long time. In fact, metal roofs are among the longest-lasting roofing materials in the Sunshine State.

When properly installed, a traditional shingle roof in Florida will last for 20-25 years. For metal roofs in Florida, however, the lifespan is closer to 50-70 years. This range partially depends on which type of metal roofing you choose, with standing seam roofs lasting longer than corrugated metal sheets. But in either case, you can count on a metal roof in Florida to last for a long time.
Preferred by Homeowners Insurance
As a homeowner in Florida, you already know that the homeowners insurance market is in a crisis right now. With more insurers leaving the state and Citizens taking on more policies, many homeowners are understandably worried about getting and keeping a homeowners insurance policy at all — and that’s not even mentioning the many Floridians who want to lower their high premiums.

The good news is that metal roofs in Florida make for a great solution to both these problems. Because they’re durable and last for a long time, homeowners insurance companies love metal roofs. So by upgrading your roof, you can make your home much more appealing to insurance companies while also lowering your premium!
Cons of Metal Roofs in Florida


Metal roofs in Florida have plenty of great things about them, but there are downsides too. None of these make metal roofing a bad option for Floridians, but they are important to consider before making a major investment in your home like a metal roof replacement.
High Roofing Costs
Most locals know two key facts about metal roofs in Florida: they last a long time and are expensive. But many Floridians are surprised to learn that there’s actually a wide range of metal roofing costs.

Standing seam metal roofs, for example, cost anywhere from $10 to $35 per square foot. This makes them one of the most expensive roofing materials on the market. But corrugated metal roofing only costs between five and 12 dollars per square foot. In other words, depending on what kind of metal roof you choose, your total roofing costs could be more or less affordable.
Risk of Rust
In general, you don’t need to worry about rust with metal roofs in Florida. This may be surprising given our year-round humidity, but metal roofs are built with factors like this in mind. Because of additives like aluminum coatings, Florida metal roofs are highly resistant to rust. There is one exception to this, though.

If you live directly on one of Florida’s coasts, within a mile of the coastline, then you may have unique metal roofing considerations to make. While most of Florida is safe for nearly any kind of metal roof, the saltwater on the coasts is especially abrasive and can eat away at protective coatings.

For this reason, most roofers recommend getting an aluminum metal roof if your home is on the coast. Aluminum is extremely resistant to rust, so it’s one of the best ways to prepare your home for the next tropical storm if you live on the coast.
Impact Damage
No roof is immune to impact damage, and metal roofs in Florida are no exception. It does handle impacts differently than other roofs, though. Where large hail could crack a tile or completely remove a shingle, metal roofs in Florida only have to worry about denting from hail and storm debris.

Most of the time, these dents are not serious structural concerns. So while unsightly, they won’t leave your home vulnerable to the elements. For most homeowners, this is an easy issue to live with, but it’s important to know what you’re signing up for with a metal roof.

### The 7 Lies Scammy Roofers Will Tell You

In Florida, there are a lot of honest, hardworking roofers who want to help you protect your home or commercial property while charging fair rates. But those aren’t the only kinds of roofers that Florida sees. In fact, frequent hurricanes mean our communities are targeted especially heavily by bad actors looking to make a quick buck. To protect yourself, it’s essential to know the lies scammy roofers will tell you.

We’re PITCH Roofing, a local roofing company based out of Pinellas County. We were created by seasoned roofing veterans with over 60 years of local roofing experience, so we know what dishonest roofers are doing in our community. Today, we want to give you the information you need to stay safe and make sure you’re making a good investment in your property.

Now, let’s get started and talk about some of the biggest lies our customers hear from scam roofers in Florida!
The 7 Lies Scammy Roofers Will Tell You


In Florida, most scam roofers fall under the category of “storm chasers.” These roofers blow into town after a major storm and offer impossibly low prices for roof repairs and replacements. And while they’re not excellent roofers, they’re usually talented liars.

Here are the lines that should tip you off that you’re dealing with a dishonest roofing contractor.
1. This Price Is Only Good for Today
Among all the lies scammy roofers will tell you, this one is a classic. To create fake urgency, they’ll pretend that you have to agree to their terms right then and there. There will always be some “reason” why you have to decide immediately — material prices going up, work crews not being available in a few weeks, etc. But the real reason is always greed.

Roofing prices do increase naturally over time. But any dependable roofer can give you at least a few weeks to review your options and make an informed decision on this investment in your property. Anything else indicates that you’re dealing with roofers who know they can’t deliver on quality and instead resort to high-pressure sales tactics.
2. We Can Cover Your Deductible for You
When storm chasers know that you’re using insurance for your roof replacement or repairs, they see dollar signs. They may even offer to pay for your deductible so your roof is “free” for you. But like all the lies scammy roofers will tell you, this really only benefits them.

In addition to being illegal, letting roofers pay your homeowners insurance deductible is a bad idea. Roofers who do this will grossly overcharge your insurance company, which could lead to higher premiums for you in the future. Additionally, this contributes to the larger homeowners insurance crisis that hurts homeowners across the state.
3. You Need to Pay for Roofing Services Up Front


No legitimate roofer needs the entire cost of the job paid before they start working, but it’s still one of the most common lies scammy roofers will tell you in Florida. While it’s true that many reputable roofers require a deposit, this is mostly just a good-faith gesture to show that you intend to pay the full amount when the job is done as agreed upon.

Roofers who “need” the full money up front could just leave without completing the job. This is especially true if they aren’t based in Florida since they can just pack up and leave without giving you a way to hold them accountable to your agreement.
4. You Have to Get Your Roof Replaced Immediately
Sometimes a roof needs an immediate replacement. But more often, even roofs that need replacing can last a while longer with thorough repairs. Scam roofers will insist that you get a more expensive roof replacement ASAP, whereas honest contractors will tell you about all viable alternatives.

Even if they think that you should get a roof replacement, reliable roofing professionals will always walk you through your options. Because as roofers, it’s not our job to decide what happens to your roof. It’s only our job to inform you of your options and give our professional recommendations.
5. We Don’t Need a Permit to Work on Your Roof
When talking about the lies scammy roofers will tell you, this is one of the most alarming. The vast majority of roofing projects require permitting to ensure that the work is being done to Florida standards and codes. Skipping permitting is a way for unreliable roofers to cut costs, but it’s never in your best interest.

Not only does this open you up to penalties and legal trouble, but it could also leave you with a poorly installed roof, void any roofing warranties you had, and ruin your ability to keep or get homeowners insurance. In short, it’s a massive red flag that you need to choose other roofers.
6. We Can Start Tomorrow
At first, it probably sounds great to hear that a crew can start immediately to get your roof fixed or replaced. But think about it — why is that crew available in the first place?

With experienced roofers, jobs are booked up a few weeks in advance. There might be times when they can move you up the line in an emergency, but offering to start the next day is a major red flag. This should tell you that their crews are so hard up for work that there’s no wait. There are better roofers in Florida to pick from, so there’s no need to settle!
7. You Don’t Need a Detailed Estimate
Of all the lies scammy roofers will tell you, this is the one that people fall for the most often. On the surface it makes sense — you’re just agreeing to get a new roof at this great price, so why would you need an estimate that covers every little thing they’re going to do?

Well, to be sure that you’re getting a full roof, for one thing. Your roof is complex, and you need to make sure that you’re agreeing to get a functional new roofing system, not just new shingles hammered over rotting decking and around faulty ventilation. Detailed estimates ensure that you know exactly what you’re paying for and the roofers can be held accountable for the quality of their work, so never skip this crucial step.
Skip the Lies and Get a Free Estimate from the Real Pros

But you don’t have to go with scam roofers to get that kind of peace of mind. At Pitch, we make the roofing process as smooth as possible.

### The Value of Hurricane Straps for Florida Homeowners

Summer in Florida is a great time to head to the beach, enjoy some ice cream, and start preparing your roof for hurricane season. Yes, while we'd all like to keep things light and fun over the summer, the truth is that hurricane season is an extremely dangerous time for your roof. This has led a lot of homeowners to look into hurricane straps as a way to protect their homes and lower their sky-high homeowners insurance rates.

We're PITCH Roofing, and we're here to help protect your home. That's why we're explaining hurricane straps, both how to get them and what they can do for your home.

Keep reading for a foolproof guide on the value of hurricane straps in Florida!
How Do Hurricane Straps Work?

Hurricane straps, as the name implies, are strips of metal that adhere your roof to the rest of your structure. In a certain way, you can think of them as seatbelts for your roof. When the winds start whipping up and storm debris starts flying, you can count on these bad boys to keep your roof firmly in place.

This roof protection technology is usually made of galvanized steel. In other words, you can count on it staying strong even in the face of extreme winds. That's why they're among the most popular roof upgrades in Florida. This is especially true in early summer when people want to hurricane-proof their roofs.
Do I Need Hurricane Straps?
Whether or not you technically â€œneedâ€ hurricane straps depends on where you live. In some parts of Florida, these are a requirement for all new construction projects. This means that if your home is already standing and you don't need an immediate roof replacement, you might not legally need to have hurricane straps.

But they're still a good idea anyway.

Even without a legal requirement, this simple roofing upgrade can go a long way in improving your roof's wind resistance. It's every homeowner's worst nightmare to find their roof in the front yard. Unfortunately, that can happen when major hurricanes blow into town.

This additional protection can make the difference between losing a few shingles in a storm and losing your entire roof. If that seems like a worthwhile investment to you, then we'd strongly encourage investing in this roofing upgrade.
How Much Does Upgrading Your Roof Cost in Florida?
Like with any roofing project, the cost of hurricane straps will largely come down to the specifics of your home. Things like the size of your roof, your roofing materials, and local labor costs will all play a role. That said, on average hurricane straps tend to cost around $1,000 to $1,500 to install.

While this is the cost to install hurricane straps in Florida, you could pay much less in the long run.

For one thing, homeowners insurance companies love this roof upgrade. They see them as a way of substantially mitigating the risk that they'll need to pay for a new roof. This means that getting this upgrade could save you money by lowering insurance rates. Florida has some of the highest homeowners insurance costs in the country, so this is an excellent way to bring those costs down.

It's also possible to save money on the upfront costs of hurricane strap installation. Thanks to the My Safe Florida Home program, you can get two-thirds of your installation costs covered. And it's easy â€” you just apply to this public fund for home upgrades against hurricanes. With all of these savings on the table, it just makes sense to invest in your property by getting hurricane straps.

### How to Prepare Your Roof for Florida's Hurricane Season

Every year, Florida’s hurricanes get more severe and more frequent. And although we’re not quite in hurricane season yet, meteorologists already predict that hurricane season 2024 will be especially full of severe storms. As a homeowner, do you know how to prepare your roof for the upcoming hurricane season?

We’re here to make sure that you do. We’re PITCH Roofing, your local roofing partners based right here in Pinellas County. Today, we’re using our decades of local roofing experience to help you get your roof ready for the summer. Keep reading for real advice from local roofing professionals!
How to Prepare Your Roof for Hurricane Season 2025


You hear a lot of talk about “hurricane-proofing” your roof in Florida, but the truth is that no roof in Florida is completely safe from hurricanes. That said, there are steps you can take to minimize your risk of storm damage to your roof. Let’s look at the best things you can do to keep your roof safe this summer!
1. Schedule a Roof Inspection
It can take a long time for roof damage to cause issues you notice inside your home. For example, you could have missing or damaged shingles that don’t cause visible interior damage for months. But that damage is still there, and fixing it before a hurricane blows into town is crucial.

That’s why we strongly recommend getting a roof inspection ASAP. Best case scenario, your roof is structurally sound and there are no changes to make. Worst case scenario, you’re saving yourself a lot of hassle by fixing minor issues before a hurricane comes and turns them into major problems. Either way, it pays to let a professional take a look at your roof before hurricane season 2025!
2. Trim Trees and Palm Fronds
You would be surprised how much damage a tree can do to your roof. Storm debris is what we call twigs and branches that get blown onto your roof during a hurricane, and it can crack roofing materials, cause leaks, and even lead to pest infestations on your roof.

For all these reasons, it’s best to trim any overhanging trees before the wind starts whipping them into your roof. Depending on how quickly your trees grow, you may need to trim them more than once this summer. It’s a bit of a pain, but it’ll protect your roof and save you money on costly roof repairs!
3. Get Hurricane Clips
With stronger hurricanes becoming the norm, it’s natural to worry about your roof staying put. If you want extra assurance that your roof isn’t going anywhere, hurricane clips could be exactly what you need.

These sheets of metal work by adhering your roof to the walls of your structure. This way, even a Category 5 hurricane would struggle to remove your roof. It’s also a fairly straightforward roof upgrade so the costs are low — especially if you compare them to the cost of replacing your roof!
4. Get Insurance Documents Ready
If you’re lucky, you won’t need any insurance documents this hurricane season. But if you’re unlucky, you’ll be glad that you prepared for the worst.

To prepare for this year’s hurricane season, make sure that you’ve collected all of your essential insurance documents and know where they are. Items to collect include:

 	Any roofing warranties (manufacturer or installer)
 	Insurance documentation
 	Contact information for your insurance agent as well as your preferred contractors

In addition to these steps, it’s essential that you take “before” photos of your roof. These will help prove that a hurricane damaged your roof and not normal wear and tear. When submitting your claim, it can also help to include news coverage about the hurricane to show that it happened in your community and that others have also been affected by it.
5. Maintain Regular Roof Maintenance
With hurricane season on the horizon, it’s easy to get caught up in the big-picture things. But everyday roof maintenance can significantly impact how your roof stands up to hurricanes. Think of it this way: By preventing new problems from arising on your roof, your roof becomes better at standing up against high winds and heavy rain.

“Regular maintenance” includes things like cleaning gutters, getting any minor repairs you’ve been putting off, clearing mold and algae off your roof, etc. It’s never too late to protect your roof, so doing maintenance tasks like this is always a good idea to prepare your roof for hurricane season!

FAQs About Preparing a Roof for Hurricane Season 2025


1. Q: How do I know if my roof needs repairs before hurricane season?

A:Check for missing or damaged shingles, water stains on your ceiling, and roof sagging. If you have any doubt at all about the integrity of your roof, it’s best to call the professionals for a roof inspection!

2. Q: What is the best kind of roof for hurricane-prone Florida?

A: If you want to protect your home against hurricanes, metal and tile roofs are your best bet. Both of these roofs last for a long time and have great wind and rain resistance! That said, you can still get great hurricane protection with a shingle roof when you choose experienced contractors for your roof replacement.

3. Q: Can I do hurricane roof prep myself?

A: Technically, it is possible to do things like replace shingles or install hurricane clips yourself. But unless you’re an experienced roofing professional, we don’t recommend it. Improperly done work on your roof can be worse than not preparing it at all, and it could even cause problems when trying to use warranties or insurance benefits.

4. Q: What should I do about skylights when preparing my roof for a hurricane?

A: When you know that a hurricane will soon be in the area, it’s best to cover your skylight with protective plywood or storm shutters. This can prevent both your glass cracking as well as any leaking during a hurricane!

5. Q: What should I do if a hurricane damages my roof?

A: Always prioritize the safety of yourself and anyone else in your home. After the storm has passed, take photos of the damage and submit them to your insurance agent alongside your claim. Once you’ve gotten in touch with your insurance company, you should seek out roof repair services ASAP.

### Pros and Cons of Composite Roofing in Florida

While asphalt shingles are the most popular roofing material in North America, they’re far from your only shingle roofing option. Composite roofing using synthetic shingles has a lot to offer homeowners in Florida who want to balance great aesthetics with uncompromising durability. But is it right for you?

That’s what we’re here to help you find out. We’re PITCH Roofing, your trusted local roofing partners and composite roofing professionals. Today, we want to explain the good and the bad about composite shingle roofs to make sure that you get the right roof for you. To get started, let’s talk about the basics of composite roofing.
What Are Composite Roofing Shingles?

The core idea behind composite roofing is recreating the look and protection of other types of roofing, specifically slate or wood shake. Their base materials are a synthetic polymer mixed with recycled materials and some of the material that they’re trying to replicate. And the result is a shingle roofing system that offers a lot to Florida homeowners.

For one thing, composite shingles look almost identical to slate or shake roofs. That makes it a great option for homeowners who want a classic, timeless aesthetic with the protection of modern roofing technologies. Since they’re formed using molds of slate or shake roofs and made using similar products, the aesthetic offerings are virtually identical to higher-cost roofing materials.

Composite roofing is much more than just pretty, though. It’s also strong and able to stand up to the unforgiving Florida elements. In fact, composite tile roofs have so many upsides that we want to take a minute and look at them one by one.
The Pros of Composite Roofing in Florida

To get started with our deeper look into composite roofing, let’s talk about what homeowners love about this roofing material. This way, you’ll know what you have to look forward to if you choose a composite shingle roof replacement!
Unwavering Durability
With hurricanes getting worse and more common, your home needs the best protection available. And composite roofing could be exactly what you’re looking for.

For one thing, composite shingles are much less brittle than shingles made of real slate or cedar shake. That’s thanks to its composition of synthetic materials like plastic and rubber, which give it extremely high impact resistance to stand strong in the face of storm debris.

Composite roofing also holds up well to regular wear and tear. This means that even with the hot Florida sun beating down on your roof, it’s unlikely that you’ll start seeing issues like bleaching. This is much better than asphalt shingles, which don’t just get bleached by the sun, but crack and chip as it wears them down.
Great Longevity
When you get a roof replacement in Florida, you want it to last. And with composite roofing, it will. These shingles last for a long time, even through Florida’s harsh hurricane season.

Whereas even a great asphalt shingle roof might only last 20-25 years in Florida, composite shingles last for around 40-50 years. This makes them a much better investment in the long-term protection and safety of your home! To get this longevity, though, it’s important to make sure you’re getting a roof replacement from experienced, high-quality contractors.
Lower Price Than Slate Roofing
Composite roofing is not a budget roofing material by any standard that we know. But it’s also not the most expensive roofing material on the market. So while composite cedar shake shingles cost roughly as much as real cedar shake tiles, you can expect your new composite slate shingles to be much more affordable than real slate.

In fact, it’s not even close: Composite roofing costs about half as much as real slate when you factor in both material and roof replacement costs. That isn’t the only leg up that composite roofing has, though.

Composite roofing is also much lighter than slate roofing. This means that your roof will be able to more easily bear the load without roofers installing additional supports on your roof. In short, composite roofing is a cheaper, lighter way of getting the timeless look of a slate roof.
Eco-Friendly Roofing
If you want to go green with your new roof, then composite roofing is an excellent choice. Since many types of composite shingles are made with recycled materials, you can feel good about getting your new roof that’s made of materials that would otherwise be in a landfill.

This is starkly different from asphalt shingles, which are actually the biggest contributor to roofing waste in North America. In this way, composite roofing is a way to upgrade your roof and minimize environmental impact on our planet!
Aesthetic Versatility
Composite shingles are versatile in the sense that they can look like several different roofing materials. But even in addition to this already-impressive fact, composite roofing offers customization beyond choosing between types of slate and wood shake roofing.

Composite roofing also comes with a wide range of color options. From dark grays and blacks to more neutral earth tones and beyond, there’s almost no limit to the options you can choose from. We love versatility like this because it means our customers can get exactly what they’re looking for!
Cons of Composite Roofing in Florida
There’s no such thing as a perfect roofing material. And since every type of roof has its downsides, let’s talk about the biggest issues that homeowners have with composite roofing.
High Roofing Costs
Composite shingles are anything but an affordable roofing material. While they’re cheaper than slate roofing, they’re still far from cheap. But how much does a composite shingle roof replacement cost in Florida?

Roofing prices always vary from job to job, but in general, a composite shingle roof costs between eight and 14 dollars in Florida. If you have a 2,000-square-foot roof, that means your roof replacement costs will probably be between $16,000 and $28,000. In other words, this isn’t the most expensive roofing material in Florida, but it’s also far from the most affordable.
New on the Scene
You could say that composite roofing being new on the market means that it’s the latest roofing technology. And while that’s true, we’re generally suspicious of new things in the roofing industry. It’s not that we see any problems with composite roofing, but as roofers, it’s harder to trust something that we haven’t been working with for decades.

So when getting a composite roof replacement, there’s some reason for concern simply because these roofs haven’t been on the market for decades and decades like other options. But with many composite shingle manufacturers offering long-lasting limited warranties, you can still go into this new roof with assurances of protection.

### What Are Roof Replacement Costs in St. Petersburg, Florida?

There are plenty of upsides to living in Pinellas County, but one of the downsides is that your home needs to be ready for anything — even a Category 5 hurricane. If it’s time for a new roof, then it’s essential that you get a high-quality roof replacement ASAP.
