What Determines Roof Replacement Costs in St. Petersburg?

As a customer, it can be frustrating to see that roofers don’t just list prices on their websites. But there is a good reason: Roofing prices are so dependent on the specifics of the job that it’d be impossible to give a flat rate for every shingle roof in Pinellas County. So what factors can lower or raise your roof replacement costs?

Well, some of the biggest factors in St. Pete are:

 	Which roofing materials you choose (shingles, tiles, metal, etc.)
 	Rates in your local roofing market
 	Labor costs: More complicated roof replacements require more experienced and more expensive crews
 	The size of your roof
 	The complexity of your roof, including unique features like dormer windows, chimneys, skylights, etc.
 	How easy it is to access your roof

Of all of these pricing factors, the biggest one in your control is roofing materials. With that in mind, let’s talk about how much different kinds of roof replacements cost in St. Petersburg.
Shingle, Tile, Metal, and Flat Roof Replacement Costs in St. Petersburg

There is no shortage of options when it comes to picking a material for your roof replacement. While we recommend that you consider more than just the price before deciding on a roof replacement material, today we’re focusing on how much these roofing options cost.
Shingle Roofing CostsShingle roofing has some of the lowest roof replacement costs in St. Petersburg. With a lifespan of 20-25 years, this is the most common option selected by homeowners in Pinellas County, largely because of its affordability and wide range of color options.

So how much is it? Well, architectural shingles (the most popular kind) cost between four and nine dollars per square foot in St. Petersburg. If your roof is around the average size of 1,700 square feet, that means your roof replacement may cost between $6,800 and $15,300.
Tile Roofing Costs
It’s trickier to figure out tile roof replacement costs in St. Petersburg. That’s because roofing tiles come in two different types: concrete and clay. And in addition to each material having its own pros and cons, they also have different price points.

Concrete tiles, for example, cost between nine and 16 dollars per square foot when you include installation costs. Using that same 1,700-square-foot roof as an example, your concrete tile roof replacement costs should fall between $15,300 and $27,200.

You get noticeably different numbers for clay tile roofing, though. That’s because clay tiles are a more luxurious option that can last longer in Florida’s unique climate. Specifically, clay tile roofs cost between $12 and $21 per square foot. In other words, for the average roof in St. Petersburg, a clay tile roof replacement costs between $20,400 and $35,700.
Metal Roofing Costs
Similar to tile roofing, metal roofing comes with many options that can impact total costs. But for the sake of discussing roof replacement costs in St. Petersburg, we’re just going to talk about the biggest pricing factor: getting hidden or exposed fasteners.

Metal roofs with exposed fasteners are called 5V roofing, and they’re considered an affordable metal roofing option. With corrugated metal sheets and easy installation, these roofs only cost between five and 12 dollars per square foot. In other words, they’re about $8,500 to $20,400 on average.

Standing seam roofs (metal roofs with hidden fasteners) cost quite a bit more, though. Because of their more complicated design and roof installation process, these modern roofs cost between eight and 18 dollars per square foot. In real terms, that often looks like roof replacement costs between $13,600 and $30,600.
Flat Roofing Costs
Of all of these options, flat roofing has the most complex pricing. That’s because there are many different types of flat roofs. To help you budget, let’s look at the flat roof replacement costs in St. Petersburg by the type of flat roofing material:

 	Modified Bitumen: Mod bit is an extremely cost-effective flat roof replacement option. It lasts about 15-20 years and costs between four and eight dollars per square foot, or $6,800 to $13,600.
 	TPO: A newcomer on the roofing market, TPO is taking Florida by storm. This membrane roofing material lasts 20-30 years and costs between five and 10 dollars per square foot, or $8,500 to $17,00.
 	EPDM: EPDM has the best longevity of all flat roofing options with a lifespan of 30-50 years. It costs between five and 13 dollars per square foot, so roof replacement costs in St. Petersburg usually fall between $8,500 and $22,100.

With all of this pricing information, there’s one clear next step to take to get your Pinellas County roof replacement: collecting estimates.

### Types of Metal Roofs in Florida

With hurricanes becoming stronger and more frequent, metal roofing has never been more popular in Florida. Despite all this interest, though, homeowners still have a lot of questions. Specifically, they have questions about the different types of metal roofs. But many homeowners are surprised to find that they have even more metal roofing options than they thought.

We’re here to make things simple and clear. We’re PITCH Roofing, your local metal roofing contractors, and we know your metal roofing options better than anyone. Keep reading for our breakdown on the different types of metal roofing and which one(s) could be a good fit for your home or business!
Types of Metal Roof Fasteners

Many Floridians are surprised to learn that roof fasteners are one of the biggest differentiators between the types of metal roofs. But it’s true — how your roof is fastened to your structure will profoundly impact your metal roof’s cost, effectiveness, and durability.

Now, let’s take a look at what your options are!
Hidden Fasteners
Hidden fastener metal roofs are extremely popular for residential metal roof replacements. Also known as standing seam roofing, this is an extremely efficient, high-end metal roofing option. But how does it work?

We say that the fasteners are “hidden” because they’re on the underside of the panel. That’s why standing seam roofs are mostly flat. Not only does this create a sleek, modern exterior, but with the raised edges of the panels, standing seam roofs can slot together perfectly with the fastener safely protected beneath the roofing panel.

This type of metal roof does a lot more than just look good. With the fasteners hidden and protected, they’re much less likely to experience wear and tear from the Florida elements. For this reason, metal roofs with hidden fasteners often last considerably longer than roofs with exposed fasteners.

There is a drawback, though: cost. Among the cost of all types of metal roofing, standing seam stands out as a luxury option. Because of the high manufacturing costs and complicated installation process, standing seam roofs cost around $18 per square foot. With an average roof size of 1,700 square feet, this means that your new standing seam roof may cost around $30,600. For Floridians who want the strongest possible protection, though, this is the right investment to make.
Exposed Fasteners
When looking for affordable types of metal roofing, exposed fasteners are your best option. Known for their corrugated metal panels, metal roofs with exposed fasteners (called 5V roofing) offer a cost-effective option for homeowners who otherwise wouldn’t have access to metal roofing options.

The great thing about 5V roofing is its simplicity. In short, your metal roofers will take the corrugated metal sheets and drill them down into your roof. As a result, your roof will be secured in place and will be able to resist high-strength winds, even from hurricanes.

But while your roof will be secured, weathering can be an issue for this type of metal roof. Over time, the sun and rain can wear away at these exposed fasteners and weaken your roof. That’s why, if you do get a 5V metal roof, you should get it inspected at least every two years and after any major storms. This way you can keep your roof protected without breaking the bank.

For budget-conscious homeowners, metal roofs with exposed fasteners are the best option. A 5V metal roof will cost around nine dollars per square foot thanks to their lower manufacturing costs and easy installation. Using that same 1,700 average-sized roof, this means a 5V roof replacement may cost around $15,300.
Types of Metal Roof Materials

Your fasteners play a huge role in your total metal roofing costs. But the type of metal that you choose can be just as important in determining the quality and cost of a new metal roof.

There are many metal roof material options, but in Florida, the most common are:

 	Aluminum: This metal is ideal for coastal parts of Florida because of its unbeatable anti-rust properties. That, coupled with its great energy efficiency, makes it one of the more popular high-end types of metal roofs.
 	Galvalume: Galvalume is hardened steel that has been treated with aluminum and zinc coatings. As a result, it has great rust resistance and can even heal minor injuries to itself. And at a great price point, this is an excellent material for affordable metal roofing.
 	Copper: If you want the best metal roof regardless of the cost, then copper may be for you. A copper roof is resistant to everything Florida can throw at it and can last for up to 100 years. If you’re not scared off by its high cost of around $30 per square foot, this is a great investment in the value and safety of your property.

Whatever your roofing needs or budget, there is a metal roofing option for you. But when looking at the types of metal roofs, you shouldn’t just focus on what’s being installed on your roof. You should also carefully consider who you want to install it.

### Choosing the Best Tile Roofers in Florida

If you’re looking for tile roofers near you, it doesn’t get any better than PITCH Roofing. Our founders came together and pooled their collective 60+ years of local roofing experience to create us, your local roofing partners. But we’re not here to talk about ourselves.

But as roofers with deep roots in Florida, we want to start by talking about the history of tile roofing in Florida.
How Long Have Tile Roofers Been in Florida?

You might be surprised to learn that tile roofers have been part of the Florida landscape for centuries. Roofs made with clay tiles first came over to the New World via Spanish settlers in Florida, so we are literally the birthplace of tile roofing in North America.

For the settlers, tile roofs were exactly what they needed. They served a cultural value by reminding people of their homelands, and they did a great job keeping out the rain and pests that would have made life difficult for settlers.

Over the centuries, tile roofing would eventually fall out of fashion as new roofing technologies hit the market. But thanks to modern advances in tile roofing, this roofing material is more popular than ever. With strong protection and a classically Florida style, there hasn’t been this much demand for great tile roofers in decades.

While the history of tile roofing in Florida is interesting, it’s time to talk about the future. Specifically, it’s time to talk about the value that a tile roof could add to your home.
Benefits of Tile Roofing in Florida
Tile roofing isn’t just popular in Florida because of nostalgia. In fact, tile roofing is one of the strongest and most resilient roofing materials on the market. Don’t just take our word for it — let’s talk about the draws of tile roofing in Florida.
Long Lifespans
When properly installed by experienced tile roofers, a tile roof will last for a long time. This is true even in Florida, where roofs have to deal with more severe weather than most of the country. Thanks to their resistance to high winds and heavy rains, tile roofs are built to last.

And last they do! While shingle roofs rarely last longer than 25 years in Florida, a tile roof can easily double or even triple that amount of time. This helps offset some of their high roof replacement costs — after all, paying double for a roof that will last you three times as long could be a great deal!
Energy Efficiency
Whether you want to help the planet or just save money on your energy bill, tile roofers can help you out. Thanks to various energy-saving features throughout a tile roofing system, your home will be more energy efficient than ever once you’ve got your tile roof installed.

For one thing, tile roofs reflect sunlight. When UV rays hit your home, some of them will be deflected by the protective coating on your tiles. As a result, your home stays cooler. And as a bonus, your tiles will last even longer thanks to these coatings, since tiles can otherwise crack under the heat.

Another factor is your water-resistant underlayment. In addition to keeping out water, this also provides another layer of insulation. This keeps the cool air in and the hot air out, which means your AC system won’t need to work as hard in the summer. And that means noticeable savings!
Unique, Classic Aesthetics
Truly, there is nothing quite like a tile roof. Their distinctive look is highly sought-after in Florida, especially if you have a Spanish- or Mediterranean-style home. And with new advances in style options, there’s almost no limit to how tile roofers can help customize your roof.

Traditionally, tile roofs come in earth tones or a classic shade of red. And that style still holds up today. But with new color options, you can get tiles in virtually any color to suit your unique vision. And with different types of tiles like Spanish or French tiles, you always have options to make your roof completely unique.
How Much Does a Tile Roof Replacement Cost?

As professional tile roofers, we know that cost is important to you. And the good news is that there is a wide range of budgeting options when getting a tile roof replacement, so you should be able to find a price point that works for you.

The biggest factor in determining your tile roofing costs is the material itself. For example, a clay tile roof will always cost more than one made of concrete tiles because clay takes more time and money to manufacture. Other factors (the size of your roof, slope, accessibility, etc.) will also influence your total costs, but these are secondary to the impact made by material choices.

So how much do these different types of tile roofs cost in Florida? Well, concrete roofing tiles cost between eight and 19 dollars per square foot for both manufacturing and installation costs. For a roof that can last around 50 years in Florida, this isn’t a bad deal at all!

Clay tiles are a luxury roofing option. Their average price falls between $11 and $22 per square foot. While this is a high price point, they’re priced this way for a reason. A clay tile roof can last for a century or more when installed by experienced tile roofers, so it’s a very worthwhile investment!

A: Owens Corning shingles typically come with a limited lifetime warranty. Additionally, your roof may qualify for enhanced warranty coverage when you have it installed by Owens Corning roofers.

### New Contractor Rules & More in My Safe Florida Home Update

If you’ve heard about the My Safe Florida Home program, then you’re probably pretty excited at this chance to upgrade your home while saving money. But many homeowners still have a lot of questions. Who’s eligible for this program? How do I find reliable My Safe Florida Home Contractors? And how do I sign up?

We’re PITCH Roofing, and as Florida’s top roofing contractors, we’re here to answer all of your questions about this exciting, free program. But just in case you’re not totally sure how the My Safe Florida Home program works, let’s talk about what this opportunity could mean for your home.
What Is the My Safe Florida Home Program?


The simplest description of MSFH is that it’s a program to give you free money to upgrade your home. This program was originally started in 2006, but it was brought back in 2022 as a response to Florida’s homeowners insurance crisis. After running out of funds last year, the program is about to receive another $200 million to disperse to Florida homeowners.

That’s the short, simple version. Now let’s talk details.

The MSFH program doesn’t just give you free money to spend on roof upgrades. Instead, they’ll match your investment in your home. So for every $1 you spend on approved roof upgrades, you’ll receive $2 to spend, up to $10,000. So if you spend $10,000 upgrading your roof, you'll only have to pay for one-third of that price, or $3,333.

There are some limitations, however. Since this is free money from the state, they want to ensure that your money is being used for the right projects and that they’re investing in high-quality roofing professionals to help protect your home.

That covers the basics of the program, but now let’s talk about how you can qualify.
Who Qualifies for My Safe Florida Home?
To start, there are other qualifying criteria your property has to meet. For one thing, your home must meet all of the following qualifications:

 	Have been approved for a homestead exemption
 	Must have an insured value of under $700,000
 	The application for the permit for the home’s construction must have been filed before January 1st, 2008.

That’s how your home qualifies for this program. But there are other factors in when/if you’ll be able to use this program.

Right now, MSFH is not accepting any applications or paying out any funds. But they will start accepting applications on July 1st, 2024. From that date, applications will be open to select groups according to the following schedule:

 	July 1st – July 15th: Low-income homeowners age 65+
 	July 16th – July 30th: Low-income homeowners of all ages
 	July 31st – August 14th: Moderate-income homeowners age 60+
 	August 15th – August 30th: Moderate-income homeowners of all ages
 	August 31st and Onwards: All other homeowners

This covers who can use the program and the requirements for your home. But there are also clear guidelines on how these funds can be used to hurricane-proof your home.

In terms of roofing services, you can use MSFH funds for any of the following roofing contractor work:

 	Upgrading roof coverings
 	Reinforcing roof decking attachments
 	Installing a secondary water barrier on your roof

But when you’re talking about roofing, it’s not just about the kind of roofing services you get. You also need to consider who you can trust with this investment in your property.
Choosing My Safe Florida Home Contractors


In the earliest days of the MSFH program, you could only pick your roofers from a list of My Safe Florida Home program approved contractors. With the new funds being released starting July 1st, however, you can choose any licensed roofer that you want.

On one hand, this is great news for consumers who can now have more flexibility when upgrading their homes. But at the same time, it’s important to be careful that you don’t choose scam roofers who will take advantage of this opportunity to gouge their prices.

So how do you know the difference?

First, only choose roofing contractors based in your area. While national roofing companies or traveling contractors can do great work, they probably won’t know how to prepare your roof for Florida’s unique climate. Between high winds, heavy rains, year-round humidity, and extreme UV exposure, you just can’t afford to let inexperienced contractors on your roof!

You should also pay careful attention to how the roofers approach your project. Do they seem like they’re trying to help you make an informed decision, or are they trying to pressure you into making the choice that they want? Is their roofing quote thorough and helpful, or is it vague with no clear explanation for how much each service costs?

The funds for My Safe Florida Home might not come directly out of your pocket, but as a taxpayer, that’s still your money. Don’t let yourself be ripped off by greedy contractors who would never have received MSFH approval under the old rules.

### TPO vs. EPDM: Rubber Roof Replacement Guide

A rubber roof is one of the best ways to protect your flat roof from the Florida elements. But is it the best flat roofing option for your home or business? And if it is, which type of rubber roof should you get? To answer these questions, we need to have a clear understanding of what the different types of rubber roofs can offer.

That’s what we’re here for! PITCH Roofing was created to help our community members with real roofing problems, and today we’re doing that by taking a deep dive into rubberized roofing systems. Let’s start simple and talk about the different types of rubber roofing options.
Types of Rubber Roofs

Rubber roofs are pretty simple. They’re single-ply roofing materials made out of either rubber or a rubberized material. This means they work by creating a single, water-resistant layer across your flat roof to keep your roof strong and dry.

But in Florida, there are two types of rubber roofs that are especially popular: TPO and EPDM.

TPO (thermoplastic polyolefin) is a roofing membrane that typically comes in white. It's made from a blend of polymers, usually including ethylene-propylene rubber and polypropylene. Manufacturers combine these materials to create a durable, flexible, and heat-resistant roofing membrane that can withstand all of Florida’s inclement weather.

EPDM (ethylene propylene diene monomer) is a synthetic rubber roof that comes in both black and white. EPDM is known for its excellent resistance to weather, UV rays, and durability. That’s why it’s such a popular choice for low-slope roofs on both commercial and residential buildings.

While both of these materials are rubber roofs, they have wildly different benefits and drawbacks. Let’s take a look at them side by side so you can get the roof that’s right for you!
Choosing a Rubber Roof Material in Florida

Sadly, we can’t just tell you which roofing material is “best,” because all roofing materials have situations when they’re better or worse than others. But by looking at specific ways that these materials compare, we can help you find the best option for your rubber roof replacement.
TPO vs. EPDM: Longevity
When you get a new roof, you obviously want it to stick around for a long time. But which type of rubber roof lasts longer?

Well, assuming that each roofing option has been correctly installed, you’ll notice a slight difference in longevity. TPO roofing, for example, lasts for about 25 years on average. An EPDM rubber roof, on the other hand, can last for up to 30 years.

In other words, EPDM lasts slightly longer than TPO, but the difference is slight and probably shouldn’t be the main deciding factor when choosing your rubber roofing material.
TPO vs. EPDM: Aesthetics
Since TPO comes only in white and EPDM is available in both black and white, EPDM definitely has an edge when it comes to aesthetic versatility. But how do you know if you need a black or white rubber roof?

A white roof is great for homes, especially if the flat part of your roof is over a bedroom. White roofing materials are better at reflecting UV rays, so a white rubber roof can help your structure stay cool in the summer.

Black rubber roofs, on the other hand, are ideal for commercial structures where you can see the roof from inside the building. Thanks to their darker colors, they can hide dirt much better than a white roof, which makes them popular for hospitals and other multi-story buildings.
TPO vs. EPDM: Maintenance
Nobody wants to spend money on a flat roof replacement just for the new roof to need constant repairs. And the good news is that most rubber roofs need very infrequent repairs. But there is a difference between how often TPO and EPDM need repairing.

Specifically, TPO requires significantly less attention than EPDM. That’s because TPO seams are heat-adhered, which makes them stronger than EPDM’s adhesively-bound seams. As a result, you’re much more likely to need repairs on an EPDM roof.

But for either rubber roof material, you should watch out for issues like punctures from storm debris. Rubber roofs are vulnerable to punctures in their single-ply systems, which can expose your roof to water, so getting a roof inspection after a major storm is always a good idea.
TPO vs. EPDM: Cost
In almost every rubber roof replacement, cost is either a major factor or the biggest factor for a buyer. And we completely understand — you want great value for your investment. But when it comes to rubber roof costs, there is not a night and day price difference between materials.

Take TPO roofing for example, This rubberized roofing system costs between $10 and $20 per square foot, including material and installation costs. The average size of a roof is 1,700 square feet, so TPO roof replacements average a cost of around $17,000 and $34,000.

EPDM roofing costs a bit more, with price ranges from $12 to $26 per square foot. So while it’s more expensive than a TPO roof, the price difference is fairly small. Using the same numbers, an EPDM roof will cost between $20,400 and $44,200.
Get a Free Rubber Roof Replacement Estimate
If you’re considering a flat roof replacement, then you need to consider all of the above factors when choosing your roofing material. It can be tempting to focus on a single issue, but EPDM and TPO are so similar that you need to be careful when choosing between them. While both are great flat roofing materials, one will inevitably be better than your situation than the other.

Tile roofing has been popular across Florida for centuries. But new concrete tile roofs have made tile roofing more affordable and accessible than others. Pros and Cons of Concrete Tile Roofs

Many homeowners approach a roof replacement looking for the “best” roofing material. But in our experience, the best material doesn’t really exist. Every roofing material has good and bad qualities to it. And the only way to make a decision for your home is to be aware of both the pros and cons!

### Pros and Cons of a Galvalume Roof in Florida

Many people still picture metal roofs as noisy things made of tin, but metal roofing technology has come a long way since then. Now, a Galvalume roof is one of the most widely used options for a metal roof replacement. But because most Floridians aren’t familiar with this metal, they don’t realize how much good it can do for their properties.

As your local roofing partner, it’s our job to spread this crucial metal roof replacement information! Keep reading to hear from the PITCH Roofing experts about everything you should know about Galvalume steel and its value as a Florida roofing material. First, we’re getting started by explaining the basics of Galvalume.
Galvalume Roofing 101: New Steel, Old Protection

Galvalume steel was invented in the 1970s, but its base materials are tried and true. This new roofing technology comes from a mixture of galvanized steel, aluminum, and zinc. And if your goal is to protect your property in Florida, then this mixture could be perfect for your roof.

Galvanized steel is known for its durability and unrelenting protection. Aluminum complements this strength by providing essential rust resistance. This way, your roof will be much slower to corrode, even with Florida’s year-round humidity.

But when damage does start to develop on your roof, you’ll still be protected. That’s thanks to the zinc in a Galvalume roof, which will shed the damaged parts of itself. For this reason, roofers often say that zinc has “self-healing” properties, and this unique protection provides great longevity for metal roofs in Florida.

This means that in theory, Galvalume steel is perfectly suited to Florida. But a Galvalume roof isn’t the solution to everything. To see if this metal roofing material is right for you, you have to look at the pros and cons!
Pros and Cons of a Galvalume Roof in Florida

There’s no such thing as the perfect roof. Every roof, even metal ones, will have both good and bad qualities. Now, let’s look at the good and the bad of a Galvalume roof so you can make an informed decision!
Pro: Perfectly Suited to Florida’s Weather Patterns
You don’t need to be a roofing expert to know that the weather in Florida is tough on roofs. Between the humidity, intense UV exposure, and hurricane-force winds, any number of weather events could destroy your roof. But for all of these threats, a Galvalume roof is a pretty good answer.

Galvalume steel is generally rated for up to 140 mph in wind resistance. So even with a major hurricane raging outside, you can rest assured that your roof isn’t budging. And when properly installed, a Galvalume roof should create a waterproof barrier around your structure that keeps water out even when it’s being pushed by high winds.

And while UV rays are a year-round roofing concern, Galvalume steel handles them extremely well. By reflecting UV rays away, it reduces the wear and tear that the sun can do to your roof over time. It also lessens the amount of cooling that your AC system needs to do in the summer!
Con: Occasional Oil Canning
Oil canning is a possibility for any standing seam roof, including Galvalume. And while this isn’t a structural concern for your roof, it’s still worth being aware of as a possibility.

Oil canning is a wavy, distorted pattern that can spread across your roof. It doesn’t weaken your roof at all, but many property owners don’t like the way it looks. Thankfully, there is a way to drastically lower your roof’s risk of developing oil canning.

Developing oil canning is not a random event. It happens when inexperienced roofers install metal roofing panels too closely together, causing them to push against each other as they expand with the sun’s heat. And since it’s due to an installation error, you can minimize your risk by choosing experienced professionals for your Galvalume roof replacement.
Pro: Long-lasting Protection
Thanks to all of its durability features, a Galvalume roof will last for a long time. Even with all of Florida’s harmful weather, Galvalume steel still lasts for around 60 years. This is a good lifespan even for a metal roof since other types of metal roofing might only last around 40 years.

While metal roofs are more expensive than some other roofing materials, they’re worth the investment. A Galvalume roof, for example, will last more than twice as long as a standard shingle roof replacement. This more than makes up for the higher up-front costs of roof installation!
Con: Not Suited for Coastal Florida
Remember how we said that a Galvalume roof is resistant to rust? That’s still true, but there are limitations to this protection. Specifically, Galvalume steel may not be the best choice if you live on one of Florida’s coasts.

The root problem with coastal areas is the salt water. The salt works its way into the air, which can greatly speed up how fast a metal roof will develop rust. And while zinc and aluminum both have great rust-resistant qualities, they’re not immune, and these coatings can’t stand up to salt water over years. So if you live within a mile or two of the coast, you may want to choose another roofing material.
Pro: Low-cost Metal Roofing
When talking about affordable metal roofing, it’s important to have clear standards. An architectural shingle roof will always be cheaper than a metal roof. But when looking at how much metal roofing costs, a Galvalume steel roof costs a very reasonable amount.

So how much does it cost, exactly? The price range for a Galvalume steel roof is between $10 and $19 per square foot. While this isn’t a cheap price, it’s very affordable compared to other metal roofing costs. So if you want the protection of a metal roof without the sky-high prices, a Galvalume roof may be the perfect choice.

### The Value of Architectural Shingles for Florida Roof Replacements

Did you know that architectural shingles are the most popular roofing material across all of North America? 3-tab shingles used to dominate the roofing scene, but thanks to new advances in roofing technology, homeowners are raving about architectural shingles. But are these asphalt shingle roofs all they’re cracked up to be?

We’re PITCH Roofing, your local roofing partners. Our team of veteran roofers has seen it all across their years of Florida roofing experience, so we know how strong a roof needs to be to survive Florida’s weather. Since we want you to make an informed decision about your roof, let’s discuss what you need to know about architectural shingles!
Architectural Shingles’ Composition and History

When it comes down to it, architectural shingles are pretty simple and straightforward. They’re made with a fiberglass backboard for support and stability and then coated in asphalt for durability and waterproofing. Finally, manufacturers coat the shingle in protective mineral granules.

In theory, this is identical to how old 3-tab shingles used to work. But when architectural shingles hit the market in the 1970s, they came with some pretty big changes.

For one thing, architectural shingles are made with thicker layers of asphalt and fiberglass. This gives them more heft and strength, which really matters when a hurricane is raging around your home. It also makes them less likely for heavy rain to soak through your shingle roof.

Architectural shingles also have distinctive visual features. 3-tab shingles were known for their flat, segmented appearance. But architectural shingles have a distinctive pattern that creates the illusion of depth and dimension on your roof. For this reason, they’re also sometimes called dimensional shingles.

This covers the basics of architectural shingles, but there’s still more you need to know before deciding on a roof replacement material. For that, we’ll have to look at the protective features of these asphalt roofing shingles.
How Architectural Shingles Hold Up in Florida
Architectural shingles are popular across the US, but can they stand up against Florida’s weather? It’s no secret that roofs down here have it especially rough between hurricanes, UV exposure, and pests. Let’s see if dimensional shingles are up to the task of handling all of these dangers!
How Laminate Shingles Resist Water
Architectural shingles are also called laminate shingles thanks to the ceramic coating on each shingle, and this matters a lot when it comes to keeping your roof dry and secure. This laminate creates a water-resistant barrier to prevent rain from soaking through your shingle. Add on all that water-resistant asphalt and architectural shingles have very little to fear even from heavy downpours.

As a result of this great water protection, architectural shingles are also highly resistant to pests and mold, which often result from waterlogged shingles. By keeping your shingles dry and sturdy, these protective measures guard against much more than just rain!
Staying Strong in the Sunshine State
Many people are surprised to learn just how bad the sun is for your roof. It’s inescapable in Florida, but over time the sun will cause shingles to dry out and crack. This makes the damaged shingles all but useless in defending your home.

But remember those protective mineral granules we talked about? By packing them tightly onto each shingle, manufacturers greatly increase the UV resistance of architectural shingles. This means that your shingles will deflect some UV rays away from your home, protecting themselves and your roof as a whole.

With many different color options, you can even increase these UV-reflective properties. All you have to do is pick a light-colored shingle and enjoy the cooling effects of your new shingle roof!
Mitigating Hurricane-Force Winds
In Florida, storms with high winds are just a fact of life. Even without the occasional hurricane, tropical storms can reach winds up to 73 mph. Thankfully, architectural shingles are more than up to the task of withstanding these winds.

Most architectural shingles come with a wind rating between 110 and 130 mph. For context, 130 mph wind speeds are equivalent to a Category 4 hurricane. So while your roof will not be immune to high winds, it will be able to withstand even major hurricanes without issue.

If the winds exceed 130 mph, that doesn’t mean that your roof is going to blow away. However, you could lose some shingles in the storm. If this happens, you will need shingle roof repair services to install new shingles and make sure there’s no lingering water damage to your decking. That’s why, with any type of shingle roof, you should get a roof inspection after major storms!
Long-Lasting Durability
With all these protective features, you’d be right to assume that an architectural shingle roof will last you a long time. Older 3-tab shingles can only withstand Florida’s weather for about 15 years. But architectural shingles average 20-25 years of life, even in Florida.

For a shingle roof, that’s a very respectable lifespan. It’s certainly not as long as luxury roofing materials like metal roofing or tiles, but for this low of a price point, you will not find a better, longer-lasting roofing material.

With that in mind, it’s about time we talked about how much architectural shingle roofs cost in Florida.
Cost of Architectural Shingles in Florida

At Pitch, we understand that affordability is important. And if you’re looking for a budget-friendly shingle roof replacement, there is no better option than architectural shingles. In addition to their great protective features, these shingles come with very low manufacturing and installation costs.

So how much are they, exactly? It’s impossible to calculate the cost of your roof replacement without knowing the specifics of your roof’s situation. That said, architectural shingles generally cost between four and seven dollars per square foot. So if you had a 2,000-square-foot roof, then your new architectural shingle roof costs would be between $8,000 and $14,000.

The only roofing material cheaper than this is 3-tab shingles, which most reputable roofers have stopped using because of their poor performance in Florida. So if you want a high-value roofing system that won’t cost too much, architectural shingles are by far your best bet.

### Should You Get a 3-Tab Shingle Roof Replacement?

If you need an affordable shingle roof replacement, then you’re probably considering 3-tab shingles. For years, these asphalt shingles were the most popular roofing material in North America. But have new advances in roofing technology made this classic option outdated in today’s Florida?

We’re PITCH Roofing, and today we’re answering all of your questions about 3-tab asphalt shingles. As experienced Florida roofers, we know exactly how tough local roofs need to be, so let’s see if this shingle option has what it takes to protect your home in Florida.
What Are 3-Tab Shingles?

3-tab shingles are named for the three tabs on each shingle strip, creating the look of multiple shingles where there’s only one. This gives these asphalt shingles a distinctive, flat look that is easy to identify.

These shingles are made from a fiberglass baseboard that is coated in asphalt and given a topping of protective granules. The idea is for the fiberglass to provide structural stability while the asphalt is waterproofing. The mineral granules serve dual purposes of both providing color to the shingle and reducing damage from UV rays.

Invented in 1935, 3-tab shingles have a long history in North America. But do they hold up to modern roofing standards? To answer that, we’ll have to look at how these shingles perform.
Are 3-Tab Shingles Strong Enough for Florida Homes?
Few places in the US need stronger roofs than Florida. With hurricanes and tropical storms as an annual threat, your home needs to have strong protection against the wind and rain. And since we’re in the Sunshine State, you’ll also want a roofing material that the sun won’t wear down.

Let’s see if 3-tab shingles have what it takes to stand up to all of these local roofing hazards!
Wind Resistance
In Florida, hurricanes can whip up winds exceeding 140 mph. And even a tropical storm can create winds of up to 73 mph. Given these numbers, many homeowners are surprised to learn that 3-tab shingles are only rated for winds of up to 60 mph.

Does that mean that a roof with 3-tab shingles will be blown away by any hurricane that goes by? Not necessarily. But you can bet that when your area gets winds over 60 mph, you’re going to start losing shingles. When that happens during a hurricane, it could lead to extensive water damage that will not be cheap to fix and may even require another roof replacement.
Water Resistance
In theory, 3-tab shingles can keep water out of your home. However, these shingles are remarkably thin. As a result, they can become soaked through even with their water-resistant features like asphalt and protective coatings.

Another issue with the water resistance of a 3-tab shingle roof in Florida is related to its wind resistance. If a passing storm blows a shingle or two loose, you might not immediately notice. You might only see a problem when the damage is done, after the water has made its way in and caused leaks or roof sagging.
UV Resistance
While we often think of wind and rain as the big roof killers, the sun can be just as harmful. With shingles, it can lead to drying and cracking, which can ruin the shingle’s functionality. Thankfully, to some extent, 3-tab shingles can resist UV rays thanks to protective coatings and their granules.

The problem, though, is that we now have other shingles with granules that come more tightly packed. Whereas they’re loosely scattered on 3-tab shingles, they’re much more clumped together on modern shingles. This provides better UV resistance and prevents shingles from prematurely drying on your roof.
Why Do People Choose 3-Tab Shingles?
As you can see, 3-tab shingles don’t have too much going for them. Yes, they can technically withstand high winds and rains and UV rays, but only up to a certain point. And across the board, there are always shingle options that do all these things better.

So what’s the appeal of 3-tab shingles? Why do people keep choosing them, even as more and more roofers stop offering 3-tab shingle roof replacements?

In a word: price. 3-tab shingles have remarkably low up-front costs. In fact, you can often get 3-tab shingles installed for two or three dollars per square foot. That’s hands-down the cheapest roofing material on the market, at least when it comes to initial roof replacement costs.

We specify this because 3-tab shingles are not cheap in the long run. When you have something that thin and cheap to manufacture on your roof, it won’t stay for long. In the best-case scenario, it might last for 15 years, but there’s every possibility that your roof will fail before that date, especially in Florida where any major storm could seriously damage your roof.

At Pitch, we don’t offer 3-tab shingle roof replacements anymore. With so many better options on the market, it would be irresponsible to give you a roof that we knew couldn’t stand up to local weather patterns. But we’re happy to say that we can still give you an affordable shingle roof replacement that will last!
3 Tab Shingles - Video

The Best Alternative to 3-Tab Shingles

3-tab shingles used to be the most popular asphalt shingle option, but in 2024 it’s safe to say that architectural shingles are king. These improved shingles follow the same basic formulation as 3-tab, but they’re made up of much thicker, hardier layers to provide better protection.

This improves their resistance to wind, rain, and UV rays, but it’s not the only improvement. We also call these laminate shingles because of their protective laminate coatings to fight water and UV rays.

When it comes to aesthetics, architectural shingles are also known as dimensional shingles thanks to their unique patterning that creates dimension and depth on your roof that is greatly superior to the dull, flat look of 3-tab shingles.

There is one looming issue though, and that’s how much architectural shingles cost. We have good news on that front, too: Architectural shingles only cost four to six dollars per square foot. While this is more than 3-tab shingles, it’s still much more affordable than almost any other roofing material.

If you need an affordable shingle roof replacement, don’t choose 3-tab shingles. The cost may be low up-front, but you’ll pay for it across the lifetime of your roof. Instead, choose architectural shingles for a roof that will last 20-25 years and keep your home safe throughout its lifetime.

### Should I Get a Corrugated Metal Roof? 5V Roof Replacement Guide

For both homes and businesses, metal roofs are becoming a staple in Florida. And it makes sense — as Florida’s hurricanes get worse, property owners need stronger roofs that can stand up to the element. At the same time, though, many Floridians have concerns about metal roofing costs. Is a corrugated metal roof the solution?

It’s not as simple as a yes or no answer, but PITCH Roofing is here to walk you through everything you need to know about corrugated metal roofing. Keep reading for a step-by-step breakdown of corrugated metal roof pros, cons, and costs!
What Is a Corrugated Metal Roof?

There are a few names you might know a corrugated metal roof as: 5V roofing or exposed fastener metal roofing. But these all describe the same roofing system, which uses corrugated metal roof panels and drills them directly down onto your roof. Since the screws go through both the panel and roof decking, you can be confident that your roof isn’t going anywhere.

These roofs look noticeably different from standing seam metal roofs. Standing seam is mostly flat and smooth, whereas a corrugated metal roof has a distinctive S or V shape, with hills and valleys across each roofing panel.

This covers the basics of what a corrugated metal roof is, but this isn’t nearly enough information to make an informed decision on your roof. For that, you’ll have to consider the pros and cons of getting a corrugated metal roof replacement.
Pros and Cons of a Corrugated Metal Roof
There are both ups and downs to the unique designs of corrugated metal roofs. To figure out if the good outweighs the bad, you’ll need to look at this roofing material from many different angles. Let’s see what Pitch’s veteran roofers have to say about this metal roofing option!
Pro: Perfect Protection for Floridians
Metal roofing protects against the worst that Florida has to offer. In the Sunshine State, most weather that we see could do serious damage to your roof. Let’s look at how corrugated metal roofing handles each and every one of these problems:

 	High Winds: Corrugated metal roofs are rated for winds of up to 120 mph!
 	Rain: When properly installed, a 5V roof creates a water-tight barrier that not even Florida’s downpours can break through.
 	Sun Exposure: Metal roofs resist UV rays by reflecting them away from your structure, which also helps reduce monthly energy bills.
 	Mold: Unlike shingle roofs, metal roofs can’t be soaked through and develop mold! This also reduces the risk of pest infestations.

For all of these reasons, a corrugated metal roof is a great choice if you want to Florida-proof your roof!
Con: Faster Wear and Tear
Because it uses exposed fasteners, a corrugated metal roof will age faster than one with hidden fasteners. Over time, the elements can wear down the fasteners on your roof. Realistically, this doesn’t mean that your roof is going to be blown off your home or business. But it does mean that water could use these penetrations to infiltrate your roofing system.

It isn’t all bad news, though. For one thing, you can lower your roof’s risk by choosing reliable installers who can set your roof up for a long, healthy life. And although corrugated metal roofs age faster, they can still last for 30-45 years. That’s significantly more than even the best architectural shingle roof!
Pro: Affordable Metal Roofing
If there’s one problem that almost everyone has with metal roofing, it’s the cost. Standing seam roofs can cost $25 per square foot or more in Florida, and that simply isn’t a reasonable number for most Floridians. Thankfully, getting a corrugated metal roof is much more affordable.

5V metal roofing costs between five and 12 dollars per square foot for both manufacturing and installation, making it less than half the cost of a standing seam roof. This makes it much more affordable for Floridians to hurricane-proof their roofs!
Con: Requires Regular Maintenance

Remember how we mentioned that a corrugated metal roof will age faster than other metal roofs? That comes with increased maintenance. But before you give up on this affordable metal roofing option, let’s talk about what that really means.

The problem with these roofs is the exposed fasteners. As the roof gets older, these fasteners can loosen. And when that happens, it creates opportunities for both water and pests. To keep these things out of your roofing system, you’ll need regular maintenance as your roof gets older.

This doesn’t have to be a huge investment of time or money, though. There is very little risk of your fasteners loosening in the first handful of years after its installation, and after that, a yearly inspection will be enough to make sure that the fasteners stay tight. When they do start to loosen, having them tightened shouldn’t even be an expensive repair!
Pro: No Risk of Oil Canning
With standing seam metal roofs, oil canning is a real possibility as the roof ages. This unsightly sign of aging doesn’t weaken a roof’s structure, but it does dampen the overall appearance of the roof. And luckily, it’s not something that you have to worry about with a corrugated metal roof.

Oil canning happens when standing seam roofs are adhered together too tightly, so it’s a non-issue for 5V roofs. This is partially why it’s not as simple as saying that one type of metal roofing is better than the other. They both have their benefits and flaws, and it’s up to you to decide which one suits your structure best!

### The Good and the Bad of EPDM Roofing in Florida

EPDM roofing got a major upgrade in the 1990s, and it changed the flat roofing game. While this improved EPDM is still new on the scene, roofers and property owners alike are raving about its durability and longevity. But is this flat roofing material strong enough to handle Florida’s unique weather patterns? And how does it compare to other flat roofing options on the market?

We’re here to answer all these questions and more. PITCH Roofing was founded to solve Florida’s rampant roofing issues, and today we want to do that by sharing the must-know information about EPDM roofing membranes. Keep reading for more information on pros and cons, costs, and everything else to know about this rubber roof!
What Is EPDM Roofing?

EPDM (ethylene propylene diene monomer) roofing was originally developed in the 1950s, but the version we know today has many differences. While they’re both rubberized flat roofing systems, EPDM roofing got a major update in the 1990s.

Initially, EPDM showed signs of having weak flashing. This allowed leaks and damage to wear at the edges over time. But thanks to new advancements in flashing technology in the 1990s, today’s EPDM roofs are much better at repelling water and staying strong even across decades.

EPDM roofing as we know it today is strong and durable. It’s also more versatile than many other flat roofing materials, coming in both black and white. This affords you the flexibility to get a roof that matches your preferences!

This covers the basics of EPDM roofing, but you probably still have a lot of questions. To answer those, let’s talk about some of the biggest advantages of EPDM roofs.
Pros of EPDM Roofing in Florida
There are a lot of things to love about EPDM roofing. Keep reading to see the best features that these rubber roofs have to offer!
Solid Longevity
The lifespan of your flat roof is one of the most important factors in a roof replacement. And EPDM compares well with other low-slope roofing materials with a lifespan of 20 years when properly installed.

This is about average when compared to flat roofing materials, which don’t last as long as sloped roofing materials (like shingles or tiles). The reason for this difference is that flat roofs, especially in Florida, have a tough job of keeping water away from the vulnerable parts of your roofing system. And in hurricane-prone Florida, 20 years of protection is nothing to sneeze at.
Easy to Repair
As a rubberized roof, EPDM is fast and easy to repair. If your roof were to tear, for instance, it would be simple for a roofer to patch the tear with a rubber patch kit.

For more major repairs, entire sections of your flat roof may need to be replaced. But this will still be comparatively affordable and quick since EPDM roofing is among the easiest roofing materials to install. And the less time that roofers have to spend installing your roof, the less they’ll charge!
Energy Efficiency
Many people are surprised to learn that EPDM roofing is as energy-efficient as it is. This advantage comes from several different factors. First, since EPDM is available in white, it can help reflect UV rays away from your home, which is both good for the material and your energy bill.

Even if you get a black EPDM roof, though, it still has some energy efficiency. That’s because the materials that make up EPDM roofing are also great insulators. With great thermal insulation, EPDM can help keep your structure at a consistent temperature and keep your air conditioning system from working too hard in the summer months.
Cons of EPDM Roofing in Florida
While EPDM roofing has a lot going for it, no roof is 100% resistant to all threats. Let’s talk about the downsides of EPDM so that you can make an informed decision for your property.
Vulnerability to Trapped Water
Like all flat roofing materials, EPDM roofs are especially vulnerable to water pooling. This happens when a contractor or DIYer improperly installs a flat roof. Well-installed flat roofs have a slight slope to them to help water move off your roof, but a truly flat roof will allow water to pool.

Over time, this trapped water can wear away at an EPDM roof and lead to a total roof failure. That’s why it’s essential to carefully choose local roofing contractors who understand both how flat roofs work and local ordinances for your county.
High Puncture Risk
As a rubber roofing system, EPDM roofs can be punctured by storm debris or hail. When this happens, it could lead to leaks or other issues in your roofing system. And while protective coatings can mitigate this risk, there’s no way to remove it entirely.

That’s why proper roof maintenance is important. If you notice a leak in your roof, it’s important to immediately reach out to roofers for leak repair services. The silver lining is that since EPDM roofing is so quick and easy to repair, it shouldn’t take much out of your monthly budget!
How Much Does EPDM Roofing Cost?

Price is another major factor in every roof replacement. And we have good news: EPDM roofing is one of the most affordable flat roofing materials. Thanks to its low cost to manufacture and install, EPDM roofs are extremely budget-friendly for most Floridians.

So how much do they cost, exactly? Including manufacturing and installation, EPDM roofing costs between $3.50 and $10 per square foot. This makes them an affordable option for small jobs like carports as well as larger, commercial roofing projects!

We know this is a wide cost range, but it’s the most accuracy we can give without seeing your roof first. And to get a more accurate, reliable estimate, all you have to do is ask!

### How to Find Affordable Roofers in Your Community

When you need affordable roofers near you, call PITCH Roofing. We were founded by roofing veterans who saw the state of the Florida roofing industry and decided to do their part to help. Now, we provide affordable roofing services across the Sunshine State.

But we’re not just here to talk about ourselves. We’re also here to share essential information about warning signs of bad roofers — many of whom brag about being affordable, when the truth is that they provide low-value roofing services that aren’t worth what you pay. And while everyone wants to save money, the most important thing is making sure that your structure has a strong, dependable roof.

We know that it’s not easy to find affordable roofers in Florida. But there are budget-friendly roofing options available in your community. Now, let’s talk about how you find them.
The Problem with Finding Affordable Roofers in Florida


Many hurdles can get in the way of finding affordable roofers. Fluctuating prices, predatory roofers, and the fine line between affordable and cheap are all complicating factors.

But we can simplify these issues so that you know how to navigate them. One by one, let’s break down the local issues that make it hard to find budget-friendly roofing contractors.
Ever-changing Roofing Costs
It’s no secret that prices increase over time across nearly every industry. But the roofing industry is especially prone to significant swings in cost.

This is partially because of the sheer variety of materials that roofers work with. Asphalt shingles, clay tiles, metal roofs — they all require wildly different base materials. And the costs for these things are always changing. So we could see one month where the price of shingles is up 20%, and then when it stabilizes in a month, the metal roofing cost will have jumped significantly instead.

This makes it hard for consumers to know if they’re getting a good deal. After all, if you got a quote three months ago and now every quote you get is much higher, it could feel like nobody is willing to give you affordable roofing services. But the truth may be that the definition of “affordable” has changed over the past 90 days.

There is one way around this, though: moving quickly. Collect as many estimates as you need to, but collect them back to back so that there’s little time between them. Then, pick the roofers you like best and get locked in at that rate. Because while you can’t lower roofing prices, you can get in before the next big price jump.

It can be intimidating to act fast like this, but remember that roofing prices only increase over time, so this is the best way to get your roof done before the industry sees another large shift.
Predatory Roofers
You’ve probably heard the horror stories about unreliable roofers. They come in, they promise the best, most affordable roofing services, and once they’re paid, you never hear from them again. Sadly, this scenario has been a reality for many Floridians over the past decade.

In fact, Florida is heavily targeted by predatory roofers. We call them storm chasers — fly-by-night roofers who blow into town after a storm. They go around offering dirt-cheap roof replacements and repairs but never deliver on the great results they promise. While there isn’t a way to stop them knocking on your door, there are ways to identify these scammers masquerading as affordable roofers.

First, you should make sure to only work with local roofing professionals. If a company doesn’t have an established local headquarters, then you shouldn’t do business with them. Why? Because it’s a surefire sign that they’re going to be out of the state in a few weeks. And when that happens, you’ll have nobody to hold accountable for the state of your roof.

You should also be wary of roofers who insist on working directly with your homeowners insurance. Scam roofers often over-charge your insurance company, which has contributed to the growing homeowners insurance crisis. A reliable, affordable roofing company, though, should be open to a variety of financing options and not make you feel pressured to use your insurance just so they can bill them for extra money.
Cheap vs. Affordable Roofing


Roofing is expensive, and it’s natural to want affordable roofers who can give you a better price. At the same time, though, you have to be careful not to settle for cheap roofing. Let’s talk about the difference between these two things.

Affordable roofers will offer you high-quality work at a fair, honest price. They will discuss costs with you, but there will be a limit to how far they can come down. At the end of the day, everyone needs to eat. This means you might not get the absolute lowest cost even from honest and fair roofers. But good, affordable roofers like Pitch routinely offer fair prices based on the real market prices, not just markups for the sake of extra profit.

Cheap roofing is a whole other ball game. When a cheap roofer is at your door, they’ll probably offer you an unbeatable price — something like a brand-new shingle roof on a 1,700-square-foot home for $8,000. But there are only two possible reasons that they could or would offer such a low price.

The first is that they simply don’t plan to do the job. You’d be shocked how often roofers take huge deposits on roof replacements and then leave town, never to be seen again.

Or, if they plan to do the job, you can bet that they’ll do it poorly. If they promise a shingle roof, they’ll use cheap 3-tab shingles that other roofers have stopped using because they’re unreliable. And instead of sending experts onto your roof, they’ll send inexperienced subcontractors who may have never even been on a roof before that day. That means the final result will be a cheap, poorly installed roof that likely wouldn’t survive a tropical storm.

Now that we’ve talked about who cheap roofers are and what they’re really about, let’s talk about how to identify the real deal: affordable roofers in your community.
Tips for Finding Affordable Roofers in Florida
Just like there are ways to spot the bad guys, there are also signs that you’re dealing with genuine affordable roofers. As veteran roofers ourselves, we know exactly how to tell honest workers apart from scammers.

First, only work with roofers who are based in Florida. For example, Pitch is headquartered in Pinellas County because we’re owned and operated by locals. An established presence in Florida guarantees that you’ll be able to get answers to your questions if there’s a problem with your roof, and it shows that we know how to handle Florida’s unique roofing needs better than traveling roofers would. In most cases, location is the cornerstone of affordable roofing.

You should also ensure that your roofers have all of the necessary licensing and insurance to work in your county. Don’t just settle for a piece of paper, either. Ask for the number of their contractor’s license so that you can look it up for yourself. This way, you’ll know that you’re working with licensed professionals instead of scammers preying on ignorance.

But ultimately, the best way to tell if you’re dealing with an affordable roofing company is to see how they handle their roofing estimates.

### How Much Does a Metal Roof Cost in the Greater Tampa Bay Area?

Everybody raves about metal roofs — their longevity, their weather resistance, and even their looks all have huge appeal. But how much a new metal roof costs is a pain point for many Floridians. But with the looming homeowners insurance crisis and increasingly frequent storms, it may be worth looking into what type of metal roof you can afford.

Luckily, PITCH Roofing is here to help. As professionals on all forms of roofing in Florida, we know that there’s a huge range of metal roofing costs. Today, we want to explain your metal roofing options to get you a roof that will protect your property without sacrificing curb appeal or personal style.

To get started, let’s quickly review what you should know about metal roofing.
The Value of Metal Roofing in Florida


In the local roofing industry, almost all contractors agree that metal is one of the best roofing options for Florida. Some of its key features are:

 	Long Lifespan: A well-installed metal roof can last for 40-70 years! This is partially why many consider even high metal roof costs to be worth the investment.
 	Wind Resistance: Top-quality shingle roofs struggle with winds in excess of 110 mph. But with metal roofing, your roof can easily withstand winds up to 140 mph or more!
 	Mold and Pest Resistance: Mold and pest infestations find little to no chance to develop on a metal roof, which keeps it healthy and secure in the long term.
 	Water Resistance: Unlike shingles, metal can’t be soaked through. As a result, metal roofs can better protect your structure and keep it dry.
 	UV Resistance: It’s no secret that the Florida Sun is a major roof killer. But because metal roofs reflect UV rays away from your structure, they can better handle the heat and lower your energy bills.

Given all of these great features of metal roofing, you’d think that you’d see them all across the Sunshine State. While metal roofs are becoming more common, many people still get hung up on how much a metal roof costs. And while part of this disconnect is due to real financial issues, many people simply assume a metal roof is more expensive than it is.

Usually, someone will see a top-of-the-line metal roof, ask how much it costs, and be astounded when the price is $30,000 or more. But while some metal roofs cost this much, many more metal roofing options are available at much lower prices.

With this in mind, let’s talk about the latest updates on the cost of a metal roof replacement in Florida.
The Cost of a Metal Roof in Florida
While metal roofs can be extremely expensive, there are plenty of more affordable roofing options. Most people assume that these cost differences come down to material differences, and they’re right, to some extent; a Galvalume roof costs much less than a copper roof, for example.

But the bigger metal roof cost factor is how your roof is fastened to your structure. Metal roofs come with two distinctive styles of fasteners, hidden and exposed, and which one you choose will profoundly impact your total metal roofing costs.

With that in mind, let’s talk about how much each of these metal roofing options will cost and, just as importantly, how they’ll perform.
Exposed Fastener Metal Roof Costs
Also called corrugated metal roofing or 5V, metal roofs with exposed fasteners are drilled down onto your structure. With screws across the length of your roof, this approach ensures that your roof is securely adhered.

Because corrugated metal roofing panels are easy to manufacture and quick to install, 5V metal roof costs are generally low. Costs range from as low as five dollars up to $12 per square foot. Or, on a 2,000-square-foot roof, from $10,000 to $24,000.

Metal roofs with exposed fasteners don’t last quite as long as roofs with hidden fasteners, but they’re still much more durable with shingles and can stand up to Florida’s harsh weather. And with a price range that’s much more appealing than other types of metal roofing, 5V metal roofing is a great, more affordable option.
Standing Seam Metal Costs
Metal roofs with hidden fasteners are called standing seam. These metal roofing panels are much flatter, with only a small line where the seams lock together. This is their “hidden” seam, which attaches from beneath the panel rather than on top of it.

This process is more expensive to make and requires more time and know-how to install, so naturally standing seam metal roofs cost more than 5V. Specifically, standing seam metal roof prices in Florida range from $10 to $25 on average. Using our metric of the 2,000-square-foot roof, that puts your metal roof replacement costs between $20,000 and $50,000.

A standing seam metal roof is the top-performing metal roofing option. It lasts a long time, it stands up to Florida’s weather, and its sleek aesthetic is perfect for homes in Florida. Of course, its price is not affordable for everyone. But if you want to invest in your property and aren't worried about metal roof costs, there’s no better option than standing seam.
Metal Roofing Material Costs


We’ve covered how your choice of fasteners will impact the cost of your metal roofing system. But the type of metal roofing material you choose will also impact the total metal roofing costs.

However, we can’t say exactly how much each material will cost. That’s because your choice of fastener will heavily impact the cost regardless of the material type. Instead, we can tell you how much each metal roofing material costs relative to other options. This way, you’ll have some idea of what materials could put you in the higher or lower cost range for your metal roof of choice.

With that in mind, the metal roofing materials in order from the lowest cost to the most expensive are as follows:

 	Galvanized steel
 	Galvalume steel
 	Aluminum
 	Zinc
 	Copper

This list should help you when trying to get a good price on your new metal roof. For example, if you’re extremely concerned with budget, then the best choice for you may be a galvanized steel 5V metal roof. But the only way to know how much your new roof will cost is with a free roofing estimate.

### How Your Roof Could Save You from the Homeowners Insurance Crisis

Did you know that Florida is in a crisis? The homeowners insurance crisis has left countless Floridians with no means to protect their homes. And day by day, more insurers pull out of Florida and leave their policyholders with little time to find new insurers in an increasingly challenging market.

It’s a difficult situation, but there are still things you can do to protect yourself and your property. We’re PITCH Roofing, your local roofing partners. And today, we’re walking you through the homeowners insurance crisis in Florida and what you can do to give yourself the best odds of keeping your policy and saving money.
The State of the Florida Homeowners Insurance Crisis


Since 2017, 11 of the major homeowners insurance providers in the state of Florida have liquidated, and even more have simply terminated their policies in the state. But why is this happening?
Natural Disasters
There are many factors contributing to this ongoing crisis. For one thing, hurricanes are becoming both more common and more severe. In 2018, the federal government estimated that Florida spent between five and ten billion dollars recovering from hurricanes.

That number is likely outdated, as climate change has caused hurricanes to worsen over time. We are already seeing more and more hurricanes and severe weather events every year. Scientists theorize that the warmer water could provide more opportunities for hurricanes and other tropical storms.

Insurance companies are businesses, so when they have to start paying out more policies for higher values, their profit margins slim down. When that number gets low enough, they decide to leave Florida for an area where natural disasters aren’t as common or as costly.
Rising Property Values
Another part of this problem is that property in Florida has become substantially more expensive over the past decade. In fact, the median home sales price in Florida for 2023 was $415,300. Many people take out policies worth at least the value of their homes, so policy sizes have only increased alongside the cost of a home.

And when the insurance companies have to pay out these policies, they take a serious financial blow, especially at the higher rates that we’re seeing tropical storms. In this way, the problem compounds itself and gets worse over time.

As you can see, this is a large issue that no individual can solve by themself. And truthfully, there’s no way to guarantee that your insurer won’t leave Florida. But you can take steps to protect your home and give yourself the best possible chance of a low-cost, reliable homeowners insurance policy.

Most Common Shingle Roof Repairs

If you’ve noticed an issue with your roofing system, you don’t want just anyone on your roof to fix it. Sure, it’s simple to hammer a shingle into place, but securing your roof requires much more expertise and know-how than that.

We want to give you complete peace of mind when you choose our PITCH Roofing contractors. Today, let us show you that we know shingle roofs inside and out as we walk you through the most common shingle roof repairs in Florida:

 	Replace Missing or Damaged Shingles: Florida’s climate is uniquely good at destroying individual shingles. When it cracks or removes them entirely, our roofers will install new shingles and ensure that there’s no residual damage to other parts of your roofing system.
 	Seal Leaks: Problems with your flashing or ventilation can lead to leaks. Our crew can seal these areas and fix the source of any leaks.
 	Fixing Nail Pops: As temperatures fluctuate, nails used to secure shingles may pop out, leading to potential water leaks. We hammer these nails back in and seal the area to prevent further damage.

 	Replacing Damaged Flashing: Flashing, typically made of metal or rubber, seals joints and transitions on the roof. Damaged or deteriorated flashing can lead to leaks, so we replace it to maintain your roof’s watertight seal.

As you can see, there are a lot of ways that shingle roofs can need repairs in Florida. And when an issue pops up, it’s important that you act quickly to protect your home.

### How to Choose a Metal Roof vs. Shingles

If you’re due for a new roof, you’re probably tempted to upgrade to a metal roof. A lot of Floridians are — metal roofs are more durable, better able to handle storms, and they last longer than shingles. Despite these benefits, though, many Floridians are still on the fence when it comes to choosing a metal roof vs. shingles.

We’re here to help you make a decision. And when you need expert advice on roofing in Florida, there are no better experts than those at PITCH Roofing. Let’s talk about the deciding factors between metal and shingle roofs to help you get ready for your upcoming roof replacement!
The Value of a Metal Roof vs. Shingles


You might already know that metal roofs are more expensive than shingle roofs. But just how much more expensive, exactly? To tell which roof is better for your home, it’s important to know the value of each roofing material.

Of course, there’s a wide price range for both metal and shingle roofs. For example, a copper roof will cost substantially more than a roof made with Galvalume. But if we’re looking at average metal roofing costs, those tend to fall between $10 and $18 per square foot.

Shingles come at a much more budget-friendly price. Shingle roofing costs are generally low, even for high-quality architectural shingles. In fact, these shingles generally cost between five and eight dollars per square foot.

Comparing these numbers, we can see that a 2,000-square-foot metal roof replacement would cost between $20,000 to $36,000. That same roof would cost between $10,000 and $16,000 to replace with asphalt shingles.

As you can see, a shingle roof replacement costs roughly half as much as a metal roof replacement. But the price tag shouldn’t be the only way that you determine the value of your roof. To fully understand the value of a metal roof vs. shingles, you’ll have to consider what kind of product your money buys you.
Long-term Roofing Maintenance Costs
Nobody could deny that metal roofs cost more up-front than shingle roofs. You don’t just pay for your roof once, though. You pay for it across its lifespan, so you should consider what kind of bills your new roof could wrack up over the years.

And if you want a roof that won’t need a lot of repairs, then a metal roof might be worth that higher price point. While metal roofs are rated for winds of 140+ mph, high-quality shingle roofs are usually rated for around 110 mph winds. When a storm comes through and blows shingles off one roof, the metal roof next door will be completely undamaged and won’t require any repairs.

Across the lifespan of your roof, this represents savings of thousands of dollars. And it’s doubled when you consider all of the things that metal roofs can protect your home against better than shingles, including:

 	Fire: Metal roofs are non-combustible.
 	Hail: Metal roofs are highly resistant to denting, while hail can cause roofing shingles to bend or break off.
 	Leaks: Metal roofs have fewer seams and joints than shingle roofs, reducing the risk of leaks and water infiltration over time.
 	Pests: Since metal roofs don’t have as many entry points as shingles, they’re much more resistant to common pests like bugs and mice.
 	Mold: Year-round humidity is a serious problem for Florida roofs, but since metal roofs don’t absorb moisture like shingle roofs, they’re better able to resist mold and mildew.

You should consider all of these factors when determining what kind of roof you can afford. After all, saving a bit of money now doesn’t help when you’ll just spend that money on repairs in the future.
Think of Future Metal Roof vs. Shingle Roof Replacements


Finally, when deciding between a metal roof vs. shingles, you should try to think about your future roof replacements. After all, whatever roof you decide to get probably won’t be the last one that your home ever sees. So it only makes sense to compare the costs of roof replacements over time to make a truly equal comparison. And when we do that, metal roofing starts to look a lot more appealing.

Let’s start by looking at how long these roof replacements will last. An asphalt shingle roof will, under the best circumstances, last about 25 years with proper installation and maintenance. This isn’t bad, but it doesn’t hold a candle to the 50-70 years you can expect a metal roof to last in Florida.

When we look at it this way, you can see that one metal roof replacement lasts as long as two shingle roof replacements. This means we should mentally double the cost of a shingle roof replacement in order to compare it to the value of a metal roofing system. When we do this, it’s clear that a metal roof costs about as much as a shingle roof in the long run. And with a metal roof, you at least get enhanced security and minimal repairs over the years.
