### TPO Roof Replacements: Pros, Cons, and Cost!

Did you know that flat roofs have very different needs from sloped roofs? It’s true; flat roofs need to be much more water-resistant than sloped roofing materials to protect against leaks. And when it comes to water resistance, no roofing material can top TPO roofing.

We’re PITCH Roofing, and today we’re explaining everything you need to know about TPO flat roofs. As your trusted local roofing partners, let us answer all of your questions about TPO pros and cons, cost, and other factors so that you can make an informed decision for your flat roof replacement!
TPO Roofing 101

The first thing to know about TPO, thermoplastic polyolefin, is that it’s a single-ply roofing membrane. In other words, it’s a rubber roofing system that applies in one layer across the length of your roof. And that’s the perfect roofing system for a flat roof.

TPO roofing suits flat roofs because it addresses the biggest issue that flat roofs run into: poor drainage. While water shouldn’t be trapped on your TPO roof for long if it’s been properly installed, it will always take longer for a flat roof to drain than a sloped roof. That’s time that water is just sitting on your roof and looking for a way in.

Thankfully, TPO roofing is completely waterproof. This ensures that your roof won’t develop leaks while it waits for water to run off. Whereas a sloped roofing material like shingles would be totally soaked through, TPO stands strong and keeps your roof safe and dry.
Advantages of TPO Roofing
As we’ve established, TPO roofing does a great job of resisting leaks and water damage. But that isn’t the only reason it’s popular. Let’s talk about some of the other great features of a rubber roof:

 	Good Lifespan: A properly installed TPO roof can last for up to 25 years. This may not seem long, but in the world of flat roofing, this is a long life for a roofing system.
 	UV Reflection: Thanks to its white composition, TPO roofing actively resists and reflects UV rays. This means lower energy bills and increased durability!
 	
 	Puncture Resistance: Punctures from storm debris are one of the biggest issues that rubber roofs face. But TPO roofing is hardy and able to resist puncture damage, ensuring protection for the more vulnerable parts of your roofing system.
 	Strong Seams: TPO roofing uses air-welded seams, which are especially durable and hardy. So once your roof is installed, you can trust that it’s not going anywhere!

All of these factors make TPO roofing one of the best flat roofing materials in Florida. But there’s no such thing as a “perfect” roofing material, so it’s important to be aware of the negatives as well as the positives.
Downsides of TPO Roofing
Knowing the downsides of your roofing material is just as important as knowing its strengths. With that in mind, let’s talk about the cons of getting a TPO roof:

 	Brand New: In the world of roofing materials, TPO is very young. It came out in the 90s, so while it’s been around for almost 30 years, that isn’t enough time to know everything that can go wrong with these roofs. That said, so far they’ve performed quite well!
 	Requires Maintenance: Like all flat roofs, a TPO roof will need repairs as it ages. Specifically, you may start to notice problems with leaks in the later years of its life.
 	Variations: Since this is a new roofing material, nobody is sure what the “best” formulation is. As a result, manufacturers offer a variety of different thicknesses and components. That’s why you need experienced Florida roofers who know what works in our unique climate!

All things considered, even the bad side of TPO roofing isn’t that bad. But we know that there’s one big part of TPO roofing that we haven’t talked about: the price of a new TPO roof in Florida.
Cost of a TPO Roof in Florida

We know that everyone is worried about the price of a roof replacement. But the good news is that TPO is a very budget-friendly flat roofing option. This is thanks to its low-cost manufacturing as well as its relatively simple and easy installation, which keeps labor costs down.

So how much does a TPO roof replacement cost? In Florida, you can expect to pay between $12 and $18 per square foot, including installation costs. So if your flat roof was 2,000 square feet, then the cost of your new TPO roof would be between $24,000 and $36,000.

While this isn’t as affordable as a modified bitumen roof, it’s still a very good price. That’s especially true when you consider the durability and longevity of TPO roofing. For many property owners, they view the price of a new TPO roof as an investment in the property. And when you think about it this way, doesn’t it make sense to get a high-value roof instead of the cheapest available?

### Standing Seam Metal Roof Pros and Cons for Floridians

Have you noticed more and more metal roofs cropping up across Central Florida and the Greater Tampa Bay region? It’s not just you — Floridians are increasingly relying on metal roofs to protect their homes against hurricanes and other extreme weather events. And specifically, standing seam metal roof replacements have become extremely popular for residential structures.

There are lots of reasons for this, and we’re going to walk you through them all. We’re PITCH Roofing, your local roofing partner with decades of experience. Keep reading to see real insights from our local experts on all things standing seam!
What Is a Standing Seam Metal Roof?


Many people are surprised that the designation “standing seam metal roof” has nothing to do with the type of metal or coatings applied to your roof. Rather, it’s all about your metal roof’s fasteners.

A standing seam metal roof has hidden fasteners. In other words, the metal panels slot together underneath the panel and are adhered that way. This is notably different from 5V metal roofs, which are screwed into your roof from the top down.

While this may seem like a small difference, having hidden fasteners gives many advantages to standing seam metal roofs. But at the same time, it can also lead to problems for some homeowners looking for metal roof replacements.
Pros and Cons of Standing Seam Metal Roofs
While standing seam roofs are popular and high-quality, they aren’t perfect. And if you don’t know the upsides and downsides of having a standing seam metal roof, you could have some nasty surprises waiting for you.

We’re here to make sure you’re informed, so let’s talk about the good and the bad of a standing seam metal roof replacement!
Pro: The Best Metal Roof for Homes
Sometimes people avoid metal roofs for their homes because they don’t want their new roof to look industrial. This is understandable, but it’s also not something that you have to worry about with a standing seam metal roof.

Thanks to their hidden fasteners, standing seam metal roofs have a sleek, smooth profile. This perfectly suits residential structures and creates a very modern aesthetic without looking industrial.
Con: High Metal Roofing Costs


There are many great things about standing seam roofs, but their price point is not one of them. Metal roofing in general tends to be expensive, especially if you’re comparing it to asphalt shingle roofing. But because of the high cost to manufacture standing seam panels and their difficult installation process, getting this type of metal roof is not cheap.

So what’s the damage? A standing seam metal roof costs between $10 and $35 per square foot, but their average price is closer to $20 per square foot. This price can fluctuate depending on the particulars of your roof and local pricing factors, which is why the price range is so large. To get a more accurate number for your metal roof replacement, we strongly recommend getting a free roofing estimate from trusted roofers.
Pro: Great Durability and Minimal Maintenance
Standing seam metal roofs don’t just look great. They’re also among the hardiest and most durable roofing materials available in Florida. Let’s talk about just a handful of the ways that standing seam roofs stand up to Florida’s weather:

 	Thanks to their hidden fasteners, standing seam metal roofs can expand and contract with the Sun’s heat, which prevents premature aging of your roofing system.
 	Standing seam roofs can resist winds of up to 140 mph, which means they can withstand a Category 4 hurricane!
 	Most metal roofs in Florida receive anti-rust coatings, which will prevent the year-round humidity from wearing on your roof.

Because of these protective features, standing seam metal roofs need very little maintenance. So if you want a metal roof that you don’t have to worry too much about, choose standing seam!
Con: Potential Oil Canning
Oil canning sometimes happens on standing seam roofs, and while it doesn’t structurally weaken your roof, it’s certainly unsightly. But what even is oil canning?

Oil canning is a process that can happen when your standing seam panels are adhered together too tightly. This starts as a bubbling due to your roof trying and failing to expand with the heat, and it eventually leads to wavy patterns on your otherwise smooth roof. This can slightly, but not drastically, decrease your home’s curb appeal.

The good news is that you can avoid oil canning. It only happens when roofers incorrectly install the panels and place them too close together. This is part of why choosing reputable roofers is so important!
Pro: Long-lasting Protection
One of the best features of a standing seam roof is how long it lasts. Whereas your typical shingle roof might last 20 or even 25 years, a properly installed standing seam metal roof can last for 50-60 years.

This long lifespan is one of the biggest reasons that people choose standing seam metal roofs. But to get a roof that lasts this long, you’ll have to carefully choose your contractors. Even minor issues during installation, like scraping paint off your panels, could allow rust to set in and shorten the lifespan of your roof.

That’s why it’s crucial to be picky about your roofing contractors. And at Pitch, we certainly don’t expect you to accept that we’re the best around just because we say so. Instead, we prove our competence. And that starts with your free roofing estimate!

### Pros and Cons of a Modified Bitumen Roof

If you’re in the market for a flat roof replacement, then a modified bitumen roof is certainly worth considering. After all, mod bit roofs are some of the most common flat roofs in Florida! But are these roofs really worth the investment in your property? And what do you need to know about the downsides of modified bitumen roofing?

PITCH Roofing is here to answer all of these questions and more. Our team of roofers has decades of local roofing experience, and today we’re using that to explain the good and the bad about modified bitumen. But before we get too deep into the pros and cons, let’s talk about the basics of modified bitumen roofing that you’ll want to know.
Modified Bitumen Roofs Explained


Modified bitumen is unique thanks to its asphalt-based composition. Whereas other flat roofing options are based primarily on rubber, mod bit’s asphalt can be modified to provide different types of protection to your structure.

For example, mod bit usually comes in two types: SBS and APP. SBS (styrene-butadiene-styrene) mod bit uses a rubberized polymer to make the asphalt more elastic and flexible, which helps protect against two of Florida’s largest issues: heavy rains and high winds. APP (atactic polypropylene) mod bit, on the other hand, uses a plasticized polymer that will only expand under high temperatures. This helps it withstand Florida’s year-round UV exposure.

Regardless of what type of modified bitumen roof you get, though, the good and the bad of mod bit look largely the same. And if you need a flat roof replacement, knowing what to expect from your new roof is crucial.
Modified Bitumen Roofing - Video

Pros and Cons of a Modified Bitumen Roof
Modified bitumen roofing came about as the successor to built-up roofing (BUR). And by improving on this old-school roofing material, mod bit has increased its strength and removed many key weaknesses of BUR.
Now, let’s talk about what this new and improved flat roofing material can do for you!
Pro: Low Flat Roof Replacement Costs
Part of what makes mod bit roofing so popular is its affordable price point. Pricing factors can cause exact numbers to vary, but generally, a modified bitumen roof costs four to eight dollars per square foot.

The average size for a roof is generally considered to be around 1,700 square feet. So on an “average” roof, a modified bitumen roof replacement would cost between $6,800 and $13,600. This low cost is thanks to how cost-effective mod bit is to manufacture and how easy it is to install.

As a result, modified bitumen is one of the most affordable flat roofing materials. So if budget is a primary concern for your flat roof replacement, mod bit could be just what you need.
Con: Unremarkable Life Expectancy
Lifespan, like cost, is usually one of the biggest factors when considering a flat roof replacement. And while modified bitumen comes at a great price point, it’s important to consider how long your new roof will last.

A modified bitumen roof will last for a fair amount of time, but there are undeniably other options that last longer. Specifically, modified bitumen roofs average 15-20 years of life. A TPO flat roof, on the other hand, could last 20-25 years.

This is why it’s not enough to just look at price or any one factor. By knowing both the good and the bad, you can better determine the total value of your new roofing system.
Pro: Thick, Durable Composition
Single-ply roofing membranes are popular for their flexibility and water resistance. But modified bitumen isn’t a single-ply roofing material. Instead, it’s usually made of two or three layers of asphalt, fiberglass, and either plastic or rubber polymers.

For example, your average single-ply roofing membrane is around 60 mils thick. A two-ply modified bitumen roof, however, is closer to 240 mils thick. This offers increased protection against storm debris and other sources of puncture damage that could easily cause a leak in a thin roofing system.
Con: Attracts Heat and UV Rays
In most cases, modified bitumen roofs are black. As a result, they tend to attract more heat than other flat roofing materials. In fact, even when they come in white, mod bit roofs don’t reflect much UV light and end up with similar issues.

This can create trouble by attracting too much heat to your roof. When this happens, your energy bill can increase substantially, especially if your previous roofing material wasn’t black.

There is one piece of good news, though. Most manufacturers offer cap sheets that greatly improve how much UV light your roof can reflect. If you’re worried about your energy bill, ask your roofer about an additional cap sheet when you get your free roofing estimate!
Pro: Great for Foot Traffic
Modified bitumen roofs are great for both homes and commercial structures. But mod bit does have a particular advantage with commercial applications since it can help protect high-traffic roofs.

Thanks to its durable asphalt composition and multiple layers, modified bitumen works for areas that see a lot of foot traffic. That said, you should not install modified bitumen for a patio or other area that’s intended to see a lot of use every day. Rather, mod bit works for areas that see a lot of incidental foot traffic, such as space connecting two parts of a building or an incidental, unofficial deck for employees.

### Your Guide to Clay Tile Roofs from Florida Roofing Pros

Did you know that Florida is the American home to the clay tile roof? Ever since Spanish settlers brought clay roofing tiles over to the New World, Floridians have loved the style and protection that they offer. And if you’re interested in getting a clay tile roof for your home, then you’ll be glad to know that their popularity is still going strong in The Sunshine State.

Pros and Cons of a Clay Tile Roof

While clay tile roofing is a signature Florida style, it’s not for everyone. So before you commit to a roof replacement, let us fill you in on everything you need to know to make an informed decision.
Pro: Florida-resistant Protection
Part of the reason that clay roofs are so popular in The Sunshine State is how well they can withstand the local weather patterns. For example, clay tiles can handle winds exceeding 150 mph. This makes them ideal for withstanding even hurricane-force winds!

Clay tiles are also carefully designed to help water move off your roof. How they do this can depend on the type of clay tiles that you choose, but each style has its own way of neatly moving water off your roof without giving it the opportunity to reach your vulnerable roof decking.

As the cherry on top, clay tile roofs don’t rot and are resistant to bugs. This is a major improvement over shingle roofs, which can soak through and lead to algae growth and pest infestations.
Con: Clay Tiles Are Brittle
In most cases, getting a clay tile roof is a great way to protect your home from the elements. But there’s one exception: Clay tiles are at a high risk of being damaged by falling branches and other types of impact damage.

In Florida, this can cause some problems as falling storm debris can crack shingles. But there is a silver lining here: Replacing clay tiles is a quick and low-cost roof repair. So while this is definitely a downside for clay tile roofs, it’s not usually a dealbreaker for most homeowners.
Pro: Fantastic Curb Appeal
Clay tile roofs aren’t just beloved for their function. Floridians also can’t get enough of the classic, timeless beauty that these roofs offer. And no matter what your vision is for your clay tile roof, you can bet that there’s an option that will let you achieve it.

That’s because clay roofing tiles come in a variety of styles. From French tiles to mission tiles, there are plenty of styles and tile patterns to choose from. In fact, some types of tiles allow you to arrange them in unique patterns, ensuring that your roof is completely original and suited to your tastes.

No matter what type of clay tile you choose, you can count on it increasing your home’s curb appeal considerably. This is doubly true of Spanish-style homes in Florida, which combine perfectly with the classic look of clay tile.
Con: High Clay Tile Roof Costs
There’s no denying it: Clay tile roofs are anything but cheap. This is a premium roofing material, which means it comes at a premium price. Specifically, clay tile roofs cost about $12 to $21 per square foot, including roof installation costs.

To put this another way, let’s consider that the average roof is around 1,700 square feet. On a roof of this size, assuming that there are no unique roofing features, you could expect a clay tile roof replacement to cost between $20,400 and $35,700.

This price tag is the biggest reason why more homeowners don’t choose to get a clay tile roof. But if this price is something that makes sense in your budget, then you should treat a clay tile roof as an investment in your home’s long-term protection. Because just like we can’t deny that clay tile roofs are expensive, we also know for a fact that they’re well worth that cost.
Pro: Unbeatable Longevity
Without a doubt, the stand-out, best-selling feature of a clay tile roof is its longevity. In fact, clay tile roofs can last longer than any other sloped roofing material — even metal roofs. So how long does a clay tile roof last? With the right maintenance and care, clay tile roofs have been known to last for longer than 100 years!

This is why so many Florida homeowners choose a tile roof replacement despite the intimidating price tag. Yes, clay tile roofs have high up-front roof replacement costs. But their unmatched longevity can partially offset the high costs, even with Florida’s harsh climate.

There is one important caveat to this, though. Your clay roofing tiles may last for a century, but your roof underlayment won’t. This part of your roof protects against water, and it will only last for about 20 years. So while you won’t need to replace your roof as often as with other roofing materials, your underlayment will need to be replaced more frequently (but this is a much less expensive job than a tile roof replacement).
Types of Clay Roofing Tiles

If you’re still interested in a clay tile roof after reviewing the pros and cons, the next step is considering what type of tile you want for your new roof. And as experienced Florida roofers, there’s almost no limit to the types of clay tiles that we can install for you.

Some of the most popular types of clay roofing tiles include:

 	Spanish Tile: People also refer to Spanish tile as barrel tile because of its rounded, half-barrel shape. Not only does this create a classic Spanish feel on your structure, but it also allows for efficient water shedding and ventilation.
 	French Tile: Unlike Spanish tiles, these tiles are flat with divots in the center of the tile. This creates a pathway for water to flow seamlessly off your roof. If you prefer a more modern aesthetic, you can apply these tiles in a more staggered pattern that creates visual interest on your roof.
 	Mediterranean Tile: Also called S-tile due to its unique profile, Mediterranean tiles are meant to tightly overlap and interlock to ensure that nothing can get into the more vulnerable layers of your roofing system.
 	Mission Tile: These tiles get their name from the missions in the American Southwest, but their style fits just as well in Florida. Available in gorgeous earth tones, mission tiles are a versatile option for your clay tile roof.

### How to Get the Best Shingle Roof Replacement for Your Florida Home

Did you know that shingles are the most popular roofing material in North America? That’s because they’re well-suited to a variety of different climates, even Florida’s. But despite how popular roofing shingles are, many people still have questions when the time comes for their shingle roof replacement.

Let’s start with one of the biggest areas we see questions about: your options for a shingle roof replacement.
Shingle Roof Replacement Material Options

As master roofers, we’re dedicated to giving you exactly what you want. That’s why we provide a variety of different shingle options for you to choose from. Keep reading to see what our roofing experts can do for your home!
3-Tab Asphalt Shingles
3-tab shingles are thin, lightweight shingles that are made of one layer of asphalt and one layer of support, usually fiberglass. For many years these were the most popular roofing materials in the country, but newer advances in roofing technology have done a lot to decrease their popularity.

Take, for example, the wind resistance of 3-tab shingles. These shingles can only handle winds of 60-70 miles per hour. In other words, they can’t withstand even a Category 1 hurricane, which makes them an unreliable choice for structures in Florida.

So why do people get 3-tab asphalt shingles? Well, because they’re affordable. 3-tab asphalt shingles are the cheapest roofing material on the market, but it’s important to be wary of this low price. Because while they come with low shingle roof replacement costs, these shingles also don’t add as much value to your home as other shingles.

A 3-tab shingle roof will only last for 15-20 years. And your roof could last for an even shorter time, especially if a hurricane passes through the area. For this reason, many manufacturers don’t even offer 3-tab shingles anymore, so we would encourage anyone to think very carefully before deciding on a 3-tab shingle roof replacement. While low up-front costs are nice, it’s important to make sure that your roof adds value to your home so that you’re getting a great return on your investment.
Architectural Asphalt Shingles
Made up of alternating layers of asphalt and fiberglass, architectural shingles are the most popular roofing material in Florida. They’re much thicker and hardier than 3-tab asphalt shingles, but they’re still easy to manufacture, which can help keep shingle roof replacement costs down.

Architectural shingles are durable and able to withstand winds of 80-120 mph. They’re also able to resist water and protect your roofing underlayment, even in severe storms. As a bonus, new types of architectural shingles come with the ability to release small amounts of copper over time, which can prevent mold and algae from growing on your roof for decades.

With all of these protective features, architectural shingles can last for 20-25 years. Keep in mind that your roof will likely need occasional maintenance over this time, especially if a major storm comes by. Missing or damaged shingles are some of the most common roof repairs that we see in The Sunshine State.

As the cherry on top, architectural shingles offer great aesthetics. People also call these dimensional shingles because of their unique patterning which creates dimension and depth on your roof. And with a variety of color options, we know that you’ll be able to find a great architectural shingle that fits your style.
Composite Shingles
Composite shingles are often called synthetic shingles because of the unique, synthetic polymer that they’re made of. While these shingles come from something synthetic, they near-perfectly replicate the look and style of a cedar or slate roof at a much more affordable cost.

Synthetic shingles are even better at resisting wind than architectural shingles. In fact, they’re capable of withstanding winds up to 150 mph. They’re also resistant to weathering by UV light and are more lightweight than asphalt shingles, which can take some burden off your home’s structure.

Given these enhanced protective features, it’s no surprise that composite shingles can go much longer in between shingle roof replacements. In fact, their lifespan can be as long as 50 years. This great longevity comes at a price, though. Because while composite shingles are much cheaper than real slate or wood, they’re still far more expensive than asphalt shingles.
The Cost of a Shingle Roof Replacement in Florida

When calculating your shingle roof replacement costs, there are many factors to consider. Who installs your roof is a big factor, as are the condition and features of your roof. But the single biggest consideration for your shingle roof replacement costs will always be the type of shingle you choose.

Let’s start by looking at 3-tab shingles. As we mentioned, these shingles are uniquely cheap. They can even cost as little as two dollars per square foot. But since they have such poor longevity, we rarely recommend that homeowners choose this kind of shingle.

Now it’s time to consider architectural shingles. Since they’re easy to mass-produce, these shingles average around five to nine dollars per square foot. In other words, if your roof is near the average roof size of 1,700 square feet, you can expect this type of shingle roof replacement to cost around $8,500 to $15,300.

Composite shingles come with very different figures. Their average prices tend to fall between seven and 14 dollars. For an average-sized roof, that means you could be looking at between $11,900 and $23,800 for a composite shingle roof replacement. It’s important to note that while this is a high up-front cost, this is still much cheaper than an actual slate or cedar roof.

These factors are the ones that most affect the cost of replacing and installing a shingle roof. But what about the cost of your roof across its lifetime? To make sure that your roof will hold onto its value, then the best thing you can do is carefully choose your shingle roofing contractors.

### What to Do When You Need Roof Leak Repair Services

Nobody is happy to see water dripping from the ceiling of their home or business. But when you find yourself in need of a roof leak repair, it’s important to act quickly to prevent the worst of the damage. Otherwise, you could find your situation going from a quick roof repair to a total roof replacement.

Handling a Roof Leak Repair in 5 Steps

Leaks rarely come at a good time, so it’s normal to feel stressed or overwhelmed when your roof develops one. But the good news is that you only need to follow five simple steps to solve this issue.

Let us walk you through the step-by-step way to handle a leaking roof!
Step 1: Prevent Further Damage to Your Home or Business
Roofing problems are bad enough, but the last thing that you want to add to the situation is damage to the interior of your structure. For that reason, the first step in handling a roof leak repair is putting something under the leak to catch the water.

Don’t just put it under the leak where it comes from your ceiling, though. If you have attic access, you should go to your attic and put a bucket directly under the leak. This won’t prevent all water damage to your roof, but it will stop that damage from spreading throughout the interior of your home or business.

If you don’t have attic access, then the best thing you can do is catch the water as it comes down from the ceiling. This isn’t ideal, but it will at least stop the water from pooling inside your structure, which could create a whole host of other issues.
Step 2: Identify the Source of the Leak
This step isn’t strictly necessary, but it can go a long way in making your roof leak repairs easier. Check your attic to see where the leak is coming into your structure. If you can, snap a photo or two to show to your contractor.

Knowing where the leak is coming from can help roofers identify what the issue is, which in turn speeds up the job. And the less time that roofers have to spend working on your roof repair, the lower your overall roof leak repair costs! But don't worry if you can't find the source of the leak. Experienced roofers should have no problem finding it and fixing it for you!

This is arguably the most important step in getting roof leak repair services. This is where you reach out to a local roofing company and have someone out to take a look at your roof. ### 2025 Guide to Metal Roofing in Florida

Did you know that metal roofs are experiencing a renaissance in Florida right now? Shingles and tiles have been the most popular Florida roofing materials for generations, but new metal roofing technology has made steel roofs one of the most popular roof replacement options in the state. If you’re considering upgrading to a new metal roof, you could gain a lot of benefits from this investment in your property.

We should know; our founders worked in the roofing industry for a combined 60 years before creating PITCH Roofing. That gives us unique insights into the value of getting a metal roof in Florida. Let us share our roofing expertise as we talk to you about metal roofing costs, perks, and options in The Sunshine State!
What to Know Before Getting a Metal Roof in Florida


Many Floridians who are curious about metal roofs need a refresher on just what they are and how they add value to a property. To make sure you’re up to speed, let’s talk about the must-know metal roofing factors that you may be missing!

One of the primary benefits of getting a metal roof in Florida is longevity. A traditional shingle roof will rarely last more than 20 years, but metal roofs can last anywhere from 40 to 70 years. So while metal roofs cost more than shingle roofs, the higher up-front investment is often worth it thanks to the longevity of your new roof.

Metal roofs aren’t just popular because they can last a long time, though. Because in Florida, your roof is only guaranteed to last for as long as it can stand up to tropical storms and hurricanes. And metal roofs stand up to high winds and heavy rains like no other.

Take their wind resistance for example. Your average metal roof can easily withstand winds of up to 140 mph — the equivalent of a Category 4 hurricane! And the surface of metal roofs is great for quickly removing water from your roof without allowing it past the tightly interlocking metal sheets.

Some people have concerns about the effects of humidity and lightning on metal roofs. But the truth is that metal roofs aren’t any more likely to attract lightning than other roofing materials. And while rust can be a problem for steel, modern metal roofs have aluminum coatings and other rust-preventing technologies that make metal roofs well-suited for even coastal environments.

Now that you're up to speed on metal roofs in Florida, let's discuss your metal roofing style options!
Types of Metal Roof Replacements
In the world of metal roofing, how your sheets of metal adhere to your roof can change everything about your roofing system. In fact, metal roofing styles are defined by having either concealed or exposed fasteners. These two types of metal roofing are called 5V and standing seam, respectively.
5V Roofing
5V roofing has exposed fasteners, meaning that roofers secure the metal sheets by drilling them into your roof from the top down. This type of metal roofing uses crimped, wavy sheets, which is where 5V metal roofing gets its name from, specifically the five V-shape patterns on each sheet.

And this style of roofing has some great advantages. For one thing, it’s cheaper and faster to install than standing seam roofing. Moreover, thanks to being securely drilled into place, you don’t have to worry about your 5V metal roof going anywhere any time soon.

There are also downsides, though. 5V metal roofing doesn’t allow your roofing sheets to expand and contract with the sun’s heat. By forcing the panels to be totally still, it can lead to faster weathering and premature aging. Additionally, exposed fasteners are more exposed to the elements, which can lead to rusting over time, especially if you live in coastal Florida.
Standing Seam Roofing
Metal roofs with hidden fasteners are called standing seam metal roofs, and they come with their own pros and cons. For one thing, these panels have a sleeker, flatter appearance that many people prefer for residential structures.

More than just style preference though, standing seam roofs are some of the best-equipped to handle Florida’s weather. Their hidden fasteners are protected beneath the panels, and the metal sheets can freely expand and contract with the weather. This ensures that they aren’t aging sooner than they should.

The biggest disadvantage to standing seam roofing is the cost, which is often much higher than that of 5V roofing. This is because of the more particular design of standing seam panels and the longer installation time. Still, for people with the resources to make a major investment in their properties, standing seam represents a commitment to protecting your structure for many decades to come.
Cost of a Metal Roof in Florida


We’ve alluded to some types of metal roofs costing more than others, but how much do these roofs actually cost in Florida?

Before we can give you numbers, it’s important to remember that these are averages that may not be accurate for your situation. Different parts of Florida come with different needs. For example, aluminum panels are necessary for coastal Florida homes, whereas further inland, you may choose Galvalume steel panels. These kinds of choices can make a major pricing difference.

With that caveat in mind, let’s talk about the cost of standing seam and 5V metal roofs.

Standing seam metal roofing sheets tend to cost between $10 and $35 per square foot. So if your roof is 2,000 square feet, then you’re looking at metal roof replacement costs between $20,000 and $70,000.

5V metal roofs are significantly more affordable with metal roofing costs between $5 and $10 per square foot. This makes a metal roof replacement much more affordable for a 2,000-square-foot roof, with prices between $10,000 and $20,000.

You may have noticed that these metal roofing costs have wide ranges. That’s because the cost of a metal roof replacement will always come down to the specifics of the job. So to get a reliable, accurate metal roof replacement cost estimate, you’ll have to get in touch with roofing experts in your area.

### The Average Roof Replacement Cost in Florida: 2025 Edition

If the time has come to replace your old roof, then you probably have questions about the latest roof replacement costs in Florida. Turning to roof replacement cost calculators can seem tempting, but the truth is these tools are largely inaccurate because they don’t take into account the complexities of your roof, local market conditions, or building codes for your county.You need a human’s insight and knowledge to get an accurate roof replacement cost. That’s what PITCH is for! As a local roofing company based right here in Pinellas County and Hillsborough County, we’re happy to use our 60+ years of local roofing experience to get you an accurate roof replacement price estimate.To get started, let us give you a quick overview of the various factors that impact the cost of your roof replacement in Florida.Roof Replacement Cost Factors in FloridaWhether you’re getting a residential or commercial roof replacement, you’ll likely be surprised to learn how many different factors affect roof replacement costs in Florida. Many people already know that roof size and roofing materials play a role in pricing, but some of the more unexpected pricing factors include:Roof pitchAny damage done to your roof deckingUnique roofing features like skylights, chimneys, or dormer windowsLocal market conditions and labor costsRoofing warrantiesRoof accessibilityCounty permitting regulations

How Much Does a Roof Replacement Cost?The short answer: Between $9,000.00 and $40,000.00 for a 2,000 square foot roof in Florida, depending on material and location.As you can see, more than a few factors go into calculating your total roof replacement cost. So to get you an accurate, reliable number, you’ll need to work directly with an experienced roofing contractor. But does that mean that there’s no way to find out how much your roof replacement might cost without an estimate?Thankfully, no. While you do need a quote to get an exact number, you can still get a ballpark figure for your new roof by looking at the average roof replacement costs in Florida.Average Roof Replacement Costs in FloridaLooking at the average cost of a roof per square foot can give you an idea of how much your new roof will cost. But to get an accurate number, we need to take this material by material.There are plenty of roofing material options in Florida, so let’s get started and give you a place to start with planning for your roof replacement costs!Asphalt and Composite Shingle Roofing Costs Per Square FootShingles are the most common roofing materials in North America, and at Pitch, we offer a choice between asphalt shingles and composite shingles. To help you make an informed decision, let’s take a brief look at each of these options and their shingle roof replacement costs.Architectural asphalt shingles can last for 25-30 years, and because of their dimensional patterning, they’re great at generating visual interest on your roof. Architectural shingles are also a very affordable option with prices ranging from $4.50 to $8. So if your home’s roof is 2,000 square feet, then your roof replacement costs will likely fall between $9,000 and $16,000.Composite shingles, on the other hand, are made of a synthetic material that looks almost identical to slate shingles. As a result, they both add more value to your home and can last for 40-50 years. Naturally, though, these features come with a price increase. Composite shingles cost between $7 and $14 per square foot, or $14,000 to $28,000 on a 2,000-square-foot roof.Tile and Concrete Tile Roofing Costs Per Square FootTile roofing has been a staple in Florida since Spanish settlers brought it with them when traveling to the New World. And while tile roof replacement costs will vary depending on the style (for example, Spanish tiles vs. French tiles), the biggest factor in tile roofing costs is the material type used.Many homeowners choose concrete tiles as a way to lower roofing costs while getting a classic aesthetic for their homes. And with a lifespan of 40-50 years, concrete tiles have the strength and durability to stand up against Florida’s unpredictable weather. With a cost of $7 to $19 per square foot, or $14,000 to $38,000 for a 2,000-square-foot roof, concrete tiles are a more affordable tile roofing option.Clay tile is the gold standard for tile roofing thanks to its hardy structure that can allow your roof to last for more than a century. The classic beauty and strength of clay tile comes at a premium, however, with costs between $12 and $21 per square foot. On a 2,000-square-foot home, this puts your roof replacement costs between $24,000 and $42,000.Metal Roofing Costs Per Square FootIf you want to hurricane-proof your home or business, metal roofing is one of the best options on the market. While there are some price variations based on the composition of your metal roofing sheets, the biggest price factor is whether you get a standing seam or 5V roof replacement.5V metal roofing gets its name from the wavy pattern on the metal roofing sheets, but its most identifying mark is its exposed fasteners that drill the roof down into place. This is a cheaper and simpler installation method, but it does lower the life expectancy of your roof to about 30 years. Still, with costs between $7 to $19 per square foot (in other words, $14,000 to $38,000 on a 2,000-square-foot roof), many property owners choose this as an affordable metal roof replacement option.If you don’t mind a higher metal roof replacement cost, though, then standing seam could be for you. With its sleek exterior and hidden fasteners, standing seam is perfect for residential structures and boasts a lifespan of up to 70 years. For many homeowners, this makes it worth the higher price point of $10 to $23 per square foot, or $20,000 to $46,000 for an average roof in Florida.Flat Roofing Costs Per Square FootAs experienced roofers, Pitch handles both sloped and flat roofing materials. So whether your home or business needs a roof replacement, we can get you a great product at an even better cost. In Florida, three flat roofing options stand head and shoulders above the rest, and these are:TPO: This flat roofing membrane can last for 20-30 years and costs between $5.50 and $9 per square foot. With our established roof measurement, that’s $11,000 to $18,000.EPDM: This rubberized roofing membrane has a uniquely long lifespan among flat roofs: 50 years. It is a bit more expensive, though, coming in at $4 to $12 per square foot, or $8,000 to $24,000. Part of the reason for this wide price range is that different types of EPDM have different compositions, which makes it important to choose experienced local contractors who can get you a good product for Florida’s unique climate.Modified Bitumen: Manufacturers make mod bit using multiple layers of asphalt and other protectors, so it is unlike the membrane roofing options on this list. It only lasts for about 20 years, but it does have the lowest flat roof replacement costs at $4 to $8 per square foot, or $8,000 to $16,000.

Sooner or later, every roof needs replacing. And as a homeowner, it’s in your best interest to get it done sooner rather than later. Hurricane season is no joke, and having a strong roofing system is essential to protecting your property from severe tropical storms.

No matter what your idea of the perfect roof is, PITCH can make it a reality. As long-time Florida roofers, we’ve mastered a wide variety of roofing materials. Some of the types of roof replacements we can offer you include:

 	Synthetic and asphalt shingles
 	Clay and concrete tiles
 	Hidden and exposed fastener metal roofs
 	TPO and modified bitumen flat roofs

Roofing is never one-size-fits-all. Instead, your roof should be tailored to your preferences and the needs of your property. When you choose PITCH for your Bonita Springs roof replacement, that’s exactly what you’ll get!
Bonita Springs Roof Repairs
If you act quickly, sometimes roof repairs are enough to avoid a roof replacement. Time is of the essence, though, especially if you have a roof leak. With over 60 years of local roofing experience, we have the skills and know-how to quickly fix your roofing issue before the damage has a chance to spread.

We handle a wide variety of roof repairs every day, but some of the most common issues we see are:

 	Missing or damaged shingles
 	Cracked roof tiles
 	Roof leaks
 	Damaged flashing

Regardless of what roof repair(s) you need, PITCH Roofing always delivers quality results. Instead of quick patch jobs, we do in-depth roof repairs that fix the issue at its source. To us, this is the crux of roofing done right!

Pinellas County Roof RepairsThe best way to avoid a roof replacement is through timely roof repairs. In Florida, lots of little things can go wrong with your roof. Take missing shingles, for example. On their own, these are simple, minor roof repairs that a handyman can knock out quickly. But over time, missing shingles can let water into your roof, which could spread throughout your roofing system and lead to needing a total replacement.At PITCH, our crews know roofing systems inside and out. So whether the problem is obvious or you’re not sure what’s wrong with your roof, we’ll come out, take a look, and develop a plan that resolves your issue. ### Jasmine Estates

Pasco County is a great place to live, but it comes with its downsides. For one thing, storm chasers love to blow into town after a storm and promise dirt-cheap roof replacements and repairs. Going with out-of-town roofers is almost never the right move, though. If you want high-quality roofing services, you need the help of experienced Jasmine Estates roofers.As a dedicated local roofing company, PITCH Roofing has the experienced contractors that you want working on your home or commercial property. With a combined 60+ years of experience under our belt, you can trust that we’ve seen and fixed your issue before. Let’s talk about some of the ways that our veteran Pasco County roofers can help!Roof Inspections in Pasco CountyYou’ve probably heard that an ounce of prevention is worth more than a pound of cure, and that’s especially true in roofing. If you want to stay ahead of wear and tear on your roof, annual roof inspections are a must. And while many homeowners put them off for fear of getting bad news, routine roof inspections will actually go a long way in saving you money on roofing expenses.Think of it this way: If there’s a problem with your roof, it will be cheaper to address it now than in six months. Problems caught by roof inspections are so minor that you probably haven’t noticed them. By addressing issues at this early stage, you can keep your roof repair costs as low as possible! On the other hand, waiting too long to fix your roof could lead to more damage and even cause you to need a roof replacement.

Pasco County Roof RepairsIt can be tempting to put off roof repairs. While homeowners tend to take leaks seriously, “smaller” issues like missing shingles or bent gutters are often put on the back burner. This can be a costly mistake though, because putting off roof repairs is the easiest way to end up needing a roof replacement.Let’s use missing shingles as an example. At first, missing shingles probably won’t cause you any serious problems. In a couple of months, however, the weak point in your roof may have damaged nearby shingles, your roof decking, and potentially even caused a leak that puts your entire roofing system at risk. For this reason, we strongly encourage our customers to act quickly when there’s a problem with their roofs.When you’re having roofing trouble, PITCH will be there to provide a lasting solution. Our experienced roofers don’t believe in half-fixes or patch jobs. Instead they address roofing issues at the root so that our customers can enjoy complete peace of mind and long-term protection! And there is no doubt that PITCH Roofing offers the very best Florida roofing services. Don’t take our word for it, either — our reviews speak for themselves!At PITCH, we believe that everyone deserves high-quality roofing services. ### Wauchula

As an inland community, Wauchula, Florida is insulated from the worst effects of hurricanes and other tropical storms. But there are still plenty of factors that can damage your roof. Hardee County regularly experiences high winds during hurricane season, not to mention humidity and extreme UV exposure. That’s why you want experienced roofers working on your property when you’re having trouble.That’s us. We’re PITCH Roofing, a local roofing company with more than 60 years of combined experience under our belt. Today, we want to talk about what we can do for your residential or commercial roof in Wauchula!Wauchula, Florida Roof ReplacementsSooner or later, every roof gives out. Whether your roof reaches the end of its life or is damaged in a severe weather event, the best thing you can do is get a new one before the next storm blows into town. And at PITCH, we have the know-how to provide you with nearly any roof you could want.We handle a wide variety of Wauchula roof replacements, including:Asphalt and synthetic shinglesClay and concrete roofing tilesHidden and exposed fastener metal roofsTPO and modified bitumen flat roofsWith our expertise, we’ll be able to install the roof of your dreams. That’s a roof that can protect your property, add value, and is built to last in Florida’s unpredictable weather. And as Owens Corning Preferred Contractors, you can count on us to deliver the highest-quality materials and warranties!

Roof Installations in Redington Beach

We know that roof replacements rarely come at a convenient time, but they’re essential to protecting your home or commercial property. An old, worn-out roof won’t be able to protect your property from the next major storm. As your local roofing partner, PITCH Roofing will be happy to help you get a new roof that suits your taste and is 100% hurricane-ready!

With many years of roofing experience, our crews can handle virtually any type of roof replacement. That includes:

 	Synthetic and asphalt shingles
 	Concrete and clay roofing tiles
 	Exposed and hidden fastener metal roofing
 	Modified bitumen and TPO flat roofing

Pinellas County Roof Repair Services
Timely roof repairs are some of the smartest investments you can make in your property. Even minor roofing damage can have far-reaching consequences if not addressed promptly. For example, a minor roof leak can spread throughout your roofing system. In a matter of months, the issue can go from a quick roof repair to a partial or full roof replacement!

That’s why we highly encourage Redington Beach residents to keep an eye on their roofs for any signs of damage. When you spot something off, all you need to do is call the pros at PITCH Roofing and we’ll come running to see what the issue is and what kind of roof repairs you need. No matter what roofing issue you’re dealing with, you can bet that we’ve fixed it before and know how to help!

Treasure Island is one of many beautiful communities in Pinellas County. And like many other Pinellas County communities, it’s plagued by storm chasers. These fly-by-night roofers promise great things after a storm, but they leave you high and dry when you need them most. That’s why your best bet is to stick with real, local roofing professionals.We’re PITCH Roofing, your Pinellas County roofing partner. As long-time Pinellas residents and roofers, we know what it takes to keep your Treasure Island roof safe during the next storm. Let’s talk about what our roofers can do to help you protect your property and enjoy complete peace of mind!Essential Roofing Services in Treasure IslandWe’re seasoned Florida roofing contractors, which means you can count on us to fulfill virtually any roofing services you need. Let’s take a look at some of our most common roofing services in and around Treasure Island!We don’t think you should have to choose between protection and your dream roof, either. As experienced contractors, we have mastered a wide variety of roofing materials. With us, you can get a roof that suits your tastes and style without sacrificing protection or reliability. Some of the most common types of Treasure Island roof replacements we handle are:Asphalt and synthetic roofing shinglesClay and concrete roofing tilesExposed and hidden fastener metal roofingTPO and modified bitumen flat roofing

Even minor issues like missing shingles can become a major vulnerability during a hurricane. In our experience, the best way to prevent serious damage to your roof is to make sure the minor problems don’t have a chance to worsen.At PITCH, we don’t believe in cheap patch jobs that fail to address the root of the problem. Instead, we believe in in-depth, comprehensive roofing solutions that you can count on. When you call us to fix up your roof, you can count on us to be timely and provide a long-lasting fix that will keep your roof strong and ready for anything!Local Solar RoofingDid you know that Pinellas County averages 360 days of sunshine every year? This makes Treasure Island one of the best places in the country for solar roofing. If you’re looking to go green and lower your monthly energy bill, PITCH Roofing is ready to set you up with high-quality solar roofing panels!In addition to being good for the environment and your energy bill, solar panels also benefit your home’s overall value. Homes with solar panels see significant increases in their property values, especially in sought-after communities like Treasure Island. ### Bradenton

Florida’s weather patterns are famous for being tough on homes and businesses across the state. But the danger is especially acute in Bradenton. Located along the Manatee River, Bradenton has seen first-hand some of the worst weather conditions that Florida has to offer. To hold up against severe weather events like hurricanes, Bradenton residents need high-quality roofing services.Luckily, that’s exactly what we provide. We’re PITCH Roofing, your Manatee County roofing partners. Today, we want to talk about what we can do for you to keep your home or commercial property safe and protected. Sarasota County Roof Replacements

Even the best roofs need replacing eventually. When your current roof reaches the end of its lifespan, the experienced crews at PITCH Roofing will be ready to remove it and install whatever type of material you want for your next roofing system.

Over the decades as Florida roofing professionals, our contractors have mastered the following types of new roof installation:

 	Asphalt and synthetic shingle roof replacements
 	Clay and concrete tile roof replacements
 	Standing seam and exposed fastener metal roof replacements
 	Modified bitumen and TPO flat roof replacements

No matter what kind of roof you’re looking for, our experienced professionals will know how to install it. And with 0% roof financing available, we can help you out no matter how much you have saved up! Because at PITCH, we believe that quality roofing services should be available to everyone.
Lakewood Ranch Roof Repairs
In Florida, plenty of natural weather events can damage your roof. From torn-off shingles to leaking roofs to cracked tiles, our roofers have seen it all. When you find yourself with a damaged roof, waiting to call in professionals is one of the biggest mistakes a homeowner can make.

That’s because roofing problems only get worse with time. This applies even to minor roofing damage. For example, UV rays drying out and cracking your shingles is a minor issue at first. Over time, though, this problem can worsen until you’re dealing with leaks, roof sagging, and other major roofing problems. If you want the lowest repair bill possible, it’s smart to get help ASAP!
Other Roofing Services Near You
Roof replacements and repairs are two essential roofing services for Lakewood Ranch residents. But they’re not the only ways that we can help. In addition to fixing up or replacing your roof, our Florida roofers can also provide:

 	Roof inspections
 	Soffit and fascia replacements and repairs
 	Gutter installation and repairs
 	Leak detection and repair
 	Storm damage restoration

No matter what roofing problem you’re experiencing, our roofers are ready to help. If you’re dealing with a roofing problem, even if it’s not on this list, reach out to our friendly staff. There’s a very good chance that our veteran roofing contractors will know how to help!

### Sarasota

As a coastal community, Sarasota is uniquely vulnerable to Florida’s inclement weather patterns. That means both residential and commercial roofs in Sarasota County need extra protection. And with PITCH Roofing, your locally-based roofing contractors, extra protection is exactly what you’re going to get.As veteran Florida roofers, nobody knows how to Florida-proof a roof better than we do. Don’t just take our word for it, though. Instead, let us walk you through the next-level roofing services we provide to our Sarasota community!Sarasota, FL Roof ReplacementsEvery roof needs replacing sooner or later. But with hurricane-force winds and Florida’s harsh UV rays, Sarasota roofs stand up to more than most. When time inevitably takes its toll on your roof, you can count on our roofers to be there when you need them.We don’t just mean classic shingles, either. As experienced Florida roofers, we have years of experience installing just about any kind of roof you can imagine. ### Homeowners Insurance Guide

PITCH ROOFING

																												The Pitch Roofing DifferenceAt PITCH Roofing, we believe in fair and transparent pricing, no matter the circumstances. 				Homeowners insurance is a big deal everywhere, but in Florida especially. Between the homeowners insurance crisis, major hurricanes becoming more common, and confusion about how to use insurance, Floridians have a lot of questions about their homes’ coverage.PITCH Roofing is here to give clear, reliable answers. As veteran Florida roofing contractors, we’ve been working with both homeowners and their insurance companies for years. In this comprehensive guide to Florida homeowners insurance, we’re covering how Florida homeowners insurance got to where it is, how to make a claim that will be approved, and how to lower your insurance premium.But first, let’s start with some background about how Florida got into its current homeowners insurance crisis!

The History of the Homeowners Insurance Crisis in FloridaSince 2017, more than a dozen major homeowners insurance companies in Florida have been liquidated. And this number doesn’t even include the dozens of insurers who have pulled out of Florida entirely or stopped offering homeowners insurance policies in the Sunshine State.The result is fewer options for consumers and much higher premiums. Clearly something is wrong in the world of Florida homeowners insurance, but what is it?There are several causes behind the homeowners insurance crisis, and we’re going to look at each one individually so you can have the complete picture.Natural DisastersFlorida is seeing more and more major hurricanes, especially those coming from the Gulf of Mexico. Homeowners are seeing extreme damage to their property as more powerful storms continue to batter Florida. And fixing that damage is not cheap. In 2018 alone, the federal government released an estimate that Florida had spent between $5 and $10 billion recovering from major storms.Most of this damage is a direct result of high winds during hurricanes. Shingles can rarely withstand winds exceeding 110 mph, so when a major hurricane comes to town, it’s normal for homeowners to find shingles in their yards the next morning. In the worst-case scenario, you may even lose enough shingles to require a roof replacement, which is a major expense for insurers.The high winds from hurricanes aren’t the only problem, though. Flooding is becoming a larger issue thanks to storm surge, as Tampa Bay saw with Hurricane Helene. Areas that have not traditionally flooded are now seeing significant flooding during major storms, which further increases the amount that insurance companies have to pay out to their policyholders.Property insurance providers have taken notice of Florida’s natural disasters in a big way. Year after year, they find themselves having to pay out more and more to undo the damage of Florida’s frequent storms. This has led to thinner profit margins, and some insurance providers have had to liquidate as a result.Even for insurers who are still making enough to keep operating, though, this situation isn’t sustainable. Insurance providers are businesses first, so as profit margins get thinner, they see less reason to stay. And with so many other states where natural disasters are less common, many insurers are deciding that the safe bet is to leave Florida before they go under.High Property ValuesThe above problem is especially bad because of Florida’s ever-rising property values. It’s no secret that homes have gotten expensive in Florida, especially the Greater Tampa Bay region. In fact, the median cost of a home in Florida was over $415,000 in 2023. Since most homeowners take out policies worth at least the value of their homes, insurance providers have been paying out larger and larger sums after major storms.In this way, the Florida homeowners insurance crisis compounds on itself over time. Natural disasters lead to more frequent payouts, and those amounts only get higher because property in Florida is extremely valuable right now. This leaves insurance companies in a tight spot, but it also makes life harder for Floridians who just want affordable coverage to protect their homes.Unfortunately, this isn’t the full extent of Florida’s homeowners insurance problems. “Storm chaser” roofers have caused a lot of the damage that Floridians are still dealing with.Fraudulent Storm ChasersFirst, let’s define what a storm chaser is. Storm chaser roofers are people who blow into town after a storm and offer very low-cost roofing services. If you’ve ever had someone knock on your door after a storm and offer to take a look at your roof, there’s a very good chance that you’ve met a storm chaser.On the surface, they offer a great deal — local contractors can get busy after a disaster and have wait lists, while storm chasers are readily available almost always have the lowest prices. There are a couple of crucial problems with storm chasers though. And because of these problems, storm chasers have caused countless headaches for Florida homeowners and their insurers.For one thing, storm chasers rarely do quality work. They’re often unlicensed, and getting a new roof from unlicensed roofers is a fast way to run into problems with your insurance provider. In the rare cases where they have valid licenses, they often rely on cheap labor and materials. This means that their work is shoddy, prone to failure, and likely to cause more problems than it solves.Another major issue with storm chaser roofers is that they’re often dishonest. They’ll promise you a free roof because your insurance will cover it then bill your insurance company for much more than the value of their work. This further increases the financial strain on insurers, who then have more incentive to leave Florida.The worst part? Storm chasers don’t stick around. By the time you can complain about the leaks in your roof or your troubles with your insurance policy, they’ve already moved on to the next area and there’s nobody to hold accountable. This leaves you with little recourse, which is why it’s important to pick reliable, local roofing contractors when you need roofing work done.

																										The Future of Homeowners Insurance in FloridaThe good news is that steps are being taken to address the homeowners insurance crisis in Florida. In 2022, the Florida legislature passed measures to create a fund for homeowners insurance providers to use to pay out policies in the event of a natural disaster. This means that you will still be able to submit a claim in the event of a natural disaster.There are other ways that Florida is trying to lessen the damage from the crisis, too. Citizens Property Insurance is one example. Often called the “insurer of last resort,” Citizens covers homes that wouldn’t qualify for coverage on the private market. Citizens is a not-for-profit, tax-exempt entity. This means they help homeowners maintain coverage as other insurers leave the state.The My Safe Florida Home program is another crucial part of fighting the homeowners insurance crisis. This publicly funded program allows homeowners to make hurricane-proofing upgrades to their homes while paying only a fraction of the total costs. By making homes more secure, homeowners enjoy lower insurance rates and insurers are less likely to have to pay out policies, which helps everybody.Later in this guide, we’ll give you tips for lowering your insurance premium using the My Safe Florida Home program. But for now, we want to focus on how you can make the most of your coverage and submit an insurance claim that has a high chance of being approved.How to Get Homeowners Insurance to Pay for a New RoofThere are clearly problems in Florida’s property insurance industry. But that doesn’t change the fact that when a storm damages your roof, you need and deserve to use your policy to pay for the repairs or replacement. If you’re not sure how to go about filing an insurance claim for a roof replacement or repairs, PITCH has got you covered.While your policy documents can look complex and confusing, the truth is that you can submit a claim in as little as four easy steps. Now, let’s talk about how you can start filing your claim for a roof replacement or repairs!1. Review Your Homeowners Insurance PolicyWith Florida’s high homeowners insurance premiums, it’s tempting to think that having insurance means you never have to pay for roofing services. Unfortunately, the truth is a bit more complicated. With homeowners insurance policies, your coverage only kicks in under certain set conditions.The good news is that most homeowners insurance policies cover storm damage. To be sure, though, it’s best to review your policy. If you can’t find your policy or the technical language isn’t helpful, you can also reach out to your agent with any questions about your policy.Generally speaking though, you can expect your homeowners insurance policy to cover you if your roofing damage is due to any of the following:High winds (e.g., missing shingles)Water damage (e.g. leaks caused by a hurricane)Hail (e.g., damaged shingles or cracked tiles)Once you’ve confirmed that your policy will cover your roofing damage, you can get ready to make your claim to your insurance provider. Insurers receive many claims, though, and they hire people specifically to look for situations where they don’t have to pay out your policy. That’s why it’s essential to start gathering evidence for your home insurance claim.2. Gather Proof for Your Roofing Insurance ClaimBecause of dishonest storm chasers, insurance providers are more cautious with paying out claims than ever before. So when submitting your claim, you need to prove two things. First, that your roof has sustained damage. And second, that a storm caused that damage.Fortunately, it’s pretty easy to prove that your roof has been damaged. Start by taking photos of the damage — as detailed as you can get. If you can get up on your roof to take close-up photos, great. If not and you can’t see the damage from your yard, most roofing companies will be happy to take photos of the damage as part of a routine roof inspection. When taking these photos, it’s best to have both close-up shots and far-away pictures. This ensures that your insurer can see the details of the damage as well as its overall effect on your roof.Your next step is to prove that a severe weather event damaged your roof. This is pretty simple for hurricanes. All you have to do is send a news article showing that your area was affected by a major storm. Alternatively, if, say, a tree fell on your roof, it would be enough to take a photo of the tree from the ground to show where it was and how it fell on your roof.Once you’ve collected evidence for your claim, you’re ready to submit it. After a hurricane, you’ll want to submit a claim ASAP. Lots of other homeowners in your area are likely also trying to get insurance to pay for their roofs, and processing all of these requests takes time. The sooner you start, the sooner you can get approved.But even if your insurer agrees that you’ve met the requirements of your policy, your work isn’t done quite yet. After all, you still have to establish exactly what kinds of roofing services you need and who’s going to perform them.3. Get a Roof Inspection to Determine What Your Roof NeedsAt this point, you’ve already proven that a severe weather event damaged your roof. Now you just need to determine what kind of roofing services you need. For most insurers, the only acceptable way to determine that is by scheduling a roof inspection.As part of your inspection, a roofing professional will take a look at your roof to assess the damage. If your roof is structurally sound, they will access your roof to take a closer look at the issues. They probably won’t need to enter your home to inspect your roof. However, they may need to talk to you about the issues you’ve noticed or look at a leaking ceiling from the inside.Once they’ve completed the inspection, your roofer will recommend either replacing your roof or repairing a smaller section of damage. You’ll then submit this recommendation to your insurer so that they can approve the repairs or replacement that you need.It’s important to be choosey when picking roof inspectors, though. For one thing, if your inspector isn’t affiliated with a licensed roofing company, your insurer probably won’t accept their report as valid. It’s also useful to pick roofers who know the insurance process and have done this before. Submitting a vague, unofficial report is almost as bad as not submitting any report at all.A roof inspection is a crucial part of making a homeowners insurance claim for your roof. That’s partially because your insurer needs to know what services you need, but also because your insurer needs to know how much those services are going to cost.4. Collect Roofing EstimatesAt this point, the only thing left to do is find out how much your roofing services will cost your insurer. Since you’ve already gotten a roof inspection, this should be no problem! When talking to your insurance agent, they should be able to tell you about their requirements for roofing estimates.For instance, some insurers only want to see one estimate and will pay that. For others, they may require estimates from multiple roofers. Other insurers might want multiple estimates from the same roofer. For example, if you need a roof replacement, they might want estimates for shingles, tiles, and metal. Generally speaking though, we wouldn’t recommend expecting your insurer to cover the cost of upgrading your roof from shingles to metal.As mentioned above, storm chasers are infamous for over-inflating their roofing estimates. That’s why it’s important to get an estimate from local roofers you can trust. At PITCH, we offer free, no-obligation roofing estimates so you can know exactly what you’re paying for and compare your options apples to apples. With insurance companies so wary of paying out more than they have to, this directness and transparency is exactly what your insurer is looking for! And with licensed insurance adjusters on staff, there is no better crew to help you navigate the insurance claim process.

																										Lowering Your Insurance Premium Through RoofingIn Florida, homeowners insurance premiums are higher than ever. And for most Floridians, those numbers are only going to increase. But there are ways to improve your roof and thus lower your premium, and some of these methods don’t even require much up-front investment on your part.Because of the state of homeowners insurance in Florida, insurers are extremely risk averse. Every old, worn-down roof makes them worry about potential payouts they could have to make. That’s why upgrading your roof can significantly lower your homeowners insurance premiums — by giving your insurer assurance that your home is protected, they’ll see you as a lower risk and offer you better rates.There are many different ways to upgrade a roof, though. Let’s talk about some of the ways you can lower your homeowners insurance in Florida by taking care of your roof!Roof ReplacementsIf you have a 20-year-old shingle roof, you’re probably paying a lot to insure that roof. In some cases, you may technically be able to get by for another couple of years before time or a weather event forces you to replace it. But in others, the right call could be installing a new roof to lower your insurance rates.A roof at the end of its life is extremely vulnerable to storm damage, and insurers know that. That’s why insurers charge more for old shingle roofs, even if there’s technically nothing wrong with them. By getting a new shingle roof put on with high-quality architectural shingles, you can greatly strengthen your hurricane protection. While this requires some up-front investment, it could be cheaper in the long run by saving you money on insurance premiums.And that’s just for replacing a shingle roof with new shingles. There is one way to get an even boost to your home’s protection: you can save money by upgrading to a metal roof.Going from shingles to metal roofing is a big improvement to your roof’s security. Whereas shingle roofs start to lose shingles at around 110 mph, metal roofs can easily withstand winds of 140 mph or more. Metal roofs also last much longer — three times as long as shingle roofs in some cases.Your insurer knows all of this, so by upgrading to a metal roof, you can drastically lower your level of risk and enjoy cheaper premiums. If metal roofing is in the budget, it could save you a lot of money in the long run!Hurricane-Resistant Roof ImprovementsYou don’t have to replace your entire roof to lower insurance premiums and keep your home safe. In fact, there are several simple improvements you can make to your roof that will greatly improve how well your home stands up to tropical storms and hurricanes.Some of the best ways to upgrade your roof without fully replacing it include:Hurricane Straps: These strips of metal re-adhere your roof to your home’s walls. This means that, even in the event of a hurricane, your roof isn’t going anywhere. These have been a requirement of new constructions since 2002, but your roof may not have them if it hasn’t been replaced since then.Secondary Water Barrier: Every roof comes with a water-resistant underlayment. But adding a secondary water barrier can further improve water resistance and reduce your risk of leaks in the event that your roof loses shingles during a storm.Roof Deck Attachments: Similar to hurricane straps, roof deck attachments help adhere your roof to the rest of your structure. This ensures that in all but the most severe weather, your roof will stay put.Making any of these roof improvements can protect your home in the event of a disaster and lower your homeowners insurance premiums. But at PITCH, we know the funds for roofing upgrades aren’t always there. If you’re interested in a way to save money while upgrading your roof, the My Safe Florida Home program could be exactly what you need.My Safe Florida HomeFor years and across multiple rounds of funding, the My Safe Florida Home program has been helping Floridians improve the hurricane resistance of their homes. But how does this program work, and how do you use it?There is one important note to make at the start. At the time of writing in October 2024, My Safe Florida Home has used up all of its funding and is not accepting new applications. That said, the program has run out of funding before and was then replenished in future legislative sessions. This means that there is every possibility that this program will receive more funding in 2025 and the coming years.Here’s how it works: For every $1 you spend on approved improvements (including the roof upgrades above), the program will give you $2, up to $10,000. For example, if you spent $15,000 on roof upgrades, My Safe Florida Home would give you back $10,000.That’s why this program is so popular among Florida homeowners. You can make significant roof upgrades while paying only a third of the total roofing costs. And when you consider the lower insurance premiums you’ll have after improving your roof’s safety, the savings could be even greater.When My Safe Florida Home receives more funding, you can find details on how to apply on their website. Historically, though, the program has given priority to low-income households as well as seniors. You can also check our website for future updates — as experienced local contractors, we’re the first to hear about changes to these programs, and we’ll always keep you informed of the latest roofing news in Florida!
